# PageV1P149
anchors:
- Root: ر-ف-ع (rafʿa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Elevation, raising, lifting upward — physical or spiritual exaltation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, rafʿa denotes the elevation of deeds and voices to the divine presence, signifying acceptance and proximity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical raising; metaphorical for the ascent of spiritual acts (e.g., dhikr) to God.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional clause (sharṭ) with "in lam" — expressing a graded hierarchy of merit, where the apodosis (jawāb) is governed by the protasis (sharṭ), indicating a logical necessity of falling back to a lesser but still virtuous station.
translation:
I say: Know that the sixth station of the method of ascent is this: if one cannot perform the most excellent deed, then one should not fall short of performing a virtuous deed. For the Prophet ﷺ said: «The most beloved of deeds to Allah are those that are most constant, even if they are few» — and constancy in a lesser virtue is better than abandoning it entirely for an excellence one cannot sustain.

In the Muwaṭṭaʾ (of Imam Mālik): When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his head from the bowing (rukūʿ) and said: «Allah hears the one who praises Him», a man behind him said: «Our Lord, to You is all praise — abundant, good, and blessed therein.» When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished his prayer, he said: «Who was the speaker just now?» The man replied: «I, O Messenger of Allah.» He ﷺ said: «I saw thirty-some angels vying with one another — which of them would write it first.»

Abū ʿUmar (Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr) said: In this (ḥadīth) is (proof) that raising the voice in dhikr during prayer does not harm; and likewise raising the voice with «Our Lord, to You is all praise.» Our evidence also includes what Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal narrated from Ibn Abī Awfā, who said: A man came while we were in the row behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: «Allah is Greater, greatly — and glory be to Allah morning and evening.» He said: The Muslims raised their heads and found the man strange, saying to themselves: Who is this raising his voice above the voice of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished, he said: «Who is this loud-voiced one?» It was said: This one, O Messenger of Allah. He ﷺ said: «By Allah, I saw speech ascending to the heavens until a door was opened for it, and it entered therein.»

In Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī: A man heard another man reciting «Say: He is Allah, the One» (Qul huwa Allāhu aḥad) and repeating it. When morning came, he went to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned that to him — and it seemed as though the man (who heard it) was belittling it. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: «By Him in Whose hand is my soul, verily it equals one-third of the Qurʾān.»

And in it also: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a man on a military expedition (sariyyah), and he would recite to his companions in their prayers, concluding with «Say: He is Allah, the One.» When they returned, they mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: «Ask him why he does that.» So they asked him, and he said: «Because it is the description of the Most Merciful, and I love to recite it.» The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «Inform him that Allah loves him.»

And in the Sīrah (biographies): ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl had a station (maqām) he would stand at — a station that was not to be disparaged for him. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat on Friday to address the people, he would say: «O people, this is...»

title_en: The Sixth Station: On the Criterion of Blameworthy Innovation and the Principle of Commanding the Opposite
arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 149

منهج الترقي/ المقام السادس: إن لم يكن في عمل أنضل فلا أقل من أن يكون في عمل ناضل 193
رسول الله بين أظهسركم أككرمكم الله ببه. فاتنصروه» وسزروه؛ واسمعوا له
.وأطيعواء ثم يجلس إلى أن ظهر نفاقه أسكته الناس. اه

فانظروا إن رسول اله يل ترك له مقامه؛ وإنما الناس هم الذين أسكتوه؛ ولم
يكن مثل هذا بدعة مذمومة: فقد تضمن هذا كله أن البدعة المذمومة هي التي تميث
السنة أو تكاد تفضي إلى موتها. وهذا كما يقوله الصوفية: لا تحكم على أفضل من
فاضل حتى تقيس الفاتت مع الحاصل. وكذا قول الأصوليين: النهي عن الشيء أمر
بضده أو بأحد أضداده؛ فانظره. فانظر بهذه النسية الصوفية والأصولية الدعاء دبر
الصلوات وأصبح وله الحمد والصلاة رحمكم الله

وركب هذا على مسألة في "العتيية" أظنه ربيعة كلم الإمام قبل أن يسلم أنه
راعي مذعب أهل العراق: أنه بالجلوس الأخير يخرج من الصلاة: ولاشك أن
صلاته باطلة على المذهب» فلو كان كلامه بعد تسليمة التحليل وقبل تسليمة الرد لا
شك أن الصلاة صحيحة وترك سنة؛ وكلامه حيتئذ بدعة مذمومة؛ فلو كان كلامه
بعد سلام الرد لقال متكر الدعاء: لا شيء عليه: وكذا لو مس ذكره أو خرج بالفورء
ونحن نقول: وكذلك إذا دعاء ونقول: مذهب أهل السنة أن النهي عن الشيء أمر
بضده أو بأحد أضداده إن كان ذا أضداد. فالناهي إذا عن الدعاء أمر بما يفعله تاركه»
ومعلوم ما أمره الشارع بفعل ذلك خصوضاء فنسبة المفعول من المتروك نسبة
واحدة؛ فاعرضها على الشرع على البراءة الأصلية؛ أي: لا تنسبها من الصلاة بوجه
الأنه قد خرج منها بتسليمة الرد. وانظر من هذا المعنى أن العبادة إذا فرغ منها كل ما
.يفعله بعد ذلك هو من نسبة ما يترك لا تعلق له بالعبادة المفروغ منها.

قال أبو حنيفة وأصحابه: لا بقال: الصلاة خير من النوم أثناء الأذان» بل بعد
الفراغ من الأذان. وفي "الموطا”: أن عبد الله بن عمر أذن في ليلة ذات يرد وريح»
فقال: ألا صلوا في الرحال. قال الباجي في "المتقى”: يحتمل أن يكون قوله هذا
بعد كمال الأذان» وهو الأولى: فانظر قول الباجي: وهو الأولى؛ فكأنه إذا أنى
المؤذن بأذانه على السنة لم يبق عليه حسبة بما يفعله؛ يكون كما قاله ابن العربي في
خصاء البهائم؛ ثم قال: هو جائز؛ لأنه لم يقصد به تعليق الحال بالدين لصنم يعيد
ولا لرب يوحد. إنما يقصدون به طيب اللحم؛ ومن هذا المعنى قوله: حديثة

# PageV1P150
anchors:
- Root: ن-ض-ل (naḍala)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Superiority in merit; precedence in excellence (al-faḍl wa al-sabq)
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Relative excellence in religious works; the comparative of "better" (afḍal) implying a scale of virtue
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of surpassing in rank; here used metaphorically for the hierarchy of devotional acts
- Root: ب-د-ع (badaʿa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To originate something without prior example (inshāʾ mā lā sābiqa lahu)
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Innovation in religion (bidʿah) — that which contradicts established Sunnah; blameworthy when it erases prophetic practice
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: creating anew; metaphorical: introducing practice into dīn without scriptural warrant
- Root: ن-ه-ي (nahā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Prohibition; forbidding with emphasis
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In uṣūl al-fiqh, prohibition entails commanding the opposite (al-nahy ʿan al-shayʾ amr bi-ḍiddihi)
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: interdiction; metaphorical: legal implication of the contrary action
- Sībawayh Rule: Taʿlīq al-ḥukm bi-al-ʿillah (Attribution of a ruling to its effective cause) — The legal effect is tied to the precise condition (e.g., speech after the first salutation vs. after the second), requiring exact syntactic-temporal parsing.
translation:
I say — may Allah have mercy upon you — and with Him is all praise and blessing:

Reflect upon the fact that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left his station [of leadership], and it was the people themselves who silenced him. This was not a blameworthy innovation (bidʿah madhmūmah), for all of this entails that the blameworthy innovation is that which erases the Sunnah or nearly leads to its death. This is as the Sufis say: "Do not judge one who is virtuous over another who is virtuous until you weigh the lost [good] against the obtained [good]." Likewise is the saying of the uṣūliyyūn (legal theorists): "Prohibition of a thing is a command for its opposite, or for one of its opposites" — so reflect upon this.

Apply this Sufi and uṣūlī principle to the supplication (duʿāʾ) after the obligatory prayers. I say: And to Him belongs praise, and prayers [upon the Prophet], may Allah have mercy upon you.

This principle is mounted upon a question in the "ʿUtbiyyah" — I think it was Rabīʿah who spoke to the Imām before he submitted [to the view] that he was the proponent of the school of the people of Iraq: that by the final sitting [in prayer] one exits from the prayer. There is no doubt that his prayer is invalid upon that school [if he speaks before the salutation]. But if his speech occurred after the salutation of tahlīl (the first salutation that dissolves the prayer) and before the salutation of radd (the second salutation of reply), then without doubt the prayer is valid, yet he has abandoned a Sunnah — and his speech at that moment is a blameworthy innovation. But if his speech were after the salutation of radd, then the one who denies the supplication would say: "There is nothing against him." Likewise, if he touched his penis or exited immediately [from the mosque].

And we say: Likewise, if he supplicates [after the second salutation], we hold — and this is the school of Ahl al-Sunnah — that prohibition of a thing is a command for its opposite, or for one of its opposites if it has opposites. So the one who prohibits supplication [after prayer] commands that which the abandoner of it does. And it is known that what the Lawgiver commands one to do is specific [to that context]. Thus, the attribution of the performed act [after the second salutation] to the abandoned act [of supplication within the prayer] is a single attribution. So present this to the Sacred Law upon the principle of original innocence (al-barāʾah al-aṣliyyah) — meaning: do not attribute it to the prayer in any way, because he has already exited from it by the salutation of radd.

And consider from this same meaning: when an act of worship is completed, everything one does afterward is of the attribution of what one leaves [behind], having no connection to the completed act of worship.

Abū Ḥanīfah and his companions said: One should not say "The prayer is better than sleep" during the adhān, but rather after completing the adhān. In the "Muwaṭṭaʾ," ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar gave the adhān on a cold and windy night and said: "Indeed, pray in your dwellings." Al-Bājī said in "al-Muntaqā": "It is probable that his saying this was after the completion of the adhān, and this is the preferred [view]." So reflect upon al-Bājī's saying "and this is the preferred" — as if when the muʾadhdhin delivers his adhān according to the Sunnah, nothing remains upon him regarding what he does [afterward]. This is as Ibn al-ʿArabī said regarding the castration of animals: then he said, "It is permissible, because they do not intend by it to attach the state of religion to an idol they worship, nor to a Lord they unify. They only intend by it the wholesomeness of the meat." And from this same meaning is his saying: "Ḥadīthah..."

title_en: Section 114 — On the Sixth Station of Ascent: When No Better Deed Exists, at Least Engage in a Productive One
arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 150

4-_منهج الترقي/ المقام السادس: إذ لم يكن في عمل أفضل فلا أقل من أن يكون في عمل ناسل
سورة (المائدة) نعمت الفائدة حديث مكذوب» ولكن نقوله نحن من قبل أنفسنا ولاا
|نأثره على أحد فتقول: سورة (المائدة) نعمت الفائدة.

ومن هذا المعنى ما حدثثي به من أثق به أنه هو أو غيره دخمل على السيد
المفتي السرقسطي رحمه الله في عيد النحر وأضحيته مزينة: فقال له في ذلك: فقال
اله الشيخ: السميراء أرادته.

ومن نحو هذا ما حدثني به سيدي أبو عمرو بن منظور حفظه الله عمن الخطيب
بمسجد القرويين شارح الحكم ابن عباد أنه كان له بعمامته طرز؛ فقيل له في ذلك»
اففال: إنه مليح؛ وهذا صرف بحسنى!؛ أي: لا تعلق للدين لا بترك هذا ولا بفعله.

والشيء يذكر بالشيء؛ قال مالك في النظر إلى المجذوم: أما في الفقه فلم
أسمع بكراهته. وأما خوف أن يفزع أو يقع في نفسه من ذلك شيء. قال ابن رشددة
مشل هذا أمره كل للمرأة بترك الدار؛ ولما وقع في نفسها أن ذهاب مالها يسبب
سكنى الدار. ومن هذا لا يحل الممرض على المصح مخافة أن تمرض إبله بققدر
الله فيظن أن ذلك أعداها. وانظر الباب الثالث والستين من "سراج الطرطوشي”: قاد
يكون من هذا المعنى أنه قيل لحكيم: ما الحزم؟ قال: سوء الظن يعني سوء الظطن
بنفسه؛ لا بغيره كما في "العتبية" عن ابن عمر قال: في وجودي للشمس خير من
سوه ظني.

وكنت أبحث لأهل الفحص لبس الرئدين كما قال مالك في المظال: ليست
من لباس السلف, وأباحها؛ لأنها تفي من البرد؛ فشنع هذا علي؛ فكان جوابي أن
قلت: الرندين ثوب رومي يضمحل التشبه به بالعجم في جنب منفعته) إذ هو ثوب
مقتصد ينتفع به ويقي من البرد.

ونص من أثق به من الأئمة أنه ليس كل ما فعلته العجم منهيًا عن ملابسته إلا
إذا نهت الشريعة عنه ودلت القواعد على تركه؛ والمراد بالأعاجم الذين نهينا عن
التشبه بهم أتباع الأكاسرة في ذلك الزمان في سرفهم ونحوه: ويختص النهي بما
يفعلونه على خلاف مقتضى شرعناء وأما ما فعلوه على وفق الندب أو الإيجاب أو
الإباحة في شرعنا فلا نترك ذلك لأجل تعاطيهم إياه؛ لأن الشرع لا ينهي عن التشبه
بمن يفعل ما أذن الله فيه. فقد حفر ول الخندق على المدينة تشبها بالأعاجم حتى

# PageV1P151
anchors:
- Root: ن-س-ل (n-s-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To generate, produce offspring; to be fruitful, productive, yielding benefit.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Deeds that bear spiritual or worldly fruit (natījah), as opposed to sterile or idle acts.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — biological reproduction; metaphorical — any action yielding tangible benefit.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional clarification) — the phrase "نعمت الفائدة" functions as an explicative appositive to the Surah, emphasizing commendation.
translation:
I say — and this is the sixth station of ascent: When one finds no deed superior [to what he already does], then let him at least engage in a deed that is productive (nāsil).  

As for the saying, "Sūrat al-Māʾidah — excellent is its benefit," this is a fabricated ḥadīth. But we say it from ourselves, not attributing it to anyone. So we say: "Sūrat al-Māʾidah — excellent is its benefit."

From this same meaning is what was related to me by one I trust — that he or another entered upon the Sayyid Muftī al-Saraqusṭī (may God have mercy on him) on the Day of Sacrifice (ʿĪd al-Naḥr), and his sacrificial animal was adorned. He said something to him about that, and the Shaykh replied: "The Sumayrāʾ woman wanted it."  

And of similar import is what my master Abū ʿAmr ibn Manẓūr (may God preserve him) related to me from the khaṭīb of the Qarawiyyīn Mosque, the commentator on al-Ḥikam, Ibn ʿAbbād — that he had embroidery on his turban. It was said to him about that, and he replied: "It is handsome." This is a turning away with a good excuse (ṣarf bi-ḥusnā), meaning: religion has no attachment either to abandoning this or to doing it.

One thing recalls another. Mālik said regarding looking at a leper: "As for jurisprudence (fiqh), I have heard no disapproval of it. But [there is] fear that he might be frightened or that something might enter his soul." Ibn Rushd said: "The like of this is the case of the man who ordered his wife to leave the house, and it entered her soul that the loss of her wealth was caused by dwelling in that house." And from this [same principle], one does not let a sick camel graze alongside a healthy one, lest its camel fall ill by God's decree, and he then thinks that it infected it.  

And look at Chapter Sixty-Three of "Sirāj al-Ṭurṭūshī" — perhaps it is of this meaning: it was said to a sage, "What is prudence (ḥazm)?" He said: "Suspicion of evil" — meaning suspicion of oneself, not of others, as in al-ʿUtbiyyah from Ibn ʿUmar: "My finding the sun better than my suspicion of evil."

I was researching for the people of investigation the wearing of the "randayn" (a type of garment), just as Mālik said about awnings (maẓāll): "They are not from the dress of the Salaf," yet he permitted them because they protect from cold. This was censured against me. My response was to say: The randayn is a Roman garment; the resemblance to non-Arabs (al-ʿAjam) in it dissolves in comparison to its benefit, for it is a modest garment that is useful and protects from cold.

And a text from one I trust among the imams states: Not everything that the non-Arabs (al-ʿAjam) do is forbidden to wear, unless the Sacred Law (Sharīʿah) prohibits it and the principles (qawāʿid) indicate abandoning it. The intended meaning of "non-Arabs" (al-Aʿājim) whom we are forbidden to resemble are the followers of the Chosroes (Akāsirah) in that era, in their extravagance and the like. The prohibition is specific to what they do contrary to the dictates of our Law. As for what they do in accordance with the commendable (nadb), the obligatory (ījāb), or the permissible (ibāḥah) in our Law, we do not abandon it because of their practice of it — for the Law does not prohibit resembling those who do what God has permitted. For the Prophet (peace be upon him) dug the trench around Medina in imitation of the non-Arabs, until...

title_en: The Path of Ascent — Sixth Station: On Moderation in Dress and the Limits of Personal Scruple (Waraʿ)
arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 151

منهج الترقي/ المقام السادس: إن لم يكن في عمل أفضل فلا أقل من أن يكون في عمل نامل 195
تعجب الأحزاب منه» ثم علموا أنه بدلالة سلمان الفارسي عليه.

والرندين المذكور هذا باس مقتصد لا سرف فيه يتفع به ويفي البسرد
ويضاهي أيضًا لباس المظال. قال مالك فيها: ليست من لباس السلف وأباحها؛ الأنها
تفي البرده فلا فرق بين هذا وبين الرندين» وصح أن رسول الله لبس جبة رومية.
الكمين. قال ابن العربي في "مسالكه”: كانت شامية والشام في ذلك الوقت
اللروم؛ ففي هذا جواز لبس الضيق من الثياب؛ وهو مستحب في الغزو؛ ومن
التشمير والتأسي برسول اله يك ولا بأس به في الحضر. اهف ونحو هذا لأبي عمر
في "الاستذكار".

.وقال ناصر الدين المشذالي: كرهت الصلاة في السراويل؛ لأنه يحد العورة
ويصفهاء وقيل: لأنه من زي العجم؛ ورد هذا التعليل بأن رسول الله يق صلى في
جبة ضيفة شامية؛ وهي: القباء وهي من لبس الأعاجم؛ ووجه آخر منصوص لمن
أثق به من العلماء المعتمدين: أن رسول اله يل نهى العرب أن يتشبهوا بالعجم.
ولم بأت أنه نهى وفدًا قدم عليه من وفود الأعاجم أن يتقلوا عن زيهم لزي العرب»
وهذا هو مقتضى مأخذ ابن رشد؛ معلوم من المذهب كراهة التلشم؛ واستحبه ابن
رشد للمرابطين؛ قال: لأنه زيهم به عرفوا وهم حماة الدين؛ قال: وقد خلق الله
الخلق وباعد بينهم في البلادء وخالف يينهم في الأزياء؛ فلا يجب على أحد الرجوع.
عن زيه إلى زي سواه؛ والتلشم للمرابطين هو زيهم؛ فيستحب لهم التزامه؛ ويكره
لهم مفارقته. قال: ولا حرج على من صلى منهم متلثمًا بخلاف غيرهم. اه وقد
اتبين مما قررته أن خطب الرندين مضمحل في جنب الشرائس واللانص وقطائف
الحرير.

وينبغي للمتورع أن يتورع في خاصة نفسه؛ ولا يحل له ولا يجوز أن يحمل
الناس على ورعه؛ فإن الورع فضل؛ وليس بفرضص يوشك أنه إن أشار عليهم بحال
انفسه أن يدخخل عليهم شغبًا في دينهم وحبرة في قلوبهم؛ وقد لا يتركون؛ فيفعلون
وفي قلوبهم حزازة. فقد نصوا أن من أقدم على حلال صرف ينه متشابها أن قلبه
يقسى بذلك ويظلم؛ كما أنه لو أقدم على حرام يعتقد أنه حلال لا يقسى قلبه ولا
يعاقب على فعله. وإذا أقدم على حلال صرف يعتقد حرمته فعليه درك المخالفة.

# PageV1P152
anchors:
- Root: ل-ب-س (l-b-s)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To cover, clothe, envelop; the act of wearing that conceals the body.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Physical covering as a metaphor for spiritual state — the garment (libās) of taqwā {«وَلِبَاسُ التَّقْوَىٰ»} (Q. 7:26).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Ḥaqīqah — actual cloth; Majāz — the "garment" of character or piety.
- Root: و-ر-ع (w-r-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To shrink back, abstain, be cautious; the root of waraʿ (scrupulous abstention).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The virtue of avoiding doubtful matters (shubuhāt) to safeguard one's religion — a supererogatory station, not an obligation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical withdrawal from harm; Metaphorical — inner restraint from moral ambiguity.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional clause with fa-jawāb (فجواب الشرط) — the apodosis introduced by fa- after an implied condition (e.g., "if one advances upon... then his heart hardens"), governing the causal nexus between action and spiritual consequence.
translation:
I say — and this is the sixth station of the path of ascent: If one cannot attain the most excellent of deeds, then let him not fall short of performing a deed that is moderate and sound.

The two garments mentioned here — the randaīn (a type of striped cloth) — constitute a middle course, containing no extravagance; it provides benefit and suffices against the cold. It also resembles the clothing of those who seek refuge in caves (al-muẓallīn). Mālik said concerning it: "It is not from the dress of the Salaf," yet he permitted it — because it suffices against the cold, so there is no difference between this and the randaīn. And it is authentically established that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wore a Roman gown (jubbah rūmiyyah) with narrow sleeves. Ibn al-ʿArabī said in his "Masālik": "It was Syrian, and Syria at that time was under Roman influence; so in this there is a permissibility of wearing tight garments — and it is recommended (mustaḥabb) in military expeditions, as part of tucking up one's garments and following the example of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ — and there is no objection to it in settled life." End quote. Similar is stated by Abū ʿUmar in "al-Istidhkār."

Nāṣir al-Dīn al-Mashdhālī said: "I disapproved of praying in trousers (sarāwīl), because it delineates the ʿawrah and describes it." And it was said: "Because it is the dress of the non-Arabs (ʿajam)." This rationale was refuted by the fact that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed in a tight Syrian gown — which is the qabāʾ — and that is from the dress of the non-Arabs. Another transmitted opinion from one I trust among the reliable scholars: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the Arabs from imitating the non-Arabs. Yet it has not come down that he forbade any delegation of non-Arab envoys who came to him from abandoning their own dress for that of the Arabs. And this is the purport of Ibn Rushd's position. It is well-known in the school (madhhab) that wearing the lithām (face-veil) is disliked (makrūh); Ibn Rushd, however, deemed it recommended (mustaḥabb) for the frontier-guards (murābiṭūn). He said: "Because it is their distinguishing dress by which they are recognized, and they are the protectors of the religion." He said: "Allāh created creation and dispersed them across lands, and diversified their garments; so no one is obliged to abandon his own dress for another's. The lithām for the murābiṭūn is their dress; thus it is recommended for them to adhere to it, and disliked for them to abandon it." He said: "And there is no sin upon one of them who prays while wearing the lithām, unlike others." End quote.

It has become clear from what I have established that the matter of the randaīn is utterly insignificant in comparison to the sharānis (coarse woolen garments), the lānaṣ (a type of rough cloth), and the silk brocades (qaṭāʾif al-ḥarīr).

It behooves the scrupulous one (al-mutawarriʿ) to exercise his scruple (waraʿ) in his own private affairs; it is not lawful for him, nor permissible, to impose his scruple upon the people. For waraʿ is a virtue of excellence (faḍl), not an obligation (farḍ). It is likely that if he points them toward his own personal state, he will introduce into their religion a disturbance and into their hearts a vexation; and they may not abandon their ways, and so they act while harboring resentment in their hearts. For the scholars have explicitly stated: Whoever advances upon a purely lawful matter while deeming it doubtful — his heart will thereby harden and darken; just as if he advanced upon a forbidden matter while believing it lawful, his heart would not harden, nor would he be punished for his act. But if he advances upon a purely lawful matter while believing it forbidden, then upon him lies the liability of having contravened [the divine permission].

title_en: Section 116 — On Following Customary Practices (ʿAwāʾid) in Acts of Righteousness and Social Conduct
arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 152

96 ___منهج الترفي/ المقام السادس: إن لم يكن في عمل أنضل فلا أفل من أن يكون في عمل فاضل

وكان بدو عبيد لا يفرون بالزكاة المفروضة؛ فكان بعض شيوخ ابن أبي زيد
يقول: لا تبرأ الذمة بدفمها إليهم؛ وكان غيره يقول: تبرأء قال الشيخ ابن أبي زيد:
وكنت أستحب هذا لأنهم أن يؤدوها متأولين خير من أن يتركوها عامدين. قال إلى
أن شنع فيها الحال كما قال انظره في "المدارك".

وانظر من هذا المعنى عوائد الناس في صلة أرحامهم وتطييب أطعمتهم؛ ب:
بلا شك أن من الجفاء على الأقارب والجناية على العيال ترك ذلك» كما تقدم قرية
في ترك القيام للداخل ونحو هذا. قال أبو حامد في "الإحياء”: إذا جرت عادة بتتحية
العمامة على الموافقة للصاحب. فالموافقة في هذه الأمور من حسن الصحبة
والعشرة والمخالفة توحشء ولا بد من مخالقة الناس بأخلاقهم كما ورد الخبر؛ لا
سيما إذا كانت أخلاًا فيها حسن العشرة والمجاملة وتطبيب القلب بالمساعدة. قال:
وليس كل ما تحكم إباحته منقولًا عن الصحابة؛ وإنما المحذور ما يراغم سنة
مأثورة. اه وعلى هذا يتخرج ما في كتب أهل الأحكام والنص للمتيطي: قال: في
المزارعة إذا شرط رب الأرض هدايا في العيدين والنيروز والمهرجان» وساوى
ذلك مع العمل كراء الأرض» فهو جائز وتعقد فيه. وعلى العامل كذا وكذا دجاجة.
سمينة فتية في فصل التبروز وخروف سمين حي ابن شهرين؛ وفي المهرجان كذلك
بعد أن قوما ذلك كله مع عمل العامل.

وانظر من نحو قول الشيخ القدوة السرقسطي: السميراء أرادته ومن نحو قول
الشيخ شارح الحكم: لكنه مليح. ومن نحو قول ابن العربي: لم يقصد به تعليق
الحال بالدين لصنم يعيد ولا لرب يوحد؛ هو قول ابن عرفة في البوقات في المنار
قال: إنما هي قوارع لا يتركب عليها مفسدة إلا إيقاظ الناس للسحور.

قال السيد مفتي تونس البرزلي: وحاصل هذا أنهم استسهلوها؛ لكون الناس
تمالؤوا عليهاء ولا يتبني عليها مفسدة شرعية. قال هذا بعد أن ذكر أن قاضي
القيروان بعث إلى ابن عبد السلام أن بعضهم أنكر النقير على المنار في رمضانء
وقال: هي معصية في أفضل الشهور في أول قبلة؛ اختطت بالمغرب وهو جامع
الفيروان» فأجابه ابن عبد السلام: إن عاد لمثل هذا فأدبه؛ ثم رشح هذا البرزلي
قائلا: إن هذه المسائل الخلاف فبها موجود بالجواز والكراهة؛ لا ينبغي لأحد أن
يخالف فيهاء ثم نقل كلام ابن لب بلفظه معزوا لبعض الشبوخ: وأتى بنصه من قوله.

# PageV1P153
anchors:
- Root: ع-و-د (ʿ-w-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Return, repetition, habit; what recurs and becomes customary (ʿādah).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Custom as a secondary norm in religious practice, distinct from revealed command (amr) but operative in social ethics (muʿāsharah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: returning to a place or state; metaphorical: established practice that shapes communal behavior.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Responsive Construction (Jawāb al-Sharṭ) — The phrase "if not in a more excellent act, then at least in a virtuous one" uses the conditional to rank degrees of merit, with the apodosis carrying the pragmatic recommendation.
translation:
I say — and success is from God:

The Sixth Station: If one cannot engage in a more excellent act, one should not fall short of engaging in a virtuous act.

It was the case that the Banū ʿUbayd did not pay the obligatory alms (zakāh) to the poor; so some of the teachers of Ibn Abī Zayd said: "The obligation is not discharged by paying it to them," while others said: "It is discharged." The Shaykh Ibn Abī Zayd said: "I preferred the latter view, because their paying it with a mistaken interpretation (taʾwīl) is better than their abandoning it deliberately." He continued until the matter became notorious, as he mentioned — see it in "al-Madārik."

Consider, from this same meaning, the customary practices of people in maintaining family ties (ṣilat al-arḥām) and in making their foods pleasant. There is no doubt that neglecting that constitutes harshness toward relatives and a transgression against one's dependents — as has preceded regarding the neglect of standing up for the one entering, and similar matters.

Abū Ḥāmid said in "al-Iḥyāʾ": "When a custom has arisen of greeting with the turban in accordance with one's companion, then conforming in such matters is part of good companionship and fellowship, while opposing it breeds alienation. One must necessarily adapt to people's ways, as the report (khabar) has come: 'Adapt to people's character traits' — especially when those traits involve good fellowship, courteousness, and comforting the heart through assistance." He said: "Not everything that is judged permissible is transmitted from the Companions; rather, what is objectionable is that which clashes with an established sunnah." End quote.

Upon this is based what is found in the books of legal rulings, and the text of al-Matyīṭī: He said concerning sharecropping (muzāraʿah): If the landowner stipulates gifts on the two festivals, on Nawrūz, and on Mihrajān, and equates that with the labor as part of the land's rent, then it is permissible and the contract is validly concluded upon it. The worker owes such-and-such fat, young chickens at the time of Nawrūz, and a fat lamb of two months; likewise at Mihrajān — after having valued all that together with the worker's labor.

Consider also the saying of the Shaykh, the model (al-qudwah), al-Saraqusṭī: "The evening meal (samīrāʾ) intended him," and the saying of the Shaykh, the commentator on al-Ḥikam: "But it is pleasant," and the saying of Ibn al-ʿArabī: "It was not intended thereby to attach the matter to religion — neither for an idol that is worshipped nor for a Lord who is affirmed as One." This is the saying of Ibn ʿArafah concerning the trumpets (būqāt) on the minaret: He said: "They are merely alarms; no corruption attaches to them except the waking of people for the pre-dawn meal (saḥūr)."

The Sayyid, Muftī of Tunis, al-Burzulī said: "The sum of this is that they deemed them permissible because people have concurred upon them, and no legal corruption follows from them." He said this after mentioning that the judge of Qayrawān had sent to Ibn ʿAbd al-Salām that some had denounced the trumpet on the minaret during Ramaḍān, saying: "It is a disobedience in the most virtuous of months, in the direction of the first qiblah, founded in the Maghrib — and it is the congregational mosque of Qayrawān." Ibn ʿAbd al-Salām replied: "If he repeats such, discipline him." Then al-Burzulī reinforced this, saying: "These are matters of disagreement (khilāf) in which permissibility and disapproval both exist; no one should oppose them." Then he transmitted the words of Ibn Lubbah verbatim, attributed to some of the teachers, and quoted his text from his saying.

title_en: Section 117 — On the Permissibility of Speech During the Adhān, the Caller's Announcements, and the Night Vigil of the Pious Predecessors
arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 153

منهج الترفي/ المفام السادس: إن لم يكن في عمل أنضل فلا أقل من أن يكون في عمل فاضل 197

قال بعض الشيوخ: إذا كان الخلاف هكذاء وأنى بكلام ابن لب إلى آخره.
وانظر أيضًا بنسبة المؤذن لا أنهى المؤذنين للنهي عن: الصلاة رحمكم الله
ونحوها بعد الفراغ من الأذان. ولا ما في "صحيح البخاري” عن الحسن قال لا
بأس أن يضحك وهو يؤذن. قال أبو عمر: وأجاز الكلام في الأذان أحمد وقنادة
اوعروة وصرد.

.وفي "صحيح البخاري" أيضًا أن أسامة قال: الصلاة يا رسول الله وفيه أيضًا
أن رسول اله وق أعتم بالعشاء؛ فقال عمر: الصلاة نام التساء.

قال ابن بطال: فيه أن الأدون يذكر الأعلى: قال مالك: لم ييلغني أن تسليم
المؤذن على الإمام كان في الزمن الأول: قال أبو عمر: أول من فعل ذلك معاوية».
أمر المؤذن يشعره يقول: السلام على أمير المؤمنين؛ الصلاة يرحمك الله. واخقار
ابن الماشجون أن يقول: السلام عليك أيها الأميرء حي على الصلاة: قال أبو عمر:
فمن خشي الشغل عن الصلاة بما يجوز فعله فلا بأس أن يقيم من يؤذنه. وفي
الصحيح أن رسول اله قل أمر بلالا ينادي: الصلاة جامعة؛ واستحسن الشافعي أن
يقال ذلك عند كل صلاة لا يؤذن لهاء قال عياض: والذي استحسنه الشافعي حسن.

ولما ذكر أبو عمر الخلاف في الإعلام بالجنازة رشح الجواز بأن قال:
أجمعوا أن شهود الجنائز خير وعمل بر؛ وأجمعوا على أن الدعاء إلى الخير من
.وفي 'الموطا" و"رقاتق ابن المبارك": أن عمر رضي الله عنه قال لرجل: كيف
أنت؟ قال: أحمد الله إليك: قال عمر: هذا أردت منك» قال ابن عمر: كنا لعلنا لتقي
في اليوم مرا يسأل بعضنا بعضًاء وإن يريد بذلك إلا الحمد لفه.

ونقل ابن بطال أن أبا هريرة وابن عمر كانا يخرجان إلى السوق لأيام العشر
يكبران ويكبر الناس بتكبيرهما. قال ابن بطال: وكان المكبر لا ينكر عليه. وفي
الحديث الصحيح على حسب ما ذكره الترمذي: أن رسول اله يو كان إذا ذهب
اللبل يقول: "يا أبها الناس: اذكروا الله جاءت الراجفة تتبعها الرادفة؛ جاء الموت
بما فيه”"؛ قال أبي: فقلت: يا رسول اله يق إني أكثر الصلاة عليك؛ فكم أجعل

# PageV1P155
anchors:
- Root: ن-د-و (n-d-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To call out, summon, proclaim publicly; the act of making a vocal announcement to gather or alert a group.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In religious context, denotes the formal call (adhān) and any licit public invocation (nidā') aimed at spiritual benefit, not idle clamor.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for audible summons; metaphorical (majāz) when applied to the inner call of conscience or divine prompting.
- Root: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To reckon, account, or deem sufficient; also to admonish or correct (iḥtisāb) in the public weal.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The theological virtue of commanding good and forbidding evil (ḥisbah), rooted in accountability before God.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for arithmetic reckoning; metaphorical for moral reckoning and the role of the muḥtasib (market inspector of morals).
- Root: س-ر-ي (s-r-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To travel by night; a night journey or vigil.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Quranic usage, denotes the night journey of the believer's soul toward God, and the spiritual discipline of night prayer (qiyām al-layl).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical night travel; metaphorical for the soul's ascent through vigil and remembrance.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of 'Aṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — When a noun is followed by another that clarifies it without a conjunction, the second is in apposition, as in "the caller (al-mu'adhdhin)" and "the announcer (al-munādi)" in the same context, ensuring precise referential identity.
translation:
I say — and with God is success:

Some of the shaykhs have said: When the disagreement is as you have seen, and where is the recourse to the words of Ibn Lubāb and so forth? Consider also the attribution to the mu'adhdhin — not the most virtuous of mu'adhdhins — regarding the prohibition of saying "Prayer, may God have mercy on you" (al-ṣalāh raḥimakum Allāh) and similar phrases after the completion of the adhān. Nor [consider] what is in the Ṣaḥīḥ of al-Bukhārī, on the authority of al-Ḥasan, who said: There is no harm in one laughing while he gives the adhān. Abū ʿUmar said: Aḥmad, Qatādah, ʿUrwah, and Ṣāliḥ permitted speech during the adhān.

Also in the Ṣaḥīḥ of al-Bukhārī: Usāmah said, "Prayer, O Messenger of God" — and in it also, that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) delayed the ʿIshā' prayer, so ʿUmar said, "Prayer — the women have slept."

Ibn Baṭṭāl said: In this [hadith] is [evidence] that the lower may remind the higher. Mālik said: It has not reached me that the mu'adhdhin's greeting to the imam was [done] in the earliest period. Abū ʿUmar said: The first to do that was Muʿāwiyah — he ordered the mu'adhdhin to announce: "Peace be upon the Commander of the Faithful; prayer, may God have mercy on you." And Ibn al-Mājishūn disapproved of saying: "Peace be upon you, O prince; come to prayer (ḥayya ʿalā al-ṣalāh)." Abū ʿUmar said: Whoever fears being distracted from prayer by what is permissible to do, there is no harm in his appointing someone to remind him. In the Ṣaḥīḥ, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) commanded Bilāl to call out: "Prayer in congregation" (al-ṣalāh jāmiʿah). Al-Shāfiʿī deemed it good to say this at every prayer for which no adhān is given. ʿIyāḍ said: What al-Shāfiʿī deemed good is indeed good.

And when Abū ʿUmar mentioned the disagreement concerning announcing the funeral (al-iʿlām bi-al-janāzah), he strengthened the permissibility by saying: They are unanimous that attending funerals is good and a pious deed, and they are unanimous that calling to good is [also] a pious deed.

In the Muwaṭṭa' and in the Zuhd of Ibn al-Mubārak: ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him) said to a man: How are you? He said: I praise God to you. ʿUmar said: This is what I wanted from you. Ibn ʿUmar said: We would often meet in a single day, asking one another, intending thereby nothing but the praise of God.

Ibn Baṭṭāl transmitted that Abū Hurayrah and Ibn ʿUmar would go out to the market during the ten days [of Dhū al-Ḥijjah], proclaiming the takbīr, and the people would proclaim the takbīr with their takbīr. Ibn Baṭṭāl said: The one who proclaimed the takbīr was not rebuked. In the authentic hadith, as al-Tirmidhī mentioned: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), when night fell, would say: {«O people, remember God — the Rajifah has come, followed by the Rādifah; death has come with all that it contains»}. Ubayy said: I said, O Messenger of God, I pray much upon you; how much of my prayer should I devote to you?

And Zamʿah was residing at al-Muḥaṣṣab, standing in prayer for a long night; when it was the last part of the night (saḥar), he would call out at the top of his voice: O caravan that has halted for the night — will you sleep all this night? Will you not rise and depart? Then they would spring up — one could hear from here one weeping, from there one crying out, from there one supplicating, from there one reciting, from there one performing ablution. When dawn broke, he would call at the top of his voice:

"At morning, the people praise the night journey."

And ʿUrwah (may God be pleased with him) was in Basrah, standing at night, crying out in the roads, frightening [people], and reciting the words of God Most High: {«Do the people of the towns feel secure from Our punishment coming upon them by night while they sleep?»} [al-Aʿrāf: 97] — and the [following] verses.

Al-Masīlī adduced this report as evidence for the mu'adhdhins' rising at the saḥar [to call], and Ibn ʿAttāb also gave a fatwā permitting that. ʿIyāḍ said: Ibn ʿAttāb was among the muftīs — a memorizer, a deep thinker, one of the most reliable scholars, one who devoted his life to hearing hadith, recorded it, and mastered it. He said: He followed the way of the people of virtue; sound in judgment, prudent in intellect, upon the path of the early predecessors. Ibn Dhakwān asked him about the muḥtasib who rose to censure the mu'adhdhin standing in the middle of the night supplicating. Ibn ʿAttāb said: There is nothing in this to be censured; your knowledge encompasses what God has mentioned of encouragement. God Most High said: {«In houses which God has permitted to be raised, and His name to be remembered therein»} [al-Nūr: 36]. He said: Censuring in this matter is not permissible, for that is the remembrance of God, which expands the breasts of the believers and reassures their hearts — {«Truly in the remembrance of God do hearts find rest»} [al-Raʿd: 28]. And when has one who supplicates with prayer and seeking forgiveness been seen to be placed in a position of censure and reproach? Has the muḥtasib not heard the saying of God Most High: {«And do not repel those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His face»} [al-Anʿām: 52]? # PageV1P156
anchors:
- Root: ن-د-ب (n-d-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To call, summon, or invite; a thing sought after and urged.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A religiously recommended act (mandūb) — that which the Lawgiver urges without making it obligatory.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: calling someone. Metaphorical: the Law's gentle summons to an act, distinct from command (amr).
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Answer Ellipsis (ḥadhf jawāb al-sharṭ) — the protasis "if he does not do it" is followed by an implied apodosis, requiring contextual reconstruction.
translation:
I say — and this is the sixth station of the method of ascent: If one cannot attain the most excellent of deeds, then let him not fall short of performing a recommended act (mandūb). For when the righteous predecessors (salaf) set out on journeys, they would appoint one another to wake the Qur'an-reciters for their standing in prayer at the dawn hours; so you would hear their voices from every waystation. And the answer of al-Masīlī was that he said: "Everything this muezzin does is good, commanded, and urged upon — from reciting the Qur'an, supplication, reminding the people, and frightening them — it is an ancient practice of the righteous in the cities of the Muslims."

Already mentioned is the saying of Abū ʿUmar: "Whatever God has not forbidden, nor His Prophet, nor the consensus of the people has declared forbidden — there is no meaning in anyone's disapproving of it." And the saying of Shihāb al-Dīn and ʿIzz al-Dīn has preceded: that the Sacred Law is as cautious in urging recommended acts as it is in urging obligatory ones; so whatever a people deem good to do is more fitting. And the saying of Abū ʿUmar has preceded: "A recommended act is never lower in rank than the permissible (mubāḥ)." Ibn al-ʿArabī said in his Aḥkām, from one of his shaykhs: that when we entered a mosque to stay for an hour, he would say: "Intend iʿtikāf (seclusion), and you will find rest."

And consider from this meaning: a man finds no incentive to perform the major ablution (ghusl) at dawn or after it on Friday, if he does not do it, and it becomes impossible for him to bathe at the time of going out (to the mosque) — then it is better that he bathe (early). For if it were an obligation, he would have to fulfill it; and if it were a fast-breaking in Ramadan, he would not have to expiate. Ibn Rushd said: The apparent (meaning) of the Mudawwana is the disapproval of praying with the tasmiya (saying "In the name of God") at the time of slaughtering; then he said: "There is no basis for this disapproval." And the saying of Mālik has preceded: "The one who sacrifices saying: 'O God, by You and to You' — it is a supplication." Ibn Rushd said: "There is no harm in that, and he is rewarded."

In al-Tirmidhī, on the permissibility of the prostration of thankfulness (sajdat al-shukr), action upon it is (affirmed) by most scholars; and Mālik did not disapprove of it. He said in al-ʿĀriḍa: "Even if Mālik had not disapproved of it — and prostrating to God is always the obligatory (duty) — so whenever the slightest cause for prostration is found, let him seize it." End of Ibn al-ʿArabī's text.

So consider the second branch at the beginning of the book: that disagreement over the legitimacy (of an act) does not prevent the pious caution (waraʿ) of performing it; and it is never lower in rank than the permissible. And this position is my own place of finding (i.e., my ijtihād); but I have sworn not to show any opinion except what I have already shown. In sum, the attachment of all these things is only to what lies within a man's capacity (milk), as will come from Abū ʿUmar in his Tamhīd. For that reason, the sayyid, the mufti of Tunis, al-Burzulī — may God renew His mercy upon him — said, when addressing one who tore apart (the reputation of) a woman presented to him, and who sowed discord among the common folk, their mufti, and their khaṭīb: "You, O this one, have turned to a recommended act (mustaḥabb) that is permissible to abandon, or a disliked act (makrūh) better than it — and all of that is a matter of disagreement. And disagreement, when it is in..."

title_en: Section 119 — On the Sixth Station: If One Cannot Attain the Best Deed, One Should Not Fall Below a Virtuous Deed; On the Prohibition of Backbiting and Its Subtle Forms

### | الصفحة 156

0___منهج الترفي/ المقام السادس: إن لم يكن في عمل أفضل فلا أفل من أن يكون في عمل فاضل
التحريم والتحليل لا حسبة فيه؛ فكيف يحتسب فيما ليس من الحلال والحرام؛ قال
أبو عمر بن عبد البر: ألا ترى أن الصحابة رضي الله عنهم اختلفوا وهم الأسوة؛ فلم
يعب أحد منهم على مخالفه؛ ولا وجد عليه في نفسه؛ فإلى الله الشكوى؛ وهو
المستعان على أمة نحن بين أظهرها تستحل الأعراض إذا خولفت. اه كلام أبي
عمر.

نم نقل في "نمهيده' إلى أسامة بن شريك قال: شهدت الأعاريب يسألون

الحرج إلا امرأ اقترض من عرض أخيه شيئاء فذلك الذي حرج وهلك”'": وإنما
هذا لأن العرض من الظلم الذي لا يتركه الله ولو كان المغتاب ظالما أو فاسقًاا إذ
كل المؤمن على المؤمن حرام؛ دمه وماله وعرضه: فإن كان القائم مدعوا للشها:
أو ممن بسطت يده في الأرض؛ فقد قالوا: لا باح له أن يذكر من عرض الفاسق إلا
القدر المحتاج إليه لأجل التغبير عليه مع من له قدرة على التغبير عليه. وأما التفكه
بعرض المؤمن الجاني فلا يحل له ولا يجوز كما قاله عوف؛ قال: دخلت على ابن
اسيرين فتناولت الحجاج؛ فقال ابن سيرين: إن الله حكم عدل» فكما يأخذ من
الحجاج؛ يأخذ للحجاج؛ وإنك إذا لقيت الله غدا كان أصغر ذنب أصبته أشد عليك
من أعظم ذنب أصابه الحجاج؛ فالتفكه بعرض الفاسق حرام بإجماع. وقد تقدم قول
الفضيل: ما يأخذ سفيان أقل مما يستحق» ثم خلا به وعذله.

ومن "الاحياء': أخبث أنواع الغيبة إفهام المقصود على صيغة أهل الصلاح»

الحطام إذا كان قصده بهذا إفهام غيره؛ وقد يقدم مدح من بريد غبيته؛ فيقول: ما

# PageV1P157
anchors:
- Root: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To reckon, count, or account; also to deem or suppose. The noun ḥisbah denotes a voluntary act of seeking reward from God.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, ḥisbah refers to an act performed purely for divine recompense, not for worldly gain or legal obligation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "counting"; metaphorically, it means "to intend by one's action the reward of God." Here, the author denies that ḥisbah applies to matters outside the lawful/unlawful (ḥalāl/ḥarām) domain.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional clause with "in lam" (if not) — the protasis is negated by "lam," and the apodosis is introduced by "fa-lā" (then not), indicating a necessary consequence of falling short.
translation:
I say: The sixth station — if one cannot attain the best deed, then one should not fall below a virtuous deed.

Know that prohibition and permission (taḥrīm wa-taḥlīl) admit no personal reckoning (ḥisbah); so how could one seek reward in what is neither lawful nor unlawful? Abū ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said: "Do you not see that the Companions (may God be pleased with them) differed among themselves, and they are the exemplars? Yet none of them reproached his opponent, nor did he harbor resentment in himself against him. So to God is the complaint; and He is the one whose aid is sought against a community in whose midst we live, who deem it lawful to attack reputations when they are contradicted." This ends the words of Abū ʿUmar.

It is transmitted in his "Tamhīd" from Usāmah ibn Sharīk, who said: "I witnessed the Bedouins asking the Messenger of God (peace be upon him): 'Is there any sin upon us in such-and-such?' He replied: 'O servants of God, God has removed hardship, except for a man who has encroached upon the honor of his brother — that is the one who has fallen into ruin and perdition.'" (1) This is only because honor (ʿirḍ) is among the injustices that God will not leave unpunished, even if the one backbitten is a wrongdoer or a sinner, for every believer is sacred to another believer — his blood, his wealth, and his honor. If the speaker is one called to testify, or one whose hand has been extended in the land (i.e., a ruler or judge), they have said: "It is permissible for him to mention of the sinner's honor only that which is needed for the purpose of reforming him, in the presence of one who has the power to reform him." As for taking frivolous pleasure (tafakkuh) in the honor of a believer who has committed an offense, it is not permissible for him, nor is it lawful, as ʿAwf said: "I entered upon Ibn Sīrīn and began to disparage al-Ḥajjāj. Ibn Sīrīn said: 'God is a just Judge. Just as He takes from al-Ḥajjāj, He takes for al-Ḥajjāj. And when you meet God tomorrow, the smallest sin you have committed will be more severe upon you than the greatest sin al-Ḥajjāj committed.'" So taking frivolous pleasure in the honor of a sinner is forbidden by consensus. Already mentioned is the saying of al-Fuḍayl: "What Sufyān takes is less than what he deserves," then he secluded himself with him and admonished him.

From the "Iḥyāʾ": The most vicious kind of backbiting is conveying the intended meaning in the guise of righteous people — for example, one says: "Praise be to God who has not afflicted us with entering upon rulers or degrading ourselves in seeking worldly crumbs," if his intention thereby is to convey (a criticism of) another. And one may precede (the backbiting) with praise of the one he intends to backbite, saying: "How excellent is the state of so-and-so, except that he has been tried with what everyone is tried with." Thus he has combined three abominations: backbiting, hypocrisy (riyāʾ), and self-justification. And of that kind is when one mentions a person's fault, and some of those present do not notice it, so he says: "Glory be to God!" — using the name of God as an instrument to achieve his malice, while he bestows favor upon God by mentioning Him. And of that kind is his saying: "I was grieved by what befell our friend — may God forgive us!" (1) Recorded by al-Ṭabarānī in his Great Compendium, 1/184, no. 482.

### | الصفحة 157

منهج الترقي/ المقام السادس: إن لم يكن في عمل أنضل فلا أقل من أن يكون في عمل ناضل 201
وعليه؛ فهو كاذب في دعواه الغم وفي إظهاره الدعاء له؛ لو كان صادقًا لدعى له
بخلواته وعقب صلاته في دعواء

وانظر قول الفضيل: كل ما يأخذه سفيان أقل مما يستحق ونصحه حين خلا به,
وانظر ما تقدم لنا مما اختلف الشيوخ في استحبابه أو كراهته قط ما يكسون
فعله بمنسزلة النظر لما يحل. وتقدم قول ابن العربي أنه صغيرة مضمحلة في
جنب مشاهدته تفسه وأن لا يعمل بموجبه ومضمحلة بالحستات ولا أيضًا ما ترك
من ذلك بمنزلة الوتسر الذي لا سنة آكد منه ومع ذلك قال ابن العربي: قول
سحتون: من تسرك الوتر أدب» التقف هذا من أسد بن الفرات» وهي لعمر الله ملح
غير فوات؛ فإن ظهر المؤمن حمى لا يستباح إلا إذا عصى.

وقال ابن العربي: الكلام في المحرمات باب عظيم؛ ليس ما حرمته السنة كما
حرمه القرآث: ولهذا قال ابن الفاسم: من جمع بين المرأة وعمتها عالما بالنهي درئ
عنه الحدا لآن تحريمه بالسنة؛ بخلاف من جمع بين المرأة وأختهاء فإنه يحدا لأن
تحريمه بالفرآن. وفي الصحيح: قال رسول اله :"ككل ذي ناب من السباع
حرلم”

قال لبن العربي: كذا ثبت لفظ حرام في الموطأ والبخاري ومسلم؛ ويتأول لفظة.
حرام؛ أي: ممنوع؛ إذ ليس ما حرمته السنة كما حرمه القرآن ومن "المدارك” قال
مالك: لم يكن أمر الناس ولا من مضى من سلفنا الذين نقتتدي بهم ومعول الإسلام
عليهم أن يقولوا: هذا حلال: وهذا حرام؛ ولكن يقول: أنا أكره كذاء وآرى كذ
وان حلا وسو ذا لوا على ل أن سمت قو اسح طقل

َكانه لك يتن زَدْف مَجَمَلكم نه راودا آله أت لك لزعلا

# PageV1P158

### | الصفحة 158

2___منهج الترفي/ المقام السادس: إن لم يكن في عمل أفضل فلا أفل من أن يكون في عمل فاضل

أحدها: أن يعلم أن الذي بذله من الحرام أو من الحلال فهذا لا إشكال فيه.

الثانية: أن يعلم أن الذي بذله من جنس ما يكتسبه من المحرم؛ فهذا مكروه
أخذهء والورع عنه متأكد.

الثالة: أن يكون ما يبذله ليس من جنس ما يكتسبه بالسبب المحرم؛ فهذا لا
بأس بالإقدام عليه؛ فإن شك هل اشترى ذلك بالمال الحرام أو لا؟ فالورع في هذا
اخفيف ولايقضي بتحريمه؛ لأن الأسباب المحللة إذا غلبت حل لك الإقدام وإن
غلبت ندرتها حرم الإقدامء وهذا المال دائر يين أن يكون اشتراه بعين المحرم وذلك
انادرء وبين أن يكون قد اشتراه في الذمة ثم نقد الثمن الحرام فيه وهذا أغلب
المعاملتين. وهذا جار في أموال الملوك والظلمة والولاة الغشمة وقطاع الطريق
والمغنيات والزواني وجميع من يغلب عليه الكسب الحرام. والعجب ممن يحرم
هذا ومع كونه كاذبًا على الله في تحريمه؛ ولا ينظر إلى أن الامتناع من الكذب
على الله في التحريم والتحليل واجب؛ فإنه لا فرق بين محلل الحرام ومحرم
الحلال» والفلاح كله منوط بالوقوف على حدود الله لوَمنيَنيسللوَسُوكُقَدْصَلٌ
كما )4 [الأحزاب: 36]. اه بنصه.

وانظر قوله: وهذا المال دائر بين أن يكون اشتراه بعين المحرم؛ ومذهينا نحن
أنه إذا اشترى شقص شريكك بعين المحرم لك أخذه بالشفعة إن كان عين المحرم
دنائير ودراهم؛ بخلاف غيرهما. وقد بسطت مفتضى مذهينا في كتاب "التاج"
ونقلت هذه المسألة هنا لحسنهاء ومقصودي نص هذا الإمام؛ فمن يجترئ على الله
ويقول: حلال وحرام.

وقال ابن رشد في "جامع العتيية”: إذا أدى اجتهاد المجتهد إلى أن الشيء
حرام؛ فلا يجوز أن يقول: هو حرام على الإطلاق» لا على القول بنصويب
المجتهدين ولا على قول غيرهم؛ وهل يجوز أن يقول: هو حرام في رأني؟ أما على
أن الح واحد فلا يجوز ذلك؛ وأما على أن كل مجتهد مصيب؛ فجائز أن يقولة
هو حرام في رأني.

وانظر أيضًا النهي عن الشيء على الجملة إذا ورد مطلقًا في القرآن والسنة.
قال ابن العربي: هو نهي أدب وإرشادء إلا أن تدل قرينة على أنه مصلحة في البدن

# PageV1P159
anchors:
- Root: ن-ض-ل (naḍala)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Superiority in merit; precedence in excellence.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theologically, afḍal denotes that which draws one nearer to Allah in rank, as opposed to fāḍil (meritorious but lesser).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in comparative degrees; metaphorically used for spiritual stations (maqāmāt).
- Root: غ-م-م (ghamma)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Concealment, grief, or distress that veils clarity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, inner sorrow or pretense thereof; sincerity (ṣidq) is its opposite.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical oppression; metaphorical for spiritual hypocrisy in supplication.
- Root: و-ر-ع (waraʿa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Restraint, abstention; piety that withholds from doubtful matters.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Scrupulous avoidance of the ambiguous (shubhāt) to safeguard the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical withdrawal; metaphorical for moral caution in transactions.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-sharṭ) — The protasis (in lam yakun) and apodosis (fa-lā aqalla) establish a graded obligation, where the second clause is a concession to the first, requiring the listener to infer the minimal duty.
translation:
I say: The sixth station of the path of ascent — if one cannot engage in a deed that is superior (afḍal), then let him not fall short of engaging in a deed that is meritorious (fāḍil). Upon this basis, he who claims grief (ghamm) for the state of the Muslims while displaying supplication for them is a liar in his claim; for were he truthful, he would have supplicated for them in his private moments and after his prayers, in his secret invocations.

Consider the saying of al-Fuḍayl: "Everything that Sufyān takes is less than what he deserves," and his sincere counsel when he was alone with him. And consider what we have previously mentioned concerning the disagreement of the elders (shuyūkh) over whether it is recommended (mustaḥabb) or disliked (makrūh) to cut off that which they clothe — for its doing is in the station of considering what is lawful. And there preceded the saying of Ibn al-ʿArabī that it is a minor sin (ṣaghīrah) that dissolves (muḍmaḥillah) in the face of his witnessing his own self, and that one should not act upon its implication; and it dissolves by the good deeds (ḥasanāt). Nor also is that which one abandons of it in the station of the Witr prayer, for which there is no more emphatic Sunnah; yet despite that, Ibn al-ʿArabī said: "The saying of Saḥnūn — 'Whoever is grieved by the Witr is disciplined' — this is taken from Asad ibn al-Furāt." And by the life of Allah, it is a salt that does not spoil. For the believer's blood is sacred (ḥimā) and is not rendered permissible except when he disobeys.

And Ibn al-ʿArabī said: "Speech concerning the prohibited things (muḥarramāt) is a mighty chapter; for that which the Sunnah has prohibited is not like that which the Qurʾān has prohibited." For this reason, Ibn al-Qāsim said: "Whoever combines a woman with her paternal aunt, knowing of the prohibition, the prescribed punishment (ḥadd) is warded off from him, because its prohibition is by the Sunnah; unlike the one who combines a woman with her sister, for he is punished, because its prohibition is by the Qurʾān." And in the Ṣaḥīḥ, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: {«كُلُّ ذِي نَابٍ مِنَ السِّبَاعِ حَرَامٌ»} ("Every beast of prey with fangs is forbidden").

Ibn al-ʿArabī said: "Thus the word 'ḥarām' is established in the Muwaṭṭaʾ, al-Bukhārī, and Muslim; and the word 'ḥarām' is interpreted (mutāʾawwal) — meaning 'prohibited' (mamnūʿ) — for that which the Sunnah prohibits is not like that which the Qurʾān prohibits." And from "al-Mudārik" (al-Mudārikah): Mālik said: "It was not the practice of the people, nor of those of our predecessors (salaf) whom we follow and upon whom the foundation of Islam rests, to say: 'This is lawful (ḥalāl), and this is unlawful (ḥarām)'; rather, they would say: 'I dislike such-and-such, and I see such-and-such,' — and if it were lawful, they would deem it so, and if unlawful, they would deem it so." For the lawful is what Allah and His Messenger have made lawful, and the unlawful is what they have made unlawful — this is by his very text. And ʿIzz al-Dīn spoke concerning the wealth of those whose wealth is predominantly acquired by unlawful means, saying: "They have three states:

The first: That he knows that what he has given is from the unlawful or from the lawful — this is without any ambiguity.

The second: That he knows that what he has given is of the same kind as what he earns from the prohibited — this is disliked (makrūh) to take, and scrupulous avoidance (waraʿ) of it is emphatically recommended.

The third: That what he gives is not of the same kind as what he earns by the prohibited cause — then there is no harm in proceeding with it. But if he doubts whether he purchased it with unlawful wealth or not, then scrupulous avoidance in this is light, and one does not judge it as prohibited; for when the lawful causes predominate, it is permissible for you to proceed, and when their rarity predominates, proceeding is prohibited. And this wealth oscillates between being purchased with the very unlawful thing — which is rare — and between being purchased as a debt upon the person (fī al-dhimmah), then the unlawful price is paid for it — and this is the more prevalent of the two transactions. And this applies to the wealth of kings, tyrants, oppressive governors, highway robbers, singing girls, fornicatresses, and all those whose earning is predominantly unlawful. And astonishing is the one who declares this unlawful, while being a liar against Allah in his prohibition; and he does not consider that refraining from lying against Allah in prohibition and permission is obligatory — for there is no difference between the one who makes lawful what is unlawful and the one who makes unlawful what is lawful. And all success is tied to standing at the boundaries of Allah: {«وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤْمِنٍ وَلَا مُؤْمِنَةٍ إِذَا قَضَى اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَمْرًا أَن يَكُونَ لَهُمُ الْخِيَرَةُ مِنْ أَمْرِهِمْ»} (And it is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any choice in their matter) [al-Aḥzāb: 36]." — This is by his very text.

And consider his saying: "And this wealth oscillates between being purchased with the very unlawful thing" — and our school (madhhab) is that if he purchases the share of your partner with the very unlawful thing, you may take it by preemption (shufʿah) if the unlawful thing is gold dinars and silver dirhams; unlike other than them. And I have elaborated the implications of our school in the book "al-Tāj," and I have transmitted this issue here for its excellence; and my purpose is the text of this Imām — so who dares against Allah and says: "Lawful and unlawful"?

And Ibn Rushd said in "Jāmiʿ al-Utbiyyah": "If the ijtihād of a mujtahid leads to the conclusion that a thing is unlawful, it is not permissible for him to say: 'It is unlawful absolutely' — neither upon the view of the infallibility of all mujtahids (taṣwīb) nor upon the view of others. And is it permissible for him to say: 'It is unlawful in my opinion'? As for the view that only one is correct, then that is not permissible; and as for the view that every mujtahid is correct, then it is permissible for him to say: 'It is unlawful in my opinion.'"

And consider also the prohibition of a thing in general when it is mentioned absolutely in the Qurʾān and the Sunnah. Ibn al-ʿArabī said: "It is a prohibition of discipline and guidance (adab wa-irshād), unless an indication (qarīnah) shows that it concerns a benefit for the body."

title_en: Section 121 — The Sixth Station: If an Act Cannot Be Virtuous, Let It at Least Be Excellent; and the Ruling on Disputed Matters

### | الصفحة 159

منهج الترفي/ المقام السادس: إن لم يكن في عمل أنضل فلا أقل من أن يكون في عمل فاضل 203
أو في المال على الاختصاص بالمرء؛ فإنه يكون مكروهًا ولا يرتقي إلى التحريم.
ونحوه لأبي عمر في “تمهيا كاره' في غير موضع: أن النهي إذا كان واردًا
على ما في ملكك فهو نهي أدب وإرشاد: لأنه ملكك تتصرف فيه كيف شتت ما لم
يكن ملكك حيوانًا؛ قال: وعلى هذا ورد نهي القرآن والسنة؛ كالتهي عن اختناث
الأسقية والاستنجاء باليمين والأكل بالشمال. ابن العربي: واشتمال الصماء؛ كل هذا
مكروه ول يترقى إلى التحريم. ونحو هذا لابن رشد في المشي بنعل واحدة: قال
ما نصه: التهي عن المشي بنعل واحد نهي إرشاد وليس فعل ذلك بحرام. وقال
ابن العربي: النهي عن المشي في نعل واحد صحيح؛ وإن مشى في نعل واحد فلا
يكون عاصيا عند الجمهورء وإن كان بالنهي عالما. اه نصه.

وقال عياض في أول "الإكمال”: لا ينبغي للآمر بالمعروف والناهي عبن المنكر
أن يحمل الناس على اجتهاده ومذهيه؛ وإنما يغير منه ما اجتمع على إحدائه
وإنكاره. ورشح هذا محيي الدين النووي قائلا: أما المختلف فيه فلا إنكار فيه
وليس للمفتي ولا للقاضي أن يعترض على من خالفه؛ إذا لم يخالف نص القرآن
والسنة والإجماع. ونقلت من خط صاحبنا ابن طركاط رحمه الله فتيا للشاطبي؛ قال:
الأولى عندي في كل نازلة يكون لعلماء المذهب فيها قولان: فيعمل الناس فيها
على موافقة أحدهماء وإن كان مرجوحًا في النظر أن لا يعرض لهم؛ وأن يجروا
على أنهم قلدوه في الزمن الأول وجرى به العمل: فإنهم إن حملوا على غير ذلك
كان في ذلك تشويش للعامة وفتح لأبواب الخصام. وربما يخالقني في ذلك غيري»
لكن ذلك لا يصدني عن القول به ولي فيه أسوة. اه

انظر هذا الكلام من قوله في “موافقاته”: ترك الاعتراض على الكبراء محمود.
.وقوله: إن الصوفية صفوة الله ألزموا أتفسهم من التعبد ما لا يلزمهم. وأن السلف
سرمدوا اللصلاة والنصوم؛ وسووا ببين الواجب والمندوب في طلب الفعملء
واستحسن التزام الذكر الذي رآه الكتاني في النوم؛ واستحسن التزام:

لاكنت ولاكان الهوى..

دبر كل صلاة. وقال في إنشاداته وإفاداته: إنه أوصى في النوم أن لا يعترض
على أحد. كان لسيدي ابن سراج رحمه الله هنا كلام كان رحمه الله يقول: فأين هذا

# PageV1P160

### | الصفحة 160

4__منهج الترفي/ المقام السادس: إن لم يكن في عمل أفضل فلا أفل من أن يكون في عمل فاضل
من هذا كله؟ بعبارة أغلظ من هذا. وقال تفي الدين ابن الصلاح: إذا كان للمفتي
مختار يأخذ به في خاصته بينه ‎١‏ يقول: مذهبك كذا وأنا بظهر لي كذا.

.وقال الإمام الماوردي: إن المفتي إذا نابذ في فنياه شخصًا معيئاء صار خصمًا
معانثا ترد فنياه كما ترد شهادته؛ وليكتب فنيا نفسه من غير أن يعترض لفتيا غ.
بشخطئة واعتراض. اه

.وقد تبين مما قررته في هذا المقام أن ما اختلف في مشروعيته خير من

المباح» ولا شك أن ما اتفق على مشروعيته فهو أولى ودعه ليس بأهم؛ وهذا هو

المقام السابع.

# PageV1P161
anchors:
- Root: ن-ه-ي (n-h-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Prohibition, interdiction, forbidding with authority
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine and prophetic prohibitions as guidance (irshād) versus legal obligation (taḥrīm)
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Distinguishes prohibitory command (nahy) that is advisory (adab) from that which is legally binding (taḥrīm)
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional clause with "in lam" (if not) — expressing gradation of merit, with apodosis introduced by "fa-lā aqalla"
translation:
I say — may Allah guide us and you:

The Sixth Station: If an act cannot be virtuous (fāḍil), let it at least be excellent (afḍal). Or concerning wealth, when it pertains specifically to a person — for such prohibition is disliked (makrūh) and does not rise to the level of unlawfulness (taḥrīm).

Similar to this is what Abū ʿUmar stated in his "Tamhīd" in more than one place: that when a prohibition concerns what is within your own possession, it is a prohibition of discipline and guidance (adab wa-irshād) — because it is your property, and you may dispose of it as you wish, unless what you possess is a living creature. He said: Upon this basis the prohibitions of the Qur'an and Sunnah were revealed — such as the prohibition of turning water-skins upside down (ikhtināth al-asqiyah), cleansing with the right hand (al-istinjā' bi-al-yamīn), and eating with the left hand. Ibn al-ʿArabī added: and the wrapping of the body entirely in a garment (ishtimāl al-ṣammā') — all of this is disliked (makrūh) and does not rise to unlawfulness.

Similar to this is what Ibn Rushd said concerning walking in a single sandal. He stated verbatim: "The prohibition against walking in one sandal is a prohibition of guidance, and doing so is not unlawful (ḥarām)." Ibn al-ʿArabī said: The prohibition against walking in a single sandal is authentic; yet if one walks in a single sandal, he is not a sinner according to the majority (jumhūr), even if he knows of the prohibition. This ends his verbatim text.

And ʿIyāḍ said at the beginning of his "Ikmāl": It is not fitting for the one who commands good and forbids evil to impose upon people his own juristic reasoning (ijtihād) or his school (madhhab). Rather, he should only change that upon which there is consensus regarding its obligatoriness or its reprehensibility. Muḥyī al-Dīn al-Nawawī reinforced this, saying: As for that which is disputed, there is no condemnation in it. Neither the muftī nor the judge may object to one who opposes him — so long as he has not contravened an explicit text of the Qur'an, the Sunnah, or consensus (ijmā').

And I have transmitted from the handwriting of our companion Ibn Ṭarkāṭ — may Allah have mercy on him — a legal opinion (fatwā) of al-Shāṭibī, who said: The most appropriate course in my view regarding every novel case (nāzilah) in which the scholars of the school hold two opinions is that people should act in accordance with one of them — even if it be the weaker (marjūḥ) in theoretical consideration — and that they should not be opposed; rather, they should be left to continue as they have followed him in former times, and practice has proceeded accordingly. For if they were burdened with anything other than that, it would cause confusion among the common folk and open the doors of contention. Perhaps another may disagree with me in this, but that will not deter me from stating it, and I have in this a model to follow. This ends his text.

Consider this statement of his in his "Muwāfaqāt": Refraining from objecting to the eminent (akābir) is praiseworthy. And his statement: The Sufis are the elite of Allah (ṣafwat Allāh); they have obligated themselves to acts of worship that are not obligatory upon them. And that the Salaf persisted continuously in prayer and fasting, and made no distinction between the obligatory (wājib) and the recommended (mandūb) in seeking to perform acts. And he deemed excellent the adherence to the dhikr that al-Kattānī saw in sleep; and he deemed excellent the adherence to the saying:

"Would that I were not, and would that desire were not..."

after every prayer. And he said in his "Inshādāt" and "Ifādāt": He advised in sleep that one should not object to anyone.

Our master Ibn Sirāj — may Allah have mercy on him — had words here, and he used to say: Where is this in relation to all of that? — with a harsher expression than this.

And Taqī al-Dīn Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ said: When a muftī has a preferred opinion (mukhtār) which he adopts for his own private affairs, he should clarify it, saying: "Your school (madhhab) is such-and-such, but what appears to me is such-and-such."

And Imām al-Māwardī said: When a muftī, in his legal opinion, opposes a specific person, he becomes a contentious adversary, and his legal opinion is rejected just as his testimony would be rejected. He should write his own legal opinion without objecting to the legal opinion of another by way of error or criticism. This ends his text.

It has thus become clear from what I have established in this station that what is disputed concerning its legitimacy (mashrūʿiyyah) is better than the merely permissible (mubāḥ). And there is no doubt that what is agreed upon concerning its legitimacy is more worthy — and leave that which is not important. And this is the Seventh Station.

title_en: The Seventh Station — That One Remain in What Is Important If Not Upon What Is More Important
arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 161

المقام السايع
أن يكون في مهم إن لم يكن على أهم

إن لم يكن على أهم علم وعمل فلا يحتفر أن يكون على عمل مهم
فالمتجردون المراقبون وإن كانوا صفوة الخلق قائمين برض العين؛ فكذلك
المتسيون أيضًا قالمون بفرض الكفاية.

وقد تقدم قول ابن العربي: لا يتفق أن يكون الخلق كلهم على المنزلة العليا'
الأن في ذلك فساد الدنيا؛ فانشغال الإنسان مع الخلق بتجارة أو صناعة أو عللم؛

اشتغال بفرض من فروض الكفاية.

ومن كتاب "آداب الدين" للماوردي: المكاسب أربعة: زراعة نناج حيوانه
تجارة؛ صناعة. قال المأمون: من خرج من هذه الأربعة فهو كل علينا. قال في
"الإحياء': لو تركت الصناعات والتجارات هلك الخلق. قال: واننظام أمر الدين إنما
هو بالتعاون وتكفل كل فريق بعمل؛ ولكين قال عز الدين: القائم بفرض الكفاية لا
يؤجر على ذلك إذا قصد إليه؛ إلا أن ينوي به القربة؛ قال: كما لا يشاب على ترك
العصيان إلا إذا قصد بذلك طاعة الملك الديان.

ومما ينبغي أن أنقل هنا قول تاج الدين في حكمه: طلبك التجريد مع إقامة لله
إباك في الأسباب من الشهوة الخفية؛ وطلبك الأسباب مع إقامة اله إياك في التجريد
انحطاط عن الهمة العلية. وافهم رحمك الله من شأن هذا العدو اللعين أن يأتيك
فيما أنت فيه مما أقامك الله فيه؛ فيحفره عندك؛ لتطلب غير ما أقامك الله فيه
فيتشوش قلبك؛ ويتكدر وقنك؛ وذلك لأنه يأتي المتسببين فيقول لهم: لو تركتم
الأسباب وتجردتم لأشرقت لكم الأنوار. ولصفت منكم القلوب والأسرارء وكذلك
قعل قلان وفلات» ويكون هذا العبد ليس مقصوةًا بالتجريد؛ ولا طاقة له به إنما
صلاحه في الأسباب» فيتركهاء فيتزلزل إيمانه. ويذهب إيقانه: ويتوجه إلى الطلب.
من الخلق والاهتمام بالرزق» فيرمى في بحر القطيعة؛ وذلك قصد العدو منه؛ لأنه

# PageV1P162

### | الصفحة 162

ميج لوقي المقا السيع؛ أن يكون في مهم إن الم يكن على ألم

يأنيك في صورة ناصح إذ لو أناك في غيرها لم تقبل منه كما أنى آدم وحواء
عليهما السلام في صورة ناصح. وكذلك يأني المتجردين يقول لههم: إلى منى
تتركون الأسباب؟ ألم تعلموا أن ترك الأسباب تتطلع منه القلوب إلى ما في أيدي
الناس؟ ويكون هذا العبد تند طاب وقته وانبسط نوره؛ قلا يزال به حتى يعنود إلى
الأسباب» قتصيبه كدرتهاء وتغشاه ظلمتهاء ويعود الدائم في سبيه أحسن حالًا منهة
لأن ذلك ما سلك طريقًا ثم رجع عنها ولا قصد مقصنًا ثم انعطف عنه؛ قافهم
واعتصم بلله: وم نينم بطه معد درمتم 450 [آل عمران: 101].

وإنما يقصد الشيطان بذلك أن يمنع العباد الرضا عن الله فيما فيه؛ ويخرجهم
عن مختار اله لهم إلى ممختارهم لأنفسهم؛ وما أدخخلك فيه تولى إعاتتك عليه: وما
دخلت فيه بنفسك وكلك إلبه. ف يتأن مّدق [الإسراء: 80] الآيقه
فالمدخل الصدق: أن تدخل فيه لا بنفسك؛ والمخرج الصدق أيضًا كذلك.

والذي يقتضيه الح منك أن تمكث حيث أقامك حتى يكون الحق سبحانه
اهو الذي يتولى إخراجك كما تولى إدخالك؛ وليس الشأن أن تترك السبب: إنما
الشأن أن يتركك السبب.

ودخلت على الشيخ أبي العباس وفي نفسي العزم على التجريد قائل:
الوصول إلى الله مع الاشتغال بالعلم الظاهر ومخالطة الناس بعيد؛ فقال لي من غير
أن أسأله: صحيني إنسان مشتغل بالعلوم الظاهرة ومتصدر اق
الطريقة شيئًا فجاء إل وقال: يا سيدي؛ نخرج عما أنا فيه. وأتفرغ لصحبتك؛ فقلت
اله: ليس الشأن ذلك؛ ولكن امكث فيما أنت فيه وما قسم إليك على أيدينا فهو إليك
واصل. ثم نظر إلي الشيخ وقال: وهكذا شأن الصديقين لا يخرجون عن شيء
احتى يكون الحق سبحانه هو الذي يتولى إخخراجهم. فخرجت من عنده وقد
غسل الله تلك الخواطر من قلبي؛ ووجدت الراحة بالتسليم إلى الله ولكنهم كما قال
رسول الله :"هم القوم لا يشقى بهم جليسهم”7. اه من “التنوير”.

# PageV1P163
anchors:
- Root: م-ك-ث (m-k-th)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To remain, abide, stay fixed in a place or state without movement.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Perseverance in the divinely appointed station (maqām) as an act of servitude (ʿubūdiyyah), not self-directed motion.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Ḥaqīqah — physical abiding; Majāz — spiritual constancy in the station Allah has chosen for the servant.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-sharṭ) — "In lam yakun ʿalā aham" (if not upon what is more important) establishes a graded hierarchy of obligations, where the conditional restricts the scope of the preceding command.
translation:
I say — may Allah grant us and you success:

The Seventh Station: That one remain in what is important, if not upon what is more important.

If one is not upon what is more important in knowledge and action, then it is not fitting that he neglect what is important in action. For the detached ones (al-mutajarridūn) who are watchful (al-murāqibūn), even though they are the elite of creation, standing by the very eye of certainty (ʿayn al-yaqīn) — likewise, the engaged ones (al-mutasabbibūn) are also standing by the communal obligation (farḍ al-kifāyah).

Already mentioned is the saying of Ibn al-ʿArabī: It does not happen that all of creation be upon the highest station, for in that is the corruption of the world. So a man's occupation with creation — through trade, craft, or knowledge — is an occupation with a communal obligation.

From the book "Ādāb al-Dīn" of al-Māwardī: The means of acquisition are four: agriculture, animal husbandry, trade, and craft. Al-Maʾmūn said: Whoever departs from these four is a burden upon us. He said in "al-Iḥyāʾ": Were the crafts and trades abandoned, creation would perish. He said: The ordering of the religious affair is only through mutual cooperation, with each group undertaking a work. But ʿIzz al-Dīn said: The one who fulfills a communal obligation is not rewarded for it when he intends it — unless he intends by it nearness (to Allah). He said: Just as one is not rewarded for abandoning disobedience unless he intends by that obedience to the Sovereign, the Judge (al-Malik al-Dayyān).

And among what I ought to transmit here is the saying of Tāj al-Dīn in his rulings: Your seeking detachment (tajrīd) while Allah has established you in the means (asbāb) is from hidden desire (al-shahwah al-khafiyyah); and your seeking the means while Allah has established you in detachment is a descent from the lofty aspiration (al-himmah al-ʿaliyyah). Understand — may Allah have mercy on you — the matter of this accursed enemy: that he comes to you in that which you are upon, that which Allah has established you in, and makes it seem insignificant to you, so that you seek other than what Allah has established you in. Then your heart becomes disturbed, and your certainty becomes turbid. That is because he comes to the engaged ones (al-mutasabbibīn) and says to them: "If you abandoned the means and detached yourselves, the lights would shine upon you, and the hearts and secrets would become pure from you — and so-and-so and so-and-so did thus." And this servant is not intended for detachment, nor has he capacity for it — rather, his well-being is in the means. So he abandons them, and his faith trembles, and his certainty departs. He turns to seeking from creation and concerning himself with provision, and is cast into the sea of severance (qaṭīʿah). And that is the enemy's intent from him — because he comes to him in the guise of a sincere advisor; for were he to come in any other guise, he would not accept from him — just as he came to Ādam and Ḥawwāʾ (peace be upon them) in the guise of a sincere advisor.

Likewise, he comes to the detached ones (al-mutajarridīn) and says to them: "Until when will you abandon the means? Do you not know that abandoning the means causes the hearts to look toward what is in people's hands?" And this servant — when his time has become pleasant and his light has spread — he (the enemy) does not cease with him until he returns to the means. Then its turbidity afflicts him, and its darkness envelops him, and he returns worse in state than he was — because that one had traversed a path and then turned back from it, and had intended a destination and then veered away from it. So understand, and hold fast to Allah: {«And whoever holds fast to Allah has been guided to a straight path»} [Āl ʿImrān: 101].

And by that, Satan only intends to prevent the servants from being pleased with Allah regarding what they are in, and to remove them from Allah's choice for them to their own choice for themselves. For what He has caused you to enter, He undertakes to bring you out of; and what you enter by yourself, He leaves you to it. So He said: {«And say: My Lord, cause me to enter a true entrance and bring me out a true exit»} [al-Isrāʾ: 80] — the verse. So the true entrance (al-madkhal al-ṣidq) is that you enter it not by yourself; and the true exit (al-makhraj al-ṣidq) is likewise.

And what the truth requires of you is that you remain where He has established you, until the Truth — exalted be He — is the One who undertakes your exit, just as He undertook your entrance. And the matter is not that you leave the means; the matter is that the means leaves you.

And I entered upon the Shaykh Abū al-ʿAbbās — and in my soul was the resolve for detachment — saying: "Attainment of Allah with occupation in outward knowledge and mixing with people is far." So he said to me, without my asking him: "A man accompanied me, occupied with the outward sciences and seated as a teacher of the path — nothing (of detachment) — and he came to me and said: 'O my master, I will exit from what I am in, and devote myself to your companionship.' So I said to him: 'The matter is not that. Rather, remain in what you are in, and what is apportioned to you through our hands reaches you.'" Then the Shaykh looked at me and said: "And such is the affair of the ṣiddīqīn (the utterly truthful) — they do not exit from anything until the Truth, exalted be He, is the One who undertakes their exit." So I left from his presence, and Allah had washed those thoughts from my heart, and I found rest in submission (taslīm) to Allah. But they — as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "They are a people whose companion is not wretched" — end of quote from "al-Tanwīr."

[Footnote: Recorded by al-Bukhārī (5/2353, no. 6805), Muslim (4/2069, no. 2089), Aḥmad (3/3820, no. 8960), Ibn Ḥibbān (3/137, no. 856), Abū Nuʿaym (8/117), al-Ṭayālisī (p. 319, no. 2434), and al-Bayhaqī in Shuʿab al-Īmān (1/399, no. 4531).]

title_en: The Seventh Station: On the Conduct of Those Occupied with Worldly Means and the Priority of Religious Obligations

منهج الترفي/ المقام السايع: أن يكون في مهم إن لم يكن على امم فادت

قال في "الإحياء": يجب أن يهتم بالأهم؛ ويقدم حاجة الوالدة على حاجة.
الوالد. وثفقة أبويه على الحج؛ والإثيان إلى الجمعة على الوفاء بالمبعاد, وكذلك

النجاسة؛ والذي يتبين من الفقه أن الصناعات والتجارات والاشتغال بالعلم الزائد
على فرض العين؛ بل وعلم الطب كل ذلك أسباب شرعية.

قال في "الإحياء': فعلى هذا من اشتغل بشيء من هذا سيا بلا نية فهو ظالم
لنفسه. وإن كان لا درك عليه؛ ولكن فاته الأجرء وإن قصد بذلك فرض الكفاية فهو
سابق بالخيرات؛ وإن قصد بذلك الاستعفاف عن المسألة كان مقتصدًا. قال الإمام

صنعة: اترك

ابن عرفة: من عجز عن قوته وقوت عياله إلا برزق القضاءء فإنه يستحب له أن
