# PageV1P164
anchors:
- Root: ق-و-م (q-w-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "To stand upright, to establish, to maintain; the essence of one's state or condition (ḥāl)."
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): "Divine establishment (iqāmah) of a servant in a specific worldly or religious station; implies divine decree and purpose."
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): "Literal: physical standing; metaphorical: the fixed state or livelihood in which God places a person, as in 'aqāma-hu Allāh' (God established him)."
- Sībawayh Rule: "Conditional Clause with 'in' (الشّرط بـ 'إن')" (The protasis 'in lam yakun' introduces a hypothetical condition governing the apodosis, requiring careful modal sequencing.)
translation:
I say: The seventh station of elevation is that one remain in his occupation—provided it is not upon a forbidden matter.

And it was added in "Laṭāʾif al-Minan": That the aforementioned Shaykh Abū al-ʿAbbās said to him: "We, when we accompany a merchant, do not say to him: 'Leave your trade and come [with us].' Nor [do we say] to one of a craft: 'Leave your craft and come.' Nor to a student of knowledge: 'Leave your seeking and come.' Rather, we establish every person in that which God has established him, and that which has been apportioned to him—through our hands—he shall attain it."

Indeed, the Companions accompanied the Messenger of God ﷺ, yet he did not say to a merchant: "Leave your trade," nor to a possessor of a craft: "Leave your craft." Rather, he confirmed them upon their means of livelihood and commanded them to fear God within them. And he ﷺ said to the one who asked him for counsel: "Fear God wherever you are, and follow a misdeed with a good deed that erases it, and treat people with excellent character." {«اتق الله حيث كنت وأتبع السيئة الحسنة تمحها وخالق الناس بخلق حسن»}

It was said to Bishr al-Ḥāfī: "So-and-so the wealthy man is abundant in fasting and prayer." He replied: "The poor wretch—he abandoned his own state and entered into the state of another! His true state is feeding food [to others]; that is more excellent for him than starving himself, and more excellent than his prayers for himself while he amasses worldly wealth."

He said in "al-Iḥyāʾ": One must give precedence to the most important [obligation]. The need of the mother takes precedence over the need of the father. The expenditure upon one's parents takes precedence over the pilgrimage (ḥajj). And attending the Friday prayer takes precedence over fulfilling a promise. Likewise, if impurity (najāsah) touches one's garment, one should not speak harshly to his family because of it—for causing harm [to them] is more grave than the impurity itself.

What becomes evident from jurisprudence (fiqh) is that crafts, trades, and engagement in knowledge beyond the individual obligation (farḍ al-ʿayn)—indeed even the science of medicine—all of these are lawful means (asbāb sharʿiyyah).

He said in "al-Iḥyāʾ": On this basis, whoever occupies himself with any of these without [proper] intention is unjust to himself. Though there is no sin upon him, he has missed the reward. If he intends thereby the communal obligation (farḍ al-kifāyah), he is foremost in good deeds. If he intends thereby to refrain from begging, he is moderate. 

Imam Ibn ʿArafah said: Whoever is unable to secure his own sustenance and that of his dependents except through the livelihood of [judicial] decree (rizq al-qaḍāʾ), it is recommended (mustaḥabb) for him to strive in seeking it.

And from Ibn Yūnus: It is not proper for anyone to perform the pilgrimage on behalf of another; but if such occurs, the contract (ijārah) is executed [and valid].

ʿAbd al-Wahhāb said: There is no objection to taking payment for judicial rulings (qaḍāʾ) and for the construction of bridges and mosques.

From Abū ʿUmar there appears an inclination that the most worthy thing for which a man should hire himself out is acts of righteousness (aʿmāl al-birr)—when he is not obligated to perform them himself—such as supervising the witnesses of the congregation and teaching the Qurʾān. He attributed this to the companions of al-Shāfiʿī. He said: And the Kūfans said: There is no harm for one who senses in himself an aptitude (jinnah) [for such work]...

arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 164

ل منهج الترقي/ المقام سابع أن يكون في مهم إن لم يكن على أمم
يجهز غازيًا ويجعل له جعلاء قال: وقد قال رسول الله يل لعمرو بن العاص: "هل
الك في أن أبعنك في جيش فيسلمك الله ويغدمك؛ وأرغب لك في المال رغبة
صالحة”31.

ومن ابن بطال: وقد أخذ عطية فرسًا على نصف ما يغنم؛ وأجاز هذا الأوزاعي
وأحمد بن حنبل. وقال اللخمي: إذا قال الإمام: من قتل فلانًا فله سلبه أو له دنائير
أو كسوة؛ أو من صعد موضع كذا أو بلغه أو وقف فيه فله كذاء فهو ممنوع ابتدازه؟
الأنه قتال للدنياء فإن فات القتال على ذلك كان له شرطه؛ لأنه عمل على حظه من
الدنياء فهو كالمبايعة. والذي في "الإحياء': من الصناعات ما هي مهمة؛ يعني:
فيحمد من يشتغل بهاء ومنها ما يستغنى عنها لرجوعها لطلب التنعم والتزين كالنقش
والصباغة, قال: فيكره ذلك أهل الدين: فأما الملاهي والآلات التي يحرم استعمالها
فاجتناب ذلك من قبيل ترك الظلم؛ قال: وكان عمل الأخيار عشر صنائع؛ منها
الخرز والتجارة والخياطة وعمل الحديد والحياكة: قال: وكره السلف أخذ الأجرة.
على كل ما هو من قبيل العبادات؛ كغسل الموتى ودفنهم؛ وكذلك الأذان وصلوات
التراويح وتعليم القرآن وتعليم الفقه. قال: وإن حكمنا بصحة الاستيجار على ذلكه
الكن حت هذه الأعمال أن يتجر بها للآخرة وأخذ شيء عليها استبدال بالدنيا عن
الآخرة. اه وهذا مواقق لتقرير اللخمي؛ مخالف لما حكاء أبو عمر عن أصحاب
الشافعي. وقال مالك: يؤاجر نفسه في سوق الإبل أحب إلي من أن يعمل عملا لله
سبحانه بالإجارة. وقال سحنون: لآن أطلب الدنيا بالدف والمزمار أحب إل من أن
أطلبها بالدين: الى

ومضمن هذا كله أن الإجارة على أعمال البر من جملة الإجارات الجائزة: هل
هي خير من الإجارة على غير ذلك أو العكس؟ قولان. ثمرة هذا عندي أن من
حاجيات أهل القرى إمام وفران؛ فعلى مذهب مالك إجارة الفران أحل من مرتب
الإمام؛ وعلى ما تقرر من أن التسبب بخدمة المسجد خير من التسيب بخدمة الفرن
.تكون جراية الإمام أحل؛ فإذا كان للورع أن يؤم باطلا؛ فإن أم بمرتب فيراعى مقصد
المحبس والجماعة.

(1) أخرجه الحاكم في مستدركه (257/2: حديث 2926

# PageV1P165
anchors:
- Root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To make, appoint, or stipulate a reward (juʿl) for a specific task; a contractual incentive.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological terms, a conditional recompense (juʿālah) tied to a risky or uncertain outcome, permissible as an exception to general contract rules.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — a fixed wage; metaphorical (majāz) — the spiritual recompense sought from God alone, contrasting worldly hire.
- Root: أ-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Reward, wage, or compensation for labor; also divine recompense (ajr) in the afterlife.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Distinguishes worldly wages (ujrah) from eschatological reward (thawāb); the former is transactional, the latter is grace.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — monetary hire; metaphorical — the soul's exchange of temporal gain for eternal merit, a barter (mubāyaʿah) with God.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb) — The phrase "if the fighting is completed on that basis, then he has his stipulation" (fa-in fāta al-qitāl ʿalā dhālika kāna lahu sharṭuhu) follows the standard protasis-apodosis structure, where the apodosis is a nominal sentence indicating a settled legal consequence.
translation:
I say: From the methodology of spiritual ascent — the seventh station is that one be engaged in a matter of essential need (muhimm), if not upon a community [that requires it]. He equips a warrior and makes for him a stipulated reward (juʿl). He said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said to ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ: "Are you willing that I send you in an army, and God will grant you safety and booty, and I will desire for you wealth with a righteous desire?" (31)

And from Ibn Baṭṭāl: ʿAṭiyyah took a horse on the condition of half the spoils; al-Awzāʿī and Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal permitted this. Al-Lakhmī said: If the imam says, "Whoever kills so-and-so, then for him is his spoils (salab), or for him are dinars or a garment; or whoever ascends such a place, or reaches it, or stands in it, then for him is such-and-such" — this is prohibited in its inception, because it is fighting for worldly gain. But if the fighting is completed on that basis, then he has his stipulation, because he acted upon his share of the worldly, so it is like a transaction (mubāyaʿah). And what is in the "Iḥyāʾ": Among crafts, some are essential (muhimmah), meaning: praiseworthy is the one who occupies himself with them; and among them are those that are dispensable, because they revert to seeking comfort and adornment, like engraving and dyeing. He said: Thus the people of religion disapprove of that. As for musical instruments and tools whose use is forbidden, then avoiding them falls under the category of abandoning wrongdoing. He said: The practice of the righteous was ten crafts, among them: bead-making, trade, tailoring, ironwork, and weaving. He said: The Salaf disapproved of taking wages for everything that falls under the category of acts of worship, such as washing the dead and burying them; likewise the call to prayer (adhān), the tarāwīḥ prayers, teaching the Qurʾān, and teaching jurisprudence (fiqh). He said: Even if we rule the validity of hiring for that, then these works are meant to be traded for the Hereafter, and taking something for them is an exchange of the worldly for the Hereafter. End quote. And this agrees with al-Lakhmī's determination, and opposes what Abū ʿUmar narrated from the companions of al-Shāfiʿī. Mālik said: That a man hire himself in the camel market is more beloved to me than that he do a work for God, exalted be He, for a wage. Saḥnūn said: That I seek the worldly through the drum and the flute is more beloved to me than that I seek it through religion. End quote.

And the sum of all this is that hiring for acts of righteousness falls among the permissible hires. Is it better than hiring for other than that, or the reverse? Two opinions. The fruit of this, in my view, is that among the necessities of village people are an imam and a baker (farrān). Thus, on Mālik's school, hiring a baker is more lawful than the imam's stipend; and on what has been established — that engaging in the service of the mosque is better than engaging in the service of the oven — then the imam's stipend is more lawful. So if one of scrupulousness (waraʿ) may lead the prayer for free, then if he leads for a stipend, one must observe the intention of the endower (muḥabbis) and the congregation.

(1) Narrated by al-Ḥākim in his Mustadrak (2/257, hadith 2926)

title_en: The Seventh Station: On the Conduct of One Who Undertakes a Task Without Fulfilling Its Purpose
arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 165

منهج الترفي/ المقام السايع: أن يكون في مهم إن لم يكن على امم فدن

وقد تقدم قول عبد الوهاب: تسوية الإجارة على الحج بالإجارة على القضاء
وبناء الفناطير؛ فكما لا يتورع إذا حج عن غيره؛ بل يجب عليه أن يحرم من ميقات
الآجر ويزور عنه ويركع ركعتي الطواف وإن لم يفعل؛ فإما أن يحرم عليه أخذ
الأجرة أو يحط منها بقدر ما تورع؛ كما لو ترك الزيارة: فكذلك إذا تورع عن أخذ
الدعاء دبر الصلاة أو على قراءة بحزب» كان بعضهم ينتحل صنعة لا تجوز. قيل:

وبالجملة فلا يحل له أن يأخذ فائد وقف ولا إجارة منهم حتى يستوفي ما هو
مقصدهم. فإن فاضلًا ففاضل؛ وإن مفضولًا فمفضول؛ وإلا كان آكلا بديته. وفرق
بين من يأكل فائد الوقف بخدمته ومن يأكله بناموسه؛ قال الله عز وجل: لإولتكن
يخ تلفي 4 [آل عمران: 104]. وقال سبحانه: اروك
ينم طَيَةٌ 4[التوبة: 122]. قال سحنون: قمن فيه أهلية تعين عليه الخروج في
طلب العلم. قال شهاب الدين: ولا يستأذن في هذا أبويه بخلاف الجهاد. قال: لأن
الحاضر يقوم مقام غيره في الجهاد بخلاف العلم؛ إذ ليس كل أحد أهلا له يعني
العلم الذي هو فرض كفاية؛ وهو العلم الذي لا يتعلم بحال الإنسان في خاصته.
قال: فيجب على الأمة أن يكون منهم طائفة يتفقهون في الدين» والذي يتعين لهذا
من الناس من جاد حفظه وحسن إدراكه وطابت سجيته وسريرته؛ ومن لا فلا.

قال الشاطبي فيمن لم تكمل فيه الأدوات: أن انتحاله للعلم من باب العيث
اللمصلحة المجتلبة ومن تكليف ما لا يطاق في حقه؛ وكلاهما باطل شرعًا. وقال
الجوزي: من تلبيس إبليس على الفقهاء أنهم يأكلون وقف المدرسة على
المتشاغلين بالعلم؛ فيمكث سنين» ويتهي في العلم؛ فلا ييقى له حظ؛ لأنه إنما
جعل لمن يتعلم إلا أن يكون مدرساء فإن شغله دائم؛ قال في “الإحياء': ويجب أن
يكون في كل محلة وفي كل قرية فقيه يعلم الناس دينهم؛ ومن تعلم مسألة من العلم
فهو من أهل العلم بهاء يتعين عليه أن يعلم غيره: وإلا فهو شريكه في الإثم: قال
الشاطبي: فإذا فرض مثا واحد من الطلبة ظهر عليه حسن إدراك تعين على الناظر
أن يميل به نحو ذلك التقصده لما يرجى من القيام بمصلحة التعليم؛ فيصرف مثا
المعلمي العربية: فإن وقف فيقوم بذلك الذي وصل إليه؛ وإن انتهض للتفقه في
الدين فعل به كذلك.

# PageV1P166
anchors:
- Root: ت-ر-ف-ي (tarafā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Elevation, ascent, or refinement of one's state; moving from a lower to a higher rank.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Spiritual progression (taraqqī) toward higher stations (maqāmāt) in the path of religion.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is physical elevation; here used metaphorically for moral and religious advancement.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — The phrase "if he is not upon a community" (in lam yakun ʿalā umam) introduces a conditional that governs the subsequent ruling, requiring precise parsing of the protasis and apodosis.
translation:
I say: The seventh station is that one be engaged in a matter [of religious service] — if he is not upon a community [of the rightly guided], then [he must beware].

The statement of ʿAbd al-Wahhāb has already been mentioned: that the hire for performing the pilgrimage (ijārah ʿalā al-ḥajj) is equated with the hire for performing judicial duties (ijārah ʿalā al-qaḍāʾ) and for building arches (banāʾ al-fanāṭīr). For just as one does not refrain (lā yatawarraʿu) when he performs the pilgrimage on behalf of another — rather, it is obligatory upon him to enter the state of iḥrām from the mīqāt of the one who hired him, to visit [the Prophet's tomb] on his behalf, and to perform the two rakʿahs of the circumambulation (ṭawāf) — and if he does not do so, then either it is forbidden for him to take the wage, or it is diminished by the amount of what he refrained from, as if he had omitted the visitation (ziyārah). So likewise, if he refrains from taking [the reward of] the supplication (duʿāʾ) after the prayer, or from reciting a portion (ḥizb) [of the Qurʾān] — for some of them used to adopt a craft that was not permissible. It was said: [Such a one is blameworthy].

In sum, it is not lawful for him to take the benefit of a waqf (endowment) or a hire from them until he fulfills what is their intended purpose. For if he is excellent, then [he takes] as an excellent one; and if he is deficient, then [he takes] as a deficient one. Otherwise, he is one who consumes his wage (ākil bi-bidʿatihi). And there is a distinction between one who consumes the benefit of a waqf through his service (khidmah) and one who consumes it through his prestige (nāmūs). God, Mighty and Majestic, said: {«وَلْتَكُن مِّنكُمْ أُمَّةٌ يَدْعُونَ إِلَى الْخَيْرِ»} [Āl ʿImrān: 104]. And He, Glorified, said: {«فَلَوْلَا نَفَرَ مِن كُلِّ فِرْقَةٍ مِّنْهُمْ طَائِفَةٌ لِّيَتَفَقَّهُوا فِي الدِّينِ»} [al-Tawbah: 122].

Sahnūn said: Whoever possesses the qualification (ahliyyah) — it is incumbent upon him to go forth in seeking knowledge. Shihāb al-Dīn said: He does not seek permission from his parents in this matter, unlike jihād. He said: Because the one who remains [at home] can stand in place of another in jihād, unlike knowledge — for not everyone is qualified for it, meaning the knowledge that is a communal obligation (farḍ kifāyah); and it is the knowledge that a person cannot learn by his own individual effort alone. He said: So it is obligatory upon the community (ummah) that there be among them a group who acquire deep understanding in religion (yatafaqqahūna fī al-dīn). And the one who is designated for this among the people is he whose memory is sound, whose comprehension is good, whose nature (sajiyyah) is wholesome, and whose inner self (sarīrah) is pure. And whoever is not so — then not.

Al-Shāṭibī said concerning one in whom the tools [of scholarship] are not complete: That his adoption of knowledge is of the category of corruption (ʿayth) for the sake of a sought-after benefit, and of imposing an unbearable burden (taklīf mā lā yuṭāq) in his case; and both are null (bāṭil) according to the Sacred Law. Al-Jawzī said: Among the deceptions of Iblīs upon the jurists (fuqahāʾ) is that they consume the waqf of the school (madrasah) [endowed] for those occupied with knowledge — so one remains for years, and plays at knowledge, and no share remains for him; for it was only established for one who learns — unless he be a teacher (mudarris), for his occupation is continuous. He said in the "Iḥyāʾ": It is obligatory that in every district and every village there be a jurist (faqīh) who teaches the people their religion. And whoever learns a single question (masʾalah) of knowledge — he is among the people of knowledge by it, and it is incumbent upon him to teach it to others; otherwise, he is a partner in their sin. Al-Shāṭibī said: So if, for example, one of the students shows good comprehension, it is incumbent upon the supervisor (nāẓir) to incline him toward that intended purpose, hoping for the fulfillment of the interest of teaching (maṣlaḥat al-taʿlīm); so he directs him, for example, to [teach] Arabic grammar. For if he stops [there], he performs that which he has reached; and if he rises to deep understanding in religion (tafaqquh fī al-dīn), he acts likewise with him.

title_en: The Seventh Station: On the Obligation of Knowledge and the Integrity of Its Guardians
arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 166

- منهج الترقي/ المقام السابع: أن يكون في مهم إن لم يكن على مع

قال مالك؛ وقد سثل عن طلب العلم قال: أما على كل الناس فلاء قال: وأماا
من كان فيه موضع للإمامة؛ فالاجتهاد في طلب العلم عليه واجب؛ قال؛ ويجب
على عامة الناس إقامة مثل هذا وإجباره على القيام بذلك؛ من باب ما لا يتم
الواجب إلا به. اه من "الموافقات".

فانظر إذا كان الواجب على المسلمين إقامة من يحفظ لهم دينهم ويعلمهم٠‏
فمعلوم أن بيت المال ليس فيه شيء لهؤلاء» ومعلوم أن الناس لا يعطون خراججا
لمن يعلمهم؛ فما هو العلم اليوم ينحفظ إلا بالأحباس التي على الروابط ومساجد
القرى فضا عن المساجد العظام. فالواجب أن لا تنطلق يد أحد على حبس للفقهاء
حتى يقوم بحظ من التعليم وحفظ الشرع؛ ولو بأن يحكم كتب السؤاله ويفهم ما
يجيبه به المفتي ليفسره قومه. فعامي أو مظهر ورع يستحوذ على أكل الحيس لاا
يزيد على الصلاة بالناس إلا الصلاة؛ مثل الدكالي رحمه الله لا يصلي خلقه
ونوافقه نحن في مثل هذاء خصوضا إذ أحدنا لا يمكنه أن يستوفي فضائل الشريعة
لكلف الخلق؛ ويجيء مثل هذاء فيستميل القلوب بما لا يفتح فيه لمن يعلم الناسه
فيستحوذ على الوظائف ويحرمها خدام الشرع؛ فهذا في الحقيقة يأكل الأوقاف بدينه
الا بخدمته يتنزل عليه قول عياض: من توصل للدنيا بطريقة الصلاح فهو من أشد
الظلمة.

.وقيل لابن المبارك: من الناس؟ قال: العلماءء قيل: من الملوك؟ قال: الزهاد
قبل: فمن السفلة؟ قال: الذي يأكل بديته. وقد تقدم قول الزهري: إن العالم إذا لم
يخل بواجب ولم يقصر في فرض فهو أفضل من العابدين؛ ويجوز له قبول صلة
السلطان؛ وتحرم على غيره. كما تقدم عن مالك وأشهب وابن القاسم وابن وهب
والفضيل وغيرهم. فكذلك يكون أولى بالتشدم للإمامة بالمرتب. وقد نص في
'جامع الذخيرة" أن المال الذي لا يعلم ربه. فسبيله سبيل الفيء لا سبيل الصدقة.
رأى بعضهم أصبغ يخرج يده من غير كمه؛ فقال: أخرج بدك على طوقك؛ يعني:
كل ذلك يضمحل في جنب ما أعطاء لله من مزية العلم.

وقال أحمد بن حنبل لإسحاق بن راهويه: تعال أريك رجلا لم تر عينك مثله.
فأراه الشافعي» فقال: نترك علم سفيان والمقري على سنهماء فقال: ويحك؛ علم
سفيان إن فاتنا بعلو أدركناء يتزول» ولا يضر ذلك دينناء وعقل هذا الفتى أخاف أن

# PageV1P167

### | الصفحة 167

منهج الترقي/ المقام السابع: أن يكوذ في مهم إن لم يكن على أصم. للد
لا أجده أبدا. وقيل لابن وهب في المسائل الجدد فقال: أدع أنا المسائل القدم الني
اقرأناها عليه وهو نشيط لهاء حتى أنه ريما محا لي الشيء بكمه من كتابي.

وقال مالك: لقد أدركت بهذه البلدة أقواقا لو استسقي الناس بهم المططر
السقواء قد سمعوا العلم والحديث»
ألزموا أنفسهم خوف الله والزهد؛ والفتوى تحتاج لمن له تقى وإتقان وعلم وفهم؛
فيعلم ما خرج من رأسه وما يصل إليه غذاء فأما زهد بلا إتقان ولا معرفة فلا يتتفع
ابه ولا هو حجة ولا يؤخط عنه. اه

وعلى هذا يقال: لا ينبغي لمثل هذا أن يستحوذ على وظيف يستعين به خحادم
الشريعة فيأكله هو على مجرد الإمامة خاصة: فإن هذا مضاد للزهد؛ فيصير لا زهد
ولا هو ينتفع به؛ وهذا كما قال في "الاحياء” في الصوفي إذا اتسع اتساع العالم أن
التصوف يذهب بخلاف العلم؛ فيقال: العالم الفلاني يصاحب الملوك؛ ولا يقال:
الصوفي الفلاني يصاحب الملوك؛ لأن من صحب الملوك لا تصوف له. وانظر إذا
كانت المزية للإتقان والفهم. فيلتحق الأحداث بمراتب الكهول؛ ألا ترى أن عمر
رضي الله عنه كان يقدم ابن عباس في الشورى على صغر سنه. وقد رشح هذا الإمام
الماوردي ونقل: عليكم بمشاورة الأحداث؛ فإنهم قد ينتجون ريا لم يبله طول
القدم ولا استولت عليه رطوبة الهرم. قال ابن عباس: ما أتى الله عبدًا علمًا إلا
تلا قول الله تعالى: لَلوأسع يكيم 4
4 [الكهف: 13]: وقال سيحانه

شاباء والخير كله في الشباب»
[الأنبياء: 60]؛ وقوله: طاه

وتعالى: طوََنتَهُ فصتا 48 [مريم: 12].

.ولي يحبى بن أكثم القضاء ابن إحدى وعشرين سنة؛ فأراد أن يخجله رجل
يصغر سنهء فقال له: كم سن القاضي أيا مثل سن عتاب بن أسيد حين
ولاه رسول الله يك إمارة مكة وقضاءهاء كما تقدم هذا في المقام نفسه في التدلي:

أنه إث كان ورع ودين فيكون بينه وبين ربه. و

# PageV1P168
anchors:
- Root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Knowledge as the indelible mark of divine imprint upon the heart; comprehension of reality as it is.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): ʿIlm as the apprehension of a thing in its true essence, contrasted with mere opinion (ẓann); its highest form is knowledge of God and His commands.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: perception and certainty. Metaphorical: the "knowledge" that is a means to worldly ends—here, a subtle inversion where outward learning masks inner corruption.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The text pivots on "if not for..." (law lā) and "except that..." (illā an), governing the logical necessity of communal obligation.
translation:
I say: Consider, then—if it is incumbent upon the Muslims to establish one who preserves their religion for them and teaches them, then it is known that the public treasury (bayt al-māl) contains nothing for such persons, and it is known that the people do not pay tribute (kharāj) to one who instructs them. So knowledge today is preserved only through the endowments (aḥbās) attached to the hospices (rawābiṭ) and the mosques of villages—let alone the great congregational mosques. Therefore, it is obligatory that no hand be unleashed upon an endowment designated for the jurists (fuqahāʾ) unless that person fulfills a share of teaching and preserving the Sacred Law—even if only by judging the questions posed to him and understanding what the muftī answers, so that he may explain it to his people.

For a commoner (ʿāmmī) or one who merely displays piety (mutazahhid), who seizes upon the consumption of an endowment and does no more than lead the people in prayer—such a one is like al-Dakkālī (may God have mercy on him), who did not pray behind his own creation. And we ourselves are in such a situation, especially since none of us can fully exhaust the virtues of the Sacred Law due to the burden of creation. Then one such as this comes and sways hearts by means of what he does not open up for those who teach the people—so he seizes the offices and deprives the servants of the Sacred Law of them. This one, in truth, eats the endowments by means of his religion, not by his service. Upon him descends the saying of ʿIyāḍ: "Whoever reaches the world by way of apparent righteousness is among the most severe of oppressors."

It was said to Ibn al-Mubārak: "Who are the people?" He said: "The scholars." It was said: "Who are the kings?" He said: "The ascetics (zuhhād)." It was said: "Then who are the base (safalah)?" He said: "The one who eats by his religion." And already mentioned is the saying of al-Zuhrī: "If the scholar does not neglect an obligation and does not fall short in a duty, he is better than the worshippers (ʿābidīn), and it is permissible for him to accept the gift of the ruler, while it is forbidden for others." As has preceded from Mālik, Ashhab, Ibn al-Qāsim, Ibn Wahb, al-Fuḍayl, and others. Thus, likewise, he is more deserving of advancement to the imamate by rank. And it has been stated in the "Jāmiʿ al-Dhakhīrah" that wealth whose owner is unknown follows the path of the spoils (fayʾ), not the path of charity (ṣadaqah).

Some saw Aṣbagh put out his hand from other than his sleeve, and he said: "Put out your hand from your collar"—meaning: all of that vanishes in comparison to what he gave to God of the excellence of knowledge.

Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal said to Isḥāq ibn Rāhawayh: "Come, I will show you a man your eye has never seen the like of." So he showed him al-Shāfiʿī. Then he said: "We leave the knowledge of Sufyān and al-Muqriʾ upon their age." He replied: "Woe to you! The knowledge of Sufyān—if it escapes us by its elevation, we attain it by transmission (riwāyah), and that does not harm our religion. But the intellect of this young man—I fear that I will never find its like ever again."

And it was said to Ibn Wahb regarding the new legal questions (masāʾil jadīdah), and he said: "I leave the old questions which he read to us while he was eager for them—so much so that he would sometimes erase something for me with his sleeve from my book."

And Mālik said: "I have encountered in this town people such that if the people sought rain through them, they would be given rain—they had heard knowledge and ḥadīth. They imposed upon themselves the fear of God and asceticism. But legal opinion (fatwā) requires one who has piety (taqwā), mastery (itqān), knowledge, and understanding—so that he knows what issues from his head and what reaches him as nourishment. As for asceticism without mastery and without knowledge, it is of no benefit, nor is it an authority, nor is it transmitted from him."

Upon this, I say: It is not fitting for one such as this to seize an office by which the servants of the Sacred Law are aided, and then he consumes it merely on the basis of the imamate alone—for this is contrary to asceticism. Thus he becomes neither ascetic nor does he benefit from it. This is as was said in the "Iḥyāʾ" concerning the Sufi: if he expands as the scholar expands, then Sufism departs, unlike knowledge. For one says: "Such-and-such a scholar accompanies kings," but one does not say: "Such-and-such a Sufi accompanies kings," because whoever accompanies kings has no Sufism.

And consider: if the excellence lies in mastery and understanding, then the young (aḥdāth) may join the ranks of the mature (kuhūl). Do you not see that ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him) advanced Ibn ʿAbbās in the consultative council (shūrā) despite his youth? And al-Māwardī endorsed this, transmitting: "Upon you is to consult the young, for they may produce an opinion that the length of age has not worn out, nor has the moisture of senility overtaken it." Ibn ʿAbbās said: "God has not given a servant knowledge except that he recites the saying of God Most High: {«وَرَبَطْنَا عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ»} [Al-Kahf: 14]." And He said, glorified and exalted: {«سَمِعْنَا فَتًى يَذْكُرُهُمْ يُقَالُ لَهُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ»} [Al-Anbiyāʾ: 60]; and His saying, exalted: {«وَآتَيْنَاهُ الْحُكْمَ صَبِيًّا»} [Maryam: 12].

And Yaḥyā ibn Aktham was appointed to the judgeship at twenty-one years of age. A man wanted to shame him for his youth, so he said to him: "How old is the judge?" He replied: "The like of the age of ʿAttāb ibn Asīd when the Messenger of God ﷺ appointed him to the governorship of Mecca and its judgeship." As has preceded in this same station regarding the descent (al-tadallī): that if he has piety and religion, then it is between him and his Lord.

title_en: Section 127 — On the Seventh Station: Seeking Knowledge for the Hereafter, Not the World
arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 168

بلك منهج الترقي/ المقام السابع: أن يكون في مهم إن لم يكن على أهع
وقد تقدم قول الحسن: كنا تطلب العلم للدنيا فجرنا إلى الآخرة؛ وأما
المقتصد فإذا كان للمرء أن يجمم نفسه باللهو ليكون عوئًا له على الحق كما تقدم؛
فمن باب أولى بالعلم كما تقدم للمازري فيمن نسي صلاة
وإن كان في 'الإحياء' قد بدع هذا وذمه

افد قال في العلوم غير
الشرعية كالطب والحساب: إن كليهما فرض كفابة: قال: وقد يكون من العلوم غير
الشرعية ما نعده فضيلة لا فريضة؛ وذلك كالتعمق في دقائق الحساب وخفايا الطب
وغير ذلك مما يستغنى عنه ولكنه يفيد زيادة قوة في القدر المحتاج إليه. اف قانظر
من باب أولى أن نقول هذا في العلم الشرعي.

قال المازري: قال أبو حامد: وقد يكون من العلوم غير الشرعية ما هو مباح»
كالعلم بالأشعار التي لا سخف فيهاء وتواريخ الأخبار وما يجري مجراهاء وقد قال
الشيخ الصالح مؤلف كتاب ألف باء: فإن قلت: فكم ضيعت في هذا الكتاب من
زمان» وعطلت فيه من أوان» وقد كان لك الاشتغال بذكر المولى أحق منه وأولى»
اثم ذكر سيرة الفضيل في انقياضه وإقفال بابه من خارج ألا يشعر به أحد أنه بداره
ثم قال: فاقول: لكل مقام مقالء ولكل زمان رجال؛ وعلى كل كلام جواب؛ وفي
كل مسألة باب. أول ما أفول لك في ذلك: أنا لسنا كأوتك: ثم لم نبلغ بعد إلى
منزلتهم ولم نرتق إلى درجتهم؛ ثم قال كلاما إلى أن قال: هذه يا أخي منزلة والله ما
بلغتها ولا تحدثني نفسي بها إلا أن يتداركني لله بها كما تدارك أولتك؛ فهو مولانا
كما هو مولاهم؛ ونحن عبيده كما هم؛ ونحن ولله الحمد أحسن حالا من غيرناء

قيل لابن الأحنف بن قيس: لم لا تكون كأبيك؟ قال: دعوا أبي وقيسوني
بأبنائكم؛ وقال ابن العربي: رأى أبو مسلم الخولائي أن قوما قد اجتمعوا جلوشاء
فرجى أن يكونوا على خيرء فجلس إليهم؛ فإذا بعضهم يقول: قدم لي غلام فأصاب
كذا وكذاء وقال آخر: وأنا جهزت غلاماء فنظر إليهم وقال: سبحان الله هل تدرون
ما مثلي ومثلكم كرجل أصابه مطر غزير وابل فإذا هو بمصراعين عظيمين» فقالة
الو دخلت هذا البيت حتى يذهب عني هذا المطرء فدخل فإذا البيت ل سقف له
جلست إليكم أن تكونوا على خير وعلى ذكرء فإذا أنتم أصحاب دنياء ققام عنهم.
قال القاضي أبو بكر: أصح من هذا ما في الترمذي: قيل لزيد بن ثابت: حدثنا

# PageV1P169
anchors:
- Root: ج-ر-ي (j-r-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To run, flow, or pursue a course; hence "jarā" (it led/conduced) implies an inevitable consequence or drift.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, denotes the natural or divinely-ordained progression of actions toward their ultimate end (maʾāl).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical motion; metaphorical here for the unintended spiritual outcome of seeking worldly aims.
- Sībawayh Rule: Al-ʿAṭf bi-l-Fāʾ (The Conjunctive Fāʾ for Consequence) — The fāʾ in "fajarā" (so it led) marks a sequential result, not mere coordination.
translation:
I say — and this is the seventh station of ascent: that one be engaged in a matter of importance, even if one is not among its people [of excellence].

Already mentioned is the saying of al-Ḥasan: "We sought knowledge for the sake of the world, and it led us to the Hereafter." As for the moderate one (al-muqtaṣid): if a man may lawfully refresh himself with leisure so that it becomes an aid to him in [pursuing] the truth, as has preceded — then by a fortiori reasoning [this applies] to knowledge, as al-Māzarī stated concerning one who forgot a prayer.

And although in the 'Iḥyāʾ' [al-Ghazālī] deemed this blameworthy and censured it, he nevertheless said concerning non-religious sciences such as medicine and arithmetic: "Both are a communal obligation (farḍ kifāyah)." He said: "And among the non-religious sciences there may be that which we count as a virtue (faḍīlah) rather than an obligation — such as delving into the subtleties of arithmetic and the hidden depths of medicine, and other things that could be dispensed with, yet which yield increased strength in that which is needed." So consider — by a fortiori reasoning, we should say this concerning the religious science.

Al-Māzarī said: Abū Ḥāmid said: "And among the non-religious sciences there may be that which is permissible (mubāḥ) — such as knowledge of poetry that contains no frivolity, and historical reports and what runs in their course." And the righteous Shaykh, author of the book 'Alif Bāʾ', said: "For if you say: 'How much time have you wasted in this book, and how many moments have you rendered idle therein, when occupying yourself with the remembrance of the Master (al-Mawlā) was more rightful for you and more fitting?'" — Then he mentioned the biography of al-Fuḍayl regarding his seclusion and his locking his door from outside so that none might know he was in his house. Then he said: "I say: Every station has its discourse, every time has its men, every speech has its answer, and every question has its door. The first thing I say to you in this: We are not like those [predecessors]. We have not yet reached their abode, nor ascended to their rank." Then he spoke further until he said: "This, O brother, is a station — by Allah, I have not attained it, nor does my soul aspire to it, unless Allah overtakes me with it as He overtook those predecessors. For He is our Master as He is their Master; we are His servants as they are; and we — praise be to Allah — are in a better state than others."

It was said to Ibn al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays: "Why are you not like your father?" He said: "Leave my father, and measure me against your own sons." And Ibn al-ʿArabī said: Abū Muslim al-Khawlānī saw a group of people gathered as if in counsel, and hoped they might be upon good, so he sat with them. Then one of them said: "I sent forth a servant-boy, and he hit such-and-such [in trade]." Another said: "And I equipped a servant-boy." So he looked at them and said: "Glory be to Allah! Do you know what my example and yours is like? Like a man struck by a heavy, torrential rain, who found himself before two great doors. He said: 'I will enter this house until this rain leaves me.' So he entered, and found the house had no roof. I sat with you hoping you were upon good and upon remembrance — and behold, you are people of the world." So he rose and left them.

Al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr said: More sound than this is what is in al-Tirmidhī: It was said to Zayd ibn Thābit: "Narrate to us..."

title_en: The Method of Ascent — Seventh Station: On the Permissibility of Light Conversation and Its Etiquette
arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 169

منهج الترقي/ المقام السابع: أن يكوذ في مهم إن لم يكن على أصم. فنك
أحاديث رسول الله يق قال: كنا إذا ذكرنا الدنيا ذكرها معناء وإذا ذكرنا الطعام ذكره
معناء وإذا ذكرنا الآخرة ذكرها معناء بكل هذا أحدئكم عن رسول الله ية.
م في المقام الثالث قول مالك: وقوم إذا أراد الناس يتحدثون؛ يقولون:
اذكروا الله ولم يكن ذلك شأن الأخيار.

وقال عياض: في حديث أم زرع من الفقه التحدث بملح الأخيار وطرف
الحكايات تسلية للنفوس وجلاء للقلب؛ وترجم عليه الترمذي؛ فقال: باب ما جاء
في كلامه َك في السمر وأدخل حديث أم زرع وحديث خرافة.

.وقال مالك: كان عطاء بن يسار كثير الحديث؛ وكان رجلا قاضًا ربما ترك
أصحابه ومجلسه وجلس إلى غيرهم؛ فإذا قالوا له: تركتناء فيقول: ما تركتكم ملالة.
ولكن لتستريحوا وتتحدثوا فيما يينكمء ولا تملواء قال ابن رشد: هذا لما جاء أن
رسول الله كل كان يتخول الناس بالموعظة مخافة السآمة عليهم.

.وقال ابن العربي: العبادة أن يقوم المرء بالقسط في جميع أقواله وأفعاله؛
فاصله: أن لا يعصي الله. وفرعه: أن لا يخالف السنة. ثم قال: ولقد شاهدت بلك
الديار العلماء والمتبتلين لا يهدأ لهم لسان بالقرب والعلوم والملح والأمشال
والنوادر كلها مكتوبة في صحائف الحسنات؛ وأصحابهم يرون الزمانة هي العبادة
والصمت هو الطاعة؛ وذلك لكثرة جهلهم وقلة عملهم؛ ولو استرسلوا في الكلام
الكبواء ولو أعلنوا بالمقال لغووا. الى

انظر قوله: ولو أعلنوا بالمقال لغوواء ما معناه؟ راجع هذا المعنى في هذا
المقام في التدلي؛ وقول الماوردي: وقد جهلوا من المذاهب ما يعلمه المبتدئ وقد
تذكرت قول الإمام الماوردي: أن قومًا تحققوا بالعلم تحقق المتكلفين: واشتهروا
به اشتهار المنحرفين؛ إذا أخذوا في المناظرة ظهر كلامهم؛ وإذا سئلوا عن واضح
المذهب ضلت أفهامهم حتى أنهم يتخبطون في الجواب خبط عشواء؛ فلا يظهر
لهم صواب؛ ولا يتفرر لهم جواب؛ ولا يرون ذلك نقصًا إذا لفقوا على المخالف
حججما مألوفة؛ وقد جهلوا من المذهب ما يعلمه المبتدئ. وقال أبو الدرداء: لا
تتعلموا العلم لتتجملوا به؛ فإنه يوشك إن طال بكم عمر أن يتجمل أحدكم بعلمه
كما يتجمل ذو البزة ييزته.

وقد

# PageV1P170
anchors:
- Root: س-م-ر (s-m-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Night conversation; extended discourse that continues into the dark hours; also the shade of the moon (samar) under which such talk occurs.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the prophetic tradition, samar denotes permissible, non-sinful social exchange that refreshes the heart, provided it does not lead to heedlessness of God.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: talk at night. Metaphorical: any pleasant, light-hearted exchange that "illuminates" the soul like moonlight — hence the juristic license for it.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-bayān (Appositional clarification) — The phrase "بكل هذا أحدثكم عن رسول الله ﷺ" uses apposition to tie the Prophet's own practice (mentioning worldly matters alongside the afterlife) to the author's transmission, ensuring grammatical and semantic cohesion.
translation:
I say — may God guide us and you:

**The Seventh Station of Ascent:** That one should be in a matter of importance, if not upon the firmest ground. For we have the hadiths of the Messenger of God ﷺ — he said: "When we mentioned the world, he mentioned it with us; when we mentioned food, he mentioned it with us; and when we mentioned the afterlife, he mentioned it with us." By all of this, I relate to you from the Messenger of God ﷺ.

In the Third Station, there is the saying of Mālik: "There are people who, when others wish to converse, say: 'Remember God!' — and that was not the way of the righteous."

And ʿIyāḍ said: "In the hadith of Umm Zarʿ there is juristic insight: conversing with the pleasantries of the righteous and the anecdotes of tales is a solace for souls and a polish for the heart." Al-Tirmidhī titled a chapter on this, saying: "Chapter on what has come concerning his ﷺ speech in night conversation," and he included therein the hadith of Umm Zarʿ and the hadith of Khurāfa.

And Mālik said: "ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār was a man of much hadith and a judge. Sometimes he would leave his companions and his gathering and sit with others. When they said to him, 'You have left us,' he would reply: 'I have not left you out of weariness, but so that you may rest and converse among yourselves, and not become bored.'" Ibn Rushd said: "This is because of what has come — that the Messenger of God ﷺ used to be mindful of people in his exhortations, fearing satiety (sāʾam) upon them."

And Ibn al-ʿArabī said: "Worship is that a man upholds equity in all his words and deeds. Its root is that he does not disobey God; its branch is that he does not contravene the Sunnah." Then he said: "I have witnessed in those lands scholars and devotees whose tongues never rested — with closeness [to God], with sciences, with pleasantries, with proverbs, and with anecdotes — all of it written in the pages of good deeds. Yet their companions hold that silence itself is worship and that stillness is obedience. That is due to their great ignorance and little action. Were they to let loose in speech, they would err; and were they to proclaim their words, they would blunder."

Reflect on his saying: "Were they to proclaim their words, they would blunder" — what does it mean? Review this meaning in this station in the section on "al-Tadallī" (the descent). And the saying of al-Māwardī: "They have been ignorant of the school's fundamentals to a degree that a beginner would know."

I have recalled the saying of Imam al-Māwardī: "There are people who have realized knowledge with the realization of the affected, and become famous for it with the fame of the deviant. When they enter into disputation, their speech appears; but when asked about the clear points of the school, their understandings stray — until they flounder in their answers like the blind groping in darkness. No correctness appears from them, no answer is settled for them. Yet they do not see this as a deficiency, so long as they have patched together familiar arguments against the opponent — while having been ignorant of the school's fundamentals to a degree that a beginner would know."

And Abū al-Dardāʾ said: "Do not learn knowledge to adorn yourselves with it; for if your life is prolonged, one of you may come to adorn himself with his knowledge just as a man of fine garments adorns himself with his attire."

And...

title_en: Section 129 — On the Seventh Station: The Scholar's Sincerity and Self-Knowledge
arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 170

24 منهج الترقي/ المقام السابع: أن يكون في مهم إن لم يكن على أهع

.ونقل ابن أبي زيد في صدر 'مختصره': قال نبينا عليه الصلاة والسلام: "من
تعلم العلم ليباهي به أو ليرائي به أوقفه الله موقف الذل؛ وجعله عليه حسرة يوم
القيامة”"".

وقال في "الاحياء”: وقد يظن أنه إذا تكلم بالعلم أنه موصوف به؛ ولو منع عن
مجلسه الذي يدعو فيه الناس إلى الله لضاقت عليه الأرض بما رحبت؛ ولو ظهر من
أقرانه من أقبل الخلق عليه وصلحوا على يده لمات غمًا يمتليئ بالحلاوة إذا أحدق
ابه المتعلمون؛ ويستوحش إذا خلا بالله. ومثل هذا كمثل طبيب مريض يصف
المرض ودواءه بفصاحته» ويصف الصحة والشفاء؛ قفارق المرضى في العلم
بالطب ولم يفارقهم في المرض. ثم قال: ولا يتفطن لهذه إلا الأكياس: لكن أقل
الدرجات أن يعرف الإنسان عيوب نفسه ويسوءه ويكرهه ويحرص على إصلاحه.
فإذا أراد الله بعبده خيرًا بصره بعيوب نفسه؛ وأمره أقرب من مغرور متمن على الله
يعلمة أو عمله. الف

قال تاج الدين في "حكمه": العبارات قوت لعائلة المستمعين: وليس لك إلاما
أنت له آكل. وقال مالك: ينبغي لمن خول علمًا وصار رنيسا يشار إليه بالاصابع أن
يضع الثراب على رأسه؛ ويمقت نفسه إذا خخلاء ولا يفرح بالرئاسة: فإنه إذا اضطجع
افي قبره وتوسد التراب ساءه ذلك.

وقال الإمام الشافعي: وددت أن الناس انتفعوا بعلمي ولم بنسب إلي منه شيء.
وقال رجل لسحنون: جثت اليوم ولم أسمع منك شيئا. فقال له: إن كنت في وق
خروجك ممن شيّعته الملائكة فقد سمعت؛ وإلا فلم تسمع وإن كنت قد سمعت.
وأرسل أسد بن الفرات إلى سحنون وعون والصمادحي واين رشيد يسألهم عن مسألة.
فأجاب فيها ابن رشيد وعون» ولم يجب سحنون؛ فلما خرجوا عذلاه في ثرك الجواب:
فقال: منعني أنكما بادرتما بالجواب» وكرهت أن أخالفكماء فندخل عليه إخوانا ونخرج
أعداء؛ وبين لهما وجه خطهماء فجزياه خيراء واعترفاء ورجعا إلى أسده فأخيرا
برجوعهما. قال عياض: لعل سحنوئًا عول على ما عرف من فضلهما أن يفعلا من
رجوعهما ما فعلاء فرجى أن يستبين الحق بلا تعلة ولا مخالقة.

ا) أخرجه الطبراتي في معجمه الكبير (127/5: رقم 44831

# PageV1P171
anchors:
- Root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Knowledge as distinct perception; the mark/trace (ʿalāmah) by which something is known
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): ʿIlm as firm conviction (yaqīn) conforming to reality — contrasted with mere opinion (ẓann) or pretension
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: possessing knowledge; Metaphorical: being described by it (ittiṣāf) — the danger of claiming the attribute without the reality
- Root: ر-ء-س (r-ʾ-s)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Head; leadership (riʾāsah) as being at the forefront
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Temporal authority/eminence — a trial (fitnah) for the soul
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical headship; Metaphorical: social preeminence that puffs up the ego
- Root: خ-ل-و (kh-l-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Emptiness, solitude; being alone
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Khalwah with Allah — the state of sincere devotion free from creatures
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: empty space; Metaphorical: the heart's solitude with God versus its desolation when deprived of human acclaim
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional/Exceptional Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The phrase "if he were prevented from his gathering... the earth would have constrained him" uses counterfactual conditionals (law + māḍī) to express hypothetical spiritual anguish, requiring the apodosis in the jāzim or māḍī form.
translation:
I say — may Allah guide us and you to the path of the rightly guided, and cause us to die upon the way of the truthful ones:

The seventh station: That the scholar be in a state of genuine concern (himmaḥ) — not merely upon outward appearance.

Ibn Abī Zayd transmitted at the beginning of his *Mukhtaṣar*, saying: Our Prophet, upon him be prayer and peace, said: {«Whoever learns knowledge to boast with it or to show off with it, Allah will station him in the place of humiliation and make it a cause of regret for him on the Day of Resurrection»}.

And he (al-Ghazālī) said in the *Iḥyāʾ*: A man may suppose that because he speaks about knowledge, he is thereby described by it. Yet if he were prevented from his gathering in which he calls people to Allah, the earth — despite its vastness — would become straitened for him. And if one of his peers were to appear upon whom the people turned their faces, and through whose hands they were reformed, he would die of grief. He is filled with sweetness when the students crowd around him, and he feels desolate (yastaʾnis) when alone with Allah. Such a one is like a sick physician who eloquently describes the illness and its remedy, and prescribes health and cure — yet he departs from the sick in the science of medicine, but does not depart from them in the sickness itself.

Then he said: None perceive this except the intelligent ones (al-akyās). But the least of the degrees is that a man know his own faults, be grieved by them, detest them, and strive earnestly to rectify them. For when Allah desires good for His servant, He grants him insight into his own faults. And such a one is nearer [to salvation] than a deluded man who presumes upon Allah, whether by his knowledge or by his deed.

Tāj al-Dīn said in his *Ḥikam*: Expressions are nourishment for the family of listeners — and you have nothing except that for which you are a consumer. And Mālik said: It behooves one who has been granted knowledge and has become a leader pointed at by fingers, to place dust upon his head, to despise himself in his solitude, and not to rejoice in leadership — for when he lies down in his grave and pillows upon the dust, that will grieve him.

Al-Imām al-Shāfiʿī said: I wish that the people had benefited from my knowledge, and nothing of it were attributed to me.

A man said to Saḥnūn: I came today and heard nothing from you. He replied: If, at the moment of your coming, you were among those whom the angels escorted, then you have heard; otherwise, you have not heard — even if you had heard.

And Asad ibn al-Furāt sent to Saḥnūn, ʿAwn, al-Ṣamādiḥī, and Ibn Rashīd, asking them about a question. Ibn Rashīd and ʿAwn answered it, but Saḥnūn did not. When they departed, they reproached him for withholding the answer. He said: What prevented me is that you both hastened to answer, and I disliked opposing you — lest we enter upon him as brothers and depart as enemies. Then he showed them the error of their way, and they thanked him, acknowledged [their mistake], and returned to Asad, informing him of their retraction.

ʿIyāḍ said: Perhaps Saḥnūn relied upon what he knew of their virtue — that they would do what they did in retracting — so he hoped that the truth might become manifest without flattery or dissimulation.

(Reported by al-Ṭabarānī in his *al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr*, 5/127, no. 4483)

title_en: The Method of Spiritual Ascent — Station Seven: On the Etiquette and Dangers of Disputation (Munāẓarah)
arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 171

منهج الترقي المقام السابع: أن يكوذ في مهم إن لم يكن على أصم. فنك
وقال يحيى: لما قرأت كتاب أسد على ابن القاسم وضع أشهب يده في مثلهاء.
فخالفه في جلها فقلت لابن القاسم: لو أعدت نظرك؛ فقال: أفمل إن شاء الله. فلما
تقاصيته بعد أيام قال: يا أبا محمد؛ نظرت في مقالتك؛ فوجدت إجابتي يوم أجبنك
لله وحده؛ فرجوت أن أوفق» وإجابتي اليوم إتما تكون نقضًا على صاحبي» فأخاف
أن لا أوفق في الإجابة؛ فتركته. وقال الشاقعي: ما ناظرت أحدًا قط فأحبيت أن
يخطئ؛ وما كلمت أحدًا قط وأنا أبالي أن يبين الله الحق على لساني أو على لسانه.
قال: والعلم بين أهله رحم متصل؛ قال أبو حامد: فتكون المناظرة في طلب
الحق كمنشد ضالة يرى المناظر رفيقه معيًا لا خصمًا أن يطلعا على نص قاطع.
قال في 'المستصفى”: وأما في الفروع فلا يتناظر فيها لانتقال خصمه إلا
الضعيف من الفقهاء يظن أن كل مجتهد ليس بمصيب وأن الحق في واحد وصاحبه
معين» وهذا لم يقل به أحدء وقال أيضًا ما معناه: ريما يقول المناظر: أما خصمي
فقد علمت أنه لا يرجع إلي؛ ولكن أناظر لأظهر الحق لغيره. قال: وهذا أيضًا ليس
كذلك؛ إذ لا يتصور اتفاق المستمعين على ترجيح كلام أحد المتناظرين؛ وإذا كان
قصد المناظر هذاء فقد ذهبت الرحم التي قال الشافعي: فتثمر هذه المناظرة
فواحش؛ منها أنهم لا يجدون بدا من التودد باللسان» ويعلم كل من سمع ذلك منهم
أنه كذب وزور ونفاق وفجور؛ وربما يخرج المناظر لتزكية نفسه؛ فيقول لخصمه:
الست ممن يخفى عليه مثل هذاء
قيل لحكيم: ما الصدق الفبيح؟ قال: ثناء المرء على نفسه. وقد يتعدى المناظر
من الظهور على خصمه بالمقال إلى الظهور عليه بالفعال؛ فيتنافس معه في القرب
الصدر؛ ويعبر عن التواضع الذي أثنى الله عليه بالذل» وعن التكبر بعز
الدين تحريفًا للاسم وإضلالاء ويحثال إذا صد عن صدر المجلس أن يجعل بينه
وبسين الأقسران بعض الأرذال» وهذا عين الكبرء فإن ذلك يخف على نفوس
المستكبرين؛ يوهمون أنهم تركوا مكانهم بالاستحقاق, وأن ذلك متهم فضلء
والحوار لا ينحط عن أقرانه إلى ما يقع أثناء المناظرة من الوقوع في الأستاذين
وخروج الخشية من القلب؛ حتى لا يدري المصلي منهم ما الذي يقرأء ثم به أثناء
المناظرة يخرج من كلامه جميع دقائق الجدل المبتدع؛ يمنع معينه في النظر من
الاتقال من دليل إلى دليل؛ ويقول: هذا لا يلزمني ذكره؛ وهذا يناقض كلامك»

# PageV1P172
anchors:
- Root: ن-ظ-ر (na-ẓa-ra)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "To look, consider, examine; to await; to deliberate." Core sense: directed intellectual gaze with expectation of outcome.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, naẓar is the disciplined act of rational inquiry leading to knowledge (ʿilm); its opposite is taqlīd (blind following).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical sight. Metaphorical (majāz): contemplative reasoning — the "eye of the heart" (ʿayn al-qalb) turned toward evidence.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Responsive Construction (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb) — the protasis (in) governs the apodosis (fa-), marking logical dependence, as in "in lam yakun ʿalā aṣamm" (if he is not upon deafness).
translation:
I say — and success is from God alone:

The seventh station of the method of ascent: that the disputant be engaged in a matter of importance, if he is not upon deafness [to truth]. So we say:

Yaḥyā related: When I read the book of Asad before Ibn al-Qāsim, Ashab placed his hand upon its like [i.e., a parallel passage]. He then opposed him in most of it. So I said to Ibn al-Qāsim: "Would you reconsider your view?" He replied: "Perhaps, if God wills." When I returned to him after some days, he said: "O Abū Muḥammad, I examined your statement, and I found that my answer on the day I answered you was for God alone; so I hoped to be granted success [in it]. But my answer today would only be a refutation against my companion [Ashab]; so I fear I would not be granted success in answering — therefore I abandoned it."

Al-Shāfiʿī said: "I never disputed with anyone such that I wished him to err; and I never spoke with anyone while caring whether God made the truth appear upon my tongue or upon his tongue."

He said: "Knowledge among its people is a connected mercy (raḥim muttaṣil)."

Abū Ḥāmid [al-Ghazālī] said: "Thus disputation in seeking truth is like one who searches for a lost object — he sees his fellow disputant as a companion in the quest, not an adversary, so that they might both arrive at a decisive text (naṣṣ qāṭiʿ)."

He said in *al-Mustaṣfā*: "As for subsidiary matters (furūʿ), one does not dispute therein for the conversion of one's opponent — except the weak among jurists who imagine that every mujtahid is not correct, and that the truth is in one [view] alone while his companion is mistaken. But no one has ever held this."

He also said, in meaning: "Perhaps the disputant says: 'As for my opponent, I know he will not return to me; but I dispute to manifest the truth to others.'" He said: "This also is not so; for it is inconceivable that all listeners would agree upon the preponderance of one of the two disputants' speech. And if the disputant's intention is this, then the mercy that al-Shāfiʿī mentioned has departed."

Thus this kind of disputation bears foul fruits. Among them: they find no escape from flattering with the tongue, and everyone who hears that from them knows it is falsehood, fabrication, hypocrisy, and wickedness. And perhaps the disputant goes out to praise himself, saying to his opponent: "Are you not among those to whom such a thing is not hidden?"

It was said to a sage: "What is the ugly truth?" He said: "A man's praise of himself."

And the disputant may pass from overcoming his opponent by speech to overcoming him by deed. So he vies with him for proximity to the head of the assembly, and he interprets the humility that God has praised as abasement, and pride as the honor of religion — distorting the name and leading astray. And when he is turned away from the head of the assembly, he strives to place between himself and the two ends of the rows some of the base people. This is the very essence of pride (kibr); for that is light upon the souls of the arrogant — they delude themselves that they have left their place by merit, and that this is a matter of their virtue.

And the discourse does not descend from its peers to what occurs during the disputation of falling upon the two masters [i.e., the founding imams], and the departure of reverence (khashyah) from the heart — until the one praying among them does not know what he recites. Then, during the disputation, he brings forth from his speech all the subtleties of innovated dialectic (jadal mubtadaʿ). He prevents his companion in inquiry from moving from one proof to another, saying: "This is not incumbent upon me to mention," and "This contradicts your speech."

title_en: Section 131 — The Seventh Station: On the Impermissibility of Theological Disputation (Jadal) and Scholastic Theology (Kalām)
arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 172

- منهج الترقي/ المقام السابع: أن يكون في مهم إن لم يكن على أهع
فقوله: لا يلزمني ذكره؛ أي: في شرع الجدل المبدع؛ وأما في الشرع فهو كاذب
فاسق.

قال الحسن: الفقيه هو القائم ليله؛ الصائم نهاره؛ الزاهد في الدنياء يداري ولاه
يماري؛ بنشر الحكمة لله؛ فإن قبلت منه حمد الله وإن ردت عليه حمد الله. وقبل
المالك: الرجل له علم بالسنة يجادل عليهاء قال: لاء ولكن ليخبر بالسنة فإن قبل منه
وإلا سكت؛ وقال أيضًا: ليس هذا الجدل من الدين في شي

وفي الصحيح على ما ذكره الترمذي: أن رسول اله و قال: “ما ضل قوم بعد
هدى كانوا عليه إلا أوتوا الجدل”9.

قال في "الاحياء': الحى هو الدعوة إلى السنة. ومن السنة ترك الجدل في
الدعوة إلى السنة. ومته أيضًاء ينبغي أن يحرس المرء سمعه عن علم الجدل والكلام
غاية الحراسة؛ فإنما يشوشه الجدل؛ ويفسد أكثر مما يصلح؛ والمشاهدة تكفيك في
هنا بياناء فناهيك بالعيان برهاناء وليس عند المتكلم من الدين إلا العقيدة التي
يشارك فيها العوام؛ وإتما يشميز عنهم بصنعة المجادلة.

وأما معرفة لله سبحانه فلا تحصل من علم الكلام؛ بل يكاد الكلام يكون
حجابًا عنها ومانمًا منها. نجد عقيدة المتكلمين والمجادلين كخيط مرسل في الهواء
تهزه الرباح مرة هكذا ومرة هكذاء وعقيدة أهل التقوى من عوام الناس كالطود
الشامخ لا تحركه الدواهي.

ومنه أيضًا: واقبل هذه النصيحة ممن ضيع العمر في ذلك زماناء وزاد على
الأولين تصتيفًا وت ثم ألهمه الله رشده: وأطلعه على عيبه فهجره
ولا يغرنك قول من يقول: الفتوى عماد الشرع؛ ولا تعرف علله إلا بعلم الخلافه
فإن علل المذهب مذكورة في المذهب. والزيادة عليها مجادلة لم يعرفها الصحابة
والأولون: ومع أنها غير مفيدة في المذهب فهي أيضًا ضارة مفسدة لذوق الفقيه
فإن الذي يشهد له حدس المفتي إذا صح ذوقه في الفقه لا يمكن تمشيته على
شروط الجدل في أكثر الأمرء فمن ألف طبعه رسوم الجدل أذعن ذهنه لمقتضيات
الجدل؛ وجبن عن الإذعان لذوق الفقه. ثم قال: فكن من شياطين الجن في أمانء.

منهج الترقي/ المقام السابع: أن يكوذ في مهم إن لم يكن على أصم. فنك
واحترس من شياطين الانس؛ فإنهم أراحوا شياطين الجن من التعب في الإغواء
والإضلال. اه

ونحو هذا قال في “الموافقات” في القضايا الشرعية: إن علم المنطق فيها

المعلم في قوله 9: "كل مسكر خمر”

إلا أنه في "الإحياء' بعد ذمه الكلام. وأن من السنة ترك الجدل في الدعوة إلى

من قائم يقوم به يدفع به شبه المعتزلة:

وقال ابن العربي: لم يحتج إلى ذلك ناصر السنة أبو الحسن الأشعري وقد
غلب المبتدعة الذي قيل: إنه يحتاج إلى علم الكلام لنضالهم. ونحو هذا أيضًا هو
كلام القاضي أبو الوليد الباجي: نهى أيضًا عن قراءة المنطق. وقال القرافي في
المنطق: مستغنى عنه يصفاء العقل.

وقال عياض: قيل لابن وهب: صنف فلان في الرد على الجهمية: قال: رد
عليهم بالكتاب والسنة؟ فقالوا: لاء بل بالمعقول؛ فقال: أخطأ؛ رد بدعة ببدعة.

قال في "الإحياء”: وممن ذهب إلى أن علم الكلام والجدل بدعة وحرام؛ وأن
العبد لن يلق الله بكل ذتب سوى الشرك؛ خير من أن يلقاه بالكلام؛ الشافعي ومالك
وأحمد بن حنبل وجميع أهل الحديث من السلف: قال الشافعي: سمعت من حفص
كلاما لا أقدر أن أحكيه؛ وسثل مرة عن شيء من الكلام ففضب: وقال: سل عن
هذا حفص القرد وأصحابه أخزاهم الل وقال: إذا سمعتم الرجل يقول: الاسم هو
المسمى أو غير المسمى. فاشهدوا أنه من أهل الكلام ولا دين له» وقال أحمد بن
حنبل: علماء الكلام زثادقة وهجر المحاسبي مع زهده وورعه! لكونه صنف في
الرد عليهم؛ قال له: ويحك؛ ألست تحكي بدعتهم أولا؟؛ وقال: لا ينظر في الكلام
إلا من في قلبه دغل؛ ولا يفلح صاحب الكلام أبدا.

# PageV1P174
anchors:
- Root: ج-د-ل (j-d-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To twist, intertwine, or braid tightly; hence disputation as the intricate weaving of opposing arguments.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the Qur'an, jadal denotes contentious argumentation against truth, often censured (e.g., {«وَهُوَ أَلَدُّ الْخِصَامِ»} — "and he is most contentious in dispute," al-Baqarah 2:204).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is physical plaiting; metaphorically, it is specious argumentation that entangles truth with falsehood.
- Root: ك-ل-م (k-l-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Speech, wounding; kalām as "speech" about divine matters.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for scholastic theology — discourse on divine attributes and acts, which the Salaf treated as a novel innovation (bidʿah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal "speech"; metaphorically, the discipline that substitutes rational speculation for revealed texts.
- Root: ف-ت-و-ى (f-t-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Clarifying a legal ruling (fatwā) by one qualified (muftī).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Authoritative legal response derived from revealed sources, not from dialectical reasoning.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal "youthfulness" (fatā) — hence the fresh, direct clarity of a ruling; metaphorically, the unmediated application of scripture.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ) — "If it is accepted from him, he praises God; if rejected, he praises God" (fa-in qubila minhu ḥamida Allāh...). The protasis (sharṭ) governs the apodosis (jawāb) with fa-, indicating a balanced, non-contingent response in both outcomes.
translation:
I say — and this is the seventh station of ascent: that the seeker be in a state of importance, even if not upon the most solid foundation.

For his saying — "I am not obliged to mention it" — means: within the innovated discipline of disputation (jadal); but as for the Sacred Law (sharʿ), he is a liar and a transgressor.

Al-Ḥasan said: "The jurist (faqīh) is he who stands in prayer by night, fasts by day, and is ascetic in this world; he conciliates and does not dispute; he disseminates wisdom for God's sake — if it is accepted from him, he praises God, and if it is rejected from him, he praises God."

And it was said to Mālik: "A man has knowledge of the Sunnah and disputes on its behalf." He replied: "No — rather, he should convey the Sunnah; if it is accepted from him, then [well and good], otherwise he remains silent." He also said: "This disputation is not part of religion in any way."

In the Ṣaḥīḥ, as al-Tirmidhī reported, the Messenger of God ﷺ said: {«ما ضل قوم بعد هدى كانوا عليه إلا أوتوا الجدل»} — "No people went astray after having been upon guidance, except that they were given disputation."

He said in the Iḥyāʾ: "The truth (al-ḥaqq) is the call to the Sunnah. And from the Sunnah is the abandonment of disputation in the call to the Sunnah." And from this also: a man ought to guard his hearing from the science of disputation and scholastic theology (kalām) with the utmost vigilance — for disputation only confuses him, corrupting more than it rectifies. Direct observation (mushāhadah) suffices you here as demonstration; and how excellent is ocular proof as an argument! The theologian possesses nothing of religion except the creed (ʿaqīdah) which he shares with the common folk; he is distinguished from them only by the craft of argumentation.

As for knowledge of God — exalted is He — it is not obtained from the science of scholastic theology; rather, theology nearly becomes a veil over it and a barrier from it. We find the creed of the theologians and disputants like a loose thread cast in the air, which the winds shake — now this way, now that. But the creed of the God-fearing among the common folk is like a towering mountain, which calamities do not move.

And from this also: accept this counsel from one who wasted his lifetime in that [pursuit] for a long period, exceeding the earlier ones in authorship and compilation — then God inspired him with right guidance, showed him its defect, and he abandoned it.

Let not the saying of those who claim — "The legal ruling (fatwā) is the pillar of the Sacred Law, and its underlying causes cannot be known except through the science of disagreement (ʿilm al-khilāf)" — deceive you. For the underlying causes of the school (madhhab) are mentioned within the school itself. Any addition to them is mere disputation, unknown to the Companions and the early generations (al-awwalūn). And although it is useless for the school, it is also harmful, corrupting the jurist's discernment (dhawq). For that which the muftī's intuition (ḥads) attests, when his discernment in jurisprudence is sound, cannot in most cases be made to conform to the conditions of disputation. Thus, whoever habituates his nature to the formalities of disputation, his mind submits to the requirements of disputation and shrinks from submitting to the discernment of jurisprudence.

Then he said: "So be in safety from the devils of the jinn — and beware of the devils of mankind, for they have relieved the jinn-devils of the toil of seduction and misguidance." End quote.

Similar to this is what he said in al-Muwāfaqāt concerning legal matters: that the science of logic (manṭiq) therein is contrary [to the Law], because the Sacred Law was only established upon the unlettered prophetic law (al-sharīʿah al-ummiyyah). Then he mentioned the words of al-Māzarī in al-Muʿallim regarding his saying ﷺ: {«كل مسكر خمر»} — "Every intoxicant is wine."

However, in the Iḥyāʾ, after censuring scholastic theology and [affirming] that from the Sunnah is the abandonment of disputation in the call to the Sunnah, he said: "And logic — which is the investigation of the aspect of evidence and its conditions, and the aspect of definition and its conditions — is included within the science of scholastic theology; and all of that is among the innovations (bidaʿ). But innovations have occurred, so it is right that there be one who rises to repel the doubts of the Muʿtazilah."

Ibn al-ʿArabī said: "The supporter of the Sunnah, Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ashʿarī, had no need of that [logic], and he overcame the innovators of whom it was said that the science of scholastic theology was needed to combat them." Similar to this also is the statement of the Qāḍī Abū al-Walīd al-Bājī: he likewise forbade the study of logic. And al-Qarāfī said concerning logic: "It is dispensable, given the purity of the intellect."

And ʿIyāḍ said: It was said to Ibn Wahb: "So-and-so has authored a refutation of the Jahmiyyah." He said: "Did he refute them with the Book and the Sunnah?" They said: "No, rather with rational argument." He said: "He erred; he has repelled an innovation with an innovation."

He said in the Iḥyāʾ: "Among those who held that the science of scholastic theology and disputation is an innovation and forbidden — and that a servant will not meet God with any sin other than polytheism (shirk) that is worse than meeting Him with theology — are al-Shāfiʿī, Mālik, Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, and all the people of ḥadīth among the Salaf." Al-Shāfiʿī said: "I heard from Ḥafṣ speech that I am unable to relate." And he was once asked about something of theology, and he became angry, saying: "Ask about this Ḥafṣ the ape and his companions — may God disgrace them!" And he said: "If you hear a man saying 'the name is the named' or 'other than the named,' then bear witness that he is among the people of theology and has no religion."

And Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal said: "The theologians are heretics (zanādiqah)." And he censured al-Muḥāsibī, despite his asceticism and piety, for having authored refutations against them. He said to him: "Woe to you! Do you not first relate their innovation [in your refutations]?" And he said: "None looks into theology except one in whose heart is a disease; and the practitioner of theology never prospers."

وعرف ابن خلكان بمحمد بن يونس من الشافعية» فال: وكان يتهم في دينه؟
الكون العلوم العقلية غالبة عليه أنشد العماد'":

وعاطيته صهباء من فيه مزجها كرقة شعري أو كدين ابن يونس

قيل: أحكام العقل ثلاثة: واجب ومستحيل وجائز؛ ومن القسم الجائز عقا أن
يبعث الله الرسل إلى الخلق وأن الله تعالى قادر على ذلك وعلى تعريف صدقهم
بالمعجزات. ثم يصل المرء إلى أن هذا الجائز المذكور قد وقع؛ فعند هذا يتقطع
الكلام وينتهي تصرف العقل.

ومن "الإحياء": يكفيك من منفعة العقل أن يهديك إلى صدق النبي يك: فاعزل
العقل بعد ذلك عن التصرف» ولازم الاتباع؛ فلا تسلم إلاابه؛ والسلام. قال في
"الإحياء”: الإسلام يصح بمجرد التقليد من غير بحث ولا برهان؛ إذ لو مات عقب
تصديقه مات مطيعا لله وعبارة عز الدين: النظر في الأوصاف الإلهية لا يجب على
المكلفين إلا أن يكونوا شاكين: وقال في "التمهيد”” في حديث: "لثن قدر الله
على...": قول المتقدمين من العلماء ومن سلك طريقهم أن هذا رجل جهل بعض
الصفات؛ وهي القدرة» وليس هذا بكافر؛ إنما الكافر من عائد الحق لا من جهله»
ألا ترى أن عمر رضي الله عنه وجماعة من الصحابة سألوا رسول الله يل عمن القدر
وما سألوا حتى جهلوا.

.ولما ذكر في "المقدمات" فصلا في وحدانية لله تعالى سبحاته؛ قال: فهذه
عشر صفات من صفات ذاته تعالى تدرك من جهة العقل ومن جهة السمع. وسثل
عز الدين عن العامي: هل يجوز له التقليد في مسائل الاعتقاد؟ فأجاب: يكفي من
العامة التصميم على الاعتقاد المستقيم؛ لأن رسول اله ل حكم بإسلام الأعراب
والعامة. مع القطع أنهم لم يقفوا على الدلائل المتصوبة لذذلك: قال ابن الأبي: تسب
عياض عدم الكفاية بالتقليد في الاعتقاد للجهالة؛ ومذهب الأشعري أن الإيمان لا
يكفي فيه التقليد؛ وهو مذهب أكثر المتكلمين والمتأخرين؛ واخشاره الآمدي

# PageV1P175
anchors:
- Root: ع-ق-ل (ʿ-q-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The faculty of reason, intellect; binding and restraining (as a camel is hobbled).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The rational faculty that perceives necessary, impossible, and contingent truths; its scope is limited to the created order.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — the intellect's binding power; metaphorical (majāz) — its role as a guide, not an independent judge in revelation.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Resultative Construction (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb) — The clause "if he died after his affirmation" (law māta ʿaqiba taṣdīqihi) governs the apodosis "he would die obedient to God" (māta muṭīʿan), showing the legal consequence of immediate faith.
translation:
I say — and success is with God:

The seventh station of the path of ascent (manhaj al-taraqqī): that one be occupied with what is important, if not with what is more important.

Ibn Khallikān mentioned Muḥammad ibn Yūnus among the Shāfiʿīs, saying: "He was accused regarding his religion, for the rational sciences dominated him." Al-ʿImād recited:

*"And I gave him a tawny wine whose mixture was — like the delicacy of my poetry, or like the religion of Ibn Yūnus."*

It is said: The judgments of the intellect are three: the necessary (wājib), the impossible (mustaḥīl), and the contingent (jāʾiz). From the contingent category, rationally, is that God sends messengers to creation, and that God — exalted is He — is powerful over that and over making their truth known through miracles. Then one arrives at the point that this aforementioned contingent has indeed occurred; at that point, discourse ceases and the intellect's operation comes to an end.

From the "Iḥyāʾ" (of al-Ghazālī): "It suffices you, from the benefit of the intellect, that it guides you to the truthfulness of the Prophet ﷺ. So set the intellect aside after that from operation, and adhere to following (ittibāʿ); do not surrender except to him — and peace." He said in the "Iḥyāʾ": "Islam is valid by mere taqlīd (uncritical acceptance), without investigation or proof; for if one died immediately after his affirmation, he would die obedient to God."

The expression of ʿIzz al-Dīn (ibn ʿAbd al-Salām): "Reflection upon the divine attributes is not obligatory upon the legally responsible (mukallafūn), unless they are in doubt."

And he said in the "Tamhīd" regarding the ḥadīth: "If God had decreed upon..." — the saying of the early scholars and those who follow their path is that this man was ignorant of some attributes, namely, the attribute of power (qudra); and this is not unbelief (kufr). Rather, the unbeliever is only the one who rejects the truth, not the one who is ignorant of it. Do you not see that ʿUmar — may God be pleased with him — and a group of the Companions asked the Messenger of God ﷺ about the decree (qadar), and they did not ask until they were ignorant of it?

And when he mentioned in the "Muqaddimāt" a chapter on the Oneness of God — exalted is His glory — he said: "These are ten attributes of His essence — exalted is He — known by way of the intellect and by way of revelation (samʿ)."

And ʿIzz al-Dīn was asked about the commoner (ʿāmmī): "Is it permissible for him to practice taqlīd in matters of belief?" He answered: "It suffices for the common people the firm resolve upon correct belief, because the Messenger of God ﷺ judged the Bedouins and the common people to be Muslims, with the certainty that they had not stood upon the evidences established for that."

Ibn al-ʿArabī said: "The attribution of insufficiency to taqlīd in belief is due to ignorance." The school of al-Ashʿarī is that faith (īmān) is not sufficient with taqlīd; and this is the school of most of the theologians (mutakallimūn) and the later scholars. Al-Āmidī chose it.

title_en: The Method of Ascent — Station Seven: On the Impermissibility of Taqlīd in Matters of Creed

### | الصفحة 175

منهج الترقي المقام السابع: أن يكوذ في مهم إن لم يكن على أضم. فنك

وانظر "تفسير الفرطبي” آخر سورة (الأعراف)؛ شنع على من قال: لا ينفع
التقليد. واستدل بكلام ابن رشد في 'المقدمات". وانظر الصغير يرى الحية يريد مد
يده إليهاء فيلتفت إلى أبيه؛ فيراه قد ارتعدت فرائصه منها؛ وهو يحتال في الهرب
منهاء فإن الصبي يصير مثله؛ خوف الأب عن بصيرة والابن عن تقليد. ونققل
الجوزي بستده إلى ابن عقيل قال لبعض أصحابه: أنا أقطع أن الصحابة ماتوا وما
عرفوا الجوهر ولا العرض: فإن رضيت أن تكون مثلهم فكن؛ وإن رأيت طريق
المتكلمين أولى فبئس ما رأيت. قال مالك: أرأيت إن جاءه من هو أجدل منه؛ أدع.
دينه كل يوم لدين جديد؟ وهذا المعنى عن مالك كثير؛ كقوله للمرجي الذي قال له:
والله ما أريد إلا الحقء قال له مالك: فإن غلبتني قال: تتبعني؛ قال: فإن غلبتك
اتبعنك؛ قال: فإن جاء ثالث فغلبناء فال ل: اتبعناءء فال له مالك: يا هذاء بعث الله
محمدًا يق بدين واحد وأراك تنتقل. وقال لآخر: أنا على بينة من ربي؛ اذهب إلى
من هو يشك مثلك. وقال سحنون: من العلم بالله الجهل بما لم يخبر به ععن نفسه.
ومن "التمهيد" بسنده: لو كشف الغطاء لعلمت القدرية أن الله ليس بظلام للعبيد.
وكره مالك أن نتحدث بالأحاديث التي فيها حدًا وصفة من وجه أو يد وقبض يد أو
بسطها واستواء وكلام؛ وليقل بما قال الله ولينته إليه ولا يعدوه؛ ولا يفسره: ولاه
يقل: كيف. فإن ذلك الهلاك لأن الله كلف عباده الإيمان بالتتزيل: ولم يكلقهم
الخوض في التأويل. ومن "الإحياء' في حديث: "البناء والييان شعبتان من شعب
النفاق...”7, قال: لأنه المبالغة في الإيضاح؛ فإذا أجملت بادرت القلوب إلى
القبول ولم تضطرب. وانظر الشيء يذكر بالشيء؛ حكى ابن الفخار عن ابن الشاط
أنه كان إذا مر نحو

وهصزأناقتحلدممدر نس سلا

الايسان (133/6؛ رقم 7706)» والديلمي (151/2: رقم 2767. قال المناوي (428/3©: قال

# PageV1P176
anchors:
- Root: ق-ل-د (q-l-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To adorn with a necklace (qilādah); to place a rope around the neck of a sacrificial animal — hence, to follow blindly, as one leads an animal by its halter.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Taqlīd in theological discourse denotes accepting a doctrine without evidence (dalīl) or intellectual comprehension — a blameworthy submission of the rational faculty.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is physical binding; metaphorical sense is the binding of the mind to another's authority without verification.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional construction (sharṭ) with jumlatan fī maḥalli jazāʾ — the protasis "in lam yakun ʿalā aḍamm" governs the apodosis, indicating a hypothetical warning against deficient certainty.
translation:
I say — and success is from Allah:

The seventh station of the method of ascent: that one be in a state of deficiency if not upon firm certainty (yaqīn). So reflect.

And consult the Tafsīr of al-Qurṭubī at the end of Sūrat al-Aʿrāf; he censured severely the one who said: "Taqlīd is of no benefit." And he adduced as evidence the words of Ibn Rushd in al-Muqaddimāt. And observe the example: a young child sees a snake and wishes to extend his hand toward it, but he turns to his father — and behold, he sees his father's limbs trembling in terror of it, while the father is contriving to flee from it. Then the child becomes like his father — the father's fear arises from insight (baṣīrah), while the son's arises from taqlīd.

And Ibn al-Jawzī transmitted with his chain to Ibn ʿAqīl, who said to some of his companions: "I affirm with certainty that the Companions died without having known the substance (jawhar) nor the accident (ʿaraḍ). If you are content to be like them, then be so. But if you deem the path of the mutakallimūn superior, then evil is what you have deemed."

Mālik said: "Do you think — if one more argumentative than him should come to him, would he abandon his religion every day for a new religion?" And this meaning from Mālik is abundant; as his saying to the Murjiʾī who said to him: "By Allah, I desire nothing but the truth." Mālik said to him: "If you overcome me?" He said: "You follow me." He said: "And if I overcome you?" He said: "I follow you." He said: "And if a third comes and overcomes us both?" He said: "We follow him." Then Mālik said to him: "O this man! Allah sent Muḥammad with a single religion, and I see you shifting from one to another."

And he said to another: "I am upon clear proof (bayyinah) from my Lord; go to one who is in doubt like yourself."

And Saḥnūn said: "Part of knowledge of Allah is ignorance of what He has not reported concerning Himself."

And from al-Tamhīd with its chain: "Were the veil lifted, the Qadariyyah would know that Allah is not unjust to His servants."

And Mālik disapproved that we narrate the aḥādīth which contain ḥadd (limit) and ṣifah (attribute) — whether of a face (wajh), or a hand (yad), or the grasping of a hand (qabḍ yad), or its spreading (basṭuhā), or istiwāʾ (establishment upon the Throne), or speech (kalām). Rather, one should affirm what Allah has said, and stop at it, and not transgress beyond it; nor interpret it (tafsīr); nor say "how?" (kayf). For that is destruction — because Allah has charged His servants with faith in the revelation (tanzīl), and has not charged them with plunging into interpretation (taʾwīl).

And from al-Iḥyāʾ regarding the ḥadīth: "The builder and the explainer are two branches of hypocrisy..." — he said: This is because of excessive elaboration in clarification (īḍāḥ); so when one is concise (ajmala), hearts hasten to acceptance and do not become agitated.

And observe how one thing is recalled by another: Ibn al-Fakhkhār narrated from Ibn al-Shāṭṭ that when he passed by grammar... [text breaks off]

30 منج توفي العقام الع الذيكو في مهم إن ل يكن على امم

يقول: في أي وقت انكسرت الفدر في زمن الصحة أم في زمن الكسر أم في
زمن بين الزمانين؟ وقال يحيى بن معين: صدق بحديث التنزل: ولا تصفه. قال
الترمذي في حديث: "يمين الله ملتى”: هذا حديث صحيح يؤمن به كما جاء ولا
يفسرء قاله مالك والثوري وابن المبارك. ومن "التمهيد”: قد عقلنا وأدركنا بحواسنا
أن لنا أرواحًا في أبداتنا ولا نعلم كيف ذلك؛ فليس جهلنا بكيفية ربنا على عرشه
يوجب له أنه ليس على عرشه.

وقد قال مالك للذي سأله عن ذلك: السؤال عن هذا بدعة؛ وإنك امرؤ سوه
أخرجوه؛ فأخذوا بضبعيه قأخرجوه. ورأيت كلاثما معزوا لعز الدين على الأثر
الوارد: من عرف نفسه عرف ريه قال: ظهر لي من سر هذا الحديث ما يجب كشفه
ويستحسن وصفه؛ وهو أن الله سبحانه وتعالى وضع هذه الروح الروحانية في هذه
الجئة الجسمانية؛ لطيفة لاهوتية مودعة في كثيفة ناسوتية دالة على وحداتيته

وربانيته؛ ووجه الاستدلال من عشرة أوجه:

الأول: أن هذا الهيكل الإنساني لما كان يفتقر إلى مدبر وإلى محرك وهذه
الروح تدبره وتحركه علمنا أن هذا العالم لا بد له من مدير ومحرك.

: لما كان مدبر الجسد واحدًا وهو الروح علمنا أن مدبر هذا العالم واحد

لاشريك له في تدييره» نينس4 [الأنياء: 22]. هث كن
مده 4 [الإسراء: 42] الآية. هوَمَا كات مَمَهنَِلو 4 [المؤمنون: 91].

الثالث: لما كان هذا الجسد لا يتحرك إلا بإرادة الروح ويتحريكها له علمنا أن
لله مريد لما هو كائن في كونه لا تتحرك ذرة إلا يإذنه.

الرابع: لما كان لا يتحرك في الجسد شيء إلا بعلم الروح وشعوره به لا
يخفى عن الروح من حركات الجسد وسكناته شي»: علمنا أن الله سبحانه لا يعزب
عن علمه سبحانه مثقال ذرة في الأرض ولا في السماء.

الخامس: لما كان هذا الجسد لم يكن فيه شيء أقرب إلى الروح من شيء»
علمنا أنه قريب إلى كل شيء

السادس: لما كان الروح موجودًا قبل وجود الجسد ويكون موجوًا يعدي

# PageV1P177

### | الصفحة 177

منهج الترقي المقام السابع: أن يكوذ في مهم إن لم يكن على أصم. لنت
علمنا أله سبحائه موجود قبل كون خلقه ويكون موجوا بعد فناء خلقه ما زال ولا
يزال وتقدس عن الزوال.

السابع: لما كان الروح في الجسد لا يعرف له كيفية؛ علمنا أنه مقدس عن
الكيفية.

الثامن: لما كان الروح في الجسد لا يعلم له أبنية؛ علمنا أنه مقدس عن الأبنية
والكيفية؛ فلا يوصف بأين ولا كيفء بل الروح موجودة في سائر الجسد ما خلا
منها موضع من الجسدء وكذلك الح سبحانه موجود في كل مكان ما خلا منه
مكان» وتنزه عن المكان والزمان.

التاسع: لما كان الروح في الجسد لا يخفى ولا يحس ولا يجس ولا يمس»
علمنا أن الله سبحانه منزه عن الحس والجس واللمس.

العاشر: لما كان الروح في الجسد لا يدرك بالبصر ولا يمثل بالصورء علمنا أن
الله سبحانه لا يمثل بالصورء وليس كمثله شيء. وفي هذا الحديث تفسير آخر؛ وهو
أن تعرف أن صفات نفسك على ضد صفات ربك. من عرف نفسه بالعيودية عرف
ربه بالربوبية؛ ومن عرف نفسه بالفناء عرف ريه بالبقاء؛ وكما أنه لا سبيل لك إلى
معرفتك إياك كذاك بالنسبة إلى مولاك”""

قل لمن يفهم عني ما أقول قصر القول فذا شرح يطول

ام سر غامض من دونه ضربت والله أعناق الفحول

ف إياك ولا تدري من أنت ولا كيف الوصول

تنس لاتمسية
:

الاتندري صقات ركست فيك حارت في خفاياها العقول
أن منك الروح في جوهرها هل تراها كيف تسري وتجول

أين سك القلب في قالبه وهو بيت الرب حقاإذيقول

هذه الأتقاس هل تحصرها لا ولاتدري متى عنك تزول
