# PageV1P178
anchors:
- Root: ع-ر-ف (ʿ-r-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Knowledge through experience and discernment (maʿrifah) as opposed to mere cognition (ʿilm); intimate acquaintance.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Gnostic recognition of the soul's contingency leading to affirmation of the Necessary Being.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: knowing one's own created nature; Metaphorical: analogical inference (qiyās) from the microcosm to the macrocosm.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Resultative Construction (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — "man ʿarafa... fa-qad ʿarafa" establishes a causal nexus between self-knowledge and divine knowledge.
translation:
I say: At whatever time the vessel (al-qidr) broke — was it during the time of health, or during the time of breaking, or during a time between the two times? And Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn said: "Affirm the hadith of descent (al-tanazzul) as true, but do not describe it." Al-Tirmidhī said concerning the hadith "The right hand of Allah is full": "This is a sound hadith; one believes in it as it came, and it is not interpreted." This was the position of Mālik, al-Thawrī, and Ibn al-Mubārak. And from al-Tamhīd: "We have comprehended and perceived by our senses that we have souls within our bodies, yet we do not know how that is; so our ignorance of the modality (kayfiyyah) of our Lord upon His Throne does not necessitate that He is not upon His Throne."

And Mālik said to the one who asked him about that: "Asking about this is an innovation (bidʿah); and you are an evil man — expel him!" So they seized him by his upper arms and expelled him. And I have seen something attributed to ʿIzz al-Dīn concerning the reported tradition: "He who knows himself knows his Lord." He said: "There has become manifest to me from the secret of this hadith that which must be disclosed and whose description is commendable — namely, that Allah, Glorified and Exalted, placed this spiritual soul (al-rūḥ al-rūḥāniyyah) within this corporeal frame (al-juththah al-jismāniyyah): a subtle divine reality (laṭīfah lāhūtiyyah) deposited within a dense human reality (kathīfah nāsūtiyyah), indicating His Oneness and His Lordship."

The manner of inference (wajh al-istidlāl) is from ten aspects:

**First:** Since this human edifice (al-haykal al-insānī) was in need of a director and a mover, and this soul directs and moves it, we know that this world necessarily has a Director and Mover.

**Second:** Just as the director of the body is one — namely, the soul — we know that the Director of this world is One, having no partner in His governance. {«لَوْ كَانَ فِيهِمَا آلِهَةٌ إِلَّا اللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتَا»} [Al-Anbiyāʾ: 22]. And {«قُلْ لَوْ كَانَ مَعَهُ آلِهَةٌ كَمَا يَقُولُونَ إِذًا لَابْتَغَوْا إِلَىٰ ذِي الْعَرْشِ سَبِيلًا»} [Al-Isrāʾ: 42]. And {«مَا اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ مِنْ وَلَدٍ وَمَا كَانَ مَعَهُ مِنْ إِلَٰهٍ»} [Al-Muʾminūn: 91].

**Third:** Since this body does not move except by the will of the soul and its moving of it, we know that Allah has will (irādah) for whatever occurs in His creation — no atom moves except by His permission.

**Fourth:** Since nothing moves in the body except by the soul's knowledge and awareness of it — nothing of the body's movements and stillnesses is hidden from the soul — we know that Allah, Glorified, nothing escapes His knowledge: not an atom's weight in the earth nor in the heavens.

**Fifth:** Since there is nothing in this body closer to the soul than anything else, we know that He is close to everything.

**Sixth:** Since the soul existed before the existence of the body and will exist after it, we know that He, Glorified, exists before the existence of His creation and will exist after the annihilation of His creation — He has always been and will always be, and He is sanctified above passing away (al-zawāl).

**Seventh:** Since the soul in the body has no known modality (kayfiyyah), we know that He is sanctified above modality.

**Eighth:** Since the soul in the body has no known location (ayniyyah), we know that He is sanctified above location and modality — so He is not described by "where" (ayn) nor "how" (kayf). Rather, the soul exists throughout the entire body, no place of the body being devoid of it; likewise, Allah, Glorified, exists in every place, no place being devoid of Him — yet He is transcendent above place and time.

**Ninth:** Since the soul in the body is not hidden, not sensed, not touched, not felt, we know that Allah, Glorified, is transcendent above sensation, touching, and feeling.

**Tenth:** Since the soul in the body is not perceived by sight nor represented by images, we know that Allah, Glorified, is not represented by images — {«لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ»} [Al-Shūrā: 11]. And in this hadith there is another interpretation: that you know that the attributes of your self are opposite to the attributes of your Lord. He who knows himself by servanthood (al-ʿubūdiyyah) knows his Lord by Lordship (al-rubūbiyyah); and he who knows himself by passing away (al-fanāʾ) knows his Lord by permanence (al-baqāʾ). And just as you have no way to know yourself as you truly are, so likewise with respect to your Master.

---

Say to him who understands my words:  
Speech is shortened, for this explanation is prolonged.

A secret, obscure, beyond which  
— by Allah — the necks of stallions have been broken.

Beware! Do not ask who you are,  
Nor how the arrival [to Him] is.

The attributes of the Lord are woven within you;  
In their hidden depths, intellects are bewildered.

That from you the soul in its essence —  
Do you see how it courses and circulates?

Where is the heart's abode in its mold,  
While it is the house of the Lord — truly, as He says?

These breaths — can you encompass them?  
No, nor do you know when they will depart from you.

# PageV1P180
anchors:
- Root: ه-م-م (h-m-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of "concern, intent, that which occupies the mind" — the station requires the servant to be absorbed in matters of consequence.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological terms, the "concern" (hamm) of the gnostic is the knowledge of Allah's attributes and acts, not speculative inquiry into their modality.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "burdening oneself with a matter"; metaphorically, it denotes the heart's orientation toward the divine, rejecting the metaphorical "how" (kayf) as an innovation.
- Sībawayh Rule: Prohibition and Interrogative Syntax (al-nahy wa al-istifhām) — The verses employ rhetorical questions (e.g., "How do we know?") to negate the possibility of answering, following the pattern of denying the predicate (khabar) about divine attributes.
translation:
I say — may Allah guide us and you: The seventh station of spiritual ascent is that the servant be occupied with what truly concerns him, not with what does not concern him. For if drowsiness overcomes you, tell me, O ignorant one — where is your intellect and understanding? You eat bread without knowing how it passes through you or how you urinate. If your inner thoughts are corrupted by doubts, then such doubts are misguidance. How can we know of Him who is established upon the Throne? Do not say "how" He established Himself, nor "how" He descends. How can He be described or seen — how is seeing? By my life, this is nothing but excess. He is above all "how" — no "how" encompasses Him, and no "how" changes. He is above the above, with no above above Him, and He is in all directions without ceasing. He has a self and attributes and names — exalted is His decree above what I say.

And from the "Risālah" (of al-Qushayrī): Glorified is the One, the Worshipped, before limits and before letters. If you say "where," His existence has already preceded place; if you say "when," His being has already preceded time; if you say "He" (huwa), the letter hā' and wāw are His creation. Whatever is imagined in minds, He is contrary to it. {«لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ»} [al-Shūrā: 11]. And fitting to cite here is the saying of Abū Ḥāmid (al-Ghazālī) at the beginning of the Book of Trust (Kitāb al-Tawakkul) in the "Iḥyā'": He said: One who looked from the niche of Allah's lamp asked the tablet: "Why has your face been blackened, when it was white?" The tablet referred him to the pen; the pen referred him to the right hand of the writer — this is in the world of dominion and witness (ʿālam al-mulk wa al-shahādah). The hand referred him to power (qudrah) — and this is the beginning of the world of divine might (ʿālam al-jabarūt). Power referred him to will (irādah), and will to the tablet of the heart; the heart referred him to the pen — and this is the beginning of the world of sovereignty (ʿālam al-malakūt). Then he says: "O exalted pen, why do you continuously inscribe in hearts such sciences that the will follows to summon power and direct it toward the determined things?" The pen refers him to the right hand, and the right hand refers him to power — and here he deviates; so he is made firm by the firm word. And his saying: {«لَا يُسْأَلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ وَهُمْ يُسْأَلُونَ»} [al-Anbiyā': 23]. Then the awe of the divine presence overwhelmed him. When he recovered, he said: "Glory be to You — expand my breast that I may know You, and loosen the knot from my tongue that I may praise You." Then a caller called from behind the veil: "Do not aspire to praise, and do not exceed the master of the prophets (peace be upon him), who added nothing in this presence beyond saying: 'Glory be to You, I cannot enumerate Your praise; You are as You have praised Yourself.'" Then he says: "Is the heart aspiring to know You?" So it is called: "Beware of stepping over the necks of the ṣiddīqīn; return to the greatest ṣiddīq (Abū Bakr). Have you not heard him say: 'The inability to comprehend comprehension is comprehension itself.'" I have already pointed to the meaning of this narrative — so review it yourself, for it is most excellent.

And from the "Tamhīd" (of Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr), with its chain to al-Qāsim ibn Sallām, who said: When we are asked about the hadiths of the vision (ru'yah), the Throne (kursī), the laughter (of Allah), that Hell will be filled, and similar matters, we do not interpret them, nor do we know anyone who interprets them. He said: The people of the Sunnah are agreed that they pass as they came, without modality (bilā kayf). Mālik said: "Pass them as they came, without modality." And in the hadith: "Allah created Adam, then wiped his back..." — the hadith. Abū ʿUmar (Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr) said: The people of the Sunnah are agreed upon believing in these reports and abandoning disputation concerning them. Then he transmitted with his chain to al-Awzāʿī, who said: "From Allah is the revelation; upon His Messenger is the delivery; and upon us is submission."

And Saḥnūn wrote to ʿAbd al-Malik (ibn al-Mājishūn), mentioning what had occurred among them regarding the Qur'an and the Sunnah, and asking for his answer. So he wrote back: "From ʿAbd al-Malik ibn al-Mājishūn to Saḥnūn ibn Saʿīd — peace of Allah be upon you. I praise Allah to you. To proceed: You have asked about matters that are not the concern of the people of knowledge; knowledge of them is ignorance. Sufficient for you is what has passed of the early part of this ummah — that they followed with excellence and did not delve into any of these matters. The religion has been preserved for the pure virgin in her seclusion — it was not said to her 'how' nor 'where.' So follow as they followed. And know that the greatest knowledge is that a man does not wish to speak of any of these matters, lest he disbelieve and fall into the fire of Hell."

And Abū ʿUmar said: The well-established reports have confirmed the affirmation of the attributes of Allah mentioned in the Qur'an. We affirm them and do not go beyond them, and we entrust their meaning to the Messenger (peace be upon him), and we do not debate concerning them. For {«قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ»} equals a third of the Qur'an.

### | الصفحة 180

3 منهج اتوي لما لسع أن يكون في مهم إن ل يكن على امم
الأن المناظرة لا تسوغ إلا فيما تحته عمل كالزكاة واليوع.

ونقل ابن رشد في "لبان" كلام أبي عمر هذاء مرشها له ومستدا به. ولاين العربي
في الاسم الموفي ماثة؛ بعد أن ذكر أن للجنة ثماتية أبواب؛ قال: وقد تسلط على
هذه الأبواب الخلق» واتسع لهم فيها الخرق وما تكلم أحد منهم عليها بحق»
وأعظمهم خطأ المفسرون؛ وأغواهم بعد ذلك الصوفية. ثم قال: وذلك كله تعد على
القرآن. ثم قال: وطريق الحق أنا ثم بصل العلم إلينا وجه التعديد.

ثم قال: وقد بينا أن الحرز والظن لا يجوز لنا إلا في باب الأحكام؛ التي
المطلوب منها العمل؛ فأما ما خرج من الأحكام فليس للقياس فيه مدخل. وحكى
ابن حبيب أن الأمبر أرسل إلى زياد يسأله عن كفتي الميزان يوم القيامة» فكتب إليه
زياد: حدثني مالك عن ابن شهاب أن رسول اله قال: "من حسن إسلام المرء
أتركه ما لا يعنيه”7'؛ وسترد فتعلم.

ومن “التمهيد" يسنده: أن بعض الأمراء قال لمحمد بن واسع: ما تقول في
القضاء والقدر؟ فقال: أيها الأمير: إن له لا يسأل عباده يوم القيامة عن قضائه
وقدره» وإنما يسألهم عن أعمالهم.

قال أبو عمر: جملة القول إنه سر اله؛ لا يدرك بجدل ولا نظرء ولا تتتفي منه
خصومة ولا احتجاج؛ وقد تظاهرت الآثار في التسليم للقدر والتهي عن الجدل فيه
والاستسلام والإقرار بخيره وشره والعلم بعدل مقدره وحكمته؛ وفي نقض عزائم
الإنسان دليل فيما قلنا وي

وكتب عمر بن عبد العزيز: إن لل لا يطالب خلقه بما قضى عليهم وقدرء
ولكن يطالبهم بما نهاهم عنه وأمرء فطالب نفسك من حيث يطالبك ريك والسلام.

ولما خاض الناس في القدر بالبصرة اجتمع سليمان بسن يسار ورويقع

# PageV1P181
anchors:
- Root: ج-د-ل (j-d-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To twist, intertwine, or braid; hence disputation as the interweaving of opposing arguments.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theological disputation (jadal) concerning matters of the unseen (ghayb) — forbidden when it exceeds the bounds of practical obligation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical intertwining; Metaphorical: contentious debate that entangles truth with falsehood.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional restriction (taqyīd bi-l-sharṭ) — the permissibility of a thing is conditioned upon its domain, as in "lā tasūghu illā fīmā taḥtahu ʿamal" (is not permissible except in what entails action).
translation:
I say: And the third method — that which is followed — is that it is not permissible for one to engage in disputation unless it concerns a matter under which there is practical action, such as alms-tax (zakāh) and sales.

Ibn Rushd has transmitted in his "Lubāb" the words of Abū ʿUmar (Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr), commenting upon them and adducing them as evidence. And Ibn al-ʿArabī, in his book "al-Asnā fī Asmāʾ Allāh al-Ḥusnā" (The Most Exalted in the Beautiful Names of God), after mentioning that Paradise has eight gates, said: "The creatures have dominated these gates, and the breach therein has widened for them; yet none of them has spoken concerning them with truth. The greatest of them in error are the exegetists (mufassirūn), and after them the most misguided are the Sufis." Then he said: "And all of that is an encroachment upon the Qurʾān." Then he said: "And the way of truth is that knowledge of the manner of enumeration does not reach us."

Then he said: "And we have made clear that conjecture (ḥazr) and supposition (ẓann) are not permissible for us except in the chapter of legal rulings (aḥkām) wherein action is sought. As for what falls outside the rulings, there is no entry for analogical reasoning (qiyās) therein."

And Ibn Ḥabīb narrated that a certain commander sent to Ziyād asking him about the two pans of the Scale on the Day of Resurrection. So Ziyād wrote back to him: "Mālik narrated to me from Ibn Shihāb that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: {«From the excellence of a person's Islam is his leaving alone what does not concern him»}." And it will come to you, and you will know.

And from "al-Tamhīd," with its chain of transmission: That a certain commander said to Muḥammad ibn Wāsiʿ: "What do you say concerning the divine decree and predestination (al-qaḍāʾ wa-l-qadar)?" He replied: "O commander! Verily God will not ask His servants on the Day of Resurrection about His decree and His predestination; rather, He will ask them about their deeds."

Abū ʿUmar said: The sum of the matter is that it is a secret of God; it is not grasped by disputation (jadal) nor by rational consideration (naẓar), and neither contention nor argumentation can exhaust it. The traditions (āthār) have concurred upon submission to the decree, upon the prohibition of disputation therein, upon surrender and acknowledgment of its good and its evil, and upon the knowledge of the justice of its Ordainer and His wisdom. And in the frustration of man's resolutions (naqḍ ʿazāʾim al-insān) there is proof of what we have said.

And ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz wrote: "Verily God does not call His creatures to account for what He has decreed and predestined upon them; rather, He calls them to account for what He has forbidden them and commanded them. So hold yourself to account from where your Lord holds you to account. And peace."

And when the people plunged into disputation concerning the decree (qadar) in Basra, Sulaymān ibn Yasār and Rūwayfiʿ gathered together... [text breaks off]

arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 181

منهج الترقي/ المقام السابع: أن يكوذ في مهم إن لم يكن على أصم. نت
أبو العالية: فاتفق رأيهما أنه يكفي المؤمن من هذا الأمر أن يعلم أنه لا يصييه إلا ما
كتب الله له وأئه مجزي بعمله. ونقل أيضًا بسنده إلى ابن عباس قال: إن هذه الآمة
الا يزال أمرها متقاربًا أو مواتيًا أو كلمة تشبهها ما لم يتكلموا في القدر والأطفال.
قال أبو عمر: ما بين رسول اله يك لأحد من أمته حكم الأطفال الذين يموتون
صغازا بان يقطعه مجيته العذر.

وعن ابن عون: كنت عند القاسم بن محمد إذ جاءه رجل فقال له: ما كان بين
قنادة وحفص في الأطفال؟ ققال: تكلم ربيعة في ذلك؛ فقال القاسم: إذا لله انتهى
عند شيء فانتهوا وقفوا عنده. قال: فكأنما كانت نار قأطفات؛ وسثل سفيان عن
أطفال المشركين فصاح: وقال: يا صاحبي؛ أنت تسأل عن مثل هذا.

وقيل لأحمد بن حنبل: أمع الكفار ملائكة يكتبون؟ قال: أي مسألة هذه؟ لا
.ينبغي أن أتكلم في مثل هذاء وكره الجواب. وسئل عن يأجوج ومأجوج أمسلمون؟
فقال للسائل: أحكمت العلم حتى تسأل عن مثل هذا؛ وقد ثبت في الصحيح على
حسب ما ذكره الحاكم وخحرجه أبو داود: أن رسول الله يف قال: "لا أدري أعزير نبي
أم لال"؛ و"ما أدري أذو القرنين نبي أم لا؟”1".

وقال ابن العربي: يبقى النظر في كيفية قبض الروح والنقس وهل هما عرض
أو جسم ومن الحق عليكم أن لا تجعلوا هذا من فرائض معارفكم: ولا من وظائف
عقائدكم؛ وإنما عليكم أن تعلموا أن الأنفس والأرواح موجودة عن عدم مخلوقة»
وأنها باقية لا فناء لها بعد وجودهاء وأنها تتألم دون الجسم؛ كما تتألم وتتتعم معه.

ولما سرد أبو عمر في تمهيده الأقوال في الروح والنفس قال: الله أعلم
بالصحيح من هذه الأقوال؛ إذ لم يدرك قول منها بقياس ولا ورد فيه خبر صحيح

# PageV1P182
anchors:
- Root: ق-د-ر (q-d-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Measure, decree, determination of extent
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine preordination (qadar) as the eternal, exhaustive determination of all events
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: measuring; Metaphorical: God's immutable decree — here, the prohibition of speculative discourse on it
- Root: ر-و-ح (r-w-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Breath, wind, spirit — that which animates
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The spirit (rūḥ) as a created, subtle substance (jism laṭīf) distinct from the body, of which only minimal knowledge is granted
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: air in motion; Metaphorical: the life-principle — in the Qur'anic verse, its nature is withheld from human inquiry
- Root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Self, soul, breath — the principle of individual identity
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The soul (nafs) as the locus of moral responsibility and sensation, created ex nihilo and imperishable
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: breath; Metaphorical: the inner self that feels pleasure and pain
- Sībawayh Rule: Prohibition of speculative interrogation (al-istifhām al-muʿtariḍ) — the rhetorical pattern of rejecting questions that exceed the bounds of transmitted knowledge, as seen in the scholars' refusals.
translation:
I say — may God guide us and you: The path of ascent (manhaj al-taraqqī) — the seventh station: that one remain silent in a matter if one is not upon a firm foundation.

Abū al-ʿĀliyah reported: Their opinion agreed that it suffices the believer in this affair to know that nothing befalls him except what God has written for him, and that he shall be recompensed for his deed. It was also transmitted by his chain to Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "This community shall not cease to have its affair well-ordered, or harmonious — or a word similar to it — so long as they do not speak about divine decree (al-qadar) and [the fate of] infants."

Abū ʿUmar said: There is nothing transmitted from the Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — to anyone of his community concerning the judgment of infants who die young that decisively cuts off the excuse [for speculation].

And from Ibn ʿAwn: I was with al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad when a man came to him and said: "What was between Qatādah and Ḥafṣ concerning infants?" He said: "Rabīʿah spoke about that." Al-Qāsim said: "When God has ended a matter at something, then end [your inquiry] and stop at it." He said: "It was as though a fire had been extinguished." And Sufyān was asked about the infants of the polytheists, and he cried out, saying: "O my companion! You ask about something like this?"

And it was said to Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal: "Are there angels with the disbelievers who write [deeds]?" He said: "What kind of question is this? It is not fitting that I speak about such a thing." And he disliked answering. And he was asked about Gog and Magog (Yaʾjūj wa-Maʾjūj): "Are they Muslims?" He said to the questioner: "Have you mastered knowledge until you ask about something like this?" And it is established in the Ṣaḥīḥ — according to what al-Ḥākim mentioned and Abū Dāwūd extracted — that the Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — said: "I do not know whether ʿUzayr was a prophet or not," and "I do not know whether Dhū al-Qarnayn was a prophet or not."

And Ibn al-ʿArabī said: There remains the consideration of how the spirit (rūḥ) and the soul (nafs) are seized, and whether they are an accident (ʿaraḍ) or a body (jism). It is incumbent upon you not to make this among the obligatory duties of your cognitions, nor among the functions of your creeds. Rather, it is incumbent upon you to know that the souls and spirits are existent after non-existence, created, and that they are enduring, having no annihilation after their existence, and that they suffer pain apart from the body, just as they suffer and delight with it.

And when Abū ʿUmar, in his Tamhīd, enumerated the sayings concerning the spirit and the soul, he said: God knows best which of these sayings is correct; for no saying among them has been attained by analogy, nor has any sound report (khabar ṣaḥīḥ) come concerning it that cuts off the excuse and necessitates the proof. God — exalted is He — said: {«Say: The spirit is of the command of my Lord, and you have not been given of knowledge except a little»} [al-Isrāʾ 17:85]. So how can one undertake the knowledge of a thing that God has reserved exclusively to Himself, and has not disclosed to His Prophet — may God bless him and grant him peace? And the Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — said: "Adam and Moses argued." Ibn al-ʿArabī said: The correct [understanding] is that only their spirits met; and the knowledge of that...

# PageV1P183
anchors:
- Root: ك-ل-ف (k-l-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To burden, impose a task involving hardship; taklīf = religious obligation entailing effort.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Taklīf is that which exceeds ordinary capacity but remains within the bounds of what the Lawgiver may command; here, it denotes the impossibility of being charged with comprehending modality.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Ḥaqīqah — the literal sense of "not being burdened" refers to legal obligation; majāz would be impossible here, as no metaphorical extension applies to divine commands.
- Root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Firm truthfulness; taṣdīq = affirming as true without alteration.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In kalām, taṣdīq is the intellectual assent to prophetic reports, distinct from taṣawwur (conceptualization); it requires no modality comprehension.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — the heart's verification; metaphorical — none, as it is a technical term.
- Root: ق-ي-س (q-y-s)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Measuring, comparing; qiyās = analogical reasoning.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Qiyās is valid only in juridical matters (furūʿ), not in matters of the unseen (ghayb) where revelation alone governs.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — measurement; metaphorical — intellectual analogy, which is here negated.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Taʿlīq (Suspension of Judgment) — When a verb of knowledge (ʿalima) is followed by a clause whose predicate is a nominal sentence indicating incapacity, the syntax suspends the object's modality, mirroring the theological suspension of takyīf.
translation:
I say — and this is of the same kind as what cannot be borne in the matter of obligation (taklīf); rather, in it there is only affirmation (taṣdīq). Likewise, Abū ʿUmar said in his commentary on this, and he added: "For we have not been given of this kind of knowledge except a little." {«وَمَا أُوتِيتُم مِّنَ الْعِلْمِ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا»} [Al-Isrāʾ 17:85].

And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I saw ʿĪsā; then I saw the Dajjāl." Ibn al-ʿArabī said in his Masālik: "Your Lord knows best whether this was in sleep, or in sensory existence, or in imaginal existence." And likewise he said regarding his statement: "A qīrāṭ is deducted from his reward" — he said: "The qīrāṭ is a measure known only to Allah."

And he said in the Masālik, responding to a skeptic who objected: "We see sins in Ramaḍān just as they are [committed]." We said to him: "You have lied." And the answer is from several aspects; among them: It is not incumbent upon us to know the meaning of the ḥadīth, nor to interpret all things [by analogy].

And he said regarding the two mixed [liquids]: "I have not known any basis for the prohibition of that up to now."

And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The soul of the believer is a bird." Abū ʿUmar said: "This is not a place for speculative inquiry (naẓar) nor for analogy (qiyās); for analogy is only [valid] in what permits ijtihād, and ijtihād does not enter into this chapter. Rather, one submits therein, due to the soundness of the report from the one to whom submission is obligatory."

And he said regarding his statement ﷺ: "The caller to prayer is heard as far as the extent of his voice" — "I do not know how this is." And he said regarding His statement: {«وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الرُّوحِ ۖ قُلِ الرُّوحُ مِنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّي»} [Al-Isrāʾ 17:85] — "And likewise he said regarding the ḥadīth: 'The devil ties a knot on the crown of one of you [when he sleeps]...' — Allah knows best how that is; and no one can attain the reality of this." And likewise he said regarding the eating and drinking of the devils: "This cannot be grasped by reason nor by analogy." And he said: "He sent down..."

# PageV1P184
anchors:
- Root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Descent, sending down; used for revelation (tanzīl) and for settling in a place.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The descent of divine speech to the prophetic heart; also the graded revelation of the Qur'an.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical descent; metaphorical for the transmission of divine command.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-sharṭ) — The phrase "in matters wherein no definitive text exists" governs the apodosis, indicating a general principle of legal-theological methodology.
translation:
I say — may Allah guide us and you: The seventh station of the methodology of elevation is that one should be [careful] in matters wherein no definitive text exists.

Know that the Qur'an was revealed upon seven readings (aḥruf). Ibn al-ʿArabī said: "The dispute over the meaning of this has been prolonged among the scholars, and there is nothing decisive in it. The upshot, despite the magnitude of the disagreement, is the abrogation of all readings except those established in the muṣḥaf. And whatever was permitted before that has been lifted and gone."

Al-Zuhrī said concerning the hadith: "The fornicator does not fornicate while he is a believer" — they commanded these hadiths just as those before you were commanded with them, for the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded them.

Ibn al-ʿArabī said: "It is not the intent to seek the distinction between the poor man (faqīr) and the destitute (miskīn); so do not waste your time in these meanings — like the discussion of the difference between the poor and the rich, which of them is more virtuous. For the verification therein is little, and the speech about it is wearisome when it is without attainment."

Al-Qushayrī transmitted in his Epistle (Risālah): "Tomorrow neither poverty nor wealth will be weighed; rather, gratitude will be weighed with patience. So come, let us be patient and grateful."

Abū ʿUmar said likewise concerning the hadith: "No harm and no reciprocating harm" — two expressions with one meaning. And he said likewise concerning: "Do not spy, do not seek out faults, do not cut off relations, do not turn away from one another, and do not hate one another" — he said: "The meaning of these expressions is interpenetrating and converging, like a single meaning, in urging mutual affection and love."

Ibn al-ʿArabī said concerning the meaning of kalālah (one who dies without ascendant or descendant): "There are six opinions." Then he said, verbatim: "Leave us from the multiplicity of sayings and the disagreement of the people of language — for the tongue of the Arabs is vast, and the meaning of the Qur'an is apparent: that kalālah is one who has lost his father and his son, then dies."

And ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib — may Allah be pleased with him — said to the one who asked him about: {«By the scatterers scattering»} [al-Dhāriyāt: 1]...

title_en: Section 140 — On the Seventh Station: Concerning What Is Important When Not Upon a Nation

الفاكهة: فما الآب؟ ثم قال: نهينا عن التكلف. وقال ابن العربي: ما كنا لنشتغل

# PageV1P185

### | الصفحة 185

منهج الترفي/ المقام السايع: أن يكون في مهم إن لم يكن على مم فنف
وأحفظهم لمذهب مالك مع التفنن في سائر العلوم؛ وكان يلحن؛ إذ لم يكن له بصر
بالعربية مع غزارة علمه. وقد تقدم قول الباجي وابن العربي وشهاب الدين: علم
المنطق غير محتاج إلييه. وقول الشافعي: إذا مسمعتم الرجل يقنول: الاسم هبو
المسمى أو غير المسمى فلا دين له. وقد تقدم نقل الجوزي: نقطع أن الصحابة
ماتوا وما عرفوا الجوهر ولا العرض.

وعرف عياض بابسن طالب فقبال: كان من كبار أصحاب سحنون أمر
المقرئ بجامع القيروان أن لا يقرئ إلا بحرف نافع. اه

ولست أقول هذا إلا لمن لم يحصل الأهم؛ وإلا فالعلوم كلها مهمة بعد
تحصيل الأهم بفضل ربي؛ أقول: ككتابي السنن وكشف التقول.

قال في "الإحياء”: لا تستغرق عمرك في واحد من العلوم طالبًا للاستقصاء؛
فإن العلم كثيرء والعمر قصيرء وليست هذه العلوم مطلوبة لعينهاء بل لغيرهاء وكل
ما يطلب لغيره لا نبغي أن يجهد فيه المطلوب. فاقتصر من علم اللغة على ما تفهم
به كلام العرب وثنطق به ومن غريبه على غريب القرآن والحديث؛ ودع التعمق فيه
ومن النحو على ما يتعلق بالكتاب والسنة. انتهى.

وكا

ي أبن سراج رحمه الله برشح هذا ويشنع على من يتعمق في النحو
حتى يستضعف بعض القراءات؛ ويقول رحمه الله: إنما استحدث النحو لكتاب الله
ولسنة نبيه يق ولا يلفظ أحد بأفضل منهماء فهذا الذي يلهج بضعف قراءة أي علم
يفيده هذاء لعله عسى أن يمدح سلطانًا ينزه قريضه أن يلفظ بما يستحل أن يتل به
كتاب الله هذا سوء أدب.

قال عياض: كان ابن التبان من الفقهاء الراسخين في النحوء وقال مع ذلك: ما
أكثر أحد من التحو إلا وحمقه. وقال ابن الصائغ: ذهب الكوفيون إلى أن نصب
تحدثنا في قوله: أما تأتينا فتحددتا؟ بالخلاف؛ لأنهم إذا أرادوا تشريكه مع ما قبله
وموافقته له تبعه في إعرابه. وإذا أرادوا المخالقة نصبوا. فالخلاف عندهم الناصب»
وهو عندهم ناصب في الأسماء. ومنه: لو تركت والأسد لأكلك؛ ونم يرييدوا
تشريك الأسد في الترك؛ فلذلك نصبوا. ومنه نصب الخبر إذا كان ظرفا؛ فاته إذا كان
خبرًا لمبتدأ هو المبتدأ في المعنى ارتفع وإن خالفه اتتصب؛ وتعقبه السيرافي بما لا

# PageV1P186
anchors:
- Root: ه-م-م (h-m-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of "that which concerns, matters, or is of significance"; the primary object of one's care and intention.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological context, denotes that which pertains to one's ultimate welfare (maṣlaḥah) in religion and the Hereafter, as opposed to trivialities.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage refers to actual importance; metaphorical extension applies to prioritizing acts of worship and knowledge that lead to salvation.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Taqdīm wa Taʼkhīr (Fronting and Delaying) — The principle of "al-ahamm fa-al-ahamm" (the most important, then the next most important) governs both syntactic emphasis and practical prioritization in this passage.
translation:
I say: Know that the seventh station of the path of ascent is that one be occupied with what is important — if not upon a nation. ʿUmar recited: {«wa-fākihah wa-abbā»} [ʿAbasa 31], and said: "This is the fruit — so what is the pasture?" Then he said: "We have been forbidden from affectation (takalluf)." Ibn al-ʿArabī said: "We would not occupy ourselves with interpreting 'al-maysir' after God has forbidden it — for what God has forbidden its doing, and we are ignorant of it, we praise God for it."

He said: "And they differed concerning the sacrificed one (al-dhabīḥ); it was said: Isaac, and it was said: Ishmael. And this matter is not among the legal rulings (aḥkām); rather, it is among the sciences whose knowledge is not obligatory." And He, exalted be He, said: {«yas'alūnaka ʿani al-sāʿati ayyāna mursāhā»} [al-Aʿrāf 187]. Then He said: {«fīma anta min dhikrāhā»} [al-Nāziʿāt 43] — that is, the question about the Hour is a question about what does not concern one. It suffices for its knowledge that it shall inevitably come. Therefore, the Prophet ﷺ said to the questioner about the Hour: "What have you prepared for it?" — turning away from his explicit question toward what pertains to it that contains benefit. And he did not answer him concerning what he asked. Similar to this is His saying, exalted be He: {«yas'alūnaka ʿani al-ahillati qul hiya mawāqītu lil-nāsi wa-al-ḥajj»} [al-Baqarah 189] — so the answer came with what pertains to action, turning away from what the questioner intended. Then He said, exalted be He: {«wa-laysa al-birru bi-an ta'tū al-buyūta min ẓuhūrihā wa-lākinna al-birra mani ittaqā»} [al-Baqarah 189]. And righteousness (al-birr) is piety (al-taqwā), not knowledge of these matters that yield no benefit in obligation (taklīf) nor lead to it.

And ʿIyāḍ transmitted from some of them that he said: "One of them speaks in jurisprudence (fiqh), and perhaps if he were asked about the name of Abū Hurayrah, he would not know it." He said: "And Ibn ʿAbdūs used to say to some of his companions: 'Understand this matter, for it is more beneficial than the name of Abū Hurayrah.'"

And Ibn Khallikān related from one of those pointed to in grammar (naḥw) that he used to say: "I do not understand the Introduction of al-Jazūlī — and it does not follow from this that I do not know grammar."

And some of them said: "The known things (maʿlūmāt) are numerous; the lifespan falls short of attaining their aims and ends, and it is too narrow to acquire their demands and goals — with the dominance of languor, the firmness of heedlessness, the inclination of souls toward laziness, and their reliance upon failure. So it is an obligatory duty upon every possessor of intellect and resolve to occupy himself with the most important, then the next most important (al-ahamm fa-al-ahamm)."

ʿIyāḍ defined Ibn Shaʿbān thus: "He was the head of the Mālikī jurists in Egypt in his time, and the most retentive of them for the school of Mālik, with versatility in all the sciences. And he used to commit solecism (laḥn), for he had no insight into Arabic, despite the abundance of his knowledge." And there has already preceded the saying of al-Bājī, Ibn al-ʿArabī, and Shihāb al-Dīn: "The science of logic is not needed." And the saying of al-Shāfiʿī: "If you hear a man saying 'the name is the named' or 'other than the named,' then he has no religion." And there has preceded the transmission of al-Jawzī: "We are certain that the Companions died without knowing substance (jawhar) or accident (ʿaraḍ)."

And ʿIyāḍ defined Ibn Ṭālib thus: "He was among the great companions of Saḥnūn. He ordered the reciter (muqriʾ) at the mosque of Qayrawān not to recite except with the reading of Nāfiʿ." End.

And I do not say this except to one who has not attained the most important. Otherwise, all the sciences are important after attaining the most important, by the grace of my Lord. I say: like my books "al-Sunan" and "Kashf al-Taqallub."

He said in "al-Iḥyāʾ": "Do not exhaust your lifespan in one of the sciences seeking exhaustive coverage; for knowledge is abundant, and the lifespan is short. And these sciences are not sought for their own sake, but for the sake of other things. And everything sought for the sake of another should not be striven after excessively in itself. So restrict yourself from the science of language to what enables you to understand the speech of the Arabs and to speak with it, and from its rare forms (gharīb) to the rare forms of the Qurʾān and Ḥadīth — and abandon deep immersion in it. And from grammar, to what pertains to the Book and the Sunnah." End.

And Ibn Sirāj, may God have mercy on him, used to elaborate on this and censure those who delve deeply into grammar until they deem weak some of the recitations (qirāʾāt). And he used to say, may God have mercy on him: "Grammar was only innovated for the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Prophet ﷺ — and no one utters anything more virtuous than them. So this one who persists in declaring the weakness of a recitation — what knowledge does this benefit him? Perhaps he hopes to praise a sultan whose poetry he exalts from uttering what he deems permissible to recite with the Book of God. This is ill manners (sūʾ adab)."

ʿIyāḍ said: "Ibn al-Tabbān was among the jurists firmly rooted in grammar, and despite that he said: 'No one increases much in grammar except that he becomes foolish.'" And Ibn al-Ṣāʾigh said: "The Kūfans held that the accusative (naṣb) in 'tuhaddithanā' in the saying 'ammā taʾtīnā fatuhaddithanā' is by opposition (khilāf); because when they intend to associate it with what precedes it and make it agree with it, they follow it in its inflection. And when they intend opposition, they put it in the accusative. So the opposition is, according to them, the agent of the accusative (nāṣib) — and it is, according to them, an agent of the accusative in nouns. And from this is: 'law taraktaka wa-al-asad la-akalaka' — and they did not intend to associate the lion in the leaving; therefore they put it in the accusative. And from this is the accusative of the predicate (khabar) when it is an adverb (ẓarf); for when it is a predicate of a subject that is the subject in meaning, it is raised (marfūʿ), and when it differs from it, it is put in the accusative." And al-Sīrāfī refuted him with what...

title_en: On the Methodology of Ascension (Manhaj al-Taraqqī) — The Seventh Station: The Futility of Disputing Grammatical Principles Once the Objective is Achieved
arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 186

ل منهج الترقي/ المقام سابع أن يكون في مهم إن لم يكن على أمم
يلزمهم؛ ثم الكلام فيه لا معنى له؛ إذ المقصود بالعوامل ضبط القوانين؛ فكيف
انضبطت حصل المقصود ثم رد على الجرمي أن الفاء هنا ناصبة؛ إذ تقليل العوامل
ما أمكن أولى كي لا تكثر على المتعلم: فإذا أمكن أن يجعل للفاء قانونًا واحدًا لا
يختلف فهو أولى.

وقال في الاستثناء: إن قولك: قام القوم إلا زيذاء وقام القوم ليس زيداء كلاهما
اليس بمستقل؛ وأما قولهم: إن في ليس ضميرًا هو اسمها وما بعده خبر وأنه مستقل»
تأويل صناعي؛ وكذلك قولك: قام الزيدان» والزيدان قاماء كلا الفعلين مسند إلى
الزيدين لا إلى الألف: لكن لما اختلف حكم اللفظين خالفوا في التعبير عنهماء قال:
وقد تقدم هذا المعنى غير مرة ومن لم يفهم غرض أهل الصناعة في هذه
الاصطلاحات وفي مقصودهم بالتعاليل نسبهم في ذاك إلى جهل أو حماقة؛ وهو
الجاهل بغرضهم.

وممن جهل غرضهم في ذلك كل من أكثر في تلك التعاليل الهذيائية: واعتقد
أنها أمور حقيقة مقصودة لأهل اللغة. اه.

انظر هل يكون من هذا قول بعض الشيوخ أن الضمير ييرز في خبر المبتدأ إذا
كان ظرنًا وجرى على غير ما هو له على القول بأنه متعلق باسم فاعل محذوف»
وأما من يقول أنه متعلق بفعل محذوف فلا ييرزه وقال الشاطبي: لم بذكر ابن مالك
الخلاف في راقع المبتدأ والخبر؛ لأنه لا تنبني عليه فائدة كلامية: قال ابن الحاج:
كل خلاف وبحث في هذه الصناعة لا يؤدي إلى الوقوف على كيفية التكلم فهو
فضول لا يحتاج إليهء والاشتغال به بطالة. وقد أولع به المدرسون وإن لم يكن ناف
في تعليم الصغار والاشتغال به اشتغال بما لا يعني؛ وأشد من هذا من به
مهم يكسب علمًا بكلام العرب؛ ثم مضى في كلامه إلى أن قال: فقولك: زيد في
الدار الغرض فيه أنه بمعنى: زيد مستفر أو استقر في الدار؛ وقال الشاطبي في
قولهم: كسر الزجاج الحجر: إن الزجاج فاعل وإن كان المعنى بخلاف ذلك؛ اعنبارًا
باللفظ؛ إذ لا يستتب قانون التعليم إلا بذلك؛ قال: وقال شيخنا الأستاذ: الاعراب
أبدا إنما يكون على حسب العلامة التي تكون في الاسم المعرب؛ فتعرب القرية
قوله تعالى: « وَسْسَ قري 4 [يوسف: 82] مفعول. اه

# PageV1P187
anchors:
- Root: ض-ب-ط (ḍ-b-ṭ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To confine, restrain, or regulate precisely; to establish a fixed measure or rule.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological discourse, the precise codification of legal or grammatical principles (ḍabṭ al-qawānīn) so that the intended purpose (maqṣūd) is secured without deviation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of physical tightening or binding; here used metaphorically (majāz) for the intellectual "binding" of rules to ensure uniformity.
- Root: ع-ل-ل (ʿ-l-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To repeat an action; to seek a cause or reason (ʿillah); to explain by way of secondary causation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, the distinction between essential cause (ʿillah) and mere explanatory gloss (taʿlīl); the latter may be artificial (ṣināʿī) and not ontologically real.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: to give a sick person a second drink; metaphorical: to "water" a grammatical rule with explanatory justifications, which may be superfluous.
- Sībawayh Rule: Taqdīr al-ʿāmil (Appreciation of the Governing Element) — When a grammatical operator is omitted, its estimated presence (taqdīr) is determined by the minimal syntactic requirement, not by speculative elaboration.
translation:
I say: From the methodology of ascension — the seventh station — is that one should not engage in a matter that is not incumbent upon him, even if it concerns a weighty issue. For if it is not obligatory for him, then discoursing upon it has no meaning; since the objective of the grammatical operators (ʿawāmil) is merely the precise codification of the laws (ḍabṭ al-qawānīn). However these laws are regulated, the intended purpose is achieved.

Then he [the author] responded to al-Jarmī regarding his claim that the particle *fa* here is a subjunctive nāṣibah [i.e., that it governs the subjunctive mood]. For reducing the number of operators as much as possible is preferable, so that they do not multiply upon the learner. Thus, if it is possible to assign to *fa* a single uniform law that does not vary, that is more appropriate.

And he said concerning the exception (istithnāʾ): Your saying "The people stood except Zayd" (qāma al-qawmu illā Zaydan) and "The people stood, not Zayd" (qāma al-qawmu laysa Zaydan) — both of them are not independent [in their grammatical analysis]. As for their saying that in *laysa* there is a pronoun that is its subject (ism) and what follows it is its predicate (khabar), and that it is independent — this is an artificial technical interpretation (taʾwīl ṣināʿī). Likewise, your saying "The two Zayds stood" (qāma al-Zaydāni) and "The two Zayds, they stood" (al-Zaydāni qāmā) — in both, the verb is predicated to the two Zayds, not to the dual *alif*. But because the grammatical ruling of the two expressions differs, they [the grammarians] differed in their manner of expressing them.

He said: This meaning has already been mentioned more than once. Whoever does not understand the purpose of the practitioners of this craft (ahl al-ṣināʿah) in these technical conventions (iṣṭilāḥāt) and in their intent behind the explanatory justifications (taʿālīl), attributes them in that regard to ignorance or foolishness — while he himself is the ignorant one regarding their purpose.

And among those who were ignorant of their purpose in this matter is everyone who multiplied those nonsensical justifications (al-taʿālīl al-hadhyāniyyah) and believed that they were real matters (umūr ḥaqīqiyyah) intended by the people of the language. End of quote.

Consider: Is there included in this [criticism] the saying of some shaykhs that the pronoun is made explicit (yubrazu) in the predicate of the subject (khabar al-mubtadaʾ) when it is an adverb (ẓarf) and proceeds upon other than what it is [grammatically] for — according to the view that it is attached to an omitted active participle (ism fāʿil maḥdhūf)? As for the one who says it is attached to an omitted verb (fiʿl maḥdhūf), he does not make it explicit.

And al-Shāṭibī said: Ibn Mālik did not mention the disagreement concerning the rāfiʿ (the agent that raises) of the subject and predicate, because no grammatical benefit (fāʾidah kalāmiyyah) is built upon it. Ibn al-Ḥājj said: Every disagreement and investigation in this craft that does not lead to the knowledge of how to speak [correctly] is superfluous (fuḍūl) that is not needed, and occupying oneself with it is idleness (baṭālah). The teachers have become enamored with it, even though it is of no benefit in teaching young students; and occupying oneself with it is occupying oneself with what does not concern one. And more severe than this is the one for whom it is important to acquire knowledge of the speech of the Arabs [i.e., the advanced scholar who wastes time on such debates].

Then he continued his speech until he said: So your saying "Zayd is in the house" (Zaydun fī al-dār) — the purpose in it is that it means "Zayd settled (mustaqirr) or took up residence (istaqarra) in the house." And al-Shāṭibī said concerning their saying "The glass broke the stone" (kasara al-zujāju al-ḥajara): Indeed, the glass is the subject (fāʿil) even though the meaning is contrary to that — out of consideration for the wording (iʿtibāran bi-al-lafẓ); for the law of teaching (qānūn al-taʿlīm) cannot be established except by that.

He said: And our teacher the master (shaykhunā al-ustādh) said: Grammatical inflection (iʿrāb) is always only according to the mark (ʿalāmah) that is in the inflected noun. Thus, in His saying — exalted is He — {«Wa-sʾali al-qaryata»} [Yūsuf: 82], "the village" (al-qaryah) is inflected as an object of the verb (mafʿūl) [even though the meaning is "ask the people of the village"]. End.

title_en: Section 142 — On the Method of Elevation (Manhaj al-Taraqqī) and the Seventh Station: The Blameworthiness of Excessive Questioning and Rational Speculation
arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 187

منهج الترفي/ المقام السايع: أن يكون في مهم إن لم يكن على مم لل

ولابن الصائغ في قولهم: إياك والأسد أنه استغنى عن: احذر وأنه محذوف»
قال: وإنما هذا تقريب وتجوزه بل وضعت العرب إياك تدل به على احذر. فإن قيل:
سويت بين إيا واسم الفعل: فيقال: لا يذكر في أسماء الأفعال إلا ما ليس له معنى
ولا مدلول إلا الفعل؛ ثم قال: وهذه تعليلات القصد بها حفظ القوانين ورسوخها
في نفس المتعلم؛ وقال قبل ذلك: إنما قيل في أسماء الأفعال أسماء لمخالفة
أحكامها لأحكام الأفعال كما قلنا في ليس: إنها فعل: ومدلولها مدلول الحرفه
الكن لما خالفت أحكام الحروف قيل: إنها فعل؛ وقال الشاطبي: رأينا الشارع يعض
عما لا يفيد علما مكلفًا به. سثل مالك عن حديث: “النهي عن قيل وقال وكثرة
السؤال”27. فقال: أما كثرة السؤال فلا أدري أهو ما أنتم فيه مما أنهاكم عنه من كثرة.
المسائل؟.

قال الشاطبي: والحاصل أن متابعة المسائل بالأبحاث العقلية والاحتمالات
النظرية مذموم. سألت امرأة عائشة رضي الله عنها عن قضاء الحائض الصوم دون
الصلاة» فقالت لها: أحرورية أنت؟ إنكاًا عليها السؤال عن مثل هذا. وقضى عليه
السلام في الجنين بغرة؛ فقال الذي قضى عليه: كيف أغرم من لا شرب ولا أكل
ولا نطق ولا استهل؟ ومشل هذا يطل؛ ففال رسول الله ة: 'إنما هذا من إخوان
الكهان”3

وقال ربيعة لسعيد في مسألة عقل الأصابع حين عظم جرحها واشتدت
مصييتها: نتقص عقلها؟ فقال سعيد: أعراقي أنت؟ فقال: بل عالم متثبت أو جاهل
متعلمء فقال: هي السنة يا ابن أخي.

وقال في "الإحياء”: في التصديق بعذاب القبر ثلاث مقالات:

الأولى: أن ذلك أمر ملكوتي لا تصلح هذه العين لمشاهدته؛ فقد كان جبريل
عليه السلام ينزل على رسول اله يل ولا يشاهده إلا رسول اله يل وأن الحيات
والعقارب التي تلدغ في القبور ليست من جنس حيات عالمنا؛ فهي تدرك بحاسة
أخرى.

ارقم 03388 واليهقي في شعب الإيمان (25/6: رقم 399.
