# PageV1P188
anchors:
- Root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Speech, utterance; the act of articulating words with meaning.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological discourse, "qīl wa qāl" (idle talk) denotes vain disputation devoid of beneficial knowledge.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) = articulated speech; metaphorical (majāz) = heedless repetition of rumors.
- Root: س-أ-ل (s-'-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To ask, inquire, request; seeking knowledge or clarification.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, "su'āl" (questioning) is praiseworthy when seeking obligatory knowledge, blameworthy when exceeding divine limits (kathrat al-su'āl).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal = requesting information; metaphorical = contentious interrogation (taʿannut).
- Root: ع-ق-ل (ʿ-q-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Intellect, reason; the faculty of restraint and understanding.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): "ʿAql" as the instrument of discernment between truth and falsehood; "maʿqūl" (blood-wit) is a legal technical term for compensatory payment.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal = binding/restraining; metaphorical = intellectual comprehension.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of "Iḥtirās" (Precautionary Ellipsis) — When a verb is omitted after "iyyāka" (e.g., "iyyāka wa-l-asad"), the construction implies an implicit command verb (iḥdhar), as the particle "iyyā" substitutes for the verbal action itself.
translation:
I say — and success is from God alone:

Know that the method of elevation (manhaj al-taraqqī) in the seventh station requires that the seeker be engaged in a matter of importance, not merely in that which does not concern him.

And Ibn al-Ṣāʾigh said concerning their statement: "Beware of the lion" (iyyāka wa-l-asad) — that it dispenses with the verb "beware" (iḥdhar), and that this verb is omitted (maḥdhūf). He said: This is but an approximation and a facilitation, for the Arabs coined the particle "iyyā" to indicate the meaning of "beware." If it is objected: You have equated "iyyā" with the verbal noun (ism al-fiʿl) — then it is said: Among the verbal nouns, none are mentioned except those which have no meaning or indication other than the verbal action itself. Then he said: These are but explanatory rationalizations (taʿlīlāt) whose purpose is to preserve the legal principles (qawānīn) and render them firmly rooted in the soul of the learner.

And he said before that: They are called "names of actions" (asmāʾ al-afʿāl) because their rulings differ from the rulings of verbs — just as we said concerning "laysa" (not): that it is a verb, yet its signification is the signification of a particle; but because it differed from the rulings of particles, it was called a verb.

And al-Shāṭibī said: We have observed that the Lawgiver (al-Shāriʿ) rebukes that which yields no beneficial knowledge upon which one is obligated to act. Mālik was asked concerning the ḥadīth: "The prohibition of 'qīl wa qāl' (idle talk) and excessive questioning" {«النَّهْيُ عَنْ قِيلَ وَقَالَ وَكَثْرَةِ السُّؤَالِ»}. He said: As for excessive questioning, I do not know whether it refers to what you are engaged in — that which I have forbidden you from — namely, the multiplication of legal questions (masāʾil).

Al-Shāṭibī said: The upshot is that pursuing questions through rational investigations (al-abḥāth al-ʿaqliyyah) and theoretical probabilities (al-iḥtimālāt al-naẓariyyah) is blameworthy (madhmūm). A woman asked ʿĀʾishah — may God be pleased with her — concerning the making up of fasting (qaḍāʾ al-ṣawm) by a menstruating woman without making up the prayer. She said to her: "Are you a Ḥarūriyyah (Kharijite)?" Indeed, it is not incumbent upon you to ask about such a matter.

And the Prophet — peace be upon him — ruled concerning the fetus (al-janīn) that a ghurrah (a slave or a hundred sheep) be paid. The one against whom the ruling was given said: "How shall I pay compensation for one who neither drank, nor ate, nor spoke, nor cried at birth? Such a case is void!" So the Messenger of God — peace be upon him — said: "This one is but of the brethren of the soothsayers" {«إِنَّمَا هَذَا مِنْ إِخْوَانِ الْكُهَّانِ»}.

And Rabīʿah said to Saʿīd concerning the case of the blood-wit for fingers (ʿaql al-aṣābiʿ) when their wounds were severe and their affliction intense: "Do you reduce her blood-wit?" Saʿīd said: "Are you an Iraqi?" He replied: "Rather, I am either a learned man who seeks confirmation (ʿālim mutathabbit) or an ignorant man who seeks to learn (jāhil mutaʿallim)." He said: "It is the Sunnah, O son of my brother."

And he said in the "Iḥyāʾ" (Revival of the Religious Sciences): Concerning the affirmation of the punishment of the grave (ʿadhāb al-qabr), there are three doctrines (maqālāt):

The first: That this matter belongs to the dominion of the unseen (amr malakūtī) which this physical eye is not suited to witness. For Gabriel — peace be upon him — used to descend upon the Messenger of God — peace be upon him — and none but the Messenger of God — peace be upon him — would see him. And the snakes and scorpions which sting in the graves are not of the same species as the snakes of our world; rather, they are perceived by another sense (ḥāssah ukhrā).

title_en: On the Reality of Punishment in the Grave and the Futility of Probing Its Modality
arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 188

3 منيج اتقيا القام الس أن يكون في مهم إن اليكن على لم

الثائي: أن تذكر أمر النائم برى في نومه يرى حية تلدغه وهو يتألم بذلك حتى
تراه في نومه يصيح ويعرق جبينه؛ كل ذلك يدركه من نفسه ويتأذى به كما يتأذى
البقظان. وأنت ترى ظاهره ساكنًا ولا ترى حواليه حية ولا عقربا؛ والحية موجودة
في حقه والعذاب حاصل؛ ولكنه في حقك غير مشاهد.

الثالث: انظره فيه إن أردت.

ثم قال: والحق أن الكل في حيز الإمكان: ومن أنكر بعض ذلك فلضيق
حوصلته؛ والتصديق بعذاب القبر واجبء والذي أوصيك به أن لا تكثر نظرك في
تفصيل ذلك» ولا تشتفل بمعرفت؛ بل اشتغل في التدبير في دفع العذاب. كيف ما
كان فإن اشتغلت بالبحث عن ذلك فيكون مثلك كمثل من حبسه السلطان ليقطع
بده فأهمل طلب الحيلة في الهرب؛ وأخذ طول الليل يتفكر هل يكون القطع
بالموسى أو بالسكين: فالبحث عن كيفية الثواب والعقاب فضول وتضييع زمان» ولو
فرض أكمه بلغ عاقلا وأحاط بمعلومات عدا ما يدركه ببصره؛ ثم اتقشعت الغشاوة
عن عينيه؛ وامتد بصره إلى السماء والأرض والأشجار والتبات والحيوان دقعة
واحدة على سبيل الفجأة. لخيف على عقله أن ينبهر لعظيم تعجبه من شهادة هذه
المخلوقات على خالقها. وكأنه لطول الإنس بهاء كأنه كان يصل إلى حقائقها بعقله».
لولم يرها.

وقال ابن العربي: قوله ييك: 'ينزل رينا..." هذا الحديث أم في الأحاديث
المتشابهة؛ ذهب كثبر من العلماء وخاصة من السلف إلى أن يؤمن بها ولا يخاض
في تأويلها. وقد رأى شيخ القراء الوقف على قوله تعالى: لاممَِقَكمْ تأوية, إلا
[آل عمران: ‎٠]7‏ وبيشدئ بقوله: مفلل 4 [آل عمران: 7] وهو اختيار
إمام الأئمة مالك بن أنسء وهو بشهادة الله الحقء ولو ترك القطا لما تكلف سير
الليل ولا تعاطى. فرأينا أن نخلص من ذلك التأويل ما يقوم عليه الدليل: أما مالك
فقد بدع السائل عن أمثاله؛ وصدف عن إشكاله؛ ووقف عند الإيمان به؛ وهو لنا
أفضل فدوة. وأما الأوزاعي فهو إمام عظيم فتزع بالتاويل حين قال وسثل عن قول
النبي ة: "بنزل ربن...'. فقال: يفمل الله ما يشاء؛ ففتح ابا من المعرفة عظيقاء
ونهج إلى التأويل صراطًا مستقيمًاء فجمل هذا من صفات الفعل لا من صفات
الذات.

# PageV1P189
anchors:
- Root: ق-ب-ر (q-b-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The grave as a place of burial; by extension, the intermediate state (barzakh) of the dead.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): ʿAdhāb al-qabr as a veridical spiritual reality, not a mere metaphor; its perception is veiled from the living.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Ḥaqīqah — the punishment is real for the deceased; majāz would be to deny its sensory manifestation to onlookers.
- Root: ت-أ-و-ل (t-w-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Returning a word to its ultimate interpretation (maʾāl); from ʾawwala, to seek the final purport.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Taʾwīl of mutashābihāt is permissible only where textual or rational proof (dalīl) supports it; otherwise, consign knowledge to God.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal affirmation (ithbāt) for the Salaf; metaphorical reinterpretation (taʾwīl) only for attributes of act (ṣifāt al-fiʿl), not essence (ṣifāt al-dhāt).
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional clause with implicit apodosis (sharṭ muḍmar al-jawāb) — e.g., "If you wish, then reflect" (fa-in aradta fa-nẓur), where the protasis governs an elided response.
translation:
I say — and success is from God alone:

The second proof: That you should recall the affair of the sleeper, who sees in his dream a serpent stinging him, and he suffers pain from it, until you behold him in his sleep crying out, his brow sweating. All of that he perceives from his own self and is pained by it just as the wakeful person is pained. Yet you see his outward form motionless, and you see no serpent nor scorpion around him. The serpent is existent with respect to him, and the torment is realized; but with respect to you, it is not witnessed.

The third proof: Reflect upon this if you wish.

Then he said: The truth is that all of this lies within the domain of possibility (imkān). Whoever denies any part of it does so due to the narrowness of his capacity. Belief in the punishment of the grave is obligatory. What I counsel you is not to multiply your scrutiny into its details, nor to occupy yourself with knowing its modality. Rather, occupy yourself with the management of warding off the punishment, however it may be. For if you busy yourself with investigating that matter, your case will be like the man whom the sultan imprisoned in order to amputate his hand — he neglected seeking a stratagem for escape, and spent the whole night pondering whether the amputation would be done with a razor or with a knife. Thus, investigating the modality of reward and punishment is superfluous and a waste of time.

And even if we suppose a blind man who had reached the rank of a rational adult and had encompassed all knowledge save what he perceives by his sight, then the veil were lifted from his eyes, and his vision extended to the heavens, the earth, the trees, the plants, and the animals all at once, suddenly — it would be feared for his intellect that it would be overwhelmed by the magnitude of his astonishment at the testimony of these creatures to their Creator. As if, due to his long familiarity with blindness, he had been reaching their realities through his intellect, even had he not seen them.

And Ibn al-ʿArabī said: His saying — peace be upon him — "Our Lord descends..." is among the mutashābih (ambiguous) hadiths. Many scholars, especially among the Salaf, held that one must affirm them and not delve into their interpretation. The Shaykh of the Qurrāʾ (reciters) held it permissible to pause at His saying — exalted be He — {«وَمَا يَعْلَمُ تَأْوِيلَهُ إِلَّا اللَّهُ»} [Āl ʿImrān: 7], and to resume with His saying {«وَالرَّاسِخُونَ فِي الْعِلْمِ»} [Āl ʿImrān: 7]. This is the choice of the Imām of the Imāms, Mālik ibn Anas — and it is, by God’s testimony, the truth. Had the sandgrouse not been compelled, it would not have undertaken the night journey nor attempted it. So we resolved to extract from that interpretation only what is established by proof. As for Mālik, he rebuked the questioner about such matters, turned away from his difficulty, and stopped at faith in it — and he is for us the best exemplar. As for al-Awzāʿī, he is a great Imām who ventured into interpretation when he was asked about the Prophet’s saying — peace be upon him — "Our Lord descends..." and he replied: "God does what He wills." Thus he opened a mighty door of knowledge and charted a straight path to interpretation, making this belong to the attributes of act (ṣifāt al-fiʿl), not the attributes of essence (ṣifāt al-dhāt).

title_en: The Seventh Station: On the Methodology of Elevation — The Inadequacy of Language and the Necessity of Metaphorical Interpretation
arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 189

منهج الترفي/ المقام السايع: أن يكون في مهم إن لم يكن على مم فلت

وقال لي شيخ العلماء: لا يمكن لأحد أن يعبر عن جلال الله وكلامه إلا
بهذه الألفاظ الناقصة الثي يعبر بها عناء فإذا سمعت العبارة عن الله فيجب عليك
الإيمان بمعناهاء ثم تعلم أنه ليس له مثل في ذلك»
ألم )4 [الشورى: 11]. وهذا كلام بليغ؛ ولسعة اللغة في العبارة بالحقيقة
والمجاز يتمكن العالم بالله من العيارة عنه: فتقول في حديث: "ينزل رينا.
ربناء وصدق نبيناء والتزول في اللغة في الحقيقة حركة؛ والحركة آفة لا تجوز على
الل فلم ببق إلا العدول عن الحقيقة إلى المجاز؛ وهو النزول بالمعنى؛ فإن التزول
من علو الامتناع إلى علو القبول نزول معنوي» كما أن النزول من علو الفوقية إلى
أسفل المكاتية نزول حسي؛ وفي الحديث: "أنزل لك عن إحدى زوجتي"؛ فإنها
طالق فقد ارتفع
ذلك كله. ويكون من أقسام المجاز التعبير عن الشيء بقائدته وثمرته؛ ويكون ذلك
عبارة عن كثرة ما يفيض اله سبحانه من الرحمة؛ وينشر على الخلق منهاء ويوسعهم
من عطائه على جميع المعاني من إجابة دعوة وقضاء حاجة ونيل مغفرة مما كان
قبل ذلك متنا عليهم؛ كامتناع ما يكون في العلو من فوقهم. وإلى هذا أشار
الأوزاعي يقوله: يفعل الله ما يشاء؛ فجعله من صفات الفعل لا من صفات الذات»
وهنا فصل بالغ فاتخذوه دستوا واشرعوه في سائر المشكلات سبيل.

قال الشاطبي: كل علم شرعي فطلب الشارع له إنما يكون من حيث هو وسيلة
إلى التعبد به. وقال الثوري: إنما يراد العلم ليتقى الله به.

وقال مالك: عن القاسم: أدركت الناس ما يعجبهم القول؛ إنما يعجبهم العمل.
قال الجنيد: كنت بين يدي السري وبين يديه جماعة يتكلمون في الشكرء فقال: يا
غلام؛ ما الشكر؟ فقلت: أن لا يعصى الله بنعمه؛ فقال: يوشك أن يكون حظك من
الله لسانك. قال الجنيد: فلا أزال أبكي على هذه الكلمة التي قالها السري. وععن
يحبى بن معاذ الرازي قال: لبس الصوف حانوت؛ والكلام في الزهد حرقة؛ وصحية
القواقل تعرض كل هذه علاقات.

.وقال ذو النون المصري: يا أخي: كن بالخير موصوقًاء ولا تكن للخير وصافاء
وقال رويم: إذا وهب الله لك مقا وفعالا فأخذ متك المقال وترك عليك الفعال فلا

': صدق

كانت تحت سلطان نكاحه وتحت حجره ومنعه؛ فإذا قال لها:

# PageV1P190
anchors:
- Root: ع-ل-و (ʿ-l-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Height, elevation, loftiness; both physical (ʿulūw ḥissī) and abstract (ʿulūw maʿnawī)
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine transcendence (taʿālī) — God's elevation above all creaturely attributes
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal elevation (ḥaqīqah) vs. metaphorical elevation (majāz) — the shift from physical to spiritual sense
- Sībawayh Rule: Taqdīr al-jumlah (Ellipsis and implied predication) — the unstated grammatical subject in "فلم يبق إلا العدول" requires reconstruction of the full clause
translation:
I say — and this is the seventh station of the methodology of elevation: that one must be in a matter of importance, and if not upon a firm foundation, then let him desist.

And the Shaykh of the scholars said to me: "No one can express the majesty of God and His speech except through these deficient words by which one expresses one's own weariness. So when you hear an expression concerning God, it is incumbent upon you to believe in its meaning, then to know that He has no likeness in that regard." {«لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ»} [al-Shūrā 42:11]. And this is eloquent speech; and by the vastness of language in expression — both literal (ḥaqīqah) and metaphorical (majāz) — the one who knows God is enabled to express concerning Him. Thus you say in the ḥadīth: "Our Lord descends" — and we affirm our Lord and confirm our Prophet. Now "descent" (nuzūl) in language, in its literal sense, is movement; and movement is an affliction (āfah) that is not permissible to attribute to God. So nothing remains except to turn away from the literal to the metaphorical — and that is descent in meaning (nuzūl bi-l-maʿnā). For descent from the height of inaccessibility (ʿulūw al-imtināʿ) to the height of acceptance (ʿulūw al-qabūl) is a spiritual descent, just as descent from the height of physical superiority to the lower place of spatial location is a sensory descent. And in the ḥadīth: "I have released you from one of my wives" — for she is divorced — that entire matter is elevated.

And among the divisions of metaphor (majāz) is expressing a thing by its consequence and fruit. And that is an expression of the abundance of what God — glorified be He — pours forth of mercy, and spreads upon creation from it, and enlarges them from His giving — in all meanings: answering a supplication, fulfilling a need, attaining forgiveness — of what was before that withheld from them, like the withholding of what is in the height above them. And to this al-Awzāʿī pointed by his saying: "God does what He wills" — making it from the attributes of action (ṣifāt al-fiʿl), not from the attributes of essence (ṣifāt al-dhāt). And here is a decisive distinction (faṣl bāligh) — so take it as a constitution (dustūr) and make it a path in all the remaining difficulties.

Al-Shāṭibī said: "Every religious science — the Lawgiver's demand for it is only insofar as it is a means to worship through it." And al-Thawrī said: "Knowledge is only sought that one might fear God through it."

And Mālik said, on the authority of al-Qāsim: "I reached the people — speech did not impress them; only action impressed them."

Al-Junayd said: "I was before al-Sarī, and before him was a group speaking about gratitude (shukr). He said: 'O boy! What is gratitude?' I said: 'That one does not disobey God through His blessings.' He said: 'It is near that your portion from God will be your tongue.'" Al-Junayd said: "And I have not ceased weeping over this word that al-Sarī spoke." And on the authority of Yaḥyā ibn Muʿādh al-Rāzī, he said: "Wearing wool is a shop; and speech about asceticism (zuhd) is a burning; and the company of speakers — all these are afflictions."

And Dhū al-Nūn al-Miṣrī said: "O my brother! Be one described by goodness, and do not be one who describes goodness."

And Ruwaym said: "If God grants you a station (maqām) and an action (fiʿāl), and He takes from you your speech (maqāl) and leaves upon you the action — then do not be truthful [in claiming the station]."

[The text continues with a legal discussion on divorce, but the section concludes here at the page break.]

title_en: On the Degrees of Ascent and the Peril of Claiming Station Without Action
arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 190

4د منهج الترقي/ المقا اسايع: أن يكون في مهم إن الم يكن على أمم
تبال فإنها نعمة. وإن أخذ منك الفعال وترك عليك المقال فنح فإنها مصيبة؛ وإن
أخذ منك المقال والفعال فاعلم أنها نقمة.

قال أبو يزيد البسطامي: إذا رأيت إنسانا يتكلم بهذه العلوم وآخر يتككره وآخر
يؤمن به فهذا الذي يؤمن به خيرهم؛ قل له: يدعو لك. وسئل الرازي: ما بال الناس
يعرفون عيوبهم ولا يرجعون إلى الصواب؟ فقال: لأنهم اشتغلوا بالمباهات بالعلم
ولم يشتغلوا باستعماله؛ فاشتغلوا بالظواهر ولم يشتغلوا بآداب البواطن» فأعمى الله
قلوبهم؛ وقيد جوارحهم عن العبادة. وقال أبو حامد: من الذنوب ذنوب عقوبتها
والعياذ لله سوء الخاتمة؛ قيل: هي عقوبة دعوى الولاية والكرامة بالاقتراء. قال:
ومما عظم ضرره في العوام دعوى الوصال مع الله حتى ينتهي قوم إلى دعوى
المشافهة بالخطاب نشبيها بأبي يزيد والحلاج. قال: وهذا فن عظم ضرره في العوام
حتى ترك جماعة من أهل الفلاحة فلاحتهم وأظهروا مثل هذه الدعاوى: فإن هذا
كلام يستلذه الطيع؛ إذ فيه البطالة في الأعمال مع تزكية النفس ببإدراك المقامات
والأحوال. فلا يعجز الأغبياء عن دعوى ذلك لأنفسهم ولا عن تلفيق كلمات
متخبطة مزخرفة؛ ومهما أنكر عليها لم يعجزوا أن يقولوا: هذا إنكار مصدره العلم
والجدل؛ والعلم حجاب؛ والجدل عمى النفس؛ وهذا ححديث لا يلوح إلا من
الباطن بمكاشفة؛ فهذا وشبهه مما قد استطار في بعض البلاد شرره وعظم ضرره
ومن نطق بشيء منه فقتله في دين الله أفضل من إحياء عشرة؛ ثم قال: وحق العوام
أن يشتغلوا بعبادتهم وبمعاشهم ويتركوا العلم للعلماء؛ فإن العامي لو زنى أو سرق
كان يرا له من أن يتكلم في العلم: ولا ميما فيما يتعلق بالله وأسماته وكلامه.

وقد قال الحسن: أولى الناس بالقرآن من عمل بما فيه وإن لم يقرأه؛ فالحق
الاشتغال بالعمل بما في القرآن؛ إلا أن ذلك ثقيل على التفوس. والفضول خفيف
على القلب. والعامي يفرح أن يخوض في العلم؛ إذ الشيطان يخيل إلبه أنه من
العلماء وأهل الفضل: فلا يزال يحبب إليه ذلك حتى يتكلم في العلم بما هو كر
ولا يدري. اه من "الاحيا

وقال أيضًاه ومن المغترين من يدعي العلم بلله وصفاته ويهمل العمل؛ فغرور
هؤلاء أشد غرورء ويضاهي من أراد خدمة ملك يعرف أخلاقه وعادته فقصد خدمته

# PageV1P191
anchors:
- Root: ر-ق-ي (raqā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Ascending a ladder or height; gradual elevation from one level to another.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Spiritual ascent (taraqqī) through the stations (maqāmāt) of the path — an ontological movement toward God.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal climbing vs. metaphorical elevation in religious rank; here, the author uses it in the technical Sufi sense.
- Root: م-ق-ا-م (maqām)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Standing place; a station where one halts.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A fixed spiritual station (maqām) attained by persistent effort, as opposed to a passing state (ḥāl).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal standing ground vs. figurative rank in the divine path.
- Root: د-ع-و (daʿwā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Claim, assertion, summons.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): False pretension (daʿwā) to spiritual station — a grave sin of self-deification.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal call vs. metaphorical claim of unearned privilege.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Resultative Construction (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb) — The repeated "in" clauses (if... then...) establish a graded taxonomy of divine dealings, each protasis matched to an apodosis of corresponding severity.
translation:
I say: The method of ascent (manhaj al-taraqqī) is that one be engaged in a matter of importance — if one is not upon a prior foundation. If the [divine] grant of action (al-fiʿāl) is taken from you, while speech (al-maqāl) is left to you, then know that this is a trial (miḥnah). And if both action and speech are taken from you, then know that this is a punishment (niqmah).

Abū Yazīd al-Bisṭāmī said: "If you see a person speaking about these sciences, another denying them, and another believing in them — then the one who believes in them is the best of them. Say to him: 'May he pray for you.'"

Al-Rāzī was asked: "Why is it that people recognize their own faults yet do not return to what is correct?" He replied: "Because they have busied themselves with boasting of knowledge (mubāhāt bi-l-ʿilm) and have not busied themselves with its application. They have occupied themselves with outward forms (al-ẓawāhir) and have not occupied themselves with the etiquettes of the inner selves (ādāb al-bawāṭin). So God blinded their hearts and fettered their limbs from worship."

Abū Ḥāmid [al-Ghazālī] said: "Among sins are those whose punishment — God forbid — is an evil end (sūʾ al-khātimah)." It was said: "That is the punishment of claiming sainthood (wilāyah) and miracles (karāmah) by fabrication (iqtirāʾ)."

He said: "Among what has caused great harm to the common folk is the claim of intimate communion (wiṣāl) with God, until some people go so far as to claim direct address (mushāfahah) by divine speech — imitating thereby Abū Yazīd and al-Ḥallāj."

He said: "This is a matter whose harm to the common folk has been immense, to the point that a group of farmers abandoned their farming and displayed such claims. For this is speech that the base nature (al-ṭabʿ) finds pleasurable, since it entails idleness from works along with self-purification (tazkiyat al-nafs) by imagining the attainment of stations (maqāmāt) and states (aḥwāl). The dull-witted are not incapable of claiming this for themselves, nor of fabricating confused and embellished words. And whenever they are denounced for it, they are not incapable of saying: 'This denunciation originates from knowledge and disputation (al-jadal); but knowledge is a veil (ḥijāb), and disputation is blindness of the soul. This is a ḥadīth that shines forth only from the inner self by unveiling (mukāshafah).' So this and the like of it — its evil has spread in some lands and its harm has become great. Whoever utters anything of it — killing him in the religion of God is better than reviving ten [others]."

Then he said: "The right of the common folk is to occupy themselves with their worship and their livelihood, and to leave knowledge to the scholars. For if a commoner were to fornicate or steal, that would be lighter for him than speaking about knowledge — and how much more so regarding what pertains to God, His Names, and His Speech."

Al-Ḥasan [al-Baṣrī] said: "The most worthy of people regarding the Qurʾān is the one who acts by what is in it, even if he does not recite it." So the truth is to occupy oneself with acting by what is in the Qurʾān — except that this is heavy upon the souls, while superfluity (al-fuḍūl) is light upon the heart. The commoner delights in plunging into knowledge, for Satan makes him imagine that he is among the scholars and people of virtue. He does not cease making that beloved to him until he speaks about knowledge with what is a disgrace (kar) — and he does not realize it. End of quotation from "al-Iḥyāʾ."

He also said: "Among the deluded are those who claim knowledge of God and His attributes while neglecting action. The delusion of these is the most severe delusion. They resemble one who desires to serve a king — he knows his character and custom, so he intends to serve him..."

title_en: The Method of Ascent — The Seventh Station: Being Engaged in the Important When Not in the Most Important
arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 191

منهج الترقي/ المفام السابع: أن يكون في مهم إن لم يكن على أهم -
متوسلا بهذه المعرفة تاركا لما يريد ذلك الملك منه فهو مغرور؛ ولو ترك جميع ما
عرف واشتغل بما يحب ذلك الملك لكان أقرب. قال: ومن المغترين أيضًا من
اشتغلوا بتهذيب الأخلاق واتخذوا البحث عن عيوب النفس فقهاء فيقولون: هذا في
النفس عيب؛ والغفلة عمن كونه عيئا عيب؛ ويشغفون بكلمات مسلسلة تضيع
الأوقات في تلفيقها؛ ومن جعل طول عمره في التفتيش عن عوائق الحاج وآفاته
ولم يسلك طريق الحج كان مغروا.

وفي "الرسالة': قال رجل لرويم: أوصني؟ قال: ما هو إلا بذل الروح؛ فإن أمكنك
الدخول فيه مع هناء وإلا فلا تشتغل بترهات الصوفية. ومنها أيضًا تذوكرت المحبة عند
ذي التون المصري فقال: كفوا عن هذه المسألة: لا تسمعها النفوس فتدعيها.

ومنها عن الزجاجي: من أقوال الجنيد: من تكلم على حال لم يصل إليها كان
كلامه فتنة لمن يسمعه ودعوى تنولد في قلبه وحرمه الوصول إلى تلك الحال.
وسئل مالك عن علم الباطن: فقال: علم الباطن لا يعرفه إلا من عرف علم الظاهر
وعمل به؛ ثم قال للسائل: عليك بالدين المحض؛ واياك وبنيات الطريق. وقد تقدم
قوله: بغي لمن خول علما أن يمقث نفسه إذا خلا.

ومن "الاحياء': ريء بعض الشيوخ في النوم؛ فقيل له: ما خبر تلك العلوم التي
كنت تجادل عنها؟ قال: فبسط يده ونفخ فيهاء وقال: طاحت كلها هباء منثوراء وما
اتتفعت إلا بركعتين خلصتا لي في جوف الليل.

رأى سحنون ابن القاسم في المنام؛ فقال له: ما فعل الله بك؟ فقال: وجدت
أي أعمالك وجدت أفضل؟ قال: تلاوة القرآن» قلت:
فالمسائل: فكان يشير بإصبعه فيلشيهاء ورآه ابن معبد أيضًا في النوم: فقال له: كيف
وجدت المسائل؟ فقال: أف ما وجدت أحسن من الرباط.

وريء أيضًا أبو القاسم الجنيد في المنام؛ فقيل له: مافمل الله بك؟
ففال: طاحت تلك الإشارات؛ وفنيت تلك العبارات؛ وأبيدث تلك الرسوم؛ وغابث
تلك العلوم؛ وما تفمنا إلا ركمات كنا نركعها في السحر؛ وقال لله سبحانه:
« انه االبكئة شوق بدت (4)2 إلى أن فال «بمائث تنمت (4)2

[الزخرف: 70 - 72].

عند ما أحييت

# PageV1P192

### | الصفحة 192

6 منهج ارقي المقام الساع: أذ يكون في مهم إن الم يكن على أضع

.وقال تاج الدين في حكمه: لا يستحقر الورد إلا جهول؛ الوارد يؤخذ في الدار
الآخرة؛ والورد ينطوي بانطواء هذه الدار؛ وأولى ما يعتنى به ما لا يخلف وجوده
الورد هو طالبه منك؛ والوارد أنت تطلبه منه؛ وأين ما هو طالبه منك مما هو مطلبك
منه؛ ويعني بالورد: ما يصدر من العبد لله من العبادة؛ ويعني بالوارد: ما يرد على
العبد من الله من أنوار وكرامة؛ والورد أحق ما يعتنى به؛ لوجهين:

أحدهما: أنه مختص بهذه الدار يتقطع باتقطاعها.

والثاتي: أنه حق الحق منك؛ والوارد هو حظك منه؛ وقيامك بحقوقه عليك
أولى وأليق بالعبودية من طلب حظوظك ووقوفك معها.

وقال أيضًا في حكمه: مطلب العارفين من الله الصدق في العبودية والقيام
بحقوق الربوبية: قال شارحها: من غير طلب لحظ ولا بقاء مع نفس قال الله عز
لانت إلا ليود (4)2 [الذاريات: 56].

والتعيد بذل المجهود في مرضاة المعيود. بحيث لو فجأك الموت لم تجد
مستزاا على ما أنت عليه من التعيد.

.ولما لم يمكن أن يكون هذا في طوق البشرء فليكن في وفت دون وقت آخر
كما قاله يي لحنظلة: "ساعة وساعة"1".

ا) أخرجه الديلمي (253/2: رقم 3181 وأخرجه أيضَاء القضاعي (!/393) رقم 672».

# PageV1P193
anchors:
- Root: غ-ر-ر (gh-r-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of "deception" or "delusion" — one who is beguiled by appearances, heedless of underlying reality.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theological nuance — the state of one whose spiritual practice is vitiated by self-deception (ghurūr), mistaking means for ends in the path to God.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "to be deceived by glittering surface"; metaphorically, it denotes the soul's entrapment in secondary acts while neglecting the primary object of devotion.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Resultative Construction (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — The phrase "if he is in something important while not in the most important" sets a protasis whose apodosis follows with the verdict of delusion, requiring the reader to grasp the logical priority of obligations.
translation:
I say: The seventh station of the method of ascent is that one be engaged in something important when not engaged in the most important. Whoever employs this knowledge [of the spiritual path] while abandoning what that King desires of him is deluded (maghrūr). Even if he were to abandon all that he has come to know and occupy himself with what that King loves, it would be nearer [to success]. He said: Among the deluded also are those who occupy themselves with refining the moral virtues and take up the investigation of the soul's defects as jurists, saying: "This is a defect in the soul," while being heedless that their very heedlessness of what constitutes a defect is itself a defect. They become infatuated with chains of words whose fabrication wastes the hours. And whoever spends the whole of his life scrutinizing the obstacles and afflictions of the pilgrim's road, yet does not traverse the path of the Pilgrimage, is deluded.

In the "Risālah" [of al-Qushayrī]: A man said to Ruwaym: "Give me an exhortation." He replied: "It is nothing but the expending of the spirit. If you can enter into it with ease, then do so; otherwise, do not occupy yourself with the idle fancies of the Sufis." Among these [delusions] also: Dhū al-Nūn al-Miṣrī was mentioned in a gathering on love (maḥabbah), and he said: "Cease this question — do not let the souls hear it, lest they claim it falsely."

Among these also, from al-Zajjājī, from the sayings of al-Junayd: "Whoever speaks of a state (ḥāl) he has not attained, his speech is a trial (fitnah) for whoever hears it, and a claim that takes root in his heart, and it bars him from attaining that state."

Mālik was asked about the inner knowledge (ʿilm al-bāṭin), and he said: "The inner knowledge is known only by one who has known the outer knowledge (ʿilm al-ẓāhir) and acted upon it." Then he said to the questioner: "Upon you is the pure religion; and beware of the byways of the road." And his saying has already preceded: "Woe to him who has been granted knowledge, if he does not hold himself in contempt when he is alone."

From the "Iḥyāʾ" [of al-Ghazālī]: One of the shaykhs was seen in a dream, and it was said to him: "What news of those sciences over which you used to dispute?" He said: "He spread out his hand and blew into it, and said: 'They all vanished as scattered dust, and nothing profited me except two rakʿahs that I performed sincerely in the depths of the night.'"

Saḥnūn saw Ibn al-Qāsim in a dream and said to him: "What has God done with you?" He replied: "I found [my deeds]." He said: "Which of your deeds did you find most excellent?" He said: "The recitation of the Qurʾān." He said: "And the legal questions?" — and he gestured with his finger as if to wave them away. Ibn Maʿbad also saw him in a dream and said to him: "How did you find the legal questions?" He said: "Fie! I found nothing better than the frontier watch (ribāṭ)."

Abū al-Qāsim al-Junayd was also seen in a dream, and it was said to him: "What has God done with you?" He said: "Those allusions (ishārāt) have vanished, those expressions (ʿibārāt) have perished, those traces (rusūm) have been obliterated, those sciences (ʿulūm) have disappeared, and nothing profited us except the prostrations we performed at dawn." And he said to God, Exalted be He: {«كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا هَنِيئًا بِمَا أَسْلَفْتُمْ فِي الْأَيَّامِ الْخَالِيَةِ»} [al-Ḥāqqah: 24] — "Eat and drink in satisfaction for what you sent ahead in the days gone by" — until he said: {«بِمَا أَسْلَفْتُمْ»} [al-Zukhruf: 70–72] — "for what you sent ahead" — when He had revived him.

I say: The eighth station of the method of ascent is that one be engaged in something important when not in the most important.

Tāj al-Dīn said in his Aphorisms (Ḥikam): "The regular devotion (al-wird) is not held in contempt except by an ignoramus. The divine influx (al-wārid) is received in the next abode, while the regular devotion folds up with the folding of this abode. And the most worthy of attention is that whose existence does not outlast you — the regular devotion is what He seeks from you, while the divine influx is what you seek from Him. And where is what He seeks from you compared to what you seek from Him?" By "regular devotion" he means what issues from the servant to God of worship; by "divine influx" he means what descends upon the servant from God of lights and graces. The regular devotion is the most deserving of attention, for two reasons:

First: It is specific to this abode and is cut off with its cutting off.

Second: It is the right of the Real upon you, whereas the divine influx is your portion from Him. And your standing firm in His rights over you is more fitting and more appropriate to servanthood (ʿubūdiyyah) than seeking your own portions and standing with them.

He also said in his Aphorisms: "The quest of the knowers (ʿārifūn) from God is sincerity in servanthood and the fulfillment of the rights of lordship (rubūbiyyah)." Its commentator said: "Without seeking any portion, nor remaining with the self." God, Mighty and Exalted, said: {«وَمَا خَلَقْتُ الْجِنَّ وَالْإِنسَ إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُونِ»} [al-Dhāriyāt: 56] — "And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me."

And worship is the expending of utmost effort in that which pleases the Worshipped One, such that if death were to overtake you suddenly, you would find no reproach against what you are upon of worship.

And since this cannot be within the capacity of mortal man, let it be at one time and not at another, as the Prophet ﷺ said to Ḥanẓalah: "An hour and an hour" — i.e., a time for worship and a time for worldly concerns.

title_en: The Eighth Station — The Station of the Elite of the Scholars: On Striving to Fill the Virtuous Times When One Cannot Fill All Times
arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 193

المقام الثامن

مقام خواص العلماء: من لم يتمكن من تعمير
كافة الأوقات فليجتهد في تعمير الأوقات الفاضلة

إن كنت أيها المريد لا تقدر أن تعمر جميع الأوقات بالأوراد فخص الأوقات
الفاضلة.

قال في "الإحياء': لأنها مظان الخيرات وموسم التجارات؛ ومهما غفل التاجر
عن الموسم لم يربح: كذلك مريد الآخرة إن لم يغتنم الأوقات الفاضلة لم ينجح»
.وكذا يقول السادة الصوفية: من لم يهذب نفسًا ولم يلتزم وردًا فهو مغرورء فالتزام
الأوراد هو طريق القوم؛ ويشهد له القرآن والسنة وكلام الأئمة: شافعية ومالكية
وإياك ودسائس الظاهرية؛ فمرجع أصلها للذي قيل فيه: إمام الضلالة بالأندلس»
السانه وسيف الحجاج توأمان. وإنما أظهرت هنا وجذا؛ لأني كنت على مأخذ
لشيوخي في التزام بعض الخيرات؛ ثم دخلني الشغب الذي يدخ المتعلقين بهذا
المذهب الظاهري؛ فاستربت فيما كنت رويت.

ومن باب أولى فيما استنبطت من نفسي: كما نصوا أن كل مريد ينبغي أن
.يرتب لنفسه حزيًا بلتزمه يجمع فيه ما يجذب قلبه ويرجو ثوابه: ففانتي بهذه الدخيلة
الظاهرية الاقتداء بشيوخي في هذه الالتزامات» وكنت أخذت عن شيخي المتوري
مسلسلاته على شروطهاء فكاني رأيت هذا من البدع؛ فسقطت لي روايتهاء ولا والله
ما اعتضت خيرًا من ذلك؛ ونفق هذا المذهب الظاهري؛ وصرت أستحي بمأخذ
شبوخي إلى أن عثرت على ما نقله السيد مفتي تونس البرزلي في نوازله؛ فوجدته
قد صرح بمأخذ شبوخي تصريحًا لم يكن لهم رحمهم الله تصربح بمثل ذلك ثم
عثرت على أحكام بن حزم بعد موت شيوخي؛ فوجدت أن ذلك المذهب هو الذي
نفق بعينه وعباراته هي المنقولة والمتداولة: فحيتثذ تجرأت ونطقت بلسان هذا
السيد البرزلي المعظم لشيخ الشيوخ ابن لب؛ ونقله من كتابه الذي سماه 'السان

# PageV1P194

### | الصفحة 194

8 مهي قوفي لظن متم عو لد م لم سكن من نسم كل الات ليجهد في تمر لاز قافا
الأذكار". لكن لم يسمه؛ ولكنه يتقل عباراته معزوة لبعض الشيوخ؛ يل سماه في آخر
"النوازل"؛ وقال: عن كتابه الذي سماه "لسان الأذكار".

وبالجملة فمأخذ هذا السيد هو الذي تبين لي وأنا حسن الظن به؛ كما أني
مسيء الظن بمخالفه ولا أرضى مأخذه. فقال هذا السيد البرزلي في توازله: الفضائل
والترغيبات تنقل على غير الوجه الذي تتقل عليه الأحكام؛ لما في ذلك من
الاستتناس في الترغيب على الطاعة والإعانة في النفس؛ لكي يحصل لها شيء من
أخراهاء وهذا إذا شهد الشرع باعتبار جنسه؛ وليس في الأصول ما يخالفه.

وهذا كله جائز. وقد فعله جماعة في فضائل أعمال اليوم والليلة وما يقال عند
الأحوال العارضة وعلى أعضاء الوضوء وغير ذلك من أحزاب الفضلاء؛ كحزب
أبي طالب. وحزب الغزالي. وهنا كله ما لم يصادم فاعدة من قواعد الشرع: فهو
حسن لأنه يدل على الخير وعلى المثابرة عليه حتى يصير له ذلك عادة: ولا يعتقد
كون ذلك فرضاء بل هو حسن؛ لأنه يؤدي إلى محبة العبادة والانقطاع إلى اله وما
أدى من الوسائل إلى الطاعة فهو طاعة. اه من كلامه ما أنا أنسج على منواله.

انظر قوله: حتى يصير ذلك عادة؛ أيش يضر هذاء أوبخ بهذا نفسيء وإني رأيت
هذا الكلام قبل اليوم؛ ووقع مني الموقع الذي وقع مني الآن.

كان الشيخ سيدي المنتوري رحمه الله رواني تقليم الأظفار يوم الخميس»
وقال: كذلك رأيت جدك ابن بقي يقلم أظفاره يوم الخميس بسند إلى رسول اله كف
ثم رأيت أن التزام هنا بدعةء فسقطت لي الرواية على شرطهاء وعملت يدا على الله
بالمخالفة: فلا أقلم ظفرا إلا عند الضرورة لخلعه والضرر به؛ ورواني أيضًا قراءة
آبة الكرسي عن علي رضي الله عنه فال: ما أرى رجلا أدرك عقله الإسلام أو ولد
في الإسلام يبيت ليلة سوادها حتى يقرأ آية الكرسي؛ قال علي رضي الله عنه؛ ما بث
اليلة قط منذ سمعت هذا حتى أقرأها. قال سيدي المتتوري: منذ سمعت هذا من
القيجاطي ما تركت قراءتها إلا إن كنت ساهيًا أو ناسباء نم قال الشيخ: رواني هذا
الخبر أن أكون فيه على هذا الشرط؛ فكأني رأيت هذا من البدع» فلا أبال أقرأتها أم
لاء قسقطت لي الرواية على شرطهاء ووالله ما اعضت خيرًا من ذلك؛ قانظر هذه
المحرمة.

# PageV1P195
anchors:
- Root: ع-م-ر (ʿ-m-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To cultivate, inhabit, build up, or make prosperous; the opposite of desolation (kharāb). Implies active, purposeful engagement.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the theological sense, the "building" of time with devotional acts (awrād) is a form of spiritual cultivation (iʿmār) that mirrors the divine command to inhabit the earth with obedience.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage refers to physical construction or settlement; here it is a clear metaphor (majāz) for filling time with acts of worship, as one fills a house with goods.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Inna (الشّرط بـ "إن") — The protasis (condition) introduced by "in" (if) is followed by the apodosis (result) introduced by "fa," establishing a causal necessity: inability to do all necessitates prioritizing the best.
translation:
I say — and know, O seeker (murīd) — if you are unable to fill all your times with devotional litanies (awrād), then single out the virtuous times [for special attention].

He said in the "Iḥyāʾ" (Revival of the Religious Sciences): "For they are the places where good deeds are sought (maẓānn al-khayrāt) and the season of trade (mawsim al-tijārāt). Whenever a merchant neglects the season, he does not profit. Likewise, the seeker of the Hereafter, if he does not seize the virtuous times, will not succeed."

And thus say the Sufi masters (al-sāda al-ṣūfiyya): "Whoever does not discipline his soul and does not adhere to a litany (wird) is deluded (maghrūr)." For adherence to litanies is the path of the folk (ṭarīq al-qawm). And this is attested by the Qurʾān, the Sunna, and the words of the Imams — both Shāfiʿī and Mālikī.

And beware of the intrigues (dasāʾis) of the Ẓāhiriyya (literalists)! For the origin of their doctrine traces back to the one of whom it was said: "The Imam of misguidance in al-Andalus — his tongue and the sword of al-Ḥajjāj are twins." I have only revealed this here with burning distress (wajd), because I was formerly upon the method (maʾkhadh) of my teachers in adhering to certain virtuous practices; then there entered into me the agitation (shaghb) that afflicts those attached to this Ẓāhirī school, and I began to doubt what I had transmitted.

And this applies a fortiori (min bāb awlā) to what I had derived from my own reflection. For they (the Ẓāhiriyya) ruled that every seeker should arrange for himself a portion (ḥizb) to which he adheres, gathering therein what draws his heart and for which he hopes reward. So I abandoned, due to this Ẓāhirī intrusion (dakhīla), the emulation of my teachers in these adherences. I had taken from my teacher al-Mattūrī his chains of transmission (musalsalāt) upon their conditions; and it was as if I saw this [practice] as an innovation (bidʿa). So his narrations fell from me [in my estimation]. And no, by Allah, I did not gain anything better from that! This Ẓāhirī school became prevalent (nafaqa), and I began to feel ashamed of my teachers' method — until I came upon what the Sayyid, the Mufti of Tunis, al-Burzulī, transmitted in his "Nawāzil" (Legal Rulings on Novel Cases). I found that he had explicitly stated the method of my teachers with a clarity that they — may Allah have mercy on them — had not expressed with such explicitness. Then I came upon the rulings (aḥkām) of Ibn Ḥazm after the death of my teachers, and I found that that very school was the one that had become prevalent — its very expressions were those transmitted and circulated. At that point I grew bold and spoke with the tongue of this Sayyid al-Burzulī, who held in great veneration the Shaykh of Shaykhs, Ibn Lubb; and [al-Burzulī] transmitted from his book which he named "Lisān al-Adhkār" (The Tongue of Remembrances). However, he did not name it [in that passage], but rather quoted his expressions attributed to some of the Shaykhs; yet he named it at the end of the "Nawāzil," saying: "From his book which he named 'Lisān al-Adhkār.'"

In sum, the method of this Sayyid is what became clear to me, and I hold a good opinion of him — just as I hold a bad opinion of his opponent and do not approve of his method. For this Sayyid al-Burzulī said in his "Nawāzil": "Virtues (faḍāʾil) and exhortations (targhībāt) are transmitted upon a different basis than legal rulings (aḥkām) are transmitted. This is because therein lies a familiarity (istīʾnās) in encouraging obedience and an aid to the soul, so that it may attain something of its Hereafter. And this [is permissible] when the Sacred Law (sharʿ) attests to the validity of its general kind (jins); and there is nothing in the principles (uṣūl) that contradicts it."

And all of this is permissible. A group of people have indeed done this in [compiling] the virtues of the deeds of day and night, what is said at incidental circumstances, upon the limbs of ablution (wuḍūʾ), and other such litanies of the virtuous — like the Ḥizb of Abū Ṭālib and the Ḥizb of al-Ghazālī. And all of this, as long as it does not clash with a foundational rule (qāʿida) of the Sacred Law, is good (ḥasan), because it points to goodness and to perseverance upon it until it becomes a habit for him. And he does not believe it to be an obligation (farḍ); rather, it is good, because it leads to love of worship and devotion (inqiṭāʿ) to Allah. And whatever leads by means (wasāʾil) to obedience is itself obedience." End of his speech — and I weave upon his pattern (ansij ʿalā minwālihi).

Look at his saying: "until it becomes a habit (ʿāda)" — what harm is in this? I rebuke myself with this! And indeed I had seen this speech before today, and it affected me in the same way it affects me now.

The Shaykh, Sayyidī al-Mattūrī — may Allah have mercy on him — used to narrate to me the trimming of fingernails on Thursday, and he said: "Thus I saw your grandfather Ibn Baqī trimming his nails on Thursday, with a chain of transmission (sanad) to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." Then I came to see that adhering to this was an innovation (bidʿa), so the narration fell from me upon its condition. And I made a covenant with Allah to oppose it: I do not trim a nail except at necessity — for its tearing or harm to it. He also narrated to me the recitation of Āyat al-Kursī from ʿAlī — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: "I do not see a man who has attained with his intellect Islam, or was born in Islam, spending a night in its darkness without reciting Āyat al-Kursī." ʿAlī — may Allah be pleased with him — said: "I have not missed a night since I heard this except that I recited it." Sayyidī al-Mattūrī said: "Since I heard this from al-Qayjāṭī, I have not abandoned its recitation except out of forgetfulness or oversight." Then the Shaykh said: "He narrated this report to me upon the condition that I be upon this [same] condition [of adherence]. And it was as if I saw this as an innovation — so I cared not whether I recited it or not. So the narration fell from me upon its condition. And no, by Allah, I did not gain anything better from that! So look at this deprivation (maḥruma)."

title_en: On Following the Imams in Supererogatory Prayers and the Principle of Emulation (Iqtidāʾ)
arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 195

منهج فني ‏ غئ: طم عون املد ئ لمكن م تر كقة لوقت يجيد ف تسر الأرات الاضة__ 339

.وكذلك أيضًا رواني قراءة الشفع والوتر ب (الإخلاص» وقال لي: ما تركت
قراءة ذلك في شفعي؛ منذ رواني هذا الخبر الراوية ابن السراج؛ قال رحمه اله
وصرت إذا صليت الإشفاع مأموماء فإن قرأ الإمام في شفعه ب(الإخلاص) أوترت
معه» وإلا أثرك الوتر معه وأصليه بداري؛ لثلا تفوتني سورة (الاخلاص) في شفعي»
وكذلك في السلسلة؛ القاضي عياض في هذه السلسلة النزم ذلك؛ وكذلك كان
سيدي ابن سراج رحمه الله يقرأء فرأيت أنا بذلك المأخذ الظاهري أن هذا إفراط فيا
ليت شعري أيش كان مختاري أو الاقنداء بالشيوخ: أين هذا من طريق القوم؟
يقولون: كل قول وفعل بغير اقنداء فهو حظ نفس على طريقهم هذا لو لم أرو هذا
لا ينغي أن أقول للعامي: ليس معي في الصلاة؛ أصلي في شفعي بدالإخلاص) أم
بسورة (الكوثر) مثلاء فإذا اختار لي سورة قلت: اسمع من الله؛ وإذا أظهرت في هذا
الوجد فلنبذل نصحي لمن يحسن ظنه في قولي عسى اله أن يهب غشي لنفسي
النصحي لإخواني في دبي*

وقد تقدم أن مأخذ الشيوخ أنه متى أمكنهم أن يتأولوا ما ظاهره خلاف هذا
المأخذ الظاهري إلا تأولوه» ويصرحون بخلاف تلك الظواهرء كقول الباجي وأبي
عمر وابن العربي: بموت المصطفى يك أمن أن يلحق بالفرائض ما ليس منهاء.
وكذلك قول أبي عمر: من خاف على أمة محمد وك ما لم يخفه عليها نبيها فقد باء
من التعسف يما لا يخقى.

وقال عياض في إتيان النبي يك مسجد قباء يوم كل سيت حجة لجواز
تخصيص الأئمة والصالحين بعض الأيام من الجمعة بنوع من القربات سيئا أو
غيره. وعرف عياض في مداركه بالغدمي؛ وذكر من فقهه ودينه. وحكى عنه أنه قال:
كل ما بلغني من التعبد عملته: حتى لقد عملت ما بلغني عن بعض السلف أنه خختم
اثلاث ختم في ليلة؛ ووطأ أهله عند كل ختمة. وتظهر. اه. فانظر هذا المأخذ: فلا
شك أن عمله بالاقتداء منافسة في الخيرء ولو عمل خيرًا من ذلك بلا اقتداء لما برئئ
من حظ نفسه ورؤيتها.

ومن "الرسالة": عن سهل بن عبد الله التستري قال: كل قعل يفعله العبد بغير
اقتداء فهو غش النفس. وانظر أيضًا في “الرسالة" في الرجل الذي أرسله أبو القاسم
الجنيد مع الرجل الذي رغب منه أن يرسل معه أحد أصحابه يأكل معه يدخل بذلك

# PageV1P196
anchors:
- Root: ق-د-و (q-d-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To follow, to emulate, to take as a model; iqtidāʾ = following an imam in prayer.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Emulation as the outward expression of inner obedience (ṭāʿah) to prophetic precedent (sunnah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical following in prayer rows; metaphorical (majāz) — spiritual conformity in intention and action.
- Root: ن-ص-ح (n-ṣ-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Sincere counsel; purity of intention in advising others.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The believer's duty to offer sincere advice (naṣīḥah) as part of communal religious integrity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — tailoring a garment; metaphorical — purifying one's counsel from self-interest.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional sentence with فاء (fāʾ al-jazāʾ) — The protasis (condition) governs the apodosis, requiring the fāʾ before the result clause, as in "If the imam recites... then I perform witr with him."
translation:
I say — and likewise, I was told of the narration concerning the recitation of al-Shafʿ and al-Witr with {«Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ»}. He said to me: "I have never abandoned reciting that in my shafʿ since I was told this report." The narrator was Ibn al-Sarrāj — may God have mercy on him. And I said: "When I pray the shafʿ as one led by an imam, if the imam recites in his shafʿ with {«al-Ikhlāṣ»}, I perform the witr with him; otherwise, I abandon the witr with him and pray it in my own house, lest the recitation of {«Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ»} in my shafʿ be lost to me."

Likewise in the chain (al-silsilah): al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ in this chain adhered to that practice. And so did my master Ibn Sarrāj — may God have mercy on him — recite it. Then I saw, by that apparent (ẓāhirī) approach, that this is excess. Would that I knew which was my choice: emulation of the shaykhs? Where is this in relation to the path of the folk (ṭarīq al-qawm)? They say: "Every saying and deed without emulation (iqtidāʾ) is a portion of the lower self (ḥaẓẓ nafs)." On their path, even if I had not narrated this, it would not befit me to say to a commoner (ʿāmmī): "I have nothing with me in prayer; I pray in my shafʿ with {«al-Ikhlāṣ»} or with {«Sūrat al-Kawthar»}, for example." If he then chose a sūrah for me, I would say: "Hearken to God." And if I manifest this state (wajd), then let me offer my sincere counsel (naṣīḥah) to one who thinks well of my words — perhaps God may grant me, for my own self, the sincerity I offer to my brothers in religion.

It has preceded that the approach of the shaykhs is that whenever they can interpret what appears contrary to this apparent (ẓāhirī) approach, they do so, and they explicitly state the contrary of those apparent meanings — as with the saying of al-Bājī, Abū ʿUmar, and Ibn al-ʿArabī: "With the death of the Chosen One ﷺ, it is no longer feared that what is not of the obligatory acts (farāʾiḍ) might be annexed to them." Likewise, the saying of Abū ʿUmar: "Whoever fears for the community of Muḥammad ﷺ what its Prophet ﷺ did not fear for it has fallen into a distortion (taʿassuf) that is not hidden."

And ʿIyāḍ said, regarding the Prophet's ﷺ coming to the mosque of Qubāʾ every Saturday, that it is a proof for the permissibility of the imams and righteous ones specifying certain days of the week with a type of devotional act (qurbah), whether supererogatory or otherwise. And ʿIyāḍ was known in his *Madārik* as al-Ghudāmī; he mentioned his jurisprudence (fiqh) and his religiosity. And he related from him that he said: "Everything that reached me of devotional practice, I performed it — even to the point that I performed what reached me from some of the Salaf: that he completed three completions (khatmāt) of the Qurʾān in one night, and he approached his wife at each completion." And he mentioned it. So consider this approach: there is no doubt that his action with emulation (iqtidāʾ) was a competition in goodness; had he done something better than that without emulation, he would not have been free from the portion of his lower self and its self-regard.

And from *al-Risālah*: from Sahl ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Tustarī, who said: "Every deed a servant performs without emulation (iqtidāʾ) is self-deception (ghishsh al-nafs)." And consider also in *al-Risālah* the story of the man whom Abū al-Qāsim al-Junayd sent with the man who requested that he send one of his companions to eat with him, thereby entering...

title_en: Section 149 — On the Station of the Elite Among the Rightly Guided, and the Propriety of Following the Established Practices of the Pious Predecessors
arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 196

40 منهج افزفي/ لمق شان مقام خواص الملدد من لم يكن من تير كاف الأوقات فليجتهد في مر الأرات القاضلة.
السرور فلم يأكل الرجل إلا لقمة وخرج؛ وجاء الآخر إلى الجنيد؛ وقال: يا أبا
القاسم؛ ما أكل إلا لقمة واحدة وخرج؛ فقال الجنيد: لم لم تنم السرور عليه؟ فقال:
يا سيدي؛ كنت للم آكل شيئاء وكرهت أن يبدو مني سوء أدب من جهة الفاقة في
حضرتك؛ فلما دعوتني سررت؛ إذ جرى ذلك ابت
اله الجنان ثواباء فلما جلست على مائدته سوى لقمة وقال: كل فهذا أحب إلي من
كذاء فرأيت أنه دنيء الهمة. انظر الحكاية في "الرسالة". وانظر بهذا المأخذ يعلم
الإنسان.

ويروى في 'صحيح البخاري”: أن رسول الله يي صلى الركعة الثانية من صبح
يوم الجمعة مَل أتى عَلَى الإنسَانٍ» ورأيت بعضهم يتورع عن قراءتها كذلك
ويصلي بها الركمة الأولى؛ أيمكن أن يكون حظ نفس مثل هذا؟ وكان سيدي
المنتوري يلتزم قراءتها في ثانية صبح كل يوم جمعة.

ولما تغدمت خطيبا بالببازين وعادتهم التزام صلاة الصبح بالسورتين؛ ورد
بهما "صحيح البخاري” أمرني سيدي ابن سراج رحمه الله أن أوافقهم؛ ولكن ما
فعلت ذلك قط؛ إذ كنت في عنفوان ذلك المأخذ المخالف لمأخذ شيوخي. وانظر

منك» قمضيت وأنا لا أرضى

حديث الترمذي: أن رجلا أنى رسول الله يو فقال: يا رسول الله إني رأيت
الليلة وأنا نائم كاني أصلي خلف شجرة فسجدت: فسجدت الشجرة معي؛ فسمعتها
وهي تقول اللهم اكتب لي بها أجراء وضع عني بها وزراء واجعلها لي عتدك ذخراء
وتقبلها مني كما تقبلتها من عبدك داود. وفال ابن عباس: فسمعت رسول الله في

أسيرك البارحة؟”'" فقلت: يا رسول الله زعم أنه يعلمني كلمات ينفعني الله بهاء

# PageV1P197
anchors:
- Root: ج-ه-د (j-h-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Exertion of effort to the utmost limit; striving against one's lower self or external obstacles.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Spiritual striving (jihād al-nafs) as the means to elevate one's station (maqām) among the elite (khawāṣṣ).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical exertion; metaphorical — disciplined devotion in worship and etiquette (adab).
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb) — "Whoever is not from the people of such times, let him strive..." (man lam yakun... fa-l-yajtahid), indicating a general precept with a specific application.
translation:
I say — may Allah guide us and you to the path of the rightly guided, and grant us success in following the conduct of the elite among His saints:

Know that the station of the elite (khawāṣṣ) among the rightly guided is not attained by mere wishful thinking, but by rigorous striving (ijtihād) in the virtuous moments and noble hours. Whoever is not from the people of such times — let him exert himself in seeking the virtuous moments and the excellent deeds.

The story has come to us concerning the master of this station, Abū al-Qāsim al-Junayd (may Allah sanctify his secret): A man came to him and said, "O Abū al-Qāsim, so-and-so ate but a single morsel and then departed." Al-Junayd replied, "Why did you not conceal the joy (al-surūr) upon him?" The man said, "O my master, I had not eaten anything, and I disliked that any ill manners should appear from me due to my neediness in your presence. So when he invited me, I was delighted, for that occurred as a provision from Allah — a reward for the gardens of Paradise. Then when I sat at his table, he set before me a single morsel and said, 'Eat — this is more beloved to me than such-and-such.' So I saw that he was low of aspiration (danī al-himmah)." Consider this story in the *Risālah* [of al-Qushayrī]. And by this very principle (maʾkhadh), a person comes to know [the degrees of spiritual aspiration].

It is narrated in *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited in the second rakʿah of the dawn prayer (ṣubḥ) on Friday {«hal atā ʿalā al-insāni»} [Q. 76:1]. And I have seen some who are scrupulous (yatawarraʿu) about reciting it in that manner, and instead recite it in the first rakʿah. Can such a person possibly have the same portion [of spiritual insight]? My master al-Muntūrī (may Allah have mercy on him) adhered to reciting it in the second rakʿah of the dawn prayer every Friday.

And when I was appointed as khaṭīb at al-Babbāzīn, and their custom was to adhere to the dawn prayer with the two sūrahs [i.e., al-Sajdah and al-Insān], and the *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* supports them in this, my master Ibn Sirāj (may Allah have mercy on him) commanded me to conform to them. But I never did that, for I was in the prime of that principle (maʾkhadh) which opposed the principle of my own teachers. And consider — I passed away [i.e., in that state] while I was not pleased [with that conformity].

The ḥadīth of al-Tirmidhī: That a man came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I saw in a dream last night, as if I were praying behind a tree. Then I prostrated, and the tree prostrated with me. I heard it saying: 'O Allah, write for me thereby a reward, and remove from me thereby a burden, and make it for me a treasure with You, and accept it from me as You accepted it from Your servant Dāwūd.'" Ibn ʿAbbās said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recite [the Qurʾān] in that context."

The meaning of the ḥadīth is in *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī*, for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Abū Hurayrah: "What did your captive do last night?" I said, "O Messenger of Allah, he claimed that he would teach me words by which Allah would benefit me, so I released him." He said: "When you go to your bed, recite the Āyat al-Kursī: {«allāhu lā ilāha illā huwa al-ḥayyu al-qayyūm»} [Q. 2:255]. For there will not cease to be over you a guardian from Allah, and no devil will approach you until morning." And they were the most eager of people for good. So the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, he told you the truth, though he is a liar — that was the devil."

title_en: On Making Up Missed Supererogatory Devotions and Acting Upon Reports of Virtue
arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 197

منهج ني هئ طم حو املد ئ لمكن م تر كا لوقت يجيد في تسر لأرات الاضة__ 341

ومن حلية الإمام المتفق على دينه وعلمه مفتي المسلمين محبي الدين النووي
قال: ينبغي لمن بلغه فضل في عمل أن يعمل به ولو مرة. ثم قال: وينبغي لمن كان
اله وظيفة من ذكر في وقت من ليل أو نهار أو عقب صلاة أو حالة من الأحوال ففاته
أن يتداركها وبأتي بها إذا تمكن منها ولا يهملها إذ اعند الملازمة عليها لم يعرضها
اللتفويت» وإذا تساهل في قضائها سهل عليه

وانظر هذا عندي أولى من قول مالك: من غلبته عيناه عن حزيه فله أن يصليه
ما بينه وبين طلوع الفجر الأول وأول الإسفارء وإنما قلت: من باب أولى؛ لأن هذا
الوقت من كان عليه الوترء قال ابن القاسم: لا يصلي له شفعًا إن كان ركع بعد
العشاء. ومختار مالك لا يحبي المسجد إن كان ركع الفجر في بيته.

وفي "الموطا": أن عمر بن الخطاب قال: من فاته حزبه من الليل فقرأه حين
تزول الشمس فإنه لم يفتهء أو كانه أدركه.

وهذا الإمام ابن عرفة على تعظيمه للمشهور في المذهب بالسنة لهذا الباب»
حكى عنه تلميذه الإمام الأبي أنه كان يتتفل بعد العصرء فقيل له في ذلك؛ فقال:
إنما أفعله يوم يفوتني معتادي. وحكى عنه قال لآخر: لا يأني من الصلاة إلا خير.
وحكى عنه أيضًا أنه كان يختم قيامه بالليل بقراءة (الإخلاص) بعد (الفاتحة) يقرأها
عشرًا يعدها في أصابعه؛ ولم ير العد شغلا في الصلاة» ويفعل ذلك للخبر الصحيحء
افيختم برقل هو الله أحد).

ونقل عنه أنه كان يتنفل في سفره للحج ماشيّا لإجازته غير مالك. وانظر من
هذا المعنى ما حكاء عياض عن ابن وهب قال: جعلت على نفسي كلما اغتبت
إنسانًا صيام يومء فهان ذلك علي؛ فجعلت كلما اغتبت إنسانا صدقة درهم؛ فثقل
ذلك علي وتركت الغيية. وانظر أيضًا قد نقل ابن بشكوال بسنده أن من بلغه فضل
عمل فعمل ذلك العمل رجاء ذلك الثواب أعطاه الله ذلك الثواب؛ وإن لم يككن ما
بلغه حقا. وبالجملة فمريد الآخرة إن وجد باعنا على خير

أو باقتداء أو باسمع

من الله فلي
قال الشاطبي في حواده: أو برؤيا كرؤيا الكتاتي؛ تقدمت قبل هذا مع نصوص
جميع الأئمة أن الرؤيا لا يستدل بها على حكم.

# PageV1P198
anchors:
- Root: ق-ض-ي (qaḍā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To fulfill, settle, or complete what is owed; to discharge an obligation after its appointed time.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In devotional acts, qaḍā denotes compensatory performance of a missed act of worship, preserving its essential form while acknowledging the lapse of its preferred time.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is 'to decide' or 'to finish'; here it is metaphorical (majāz) for restoring the due of an act after its time has passed.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Response Construction (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb) — The phrase "if he misses it... let him make it up" employs the conditional particle to link the protasis (missed act) with the apodosis (obligation to compensate), indicating a general ruling.
translation:
I say — and this is, in my view, more appropriate than the statement of Mālik: "Whomever his eyes overcome regarding his nightly portion (ḥizb), he may pray it between that time and the appearance of the first dawn and the beginning of the morning light." I only say "more appropriate" because this time [of making up] applies to one upon whom the witr was incumbent. Ibn al-Qāsim said: He does not pray an even-numbered pair (shafʿ) for it if he had prayed the supererogatory rakʿahs after the ʿishāʾ. And the chosen position of Mālik is that he does not come to the mosque if he had prayed the dawn supererogatory in his house.

And in the Muwaṭṭaʾ: That ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: "Whomever misses his nightly portion (ḥizb) and recites it when the sun passes its zenith, then he has not missed it — or as if he had caught it."

And this Imām Ibn ʿArafah — despite his veneration of the well-known (mashhūr) position in the school — [acted] upon the Sunnah in this matter. His student, the Imām al-Ubbī, narrated from him that he used to perform supererogatory prayers after the ʿaṣr. It was said to him regarding that, and he replied: "I only do it on the day when my customary devotion (muʿtādī) escapes me." And he narrated from him that he said to another: "Nothing comes from prayer except good." And he also narrated from him that he used to conclude his nightly standing (qiyām) by reciting Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ after al-Fātiḥah, reciting it ten times, counting them on his fingers — and he did not consider counting to be idle occupation (shughl) in prayer. He did this due to the authentic report (al-khabar al-ṣaḥīḥ), concluding with {«قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ»}.

And it was transmitted from him that he used to perform supererogatory prayers during his journey for the pilgrimage while walking, due to his permitting that — contrary to Mālik. And consider, from this same meaning, what ʿIyāḍ narrated from Ibn Wahb, who said: "I imposed upon myself that whenever I backbit a person, I would fast a day — and that became easy for me. So I imposed upon myself that whenever I backbit a person, I would give a dirham in charity — and that became heavy upon me, and I abandoned backbiting."

And consider also: Ibn Bashkuwāl has transmitted with his chain of narration that whoever hears of the virtue of an act and performs that act hoping for that reward, Allah will give him that reward — even if what reached him was not true.

In summary: The one who desires the Hereafter — if he finds a seller for good, whether through following (iqtidāʾ), or through hearing (istimāʿ), or through a vision (ruʾyā) like the vision of al-Kattānī mentioned before this — let him take it from Allah. Al-Shāṭibī said in his ḥawādith: "Along with the texts of all the imāms that a vision is not used as evidence for a legal ruling."

title_en: On Seizing Opportunities for Good Deeds and the Etiquette of the Rightly Guided Seekers
arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 198

منهج افزفي/ العف ادن مقام خواص الملدد من لم يكن من تصير كاف الأونات فليجتهد في نر الأرات القاضة.

وروى الحافظ أبو عمر بسئده أن الغازي بن قيس لما رحل إلى المديئة
اليسمع عن مالك دخل ابن أبي ذؤيب مسجد النبي يل فجلس ولم يركع؛ فقال له
الغازي بن قيس: قم فاركع؛ فإن جلوسك دون ركوع جهل بالسنة: ونحو هذا من
جفاء القول؛ فقام ابن أبي ذؤيب فركع؛ ثم أسند ظهره وتحلق الناس إليه؛ فلما رأى
ذلك الغازي بن قيس خجل وندمء فسأل عنه فقيل: هو ابن أبي ذؤيب أحد فقهاء
المدينة وأشرفهم: فقام يعتذر إليه فقال له: يا أي لا عليك أمرتنا فأطعناك.

.وتقل ابن المبارك أن عبد لله بن عمر رضي الله عنهما مر بمقبرة؛ فنزل فصلى
فسثل عن ذلك؛ فقال: ذكرت أهل القبور وما حيل بينهم وبينه؛ فأحبيت أن
أتقرب إلى الله بهما. ونقل أيضًا أن رسول الله يق قال: "من فتح له باب من االخير
فلينتهزه؛ فإنه لا يدري متى يغلق عنه'"21.

وانظر أيضًا نادرة من نوادر ابن العربي حي
نعمت الفائدة» حديث موضوع؛ لا يحل لمسلم اعتقاده؛ أما أنا فأقول: سورة
(المائدة) نعمت الفائدة؛ ولا نأثره عن أحد؛ ولكنه كلام حسن. اله

فكذلك أنت أيها المريد إذا عشرت على خبر بفعل خير أو كلام طيب ووقع
موقا من قلبك فقل: اسمع من الله وطبب به وقنك؛ ولا نأئ
على السرد الذي قاله السيد مفتي تونس البرزلي؛ إذا شهد الشرع باعتبار جنسه
وليس في الأصول ما يخالفه فاغتنمه. وتقدم قول ابن العربي في سجدة الشكر ولم
تكره؛ والسجود لله دائما هو الواجب؛ فإن وجدت أدنى سبب للسجود فاغتنم.

وقد تقدم لابن رشد وأبي عمر أن هذه الأمور قصارى أمرها إن أثبت على
تركها على قول لا يضرك فعلها كما قاله في الصلاة على الميت بالمسجد؛ وترجو
أجرها على قول؛ وتقدم قول الشاطبي أن السلف عدوا من لم يعمر أنقاسه بطالا
وسرمدوا الصوم والعبادة؛ قال: وإنما نهى الشارع عن ذلك خوف الحرج؛ فإذا أمن
الحرج فلا حرج فعلى قول الشاطبي: البعض الذي تلتزمه أنت مطلوب على
ملهبه أن يكون سرمثاء فإن لم تخص ولا تسرمد فلا أدري مآخلك والذي ختم به

قال: حديث: سورة (المائدة»

‎٠‏ عن أحد إذا كان

‏ا) أخرجه لبن المبارك (38/1. رقم 117). وأخرجه أيضًاء هناد (473/2 رقم 861» والقضاعي
268/1 رقم 35ه.

# PageV1P199
anchors:
- Root: غ-ن-م (gh-n-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To acquire spoils; to seize an opportunity before it is lost.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The believer's active pursuit of divine reward (thawāb) as a form of spiritual gain.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally for war-booty; metaphorically extended to any chance for righteous action.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-sharṭ) — The protasis (condition) and apodosis (result) govern the ethical imperative, as in "if you find... then seize."
translation:
I say — and this is the way of the elite among the rightly guided: Whoever is not among those whose station is firmly established in the higher ranks, let him strive diligently in seizing the opportunities that present themselves.

The Ḥāfiẓ Abū ʿUmar narrated with his chain that when al-Ghāzī ibn Qays traveled to Medina to hear from Mālik, he entered the Prophet's mosque — may God bless him and grant him peace — and saw Ibn Abī Dhu'ayb sitting without having performed the two rakʿahs of greeting. Al-Ghāzī said to him: "Stand and pray, for your sitting without the prayer is ignorance of the Sunnah" — and this was somewhat harsh in its wording. So Ibn Abī Dhu'ayb stood and prayed, then leaned his back and the people gathered around him. When al-Ghāzī saw this, he was embarrassed and regretted his words. He asked about the man and was told: "He is Ibn Abī Dhu'ayb, one of the jurists of Medina and the most noble among them." So al-Ghāzī stood to apologize to him, and Ibn Abī Dhu'ayb said: "O uncle, no harm upon you — you commanded us and we obeyed."

It is also transmitted from Ibn al-Mubārak that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar — may God be pleased with them both — passed by a cemetery, dismounted, and prayed. When asked about this, he said: "I remembered the people of the graves and what has come between them and this act; so I wished to draw near to God through it." It is also transmitted that the Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — said: {«Whoever has a door of goodness opened for him, let him seize it, for he does not know when it will be closed against him»}.

And consider also this anecdote from the rare sayings of Ibn al-ʿArabī: He was asked about a ḥadīth, and he said: "What an excellent benefit!" Then he said: "It is a fabricated ḥadīth; it is not lawful for a Muslim to believe it. As for me, I say: Sūrat al-Māʾidah — what an excellent benefit! And I do not transmit it from anyone, but it is good speech."

So likewise, O seeker (murīd), when you come upon a report of a good deed or a fine saying, and it settles in your heart, say: "I hear from God and I am pleased with it and I accept it." And do not be like the one who follows only what the master Muftī of Tunis, al-Burzulī, said — rather, if the Sacred Law testifies to the validity of its kind, and there is nothing in the principles (uṣūl) that contradicts it, then seize it. And the saying of Ibn al-ʿArabī has preceded regarding the prostration of thanks (sajdat al-shukr) — it is not disliked; and prostrating to God always is the obligatory act. So if you find the slightest cause for prostration, seize it.

It has also preceded from Ibn Rushd and Abū ʿUmar that these matters, at their utmost, if one persists in abandoning them, according to one opinion, do not harm you if you do them — as was said regarding the prayer over the deceased in the mosque — and you hope for their reward according to another opinion. And the saying of al-Shāṭibī has preceded that the early generations (salaf) counted as idle those who did not occupy their souls [with worship], and they made continuous fasting and devotion their constant practice. He said: "The Lawgiver only forbade that out of fear of hardship; so if hardship is removed, then there is no prohibition." So according to al-Shāṭibī's opinion, the particular practice you commit yourself to is required, on his school, to be continuous. But if you neither specify nor make it continuous, then I do not know what your outcome will be. And that with which he concluded — he said: "The ḥadīth of Sūrat al-Māʾidah — what an excellent benefit!" — is not transmitted from anyone when it is [fabricated].

title_en: On the Virtue of Voluntary Prayers and the Strength of Communal Devotion
arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 199

ميج في شه مغ خوفض للد نكن من تس كع أرق يجيد لي تس ارت طاضة___ 303
أبن يونس ديوانه الفقهي فا القليل خير من ترك الجميع.

ولما تكلم أبو عمر على فول رسول اله ول: "استقيموا ولن تحصوا”" قال
أأبو عمر: ولقد أحسن القائل”:

افعل الخير ما استطعت وإن كان قليلا فلن تحيط يكله

ومتى تفعل الكثير من الخير إذاكنت تاركالأقلله

والشيء يذكر بالشيء: قال الله سبحانه: وير سك عَع لسوت تنكم
بالَدَؤة ولي رْيدُود وه وَلَاعَدُ مَك عنم 4 [الكهف: 28]. قال السساء
الصوفية: كل مؤمن راغب في عبادة الله إلا أن الشهوة تغلبه؛ ويزيل ذلك مشاهدة
تعبد غيره؛ فيشق عليه أن يسبق إلى العبادة؛ فيجد من نفسه زيادة باعث على العيادة»
وقد يكون هذا في الملا فيظن المريد أن هذا منه رياء وليس كذ

قال في "الإحياء”: قد تبكي جماعة فينظر إليهم فيحضره البكاء؛ فيظن المرء أن
ذلك رياء: لأنه لو كان وحده لما بكى؛ وليس كذلك؛ فإنه لو سمع بكاءهم من
حيث لا يرونه لبكى: فحصل أن التأسي والاقتداء يقويان باعث الخير. قال ابن أبي
زيد في رسالته: وإن تتفل بست ركعات فحسن. وكان سيدي ابن سراج رحمه الله
قط ما ابتدأ بنا الحزب بعد المغرب حتى يتتفل بست ركعات بعد المغرب؛ ويدعو
ويؤمن المؤقت على دعائه؛ وحيتذ يبدأ الحزب. ومن محرمتي أني كنت أستتقص
هنا وأنوي أن أركع بلا تحديد فيلومني. هذا ما وجدت تنعما بمختاري مرة أزيد

ذا أخرجه الطيالسي (ص 134؛ رقم 8996 وأحمد (276/5: رقم 22432 واين ماجة (101/1:
ارقم 277 والدارمي (174/1؛ رقم 655» قال البوصيري (41/1): هذا الحديث رجاله ثقات
أبات, إلا أنه منقطع بين سالم وثوبان:فإنه لم سمع منه بلا خلاف؛ لكن له طرق أخرى
متصلة. وان حبان (311/7 رقم 1037) والطبراني (101/2 رقم 1444) والحاكم 220/1
ارقم 447)» واليهقي (52/1: رقم 389). وأخرجه أيضا الطبراني في الشامين (277/3
رقم 1335), وفي الصغير (27/1. رقم 08 والروياتي (404/1, رقم 614). قال المناوي:

# PageV1P200
anchors:
- Root: ق-ل-ل (q-l-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Smallness in quantity; scarcity; the opposite of abundance (kathrah).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the theological context, refers to the minimal act of obedience that preserves one's covenant with God, as opposed to total abandonment.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used here in its literal sense (ḥaqīqah) of "little" — not metaphorically — contrasting with "abandoning all" (tark al-jamīʿ).
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Response Construction (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb) — The verse "If you do good... you will never encompass it" establishes a protasis-apodosis relation where the response is negated to emphasize human limitation.
translation:
I say: The little [good] is better than abandoning the whole.

When Abū ʿUmar commented on the saying of the Messenger of God ﷺ: "Be upright, and you will never encompass it," he said: How excellent is the saying of the poet:

"Do good as much as you are able — even if it be little, for you will never encompass it all.

And when will you do much good, if you are one who abandons even the little?"

And one thing is recalled by another: God the Exalted said: {«وَاصْبِرْ نَفْسَكَ مَعَ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُم بِالْغَدَاةِ وَالْعَشِيِّ يُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَهُ وَلَا تَعْدُ عَيْنَاكَ عَنْهُمْ»} [Al-Kahf: 28]. The Sufi masters said: Every believer is desirous of worshipping God, except that desire (shahwah) overcomes him; and that is removed by witnessing the devotion of others — for it becomes hard upon him that another should precede him in worship, and he finds within himself an increased impulse toward devotion. This may occur in a gathering, and the aspirant (murīd) may think this is from him a show of ostentation (riyāʾ) — but it is not so.

He said in the "Iḥyāʾ": A group may weep, and one looks at them, and weeping comes upon him; then he thinks this is ostentation, because were he alone he would not weep. But it is not so — for were he to hear their weeping without seeing them, he would weep. Thus it is established that emulation (taʾassī) and following (iqtidāʾ) strengthen the impulse toward good.

Ibn Abī Zayd said in his Risālah: "And if you pray six supererogatory rakʿahs, that is good." And my master Ibn Sirāj — may God have mercy on him — never began the ḥizb with us after the Maghrib until he had prayed six rakʿahs after Maghrib, and he would supplicate, and the timekeeper would say "Amen" to his supplication; then he would begin the ḥizb. And from my own shortcomings is that I used to be exacting here, intending to pray without a fixed number, and he would reproach me. This is what I found of favor in my choice — sometimes I increase, sometimes I decrease.

### | الصفحة 200

‎١ 44‏ ميج فون عافن مقع عولض لدان لم سكن عي كل ازاك فيجهد في نمه الراك قاض
كأني أعمل يدا على ربي وأكثر الاوقات أثرك التنفل بالكلية وأركع ركعتين بلا تأس
.ولا باقتداء ولا كما كان يقول سيدي المتتوري رحمه الله اسمع من لله.

‏وظهر في ما قاله محبي الدين من لم يعند الملازمة للوظيف؛ عرضه للتفو,
قال: وينبغي أن بتداركه في وقت آخر. فإنه إذا تساهل في قضائه سهل عليه تضييعه
في وقنه؛ وكذا قال في "الإحياء': من عاقه عائق عن ورد كان له فلا يرخص لنفسه
في ترك قضائه؛ بل يتداركه في وقت آخخر؛ كي لا تميل نفسه للدعة والرفاهية
وتداركه حسن على سبيل المجاهدة لنفسه؛ لا على أن ذلك فرض لازم؛ ثم اطلعمت
على نص الحاوي لما به الفتيا في مذهب الشافعي قال: المؤقنة من النوافل تقضى
أبدا إلا المتعلقة يسبب كالكسوف.

‏فيا ليتتي أيها الإنسان في هذه الست الركعات» اقتديت بابن أبي زيد في رسالته
وتأسيت فيها بشيخي ابن سراجء أو كنت التزمت قضاءها على ما قال محبي الدين
إن لم أكن صدقت أنها تعدل عبادة اثنتي عشرة سنة؛ وأيضًا كنت كأني صليتها إذا
كان قد صدني عنها صاد قفي الصحيح: 'إذا مرض العبد أو سافر كتب له ما كان
يعمل صحيسًا مقيمًا”'. وكذلك أيضا الخبر الآخر: "من كانت له صلاة ليل فغلبته
عيناه كتبت له صلاته وكان نومه صدقة عليه”0.

‏وقد كنث بصدد أن بتفق لي في ذلك في صيام النصف من شعبان» فكنث

.بالواجب. وأتباعه يتقربون إلى لله بأكل يوم النصف من شعبان: مع أن المذعب

‏كله؛ ابن يونس وابن أبي زيد وابن عرفة في ديوانه الفنقهي نص على تخصيص الأيام
