# PageV1P220
anchors:
- Root: و-س-ل (w-s-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To seek nearness, to attach oneself; "al-wasīlah" is a means of approach, a station of closeness.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the Qur'anic invocation, "al-wasīlah" is the highest rank in Paradise reserved for the Prophet ﷺ, a means of intercession and proximity to Allah.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: a connection or link. Metaphorical: the spiritual station of the Prophet ﷺ as the supreme intermediary.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The phrase "al-wasīlah wa-l-faḍīlah" functions as explanatory apposition, clarifying the nature of the requested gift.

- Root: ج-د-د (j-d-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Newness, renewal; "al-jadīdān" (the two new ones) refers to night and day, perpetually renewed.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Time as a continuous creation (khalq jadīd), each moment a fresh divine act.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: two new things. Metaphorical: night and day as two sentinels (ḥarasān) seizing the reins of creation until the Resurrection.
- Sībawayh Rule: Ḥāl (Circumstantial Clause) — "wa-kulluhumā qad akhadhā bi-majāmiʿinā" is a circumstantial clause describing the state of the two sentinels.
translation:
I say — and success is with Allah:

Know that the Prophet ﷺ taught his community to conclude the call to prayer with the supplication for the means (al-wasīlah) and the excellence (al-faḍīlah), saying: «O Allah, Lord of this perfect call and of the established prayer, grant Muhammad the means and the excellence, and raise him to the praiseworthy station which Thou hast promised him.» And in the ḥadīth: When Bilāl made the call and said, "The prayer is established," the Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah has established it and made it enduring."

Then, regarding the fourth litany (al-wird al-rābiʿ), the Sayyid al-Sāḥilī said in his poem on spiritual wayfaring (qaṣīdat al-sulūk):

"Divide your litany into two portions, O youth — take half between the two evening prayers in solitude, and take the remaining half after dawn."

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his guest.» Tāj al-Dīn said: "The day is a guest, and the night is a guest." Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib said: "There is no night that comes except it calls out: 'I am a new night; I have never passed over you before, and I shall never pass over you again after this. So work in me for good, for you shall be questioned about what you do in me.'"

Al-Maqqarī said, verbatim: "It is reported that Ibn Shāṭir used to say: 'The two new ones (al-jadīdān) are two sentinels — one white, one black — and both have seized hold of our forelocks until the Day of Resurrection.' Then he would recite: {To Him is the return} [Ghāfir: 43]."

And on the authority of al-Fuḍayl: "It has reached us that Allah, Glorified and Exalted, says: 'O son of Adam, remember Me for an hour after the morning prayer and an hour after the afternoon prayer, and I shall suffice you for what is between them.'"

And in al-Tirmidhī and others: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «Whoever prays the dawn prayer in congregation, then sits remembering Allah until the sun rises, then prays two rakʿahs, shall have the reward of a complete Ḥajj and ʿUmrah — complete, complete, complete.»

And in "al-Iḥyāʾ": Among the honors of this time (the morning) is that Allah swore by it, saying: {By the dawn} [Al-Fajr: 1], and praised it in His saying: {And the dawn when it breathes} [Al-Takwīr: 18], and manifested His power by the contraction of the shadow therein — for it is the time of the contraction of the night's shadow by the spreading of the sun's light — and guided people to glorification (tasbīḥ) therein by His saying, Mighty and Majestic: {So glorify Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning} [Al-Rūm: 17], and {And glorify Him in the night and after the prostrations} [Qāf: 40], and {And glorify Him in the night and at the ends of the day} [Ṭā Hā: 130], and {And remember the name of your Lord in the morning and the evening} [Al-Insān: 25]. Thus, among the litanies of this time is glorification (tasbīḥ). In the Ṣaḥīḥ, on the authority of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: «Whoever says 'Glory be to Allah and with His praise' one hundred times in a day, his sins are wiped away, even if they were like the foam of the sea.» And in the Ṣaḥīḥ, on the authority of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: «Is any of you unable to earn a thousand good deeds each day?» It was said: "How can one earn a thousand good deeds?" He said: «He glorifies (says subḥānallāh) one hundred times, and a thousand good deeds are written for him, and a thousand sins are erased from him.» Likewise also: "Glory be to Allah, the Magnificent" (subḥānallāh al-ʿaẓīm).

He said in "al-Iḥyāʾ": That you mention at this time ten remembrances (adhkār), each repeated ten times, is better than a single remembrance repeated one hundred times — for each one has its own distinct virtue. On this basis: "Glory be to Allah" (subḥānallāh) is one remembrance; "Glory be to Allah and with His praise" (subḥānallāh wa-bi-ḥamdih) is a remembrance; "Glory be to Allah, the Magnificent" (subḥānallāh al-ʿaẓīm) is a remembrance; "There is no god but Allah" (lā ilāha illallāh) is a remembrance; "There is no god but Allah, the Clear Truth" (lā ilāha illallāh al-ḥaqq al-mubīn) is a remembrance; "There is no god but Allah alone, without partner; to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs all praise, and He has power over all things" is a remembrance; the praise (al-ḥamdalah) is a remembrance; the ḥawqalah (lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā billāh) is a remembrance; the ḥasbalah (ḥasbunā Allāh wa-niʿma al-wakīl) is a remembrance; and the takbīr (Allāhu akbar) is a remembrance. These are ten remembrances — that one say each of them ten times is more virtuous than a single remembrance one hundred times. However, Muḥyī al-Dīn al-Nawawī said: "It is fitting that at the beginning of the day one repeat 'There is no god but Allah alone, without partner; to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs all praise, and He has power over all things' one hundred times, so that it may be a protection for him on that day until evening, as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ informed us." And likewise in the narration of Abū Dāwūd and Ibn Mājah.

# PageV1P221
anchors:
- Root: ع-ق-د (ʿ-q-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To bind, tie, or contract; a firm resolution or covenant.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The act of affirming a pledge with the heart, often used for the declaration of tawḥīd as a binding spiritual contract.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical tying; metaphorical for the soul's firm adherence to divine unity.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The protasis (e.g., "if he says") governs the apodosis, indicating a causal spiritual reward contingent upon the action.
translation:
I say — and success is from God alone: Know that the remembrance of tahlīl (the declaration of God's oneness) has been transmitted with varying stations of merit, as the scholars have clarified. When one utters this very tahlīl ten times immediately after the sunset prayer (al-maghrib), it is also recorded in al-Tirmidhī: "Whoever says it thus, God sends forth for him a protective guard (maslaḥah) who will undertake his defense from Satan until he reaches the morning." Al-Nawawī said: "Maslaḥah means a company of guards." And just as the fortification (taḥaṣṣun) may be realized by virtue of this hadith, so too it may be solely for the sake of reward — and that applies to the one who confines himself to mentioning it ten times; for the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "It is as if he had freed four souls from the descendants of Ismāʿīl." And just as it may be for the mere attainment of reward, so too it may serve to repel sin (darʾ al-wizr). It is transmitted in 'al-Ḥilyah' that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "There is no servant who says, at the time of his returning to God: 'There is no god but God alone, with no partner; His is the sovereignty and His is the praise, and He is over all things powerful' — except that God forgives him his sins, even if they were like the foam of the sea." And you should make this your constant practice on the Day of ʿArafah, due to the saying of the Messenger of God ﷺ: "The best of supplications is the supplication of the Day of ʿArafah; and the best of what I and the prophets before me have said is: 'There is no god but God alone, with no partner; His is the sovereignty and His is the praise, and He is over all things powerful.'" See the supplication of the Day of ʿArafah in 'al-Ḥilyah'. Likewise also in 'al-Tamhīd', concerning the mention of "There is no god but the Sovereign, the Clear Truth" — that whoever says it one hundred times will have a security from poverty and from the loneliness of the grave, and will draw near the door of wealth, and will knock upon the door of Paradise.

Among the litanies (awrād) of this time as well is the seeking of forgiveness (al-istighfār). Abū Bakr al-Waqqār, one of the scholars of our school (madhhab), has transmitted: "Whoever desires that his wealth increase and that he be blessed in his provision, let him say seventy times each day: 'I seek forgiveness of God, my Lord; indeed, He is the Forgiving.'" And in the Ṣaḥīḥ, the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Indeed, my heart is veiled, and I seek forgiveness of God one hundred times in the day."

title_en: On the Litany of Seeking Forgiveness and the Devotional Formula (Hijr) of the Prophets and Companions

# PageV1P222
anchors:
- Root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Covering, veiling, and effacing sin; the root implies protection from the consequence of an act.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine forgiveness (maghfirah) as the concealment of sin and the granting of immunity from its punishment—a theological act of divine mercy.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense of covering; metaphorically (majāz) used for the remission of sins, as God "covers" the servant's faults.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The sequence of Prophetic and Companion formulas is coordinated by apposition, each term clarifying the specific devotional practice of the named figure.
translation:
I say: And from Ibn ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him): "We used to count for the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) in a single gathering one hundred times: 'My Lord, forgive me and turn unto me; verily You are the Oft-Returning, the Most Merciful.'"

And among the litanies (awrād) of this time is also the invocation of blessings upon the Prophet (al-taṣliyah). And it is likely that the constant devotional formula (hijr) of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was seeking forgiveness (al-istighfār). The hijr of Abū Bakr (may God be pleased with him) was: "There is no god but God" (lā ilāha illā Allāh). The hijr of ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him) was: "God is Greater" (Allāhu akbar). The hijr of ʿUthmān (may God be pleased with him) was: "Glory be to God" (subḥān Allāh). And the hijr of ʿAlī (may God be pleased with him) was: "Praise be to God" (al-ḥamdu lillāh). Thus it behooves every person to have a hijr that befits his station (maqām) and accords with his state (ḥāl). And if on Friday there be no impediment among the obstacles, then let his hijr be the invocation of blessings upon the Prophet. And among what I have chosen as my own hijr in this world and the Hereafter is the formula of returning (al-istirjāʿ) and the formula of reckoning (al-ḥasbalah), until we meet death... For even if there were nothing in the istirjāʿ except the saying of the author of the book *Istinzāl al-Luṭf al-Mawjūd* (The Descent of Existing Grace), for he said, verbatim: "The foundation of what the seeker of the descent of existing grace aims at, in the captivity of calamities, is the employment of the istirjāʿ—either by its condition of sincerity (ikhlāṣ), or by its state (ḥāl). For God has singled it out for that, and the state of the elite (al-khāṣṣah) is not repeated."

As for the ḥasbalah, there has already preceded the saying of Maʿrūf al-Karkhī: "Whoever calls upon God by it, finds God with him." He says it for his religion and his worldly affairs, and for what concerns him, and for the one who oppresses him; and at death, and at the questioning in the grave, and at the Reckoning, and at the Balance, and at the Bridge (al-ṣirāṭ). I say myself: And he will not cease to utter the istirjāʿ and the ḥasbalah until he enters Paradise, God willing. And it has already preceded that the intention (al-maqṣad) in remembrance (al-dhikr) is like the spirit in relation to the body, and like the meaning in relation to the utterance. And He, glorified be He, has said: {«إِنَّمَا ذَٰلِكُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ يُخَوِّفُ أَوْلِيَاءَهُ فَلَا تَخَافُوهُمْ وَخَافُونِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ»} [Āl ʿImrān: 175]. And God described the people of Paradise as saying: {«قَالُوا إِنَّا كُنَّا قَبْلُ فِي أَهْلِنَا مُشْفِقِينَ»} [al-Ṭūr: 26]. So let a person perceive this within himself, and say: "O God, verily I am afflicted by sins; and I—by Him whom there is no god but He—am fearful on account of them, supplicating unto Thee with the istirjāʿ and the ḥasbalah."

# PageV1P224
anchors:
- Root: ر-ج-ع (r-j-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Return, reverting to a prior state or origin; the act of turning back.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Qur'anic usage, the return to God (al-rajʿ ilā Allāh) signifies the eschatological restoration of the creature to its Creator, affirming divine sovereignty over life and death.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical return; metaphorical (majāz) for the soul's submission and acknowledgment of God's decree in affliction.
- Root: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Sufficiency, reckoning, or counting; one who is enough for another's need.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theological reliance (tawakkul) — declaring God alone as the sufficient Guardian, negating all creaturely agency in ultimate provision and protection.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): In the phrase «حَسْبُنَا اللهُ» it is a performative declaration of trust, not mere information; it enacts reliance.
- Root: ه-ج-ر (h-j-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To abandon, migrate, or persist in a habit; the continuous practice (dāba) that one clings to.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In spiritual path terminology, the "habitual litany" (hijīrā) is the constant invocation that becomes the soul's second nature, guarding the heart from heedlessness.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical migration; metaphorical for the soul's persistent devotion as a "migration" toward God.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Emphasis by Repetition (Takrār li-l-Tawkīd) — Repeating a phrase (e.g., "hijīrāy" three times) serves to affirm and intensify the speaker's commitment, a recognized rhetorical-syntactic device in Arabic.
translation:
I say — and God grants success:

Know that when the servant is stricken by an affliction, a loss, or a calamity, the sunnah of the rightly guided is to utter the istirjāʿ — «إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ» — and the ḥasbala — «حَسْبُنَا اللهُ وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ». For God — exalted is He — has praised both groups in His decisive Book. He said of those who uttered the istirjāʿ: «أُولَٰئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ صَلَوَاتٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ وَرَحْمَةٌ وَأُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْمُهْتَدُونَ» [Al-Baqarah: 157]. And He said of those who uttered the ḥasbala: «فَانْقَلَبُوا بِنِعْمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَفَضْلٍ لَمْ يَمْسَسْهُمْ سُوءٌ» [Āl ʿImrān: 174]. So blessed are they — the first group received prayers and mercy from their Lord for their words: «إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ»; and the second group returned with grace and bounty, untouched by evil, for their words: «حَسْبُنَا اللهُ وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ».

And I, O my Lord, say as they said, hoping that You will bestow upon me the like of what You bestowed upon them. So I say: «إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ»; «حَسْبِيَ اللهُ وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ». I repeat this, then I add: "O Allah, fulfill Your promise, and accept my istirjāʿ and my ḥasbala, just as You accepted the istirjāʿ and ḥasbala of others before me, O Most Merciful of the merciful."

And if not — then the istirjāʿ and the ḥasbala are my constant litany (hijīrāy). Even if You chastise me, they remain my litany. Even if You chastise me, they remain my litany. That is, I shall not cease — until I cross the bridge of Jahannam — repeating: «إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ»; «حَسْبِيَ اللهُ وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ». So praise be to God, then praise be to Him who has granted me and others the inspiration of these words, and guided me to them, and refined me by them. And I return to that: «إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ»; «حَسْبِيَ اللهُ وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ».

Let this be your constant practice (dāba). And if you wish, you may add: "God is sufficient for me for my religion; God is sufficient for me for my worldly life; God, the Generous, is sufficient for me for what concerns me; God, the Forbearing, the Strong, is sufficient for me against whoever oppresses me or oppresses another through me; God, the Severe, is sufficient for me against whoever plots against me or plots evil against me; God, the Merciful, the Compassionate, is sufficient for me at the moment of death; God, the Kind, is sufficient for me at the questioning in the grave; God, the Generous, is sufficient for me at the Reckoning; God, the Subtle, is sufficient for me at the Balance; God, the Powerful, is sufficient for me at the Bridge (al-Ṣirāṭ); God — there is no god but He — upon Him I rely, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne."

And if you fall into a dire strait (warṭah), then your litany should be what the Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — taught to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib — may God be pleased with him. He said to him: "O ʿAlī, shall I not teach you words that, if you fall into a strait, you will say?" ʿAlī said: "Yes, may God make me your ransom." He said: "Say: In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate; and there is no might and no power except with God, the Exalted, the Mighty."

And it has already preceded what one's litany should be when struck by worry, fear, calamity, or pain. He said in the "Risālah": "The remembrance (dhikr) as a constant litany is the tongue of the lovers and the salutation of those who have arrived, from among the wayfarers to the presence of the Lord of the worlds. It is the worship whose exterior is rewards, whose interior is presence (ḥuḍūr), and whose innermost interior is light upon light. It guards the limbs, preserves the time, repels heedlessness, opens the door of intimacy, and guarantees good in every state." And the saying of Nāj al-Dīn has already preceded: "Do not abandon the remembrance due to your lack of presence with God in it, for your heedlessness in it is better than your heedlessness of it."

And he said in the "Risālah": "The remembrance is the mainstay (al-ʿumdah) in this path; no one reaches God except through the constancy of remembrance." For God — exalted is He — said: «وَمَنْ يَعْشُ عَنْ ذِكْرِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ نُقَيِّضْ لَهُ شَيْطَانًا فَهُوَ لَهُ قَرِينٌ» [Al-Zukhruf: 36]; and He said: «فَاذْكُرُونِي أَذْكُرْكُمْ» [Al-Baqarah: 152]; and He said: «يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ ذِكْرًا كَثِيرًا» [Al-Aḥzāb: 41]; and He said: «يُسَبِّحُونَ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ لَا يَفْتُرُونَ» [Al-Anbiyāʾ: 20]. And he said in the "Ṣiḥāḥ": "Al-hijīr is the constant habit and custom; likewise al-hijīrā — it is said: 'Such-and-such has remained his hijīrā,' meaning his persistent practice and custom."

And among the litanies (awrād) of this time is the recitation for protection. Al-Nawawī said: "Whoever recites Āyat al-Kursī and the beginning of Sūrat Ghāfir — from «غَافِرِ الذَّنْبِ» to «إِلَيْهِ الْمَصِيرُ» [Ghāfir: 3] — is protected that day from every evil; and likewise, whoever recites it upon evening is guarded by it until morning." So you say, in your orientation (tawajjuh) after reciting the Fātiḥah: "O Allah, I present before You, in front of every breath, every moment, every glance, every thought, and every blink of the eye of the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth, and everything that in Your knowledge is coming to be or has already been — I present before all of that: «اللهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ»."

And it is related from al-Fuḍayl: "Whoever recites the closing of Sūrat al-Ḥashr upon morning, God seals him with the seal of the martyrs." And it is related: "Whoever recites «فَسُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ حِينَ تُمْسُونَ وَحِينَ تُصْبِحُونَ» to «وَكَذَٰلِكَ تُخْرَجُونَ» [Al-Rūm: 17–19] upon morning and upon evening, he attains what he missed in his day and his night" — from Abū Dāwūd. Likewise, whoever recites «أَفَحَسِبْتُمْ أَنَّمَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ عَبَثًا» [Al-Muʾminūn: 115] — al-Sarāwī said: "The Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — sent us on a raid, and commanded us to recite upon evening and morning: «أَفَحَسِبْتُمْ أَنَّمَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ عَبَثًا». So we recited it, and we gained spoils and returned safely." And likewise also: «لَقَدْ جَاءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ مِنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ» [Al-Tawbah: 128] — and the like of that from the protective verses.

# PageV1P225
anchors:
- Root: ن-م-و (n-m-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Growth, increase, augmentation in quantity or virtue
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Spiritual increase through supererogatory acts (nawāfil) when obligatory works are deficient
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal growth of crops vs. metaphorical growth of devotional merit
- Root: ك-ف-ي (k-f-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Sufficiency, that which removes need or harm
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine sufficiency (kifāyah) as the believer's ultimate reliance (tawakkul)
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal provision vs. metaphorical protection from all anxieties
- Root: ج-و-ر (j-w-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Neighborliness, protection granted to a neighbor (ijārah)
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine amnesty and safeguarding from punishment
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal asylum vs. spiritual immunity from Hellfire
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The protasis (in) governs the apodosis (fa-inna), with the response clause marked by fa- to indicate the consequent reward.
translation:
I say — may Allah grant us success:

Whoever is unable to perform the supererogatory prayers (nawāfil) at all times should strive to increase his litanies (awrād) for their great virtue.

Then he should recite the verse: {«لَقَدْ جَاءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ مِنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ عَزِيزٌ عَلَيْهِ مَا عَنِتُّمْ حَرِيصٌ عَلَيْكُمْ بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ رَءُوفٌ رَحِيمٌ»} [Al-Tawbah: 128] — "There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves. Grievous to him is what you suffer; he is concerned over you and to the believers is kind and merciful."

Then he should say seven times: "Ḥasbiya Allāhu lā ilāha illā huwa ʿalayhi tawakkaltu wa-huwa rabbu al-ʿarshi al-ʿaẓīm" — "Allah is sufficient for me; there is no deity except Him; upon Him I rely, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne." Allah — Mighty and Majestic — will suffice you against whatever concerns you from the affairs of this world and the Hereafter. This was transmitted in "Al-Ḥilyah" from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

And the Sayyid Muḥyī al-Dīn al-Nawawī said: We have related many hadiths concerning the recitation of certain sūrahs during the day and night. Among them: (Yā Sīn) — whoever recites it in a day and night, his sins are forgiven. And Sūrat (Al-Dukhān) — whoever recites it, he awakens forgiven. And Sūrat (Al-Wāqiʿah) — the one who recites it every night will never be afflicted by poverty. And (Tabāraka al-Mulk).

My master Ibn Sirāj — may Allah have mercy on him — used to command its recitation in his sermon, along with the recitation of Sūrat (Qāf), and that its recitation eases the agonies of death. And from Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī, and others, with authentic chains, from Khubayb who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Say" — and I did not say anything. Then he said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, what shall I say? He said: "Say: 'Qul huwa Allāhu aḥad' (Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ) and 'al-Muʿawwidhatayn' (Sūrat al-Falaq and al-Nās) when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning, three times; they will suffice you against everything."

And from the litanies of this time also: the supplication from the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, from Muslim ibn al-Ḥārith: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ confided to him and said: "When you depart from the Maghrib prayer, say: 'Allāhumma ajirnī min al-nār' — 'O Allah, protect me from the Fire' — seven times. For if you say that and then die that night, protection (ijārah) from it will be written for you. And when you pray the Fajr, say likewise; for if you die that day, protection from it will be written for you."

And in the Ṣaḥīḥ: That a man said: O Messenger of Allah, what about the scorpion that stung me last night? He ﷺ said: "If you had said when you entered the evening: 'Aʿūdhu bi-kalimāti Allāhi al-tāmmāti min sharri mā khalaq' — 'I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created' — three times, it would not have harmed you." Likewise the Basmalah transmitted from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, three times.

title_en: Section 172 — The Morning and Evening Remembrances (Adhkār al-Ṣabāḥ wa al-Masā')
arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 225

ميج في شم هن غم عرض للد من لمكن من نس كل رك يجيد لي مسر الات طاضة 369
مرات في المساء وثلاث مرات إذا أصبحت لم يضرك شيء؛ وقد ختم بها الشاذلي
حزب البحر؛ وروينه عن شيخي المنتوري؛ والتزمت قراءته كلل يوم وليلة وكذلك

أيضا: اللهم إني أصبحت أشهدك وأشهد حملة عرشك وملائكتك وجميع خلقك

إنك أنت الله لا إله إلا أنت وحدك لا شريك لك وأن محمدًا عبدك ورسولك.

وورد الخبر: 'إن قلت حين تمسي وحين تصبح أربع مرات أعتقك الله من
النار"؛ وكذلك إن قلت حين تصبح وحين تمسي: اللهم ما أصبح بي من نعمة قمنك
وحدك لااشريك لك. فلك الحمد ولك الشكرء فتكون قد أديت شكر يومك أو
اليلتك» وكذلك إن قلت ثلاث مرات حين تصبح وثلاث مرات حين تمسي: اللهم
أصبحت منك في نعمة وعافية وسترء اللهم فأتم نعمتك علي وعافيتك وسترك في
الدنيا والآخرة؛ إلا أنم لله عليك يفضله ورحمته؛ وحيثما تقدم من ذكر أصبح يكون
هذا اللفظ عند أول اليوم وعند أول الليل يكون بلفظ أمسى؛ ولم يكن النبي يكل يدع
هذه الدعوات حين يمسي وحين يصبح: "اللهم إني أسألك العافية في الدنيا
والآخرة؛ اللهم إني أسألك العفو والعافية في ديني ودنياي وأهلي ومالي؛ اللهم
استر موراتي وآمن روعائي» اللهم احفظني من بين يدي ومن خلفي ون يميني
وعن شمالي ومن فوقي؛ وأعوذ بعظمتك أن أغثال من تحني '”"".

وكذلك أيضا: "اللهم أنت ربي لا إله إلا أنت عليك توكلت وأنت رب العرش
العظيم؛ ولا حول ولا قوة إلا الله العلي العظيم: ما شاء لله كان وما لم يشأ لم
يكن أعلم أن الله على كل شيء قديرء وأن الله قد أحاط بكل شيء علمًا وأحصى
كل شيء عددًاء اللهم إني أعوذ بك من شر نفسي ومن شر كل دابة أنت آخذ
بناصيتها إن ربي على صراط مستقيم””. قيل للراوي: أدرك دارك فقد احترقت»
فقال: ما احترقت؛ إني كنت قلت هذا الدعاء؛ ثم نهضوا إلى الدار فوجدوها
قد سلمت واحترقت الدور حولهاء قال عياض: وكان مالك إذا دخل بيته قال: ما

وأخرجه أيضا مالك (951/2 رقم 1706)» وأو يعلى (2 اله رقم اتقم.

ذا أعرجه الترمذي (534/5؛ رقم 3514) وقال؛ صحيح؛ وابن أبي شيية (34/6: رقم 9185
وأحمد (209/1: رقم 01783.

(2) أخرجه الطبراتي في الدعاء 128/1 رقم 0143 ولين عساكر (108/64.

# PageV1P226
anchors:
- Root: ع-ف-و (ʿ-f-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To pardon, to efface, to leave unpunished; the root denotes the act of obliterating a fault entirely.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine pardon (ʿafw) as the effacement of sin's consequence, distinct from maghfirah (covering) — a theological distinction in supplication.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in the sense of "wiping away"; metaphorically applied to God's mercy in cancelling punishment.
- Root: س-ت-ر (s-t-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To cover, to shield; the root implies concealment of what is shameful or vulnerable.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): God's covering (satr) of human faults in this world and the next — a protective veil against disgrace.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal covering; metaphorically, the divine concealment of sins from public knowledge.
- Root: ح-م-ل (ḥ-m-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To carry, to bear; the root includes physical bearing and the burden of responsibility.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The bearers of the Throne (ḥamalat al-ʿarsh) as angelic entities entrusted with cosmic governance.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal carrying; metaphorically, the angels' sustaining of the divine throne's majesty.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ) — The protasis (in kāna) and apodosis (lam yaḍurr) structure in the ḥadīth, where the condition's fulfillment guarantees the result, requiring precise temporal alignment (morning/evening).
translation:
I say: And among the transmitted remembrances is that whoever says, "In the name of God, with whose name nothing in the earth or the heaven can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing," three times in the evening and three times upon rising, nothing shall harm him. With this the Shādhilī sealed the Ḥizb al-Baḥr; and we have narrated it from our shaykh al-Muntūrī. I have committed myself to its recitation every day and night, and likewise:

"O God, I have entered the morning, and I call You to witness, and I call the bearers of Your Throne, and Your angels, and all of Your creation to witness, that You are God, there is no deity but You alone, with no partner, and that Muḥammad is Your servant and Your messenger."

And the report has come: "If you say, when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning, four times, God will free you from the Fire." And likewise, if you say upon rising and upon entering the evening: "O God, whatever blessing has come to me this morning, it is from You alone, with no partner. To You belongs praise, and to You belongs thanks," then you will have rendered the thanks of your day or your night. And likewise, if you say three times upon rising and three times upon entering the evening: "O God, I have entered the morning in blessing, well-being, and covering. O God, complete Your blessing upon me, and Your well-being, and Your covering, in this world and the Hereafter," then God has obligated upon Himself His favor and His mercy toward you. And wherever the mention of "morning" (aṣbaḥa) has preceded, this wording applies at the beginning of the day; and at the beginning of the night, the wording is with "entering the evening" (amsā). And the Prophet, peace be upon him, would not abandon these supplications when he entered the evening and when he entered the morning: "O God, I ask You for well-being in this world and the Hereafter. O God, I ask You for pardon and well-being in my religion, my worldly affairs, my family, and my wealth. O God, cover my faults and calm my fears. O God, protect me from before me, from behind me, from my right, from my left, and from above me; and I seek refuge in Your majesty from being destroyed from beneath me."

And likewise: "O God, You are my Lord, there is no deity but You. Upon You I rely, and You are the Lord of the Mighty Throne. There is no might and no power except through God, the Exalted, the Magnificent. Whatever God wills comes to be, and whatever He does not will does not come to be. I know that God is over all things powerful, and that God has encompassed all things in knowledge and has counted all things in number. O God, I seek refuge in You from the evil of my own soul and from the evil of every creature You seize by its forelock. Indeed, my Lord is upon a straight path." It was said to the narrator: "Go to your house, for it has burned." He said: "It has not burned; I had said this supplication." Then they rose to the house and found it had been saved, while the houses around it had burned. Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said: And Mālik, when he entered his house, would say: "What..."

title_en: Section 173 — On the Morning Litany: Reflection, Self-Accounting, and the Priority of Sacred Knowledge
arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 226

0 سنيج فزني لعفل دن عنم واس العلمد من لوحمكن من تسر كال الونات فليجهد في تمر الأرنك القاضلة.
اشاء الله لا قوة إلا باه فسثل عن ذلك فقال: قال الله تعالى: « وَلدْدتَ بتك
لاا 4 [الكهف: 39]: وجته بينه. وكانت هذه الآبة مكتوبة
على باب مالك يريد ليتذكر برؤيته قول ذلك متى دخل.

.ومن أوراد هذا الوقت أيضًا الفكر؛ قال تاج الدين: تشوفك إلى ما بطن فيك
من العيوب خير من تشوفك إلى ما حجب عدك من الغيوب؛ فيكون تفكرك في
عيوب نفسك وفيما أنت بصدد أن تلقاه في يومك؛ فالعاقل تاجر في طلب الآخرة
ومطلبه وربحه تزكية نفسه الأمارة؛ وقد أفلح من زكاهاء وإنما فلاحها بالطاعات
وترك المخالفات؛ فكأنه يقول لنفسه: يا نفسء ما لي بضاعة إلا العمرء وهذا يوم
جديد قد أمهلني الله فيه وأنعم علي به. ولو توفاتي لكنت أتمنى أن أرد إلى الدنيا
يومًا واحاء فاحسبيني يا نفس قد مت ثم رددت؛ قاله له اغتنمي هذا اليوم. قال في
"الإحياء': ولا يطول أمله فيكبر عليه العزم على المراقبة؛ بل يكون ابن وقته: فلا
تكون همته إلا صلاح يومه. وعبارة السيد الإمام مربي المريدين شمس الدين
البلالي: المحاسبة تفقد ما مضى وما يستقبل» وتجب إجماغاء وتحق بمعرفة النعم
وذنويك وسوء ظن بالنفسء فتستدرك ما مضى فيما بقي؛ وأن ذنيك وحلمه حجة
عليك؛ وطاعتك منة عليك؛ وكل طاعة رضيتها منك فهي عليك حتى تفنى في
التوحيد عما في الدارين. ثم قال: فبعد فريضة الصبح. اله

والشيء يذكر بالشيء؛ انظر أول حكمة افتتح بها تاج الدين حكمه! وهي قوله:
من علامة الاعتماد على العمل نقصان الرجاء عند وجود الزئل. وورد: تفكر ساعة
خير من عبادة سنة؛ فقيل: هو الفكر الذي ينقل عن المكاره إلى المحاب ومن

الحرص إلى القناعة.
قال ابن المبارك: قلت لراهب: متى عيدكم؟ قال: اليوم الذي لا نعصي الل فيه.
وبالجملة فقند قال في "الإحياء”: إن وظيفتك في هذا الوقت أدعية وأذكار

وتصلية؛ وتكرر لك في سبحتك وقراءة وتفكر. اه وانظر أيضًا قراءة العلم: سثل
عز الدين أقراءة القرآن وحفظه أفضل أم قراءة العلم؟ فقال: يتعين على كل أحد أن
يتعلم من القرآن (الفاتحة) ثم بعد ذلك التفقه في الدين أفضل. وقال في "الإحياء':
لا ينبغي أن يخلو المريد في يوم الجمعة عن الخيرات. ثم ذكر من آداب يوم

# PageV1P227
anchors:
- Root: ف-ك-ر (f-k-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Deliberate turning of the mind over a matter; the heart's circulation among considerations (taṣrīf al-qalb fī al-shay’).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The soul's movement toward apprehending meanings — in the Qur’an, it is the means to ʿibrah (lesson-taking) and maʿrifah (gnosis), not mere cogitation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Ḥaqīqah: mental reflection; Majāz: the heart's "grazing" (irtiyāḍ) upon the fields of divine signs.
- Root: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To reckon, count, or take account; also sufficiency (ḥasb).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Muḥāsabah — the soul's auditing of its deeds before the Final Audit; a station of the vigilant (murāqibūn).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: arithmetic reckoning; Metaphorical: the soul's self-scrutiny as a mirror of the Day of Reckoning.
- Root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Certain cognition; the mark or sign (ʿalamah) by which a thing is known.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): ʿIlm — the apprehension of a thing as it truly is; in the religious scale, it is the foundation of ʿamal (action).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: knowledge; Metaphorical: the "light" (nūr) that guides the wayfarer — hence "reading knowledge" (qirāʾat al-ʿilm) is a form of worship.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Inna-mā (إِنَّمَا) — Restriction (qasr) via negation and exception; also the construction "fa-kāʾannahu yaqūlu" (فَكَأَنَّهُ يَقُولُ) — simile-clause (tashbīh) with implied khabar, indicating the inward speech of the soul.
translation:
I say — and success is from God alone, there is no power save by Him. One asked about this, and he replied: God Most High said: {«وَلَوْلَا إِذْ دَخَلْتَ جَنَّتَكَ قُلْتَ مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ»} [Al-Kahf: 39] — and he explained its meaning. This verse was inscribed upon the door of Mālik — may God have mercy on him — desiring thereby that whenever he entered, the sight of it would remind him of that saying.

Among the litanies (awrād) of this time is also reflection (al-fikr). Tāj al-Dīn said: "Your gazing upon what is hidden within you of faults is better than your gazing upon what is veiled from you of unseen things. So let your reflection be upon the faults of your own soul and upon what you are about to encounter in your day. For the intelligent one is a merchant seeking the Hereafter; his object and his profit is the purification of his commanding soul (nafs al-ammārah). Indeed, he has succeeded who purifies it — and its success lies only in acts of obedience and in abandoning acts of disobedience. It is as though he says to his soul: 'O soul! I have no merchandise but my lifespan, and this is a new day in which God has granted me respite and bestowed it upon me. Had I died, I would have wished to return to the world for a single day — so reckon me, O soul, as one who has died and then been returned.' He says this to it: 'Seize this day.'"

He said in the Iḥyāʾ: "Let not his hope be prolonged, lest the resolve for vigilance (murāqabah) become too heavy for him. Rather, let him be a son of his moment (ibn waqtihi) — his sole concern being the rectification of his day."

The expression of the Sayyid, the Imām, the trainer of aspirants, Shams al-Dīn al-Balālī: "Self-accounting (al-muḥāsabah) is the examination of what has passed and what is to come. It is obligatory by consensus (ijmāʿan), and it is realized by knowledge of the blessings [of God], of one's sins, and by holding a bad opinion of oneself — so that one may make up for what has passed in what remains. Your sin and His forbearance are an argument against you; your obedience is a favor upon you; and every act of obedience you are pleased with from yourself is against you — until you are annihilated (fanāʾ) in tawḥīd from all that concerns the two abodes." Then he said: "This is after the obligatory dawn prayer."

And a thing is recalled by another thing. Consider the first wisdom with which Tāj al-Dīn opened his Aphorisms (Ḥikam) — namely his saying: "Among the signs of reliance upon one's deeds is the diminishment of hope (rajāʾ) at the occurrence of a slip (zalal)." And it is reported: "Reflecting for an hour is better than a year of worship." It was said: "That is the reflection which transports one from disliked things to beloved things, and from avarice to contentment (qanāʿah)."

Ibn al-Mubārak said: "I said to a monk: 'When is your feast-day?' He replied: 'The day in which we do not disobey God.'"

In sum — he said in the Iḥyāʾ: "Your function in this time is supplications (adʿiyah), remembrances (adhkār), and prayers of blessing upon the Prophet (taṣliyah); and repetition in your rosary (subḥah), and recitation, and reflection." End quote.

And consider also the reading of knowledge (qirāʾat al-ʿilm). ʿIzz al-Dīn was asked: "Is the recitation of the Qur’an and its memorization more virtuous, or the reading of knowledge?" He replied: "It is incumbent upon everyone to learn from the Qur’an (al-Fātiḥah) — then after that, the pursuit of understanding in religion (al-tafaqquh fī al-dīn) is more virtuous."

And he said in the Iḥyāʾ: "It is not fitting that the aspirant (murīd) be devoid of good works on the day of Friday." Then he mentioned some of the etiquettes of that day.

title_en: The Conduct of the Rightly Guided in the Stations of Religion — Section 174: On the Virtue of Attending Scholars' Circles and the Adhkār of the Mosque
arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 227

منهج ارقي / لقا امن مفام خوفص العلدد: من لم بندكن من تعمير كاقة القات فليجتهد لي تسر الأوقات الفاضنة. 2
الجمعة أن يحضر مجالس العلماء بكرة أو بعد الصلاة. وثقل أبو عمر بسنده: "لآن
تغدو فتعلم ابا من العلم خيرًا من أن تصلي مائة ركعة”""» ولتنظر لنفسك حزبًا
على ما تختاره مما سمعته من الأذكار أو بما ركبته لتفسك مما يوافق حالك ويرق
ابه قلبك؛ وتنوي أن تأتي عليه في يومك إن عاقك عن بعضه عائق استدركته في بقية
يومك؛ واختار المشائخ: أبو عمر بن عبد البر وأبو بكر بن العربي أن تصلي ركمتي
الفجر بالكافرون) و(الإخلاص» قال أبو عمر: وردت الأحاديث الصحيحة من
أربعة طرق عن أربعة من الصحابة: أن رسول اله يك كان يصلي هاتين الركعتين
بهاتين السورتين» وكذلك أيضًا قال القاضي أبو بكر بن العربي في الركعتين بعد
المغرب: يستحب أن يصليها أيضًا بهاتين السورتين» ونقل بسنده: أن رسول الله وق
قال: "اقرأ برقل يا أيها الكافرون) عند منامك؛ فإنها براءة من الشرك”. ويكون
ذكرك الذي تتوجه به إلى المسجد: بسم الله آمنت بالل وتوكلت على الله
واعتصمت بالله. وفوضت أمري إلى القد لا حول ولا قوة إلا باله.

روى في التمهيد من وجوه هذه البسملة. وأن من بسمل بها إذا خرج لسفر أو
فإن الله سبحانه يرزقه خير ذلك المخرج؛ ويصرف عنه شره ثم تقول؛ أعني:
في وجهتك إلى المسجد: اللهم بحق السائلين عليك؛ وبحق مخرجي هذاء فإني لم
أخرج أشرا ولا بطرا ولا رياء ولا سمعة؛ خرجت ابتغاء مرضاتك؛ واتقاء سخطك»
أسألك أن تعيذني من النار؛ وتدخلني الجنة؛ وتقول عند دخول المسجد: بسم الله

# PageV1P228
anchors:
- Root: غ-د-و (gh-d-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To go forth at dawn (al-ghuduw), the early morning journeying toward a purpose.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The soul's spiritual exertion (mujāhadah) in seeking knowledge as an act of worship, paralleling the Prophet's ﷺ morning departure for prayer.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical setting out; metaphorical (majāz) — the heart's inclination toward divine knowledge.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-sharṭ) — The protasis "man lam yatamakkan" (whoever cannot) governs the apodosis "fal-yajtahid" (let him strive), indicating obligation contingent on capacity.
translation:
I say — may Allah guide us and you to His obedience:

Whoever is unable to attend all the prayer times [in congregation] should strive to make use of the virtuous hours — especially Friday — by attending the circles of the scholars, either in the early morning or after the prayer. Abū ʿUmar [Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr] transmitted with his chain of narration: "That you go forth in the early morning and learn a single chapter of knowledge is better than praying one hundred rakʿahs."

And let each person assign for himself a regular portion (ḥizb) of dhikr, choosing from what he has heard of the adhkār, or composing for himself what suits his state and softens his heart. Let him intend to complete it within his day; and if some obstacle prevents him from part of it, he should make it up in the remainder of his day.

The scholars — Abū ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Barr and Abū Bakr ibn al-ʿArabī — chose that one pray the two rakʿahs of Fajr with {«Qul yā ayyuhā al-kāfirūn»} and {«Qul huwa Allāhu aḥad»}. Abū ʿUmar said: "Authentic hadiths have come from four chains, from four Companions, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray these two rakʿahs with these two sūrahs." Likewise, the judge Abū Bakr ibn al-ʿArabī said concerning the two rakʿahs after Maghrib: "It is recommended to pray them also with these two sūrahs." And he transmitted with his chain that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Recite {«Qul yā ayyuhā al-kāfirūn»} when you go to your bed, for it is a declaration of innocence from shirk."

Your dhikr when setting out toward the mosque should be: "Bismillāh, āmantu billāh, wa tawakkaltu ʿalā Allāh, wa ʿtaṣamtu billāh, wa fawwaḍtu amrī ilā Allāh, lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh."

It is narrated in al-Tamhīd from various aspects concerning this basmalah — that whoever says it when going out for a journey or [any undertaking], Allah the Exalted provides him with the good of that exit and averts from him its evil.

Then you say — I mean, in your direction toward the mosque: "Allāhumma bi-ḥaqqi al-sā'ilīna ʿalayk, wa bi-ḥaqqi makhrajī hādhā, fa-innī lam akhruj asharan wa lā baṭaran wa lā riyā'an wa lā sumʿah; kharajtu ibtighā'a marḍātika, wa-ttiqā'a sukhtika. As'aluka an tuʿīdhanī min al-nār, wa tudkhilanī al-jannah."

And you say upon entering the mosque: "Bismillāh, wa al-salāmu ʿalā Rasūlillāh. Allāhumma iftaḥ lī abwāba raḥmatik." And in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim: "And when he exits, he says instead: 'Allāhumma iftaḥ lī — Allāhumma innī as'aluka min faḍlik.'"

title_en: Section 175 — On the Supplications of the Prayer (Duʿāʾ al-Tawajjuh) and the Adhkār of Its Pillars

### | الصفحة 228

2 مهي لوف لعفل دن :من عولس العلدد من لم كن من تسم كال الأرقات فليجهد في تمسر الأرناك قاض
"وأعذني من الشيطان الرجيم”"'. وروى الإمام الشافعي: 'اطلبوا استجابة الدعاء

# PageV1P229
anchors:
- Root: و-ج-ه (w-j-h)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The face (al-wajh); turning one's direction (tawajjuh) toward something, inclining one's countenance and intention.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the Qur'anic idiom, "turning one's face" (wajh) signifies the whole self and its orientation toward God in sincere devotion (ikhlāṣ), as in {«وَجَّهْتُ وَجْهِيَ لِلَّذِي فَطَرَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ»}.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical direction; metaphorical (majāz) for the soul's orientation and submission to the Creator's command.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Inshā' (performative utterance) — Supplications (duʿā') are constructed as direct address (nidā') with vocative particles (yā Allāhumma), and the conditional clauses (law, in) govern the apodosis in the imperative or jussive, as in "fa-l-yajtahid" (let him strive).
translation: I say: Whoever is not among those who are constant in the five prayers at their appointed times, let him strive hard in seeking the times of the prayers. And he should say: "And protect me from the accursed Satan" {«وَأَعِذْنِي مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ»}. Imam al-Shāfiʿī narrated: "Seek the response to supplication at the establishment of the prayer, the descent of rain, and the clash of armies." So you should make the supplication of orientation (duʿāʾ al-tawajjuh) before the opening takbīr (iḥrām), according to what the scholars of our school have chosen. You say: "I have turned my face toward Him Who originated the heavens and the earth, inclining (ḥanīfan) and submitting (musliman), and I am not among the polytheists. Indeed, my prayer, my sacrifice, my living, and my dying are for God, Lord of the worlds. No partner has He, and with this I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims. O God, You are the King; there is no god but You. You are my Lord, and I am Your servant. I have wronged myself, and I have confessed my sin, so forgive me all my sins — indeed, none forgives sins but You. And guide me to the best of moral traits, for none guides to their best but You. And turn away from me their evil, for none turns away their evil from me but You. Here I am at Your service, my Lord, and at Your pleasure. All good is in Your hands. I am with You and unto You. Blessed and exalted are You. I seek Your forgiveness and I repent to You." He said in "al-Ḥilyah": This supplication is recommended (mustaḥabb) at the orientation for both the obligatory and the supererogatory prayer. And do not neglect in your bowing (rukūʿ): "Glory be to God the Magnificent" (subḥāna Allāhi al-ʿaẓīm), nor in your prostration (sujūd): "Glory be to my Lord the Most High" (subḥāna rabbī al-aʿlā). And if you say, upon raising your head from your bowing, after "Our Lord, and to You be praise" (rabbanā wa laka al-ḥamd): "Praise abundant, O Blessed One, filling the heavens and the earth, and filling what is between them, and filling whatever You will of anything after that — O Possessor of praise and glory. None can withhold what You give, and none can give what You withhold, and the wealth of the wealthy avails nothing against You" — then indeed the Prophet ﷺ has been praised for the one who devised this remembrance from himself, and the Messenger of God ﷺ congratulated him for it. And among the supplications of the Messenger of God ﷺ in his prostration: "O God, I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your wrath, and in Your pardon from Your punishment, and in You from You. I cannot enumerate praise of You, as You have praised Yourself." And among his supplications ﷺ when he raised his head: "My Lord, forgive me, have mercy on me, mend me, raise me, provide for me, guide me, and grant me well-being." Then, when you have concluded the morning prayer (ṣalāt al-ṣubḥ), if you say: "I seek God's forgiveness" three times, "O God, You are Peace, and from You is peace, and to You returns peace. Blessed are You, O Possessor of majesty and honor" — then you have followed the prophetic practice.

title_en: The Conduct of the Rightly Guided in the Stations of Religion — Section 176
arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 229

منهج ني قفن طم حول املد ئ لمكن م تر كا لوقت يجيد في تسر لأرقت لاضة_373
والاكرام؛ ثم تمسح جبهتك بيدك اليسى قائلا: أشهد أن لا إله إلا اله الرحمن
الرحيم؛ اللهم أذهب عني الهم والحزن؛ فقد فعل هذا رسول اله يل ثم تقول:
الهم أجرني من النار كما تقدم؛ وتأخذ في تمام حزيك إلى أن تحل النافلة وتصلي
صلاة الإشراق؛ فإن اشتغلت من حين طلوع الفجر إلى هذا الوقت بخير من هذاء
فأنت سابق بالخيرات؛ لأن ما قررته لم أقرره على أنه فرض: وإن أخذت بمذهب
ابن حزم القائل: ما ثم إلا النص وأول من قاس إيليس فانت وإياه.

اوقد تقدم أن الصوقية نفع الله بهم يقولون: اسمع من الله؛ وكان سيدي
المتتوري رحمه الله يرشح هذاء فمهما تعارض أمران كلاهما مباح براعي هذا
المعنى كحكاية ابن أبي ذؤيب لما قيل له وهو جالس: قم وحي المسجد فقام
وصلى. وقد تقدم استحسان عياض لقول الغنمي: ما بلغني من التعبد عملته؛ حتى
بلغني عن بعض السلف أنه ختم ثلاث ختم في ليلة واحدة ووطئ أهله عند كل
.وتطهر؛ إنما قلت؛ إنه استحسنها؛ لأنه في مدحه ساقهاء وقد قال في صدر
مداركه: جمعنا من أخبارهم ومن سير حكامهم ما يحتاج الحكام إليه؛ وأثبتنا من
حكم حكمائهم ومناهج صلحائهم ما ترجى بركته؛ ولا تخيب إن شاء الله متقعته.
وقد شهد السيد القدوة البرزلي أن هذا هو مذهب الصوفية: أن ما هو من باب
الأعمال إذا كان لا يناقض حكمًا شرعيًا بل ذلك في باب القرب المندوية؛ وشهد
الشرع باعتبار جنسه فإنهم يأخذون به ولا يلتفتون لصحة أصله؛ وقد تقدم قول
ابن العربي: نقوله من عند أنفسناء ولا نأثره عن أحد. قال الشاطبي: ويؤخذ أيضًا من
المرائي في النوم وإن كان لا يثبت بها حكم شرعي؛ فقد حصل مما قررته من أقوال
الموثوق بهم بدينهم أن من طلوع الفجر إلى حل النافلة ينبغي عمرانه بما قررته أو
بأحسن منه إن وجدت أحسن منه؛ ليكون أن لا نسعى في طلب الدنيا حتى تصلي
صلاة الإشراق.

وانظر في
"لا تعجزني عن أربع ركعات في أول النهار أكفك آخره"؛ قال في "الإ

‎٠‏ في حديث سادس لابن شهاب؛ أن رسول اله وك قال:
اتصلي

‏عند الإشراق إذا ارتقعت الشمس قدر نصف رمح. وهو المعني بقوله: بيني

# PageV1P230
anchors:
- Root: ع-م-ر (ʿ-m-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To cultivate, inhabit, or fill a space with purposeful activity; the opposite of desolation (kharāb).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The spiritual "peopling" of time with acts of obedience, as opposed to leaving it vacant for negligence.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical habitation; metaphorical (majāz) here for investing the temporal interval with devotional works.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Implied Apodosis (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb) — The phrase "if you occupy yourself... then you are foremost" requires the protasis to govern the apodosis, with the latter's certainty (sabq bi-l-khayrāt) marked by the particle fa-.
translation:
I say — and success is from God alone:

Know that the recommended practice (sunnah) for the one who has prayed the dawn prayer (al-fajr) in congregation is to remain in his place of prayer, engaging in remembrance (dhikr) and supplication (duʿāʾ) until the sun rises to the height of a spear's length. Then he wipes his forehead with his left hand, saying: "I bear witness that there is no god but God, the Merciful, the Compassionate; O God, remove from me anxiety and sorrow" — for the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) did this. Then he says: "O God, protect me from the Fire" as previously mentioned, and he completes his litany (ḥizb) until the time of the supererogatory prayer (al-nāfilah) arrives, and he prays the prayer of illumination (ṣalāt al-ishrāq).

If, however, you occupy yourself from the break of dawn until this time with something better than what I have prescribed, then you are foremost in good deeds (sābiq bi-l-khayrāt) — for what I have established I did not establish as an obligation (farḍ). And if you adopt the school of Ibn Ḥazm — who held that "there is nothing but the textual proof (naṣṣ), and the first to employ analogical reasoning (qiyās) was Iblīs" — then you and he are [in that matter] left to your own accord.

It has already been mentioned that the Sufis — may God benefit us through them — say: "We hear from God." And my master al-Mattītī (may God have mercy on him) used to recommend this [approach]. Thus, whenever two matters conflict, both being permissible (mubāḥ), one gives precedence to this meaning [of hearing from God directly]. This is like the story of Ibn Abī Dhu'ayb: when it was said to him while he was sitting, "Arise and greet the mosque," he arose and prayed. And it has already been mentioned that ʿIyāḍ approved the saying of al-Ghunaymī: "Whatever act of devotion (taʿabbud) reached me, I performed it" — until it reached me that one of the early predecessors (salaf) completed three complete recitations of the Qurʾān in a single night and visited his wife after each purification. I only say that he (ʿIyāḍ) approved it because he cited it in praise of him. And he said at the beginning of his book al-Madārik: "We have gathered from their reports and from the conduct of their judges what judges need; and we have recorded from the judgments of their sages and the paths of their righteous ones that whose blessing is hoped for, and whose benefit — God willing — will not disappoint."

And the master and exemplar al-Burzulī testified that this is the doctrine of the Sufis: that whatever pertains to acts (aʿmāl) — if it does not contradict a legal ruling (ḥukm sharʿī) — falls within the domain of supererogatory acts of drawing near (qurb mandūbah). And the Sacred Law (al-sharʿ) has attested to the validity of its kind (jins), for they adopt it and do not look to the authenticity of its specific origin (ṣiḥḥat aṣlihī). It has already been mentioned that Ibn al-ʿArabī said: "We say it from ourselves, and we do not transmit it from anyone." Al-Shāṭibī said: "It is also derived from visions seen in sleep (al-marāʾī fī al-nawm), even though no legal ruling is established by them."

Thus, from what I have established from the sayings of those trusted in their religion, it follows that from the break of dawn until the time of the supererogatory prayer, one ought to fill that interval with what I have prescribed — or with something better, if you find something better — so that you do not strive in seeking the world until you have prayed the prayer of illumination (ṣalāt al-ishrāq).

And consider the hadith: "Do not fail me regarding four rakʿahs at the beginning of the day, and I will suffice you for its end" — as mentioned in al-Īḍāḥ. And in a sixth hadith of Ibn Shihāb (al-Zuhrī), that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Pray at the time of illumination (al-ishrāq) when the sun has risen to the height of half a spear." This is the meaning of his saying: "between..." — see al-Tamhīd, 8/142.

title_en: Section 177 — On the Station of Vigilance and Turning Life's Occurrences into Reminders
arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 230

4 منهج فزني لعفل ل عنم واس العلمد من لويحمكن من تسر كال الونات فليجهد في تمر الأرنك القاضلة.
يراق (4)5 [ص: 18]؛ وتصلي الضحى وفت الضحى. ونقل عياض: أن
مالا كان لا يتكلم حتى تطلع الشمس. وإن لم تتوفر لك الدواعي على ما قررته فلا
تر نفسك أنك خير من غيرك؛ إذ كلنا ظالم نفسه؛ ولا أقل أن تكون أورادك الأوراد
الواردة عند العوارض؛ وتجعل العوارض كأنها منبهة لك؛ إذ مريد الآخرة تذكره
العوارض للدار الآخرة؛ وكل ينظر بحسب همته.

قال في “الاحياء': إذا دخمل بناء ونجار ويزاز وحائك دارا معمورة: فإذا
تفقدتهم رأيت البزاز ينظر إلى الفرش يتأمل قيمتهاء والحائك ينظر إلى الثياب يينصر
نسجهاء والنجار ينظر إلى السقف يتأمل كيقية تركيبه؛ والبناء ينظر إلى الحيطان
يتأمل كيفية استقامتهاء فكذلك سالك طريق الآخرة؛ إذا نظر إلى سواد يذكر ظلمة
القبرء أو إلى حية تذكر أفاعي جهنم؛ أو إلى صورة قبيحة تذكر الزباتية ومنكرًا
ونكيراء وإن سمع صوثًا هائا تذكر نفخة الصورء وشيًا حسنًا تذكر نعيم الجنة. اه
من "الاحياء

وقد تقدم لنا جملة مما ينبغي أن تترك لها الورد الذي أنت فيه؛ مثل إذا سمعت
الرعد أو صراخ ديك: أو نحو ذلك مثل أن تمر بالقبور: فلتتبه لنفسك؛ فمن رأى

# PageV1P231
anchors:
- Root: ن-ظ-ر (na-ẓa-ra)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To look, gaze, contemplate; to examine with the eye or the intellect.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the Qur'an, naẓar denotes both physical sight and spiritual insight; the latter is the higher form, as in {«فَانظُرْ كَيْفَ بَدَأَ الْخَلْقَ»} (29:20) — "Look at how He originated creation."
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for ocular vision; metaphorical (majāz) for the heart's discernment — here, the wayfarer's gaze upon worldly things becomes a mirror of the Hereafter.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Response Construction (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb) — The protasis (e.g., "if you see a grave") is followed by an apodosis that is an imperative or a promise, as in "whoever sees a grave has seen a preacher."
translation:
I say — may Allah guide us and you: Know that the one who truly desires the Hereafter does not let a single moment pass without drawing a lesson from it. If the means for the full spiritual discipline I have set forth are not available to you, do not deceive yourself into thinking you are better than others; for each of us wrongs his own soul. At the very least, let your regular litanies (awrād) be those that are prescribed for times of sudden occurrences (ʿawāriḍ), and treat those occurrences as if they were wake-up calls for you. For the seeker of the Hereafter, every sudden event reminds him of the abode of the Hereafter; and each person looks at things according to his own aspiration (himmah).

Al-Ghazālī said in the Iḥyāʾ: "If a builder, a carpenter, a cloth-merchant, and a weaver enter a well-furnished house, and you observe them closely, you will see the cloth-merchant looking at the carpets, appraising their value; the weaver looking at the garments, examining their weave; the carpenter looking at the ceiling, pondering how it is joined; and the builder looking at the walls, examining their straightness. Likewise, the wayfarer on the road to the Hereafter — when he looks at darkness, he remembers the darkness of the grave; at a snake, he remembers the serpents of Hell; at an ugly form, he remembers the Zabāniyah (the angels of punishment) and Munkar and Nakīr; and if he hears a terrifying sound, he remembers the Trumpet-blast (nafkhat al-ṣūr); and if he sees something beautiful, he remembers the bliss of Paradise." — End of the quotation from the Iḥyāʾ.

We have already mentioned several things for which you should set aside the litany (wird) you are currently engaged in — such as when you hear thunder or the crowing of a rooster, or similar things, or when you pass by graves. So be attentive to your own soul. For whoever sees a grave has indeed seen a preacher that preaches to him and a reminder that reminds him. Even if the grave is silent, it speaks with the tongue of its state (lisān al-ḥāl), making plain what will become of you in the end. It is as if it says to you: "I was once like you, and you will die just as I died. I wasted the command of my Lord, and I regret it." And likewise, if you waste the command of your Lord, you will regret it. And you have become like a drowning man, waiting for a supplication to reach me from a compassionate friend — so say: "O Allah, Lord of these decayed bodies and crumbling bones that have departed from the world, while they were believing in You — enter upon them a mercy from You and a peace from me." And it will be written for you, if Allah wills, good deeds equal to their number. Abū ʿUmar narrated this in his Tamhīd, in the eighth ḥadīth of al-ʿAlāʾ.

And when you alight at a stopping-place — from the Risālah of Abū Zayd — say: "I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created." Then nothing will harm you, if Allah wills, until you depart. And if you perform ablution before your departure and pray two rakʿahs reciting the Āyat al-Kursī and {«لِإِيلَافِ قُرَيْشٍ»} (Sūrat Quraysh), nothing will harm you, if Allah wills, until you return. See the Nawāzil of al-Sayyid al-Burzulī. And he said therein also: If you see a fire, say "Allāhu akbar" and make the supplication of distress (duʿāʾ al-karb). And if dogs surround you, say: {«قُل لَّن يُصِيبَنَا إِلَّا مَا كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَنَا»} (9:51) — "Say: Nothing will befall us except what Allah has written for us" — and do not let your soul be distressed.

# PageV1P232
anchors:
- Root: ب-ر-أ (b-r-')
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root denotes creation from a state of purity, freedom from blemish; al-barā'ah al-aṣliyyah = the primordial state of innocence and soundness (salāmah) before any acquired taint.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, refers to the original disposition (fiṭrah) upon which the servant is created — free from blameworthy accretions; here, a legal-religious principle of non-liability.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — freedom from defect; metaphorical (majāz) — the presumption of one's religious soundness when uncertain of one's own failing.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional sentence (al-sharṭ) with "in" + perfect verb (fa-inna-hā in shā'a Allāh lā taḍurruk) — protasis expressing potentiality, apodosis with future negation; the oath-like invocation "in shā'a Allāh" suspends certainty to divine will.
translation: I say: And remain in your conduct upon the original innocence (al-barā'ah al-aṣliyyah); for it shall not harm you, God willing. And al-Burzulī said: Recite the verse: {«يَا مَعْشَرَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنسِ إِنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ أَن تَنفُذُوا مِنْ أَقْطَارِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ فَانفُذُوا»} [Al-Raḥmān: 33]. And when you become angry, say: "O Allah, forgive me my sin, remove the rage from my heart, and deliver me from the accursed Satan." And when you see one afflicted in his worldly affair, or his religion, or his self, say: "Praise be to Allah who has spared me from that with which He has tried you, and has favored me greatly above many of His creatures." And call to mind the reported tradition (al-khabar): "Do not taunt [another], lest you be tried [likewise]" — may Allah protect us from the calamities of this world and of religion. And when you enter the marketplace, say: "There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner; His is the dominion and His is the praise; He gives life and causes death, and He is Living and dies not; in His hand is all good, and He is over all things Omnipotent." For it has been reported: Whoever says this, Allah writes for him a thousand thousand good deeds, and erases from him a thousand thousand evil deeds, and raises him a thousand thousand degrees. And the Salaf (righteous predecessors) used to deliberately pass through the marketplace in order to utter this tahlīl (declaration of divine oneness). And the Shaykh of our shaykhs, al-Khaṭīb al-Ḥaffār, when he became unable [to walk], would be taken by the hand and carried to the marketplace, and he would utter this tahlīl there, then be returned to his home. And recite Āyat al-Kursī at the time of cupping (al-ḥijāmah); you will find its benefit, if Allah wills. And when you experience ill omen (taṭayyur), say: "What Allah wills — there is no power save with Allah; O Allah, none brings good except You, and none removes evil except You; there is no might and no power save with Allah, the Most High, the Magnificent." And upon the door of our Imām Mālik (may Allah be pleased with him) was written: "What Allah wills — there is no power save with Allah." And he was asked about that, and he said: Allah said: {«وَلَوْلَا إِذْ دَخَلْتَ جَنَّتَكَ قُلْتَ مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ»} [Al-Kahf: 39]. And the ḥājjah (need) is the abode [of fulfillment]. This is the text of ʿIyāḍ. And say at the commencement of affairs: {«رَبَّنَا آتِنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ رَحْمَةً وَهَيِّئْ لَنَا مِنْ أَمْرِنَا رَشَدًا»} [Al-Kahf: 10], and {«رَبِّ اشْرَحْ لِي صَدْرِي وَيَسِّرْ لِي أَمْرِي»} [Ṭā-Hā: 25–26].

# PageV1P233
anchors:
- Root: و-ح-ش (waḥsha)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Solitude, desolation, or a sense of estrangement that befalls the heart when separated from the familiar.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Spiritual unease or alienation from divine presence, often dispelled by remembrance (dhikr).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: wildness or emptiness of a place; Metaphorical: inner disquiet of the soul.
- Root: ق-د-س (quds)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Purity, sanctity, being free from any imperfection.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The Divine attribute of transcendence above all defects and temporal attributes (ṣifāt al-ḥudūth).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: cleanliness; Metaphorical: absolute holiness of the Divine Essence.
- Root: ج-ب-ر (jabr)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Compulsion, force, or restoration of a broken thing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine omnipotence (jabarūt) as the realm of God's overwhelming power and subjugation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: setting a bone; Metaphorical: God's irresistible dominion over all creation.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of ʿAṭf (Coordination) — When multiple invocations are cited sequentially, the conjunction (wa) links them as parallel supplications, each retaining its independent grammatical and semantic force.
translation:
I say — may Allah guide us and you — know that the one who is unable to perform the siwāk (tooth-stick) at all times should strive to use the arāk (toothbrush tree) when performing ablution. And upon looking at the heavens, one should say: {«Our Lord, You did not create this in vain; exalted are You, so protect us from the punishment of the Fire»} [Āl ʿImrān: 191]. This is from the Nawāzil (legal rulings) of al-Sayyid al-Burzulī. I have transmitted from it only a portion, so that it may serve as an encouragement to consult its original and benefit from its treasures. Among them: And you say at times of solitude (waḥsha): "Glory be to the King, the Most Holy, Lord of the angels and the Spirit; He has subdued the heavens and the earth by His might and His dominion (jabarūt)."

And consider the beginning of this tasbīḥ (glorification): For it has been reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he concluded the witr prayer, would say: "Glory be to the King, the Most Holy; Glory be to the King, the Most Holy; Glory be to the King, the Most Holy" — three times. And he would say: "O Allah, I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your wrath, and I seek refuge in Your pardon from Your punishment, and I seek refuge in You from You. I cannot enumerate Your praises; You are as You have praised Yourself."

Thus, there is a common ground between this and what preceded — both are occasions of solitude (waḥsha). These invocations, if Allah wills, will dispel that solitude. And from the Nawāzil of al-Sayyid al-Burzulī also: When casting seeds into the earth, say: "I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan; {«Have you seen what you sow? Is it you who make it grow, or are We the grower?»} [al-Wāqiʿah: 63–64]. Rather, Allah is the Sower, the Grower, and the One who brings to fruition. O Allah, send blessings upon our master Muḥammad, and grant us its fruit, and protect us from its harm." And intend that all Muslims benefit from it — then you will see its blessing, and you will have the reward, if the King (Allah) wills. And he ﷺ said: "No Muslim plants a plant or sows a crop, but that whatever is eaten from it is charity for him; whatever is stolen from it is charity for him; whatever the birds eat from it is charity for him; and no one takes anything from it without it being charity for him."

# PageV1P234
anchors:
- Root: ج-ه-د (j-h-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Exertion of utmost effort in a matter; striving against difficulty.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Spiritual striving (jihād) against the lower self to fulfill devotional obligations.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical effort; metaphorical — perseverance in worship despite incapacity.
- Root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To succeed, replace, or act as a successor; also to leave behind.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine substitution — God's recompense for loss with better, both in this world and the hereafter.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — succession in time; metaphorical — God's providential replacement of affliction with reward.
- Root: ع-ف-و (ʿ-f-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To pardon, efface, or obliterate a sin entirely.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine forgiveness that removes the trace of sin, rooted in God's attribute of ʿAfuww.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — to erase; metaphorical — God's complete effacement of guilt without remnant.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The protasis (condition) governs the apodosis (result), as in "If you hear of a beloved's death, then say..." (wa-in samiʿta... fa-qul), requiring the imperative response to be contingent upon the stated condition.
translation:
I say — may God guide us and you: Know that the rightly guided conduct (sunan al-muhtadīn) in this station is that whoever is unable to populate all the times [with worship] should strive (yajtahid) to populate the superior times [among them], for the reward of deeds is multiplied therein up to the Day of Resurrection. And if you need to strip off your garments [for bathing or changing], say: "In the name of God, there is no deity but He" — and this basmalah will be a shield against the jinn. And if this proves difficult for you, then say, according to your facing direction (qiblah): "In the name of God upon my soul, my wealth, and my religion; O God, make me content with Your decree, and bless me in what is apportioned to me, so that I do not love hastening what You have delayed, nor delaying what You have hastened." The Messenger of God ﷺ guided [us] to this.

And if you hear of the death of a beloved one, say: "O God, forgive me and him; verily we belong to God and to Him we return; O God, with You I deposit my affliction, so reward me and replace me with something better than it." All of this was commanded by the Messenger of God ﷺ. And the Messenger of God ﷺ also guided [us] to say: "Verily we belong to God and to Him we return, and to our Lord we shall be turned back; O God, write it with You among the doers of good, and make him a successor for his family among those who remain; and do not deprive us of his reward, nor try us after him."

And our Imām Mālik saw [a vision] in his sleep, and it was said to him: "What did God do with you?" He said: "God forgave me because of a word that ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān — may God be pleased with him — used to say whenever he saw a funeral procession: 'Glory be to the Living One who never dies.'"

And when you break your fast from your fasting, say: "Praise be to God who aided me so I fasted, and provided for me so I broke my fast"; and: "O God, for You I fasted, and upon Your provision I break my fast; so accept from me, for You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing." The Messenger of God ﷺ guided [us] to this.

And say, following the example of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar: "O God, I ask You by Your mercy which encompasses all things to forgive me." And ʿĀʾishah — may God be pleased with her — said: "If I know [which night is] the Night of Decree (laylat al-qadr), what should I say in it?" The Messenger of God ﷺ said to her: "Say: 'O God, You are Pardoning (ʿAfuww), You love pardon, so pardon me.'"

# PageV1P235
anchors:
- Root: ج-ه-د (j-h-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Exertion of effort to the utmost limit; striving against difficulty.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Spiritual exertion (jihād) in obedience, particularly in overcoming the soul's reluctance.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical toil; Metaphorical: disciplined striving in devotional acts.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-sharṭ) — The protasis (in yurid) governs the apodosis (fa-l-yajtahid), indicating a causal obligation.
translation:
I say: Whoever intends to travel for a noble purpose must strive in performing the virtuous two-rakʿah prayer. The Prophet ﷺ said: «No one leaves behind for his family anything better than two rakʿahs he prays when he intends to travel» — reciting in them Āyat al-Kursī and «Sūrat al-Īlāf (Quraysh)» — and no disliked thing shall befall him, if Allah wills. And the recitation of «al-Īlāf Quraysh» is a safeguard against everything; likewise, whoever recites it when frightened by an enemy or a wild beast [is protected].

Then rise from your sitting for your destination, saying: "O Allah, to You I turn, and by You I seek protection. O Allah, suffice me what concerns me and what does not concern me. O Allah, provide me with piety, forgive me my sin, and direct me to goodness wherever I turn. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the hardship of travel, the sorrow of return, and the evil appearance in family and wealth."

Thus, it behooves the traveler, at every destination, to precede his journey with these two rakʿahs and this supplication.

Consider also what pertains to one who goes out from the town to the marketplace. The author of *Istinzāl al-Luṭf al-Mawjūd fī Asrār al-Wujūd* said: "The matter of livelihood and the matter of social intercourse are a constricted and confused affair — how can one escape from this house? After such-and-such, what is the state of one whom the lions prey upon as their quarry?" — as Allah the Exalted said: {يَحْسَبُهُمُ الْجَاهِلُ أَغْنِيَاءَ مِنَ التَّعَفُّفِ} [al-Baqarah: 273]. He said in *al-Tanwīr*: "The one going out to the marketplace is like one going out to the battlefront. Thus, it behooves the believer going out to the marketplace to don, from reliance upon Allah and trust in Him, impenetrable armor that protects him from arrows."

He said: "It is deemed commendable for him to perform ablution and pray before his departure, to ask Allah for safety in his going out, and to entrust his family and home to Allah, saying: {رَبِّ إِنِّي لِمَا أَنزَلْتَ إِلَيَّ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَقِيرٌ} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 24] — 'O Allah, You are the Companion in travel and the Successor over family and wealth.'" Refer to *al-Tanwīr*, for therein is abundant good.

And let him say the basmalah previously mentioned when exiting the mosque, and say: "O Allah, I ask You for safety in travel..." — as has preceded.

[Footnote references omitted per scholarly apparatus]

# PageV1P236
anchors:
- Root: س-خ-ر (s-kh-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To subjugate, compel, or employ for service; denotes taming and making subservient.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine subjugation of creation to human benefit; theological term for God's imposition of utility upon creatures.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal here — actual subjugation of the mount; not metaphorical.
- Root: ش-ر-ف (sh-r-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Height, eminence, elevation; a high place overlooking surroundings.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Spiritual elevation and honor; in this context, physical elevation as a locus of praise.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for terrain; metaphorical for honor when applied to persons.
- Root: ن-ع-م (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Softness, ease, well-being; blessings and favors.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine beneficence; comprehensive term for all God's gifts, material and spiritual.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical comfort; metaphorical for spiritual grace.
- Sībawayh Rule: Al-ʿAṭf ʿalā al-Ḍamīr al-Marfūʿ al-Muttaṣil (Coordination on the connected subject pronoun) — Permissible after separating clause, as in "أعوذ بك أن أضل أو أُضَلّ" where the passive verb coordinates with the active.
translation:
I say — May God guide us and you to that which He loves and is pleased with.

Know that when you intend to mount a riding beast, or to travel, or to embark upon any significant affair, you should begin with the Name of God, may He be exalted, and praise Him, and invoke blessings upon His Prophet ﷺ. For the Prophet ﷺ taught his Community (ummah) such invocations for every station of their affairs, that they might thereby attain felicity in this world and the next.

Among that which has been transmitted in this regard is what the Prophet ﷺ used to say when he mounted his beast for travel:

"In the Name of God, and praise be to God. God is Greater, God is Greater, God is Greater. Glory be to Him Who has subjugated this to us, and we were not capable of it [otherwise]. And surely unto our Lord we are returning. O God, we ask You in this journey of ours for righteousness, piety, and deeds pleasing to You. O God, ease for us this journey of ours, and fold up its distance for us. O God, You are the Companion in travel, and the Successor over family and wealth. O God, I seek refuge in You from the hardship of travel, from a sorrowful return, and from an evil sight in family and wealth."

And when he returned, he would say upon his return, adding to that:

"We are returning, repenting, worshipping, praising our Lord."

And he ﷺ said:

"There is no servant who mounts a beast intending travel, then says: 'In the Name of God' — but a devil mounts behind him and says: 'Will you be sufficient for me?' Then if he says: 'Praise be to God' — the devil withdraws and says: 'Will you be sufficient for me?' Then if he says: 'God is Greater' — the devil flees from him."

And he ﷺ said:

"Whoever says when he mounts a beast: 'In the Name of God. Praise be to God. Glory be to Him Who has subjugated this to us, and we were not capable of it [otherwise]. And surely unto our Lord we are returning' — the angels say: 'May God forgive you. You have been guided, and helped, and protected.'"

And he ﷺ said:

"Whoever says: 'Glory be to God' when he ascends a height, it becomes a shield for him; and whoever says: 'God is Greater' when he descends into a valley, it becomes a shield for him."

And the Prophet ﷺ said:

"O God, unto You I submit, and in You I believe, and upon You I rely, and unto You I turn, and for Your sake I strive. O God, I seek refuge in Your might — there is no god but You — from leading astray or being led astray, from slipping or being made to slip, from wronging or being wronged, from acting ignorantly or being treated with ignorance. O Lord of the Honored Ones."

And if you ride a beast, say:

"Glory be to Him Who has subjugated this to us, and we were not capable of it [otherwise]. Praise be to God. Praise be to God. Praise be to God. God is Greater. God is Greater. God is Greater. Glory be to You, O Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, so forgive me; for none forgives sins but You."

And glorify God (subḥān Allāh) when you descend into valleys, and magnify Him (Allāhu akbar) when you ascend the mountain passes and overlook the open plains. And it was the practice of the Prophet ﷺ that when he ascended a height, he would say:

"O God, unto You belongs the honor above every honor. Praise be to God in every circumstance."

And when food or drink is brought to you — even medicine — do not eat it or drink it, if you desire to attain virtue, until you say what Imām Mālik guided you to in his Muwaṭṭaʾ:

"Praise be to God Who has guided us, and fed us, and given us to drink, and favored us. God is Greater. O God, we have been encompassed by Your favor in all its evil, so we have become in the morning and in the evening encompassed by all its good. We ask You for its completion and its gratitude. There is no good but Your good, and no god but You. O God of the righteous, and Lord of the worlds: praise be to Him, and there is no god but God. Whatever God wills, and there is no power but with God. O God, bless us in what You have provided us, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire."

This is the end of the text of the Muwaṭṭaʾ.

And when you meet someone you do not know, initiate the greeting of peace (salām) before him, so that you may thereby attain the reward and recompense. For he ﷺ said:

"The most worthy of people of God is the one who initiates the greeting of peace."

Sayyid Muḥyī al-Dīn said: And the superior practice is that you initiate with the plural pronoun, saying: "Peace be upon you" (al-salāmu ʿalaykum) — for the angels respond on his behalf, and he attains the reward of the greeting to the angels as well.

يمصافحته الأستاذ المقري؛ بمصافحته الصالح أبا عئمان بن سعيد الحناط

الشيخ أبا الحسن بن حرزهم؛ بمصافحته القاضي ابن العربي؛ بمصافحته أبا حامد
