# PageV1P237
anchors:
- Root: س-ل-م (s-l-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root denotes safety, soundness, and freedom from defect; the greeting "al-salām" invokes divine protection and peace.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, salām is a divine attribute and a prayer for the recipient's immunity from harm in this world and the next.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — verbal salutation; metaphorical (majāz) — the act of initiating peace as a means of social harmony.
- Root: ص-ف-ح (ṣ-f-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The palm of the hand (ṣafḥ); to turn the palm toward another in greeting.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Symbolizes mutual sincerity and the removal of rancor; a physical confirmation of the verbal salām.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical contact of palms; metaphorical — the gesture signifies reconciliation and goodwill.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The text uses conditional clauses (e.g., "if the one greeted is one person") and exceptions (e.g., "except for those engaged in prayer, eating, or drowsing") to delineate precise legal and ethical boundaries.
translation:
I say — may Allah guide us and you: Know that the greeting (salām) is a confirmed Sunnah, and its virtue is immense. When you meet a fellow believer, you should say: "Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah and His blessings" (al-salāmu ʿalaykum wa raḥmatu Allāhi wa barakātuhu). If the one you greet is a single person, you still use the plural form, as it is the established practice.

Do not greet one who is relieving himself, nor one who is drowsy, nor one who has a morsel of food in his mouth, nor one who is engaged in supplication (duʿāʾ), remembrance (dhikr), or recitation of the Qurʾān — for these are states that preclude the obligation of responding.

When many people are gathered, it suffices to greet those you know; you are not required to greet every single person you encounter, for that would deviate from customary practice (al-ʿurf). The purpose of the greeting is to acquire affection (wudd) or to repel something disliked (istidfāʿ makrūh).

If there is no one in your house, then upon entering you should say: "Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah" (al-salāmu ʿalaynā wa ʿalā ʿibādi Allāhi al-ṣāliḥīn). Likewise, when you stand to depart from a group, you should greet them, for the Prophet ﷺ said: "The first greeting is not more deserving than the last" (laysat al-ūlā bi-aḥaqqa min al-ākhirah).

And consider: when you meet someone you know, you should add to the greeting a handshake (muṣāfaḥah). Sayyid Muḥyī al-Dīn said: "It is a Sunnah upon which there is consensus (mujmaʿ ʿalayhā)."

I myself shook hands with my teacher al-Muntūrī — may Allah have mercy on him — who shook hands with my grandfather Ibn Baqī, who shook hands with the teacher al-Maqqarī, who shook hands with the righteous Abū ʿUthmān ibn Saʿīd al-Ḥannāṭ, who shook hands with his father, who shook hands with Shaykh Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Ḥirzihim, who shook hands with the judge Ibn al-ʿArabī, who shook hands with Abū Ḥāmid al-Ghazālī, who shook hands with Abū al-Maʿālī, who shook hands with Abū Ṭālib, who shook hands with al-Junayd, who shook hands with his maternal uncle Sirrī, who shook hands with Maʿrūf al-Karkhī, who shook hands with Dāwūd al-Ṭāʾī, who shook hands with Ḥabīb al-ʿAjamī, who shook hands with al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, who shook hands with ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib — may Allah be pleased with him — who shook hands with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, palm to palm, in an unbroken chain reaching the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

And my teacher al-Muntūrī — may Allah have mercy on him — took my hand on another occasion and said: "I took the hand of the narrator Ibn al-Sarrāj, who said: 'I took the hand of Shaykh Abū Yaʿqūb al-Nasūlī, who said: I took the hand of Shams al-Dīn ibn Jābir, who said: I took the hand of Shaykh Abū Muḥammad al-Khallāṣī, who said: I took the hand of the righteous Abū al-Ḥajjāj ibn Ḥajjāj, who said: I took the hand of Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Lawātī, who said: I took the hand of Abū al-Ḥasan ibn al-Ṣāʾigh, who said: I took the hand of Ibn Bashkuwāl, who said: I took the hand of Abū Muḥammad...'" — and so the chain of handshaking continues through the narrators (al-rāwiyah).

title_en: On Handshaking, Its Virtues, and the Innovation of Post-Prayer Handshakes

أخذ بيدي أبو بكر المنقري؛ قال: أخذ بيدي أبو سعيد بن الأعرابي؛ قال: أخبذ بيدي

بيدك؟”' قال: قلت: غيرًا يا نبي الله: قال: "لا يلقى مسلم مسلمًا فيبش به ويرحب

الشريعة؛ وأن من أمثلة الدع المباحة المصافحة عقب الصبح والعصر. اه

# PageV1P238
anchors:
- Root: ص-ف-ح (ṣ-f-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "To strike with the palm (ṣafḥ), to turn away, to pardon; the handshake (muṣāfaḥah) is the joining of palms as a sign of amity."
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): "In the Qur'an, ṣafḥ denotes forgiveness and turning away from sin; in prophetic practice, the handshake embodies mutual pardon and the shedding of rancor."
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): "Literal: the striking of palm against palm; metaphorical: the exchange of greeting and reconciliation, as in 'they shook hands' meaning they made peace."
- Root: ب-د-ع (b-d-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "To originate, to create anew; bidʿah is an innovation in religion not sanctioned by the Lawgiver."
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): "Bidʿah is of two kinds: that which contradicts the Sunnah (misguidance) and that which is permissible or even commendable if it serves a recognized good."
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): "Literal: bringing into existence without precedent; metaphorical: any practice introduced into religion, whether blameworthy or permissible."
- Sībawayh Rule: "Conditional Clause with 'Illā' (Exception) — The phrase 'illā tanātharat' (except that they fall) is a jumla sharṭiyyah where the protasis is implied by the preceding negation, governing the apodosis as a necessary consequence."
translation:
I say — and success is from God alone:

The chain of transmission for the virtue of handshaking has reached us through multiple paths. Among them is what was related by al-Bayhaqī in Shuʿab al-Īmān, on the authority of al-Fihrī, who said: Abū al-Ḥasan Ṭāhir took my hand and said: Abū al-Fatḥ and Abū al-Layth took my hand; they said: Abū Bakr ibn Manṣūr ibn Khalaf took my hand; he said: My father Manṣūr took my hand; he said: Abū Bakr al-Munqarī took my hand; he said: Abū Saʿīd ibn al-Aʿrābī took my hand; he said: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAffān took my hand; he said: Ibn ʿAṭiyyah took my hand; he said: Qaṭarī al-Khashshāb took my hand; he said: Yazīd ibn al-Barrāʾ ibn ʿĀzib took my hand; he said: My father al-Barrāʾ took my hand; he said: I entered upon the Messenger of God {ﷺ}, and he welcomed me warmly and took my hand. Then he said to me: "O Barrāʾ, do you know why I took your hand?" I said: "God and His Messenger know best, O Prophet of God." He said: "No two Muslims meet, and one greets the other with cheerfulness, welcomes him, and takes his hand, except that their sins fall away between them as the leaves of a dry tree fall away."

And from al-Tirmidhī, Abū Dāwūd, and Ibn Mājah: that the Messenger of God {ﷺ} said: "No two Muslims meet and shake hands except that they are forgiven before they part."

The Sayyid Muḥyī al-Dīn said: As for what people have accustomed themselves to — the handshake after the dawn prayer and after the afternoon prayer — there is no basis for it in the Sacred Law in that specific manner. However, there is no harm in it, for the origin of the handshake is a Sunnah. The fact that people have been diligent in observing it in some circumstances and negligent in many others does not remove that particular practice from being a form of the handshake whose origin the Sacred Law has established.

He said: The Imām, the Shaykh, Ibn ʿAbd al-Salām mentioned in his Qawāʿid that innovations are divided according to the categories of the Sacred Law, and that among the examples of permissible innovation (bidʿah mubāḥah) is the handshake immediately following the dawn and afternoon prayers. End quote.

He also stated explicitly that it is fitting for those who shake hands to invoke blessings upon the Messenger of God {ﷺ}, and if they say: «رَبَّنَا آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ» [Our Lord, give us in this world good and in the Hereafter good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire] (al-Baqarah 2:201), this has been transmitted from the Messenger of God {ﷺ}. It has already preceded at the beginning of the book that standing up for one who enters is permissible out of fear of mutual rancor. The Sayyid Muḥyī al-Dīn said: It is recommended to stand for one who possesses excellence — whether of knowledge, righteousness, nobility, or authority accompanied by probity — as an act of piety and honor.

And consider the kissing of the hand. The Sayyid, the Muftī of Tunis, al-Burzulī, said: I kissed the hand of my Shaykh al-Baṭarnī...

# PageV1P239
anchors:
- Root: ن-ك-س (n-k-s)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To lower, invert, or bend downward; the act of inclining the head.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Denotes physical humility, distinct from the ritual bowing (rukūʿ) in prayer, which is an act of worship.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical posture; metaphorical (majāz) for submission of the heart.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-sharṭ) — "If it falls short of the limit of rukūʿ" (in-naqaṣa ʿan ḥadd al-rukūʿ) governs permissibility, with the protasis restricting the apodosis.
translation:
I say: Know that the station of the elite among the rightly guided is not attained by one who is not of the rank of the perfect ones. So let him strive in seeking the rulings that are decisive.

He (the author) said: He (the questioner) then withdrew his hand; so I said: "Will you not then narrate the book of al-Aṣbahānī concerning the license for kissing the hand, when you have not acted upon it?" He replied to me: "Mālik disapproved of it." So I said: "Mālik rejected what has been narrated concerning it, and the one who preserves (a ḥadīth) is an argument against the one who does not preserve." So he left me after that. And likewise was my shaykh, the Imām — meaning Ibn ʿArafah — and others of my shaykhs; they did not disapprove of that from me. He said: "My intent in that was seeking blessing (tabarruk) and veneration for my shaykhs." And since it was established for me from the ḥadīths, and the lack of disapproval of that from most of those whom I follow.

He said: As for bowing (al-inḥināʾ), ʿIzz al-Dīn said: "What people do of lowering their heads — there is no harm in it if it falls short of the limit of rukūʿ, for one who is honored among the people of Islam."

And consider: When you sneeze, say: "Praise be to God in every state, whatever the state may be, and may God bless our master Muḥammad and his family." For it has been narrated... And among the supplications of the Messenger of God, peace be upon him: "O God, I ask You for guidance, piety, chastity, and sufficiency." And he taught a man, saying: "Say: O God, forgive me, have mercy on me, guide me, and provide for me." And he said: "Seek refuge with God from the hardship of trial, from the overtaking of misery, from the evil of decree, and from the gloating of enemies." And Abū Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: "Teach me, O Messenger of God, a supplication I may make in my prayer." He said: "Say: O God, I have wronged myself greatly, and none forgives sins but You; so forgive me with a forgiveness from You, and have mercy on me; indeed, You are the Forgiving, the Merciful."

title_en: The Station of Supplication and Reliance on Divine Knowledge
arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 239

ميج فون شق هن م خرف للد نل كن من تس كع أرقت يجيد لي مس ارت طاضة 303

قال السيد محيي الدين الدووي: وإن كان هذا وردا في الصلاة فهو حسن
انفيس صحيح يستحب في كل موطن. قال: وتقول أنت: كثيرًا كبيرًا لتجمع بين
الروابتين. ومن دعائه :"الهم أصلح لي ديني الذي هو عصمة أمري؛ وأصلح
الي دنياي الني فيها معاشي؛ وأصلح لي آخرتي الني إلبها معادي؛ واجعل الحياة
ازيادة لي في كل خيرء واجعل الموت راحة لي من كل شر”؛ ومن دعواته كة:
"اللهم ألهمني رشدي؛ وأعذني من شر نفسي”3؛ وقال رجل: وا ذنوياه» فقال
رسول الله ي: "قل: مغفرتك أوسع من ذنوبي؛ ورحمتك أرجى عندي من
عملي

ونقل السيد محبي الدين النووي "أن لله تعالى ملكا موكلا بمن يقول: يا أرحم
الراحمين: فمن قالها ثلانًا قال له الملك: إن أرحم الراحمين أقبل عليك فاسأل.
وقد تقدم لنا في الورد الأول أنه وقت حضوره فاتتخذ لتوجهك ما يكون أرق لقلبك
وأوفق لحالك وأجرى على لساتك. وكذلك نقل السيد محيي الدين في الدعاء
منقولا عن الفشيري: إن وجدت في قلبك إشارة على الدعاء فالدعاء أولى لك.
وانظر أن جبريل عليه السلام لما قال لإبراهيم حين زج في المنجنيق وهو في أفق
الهواء: ألك حاجة؟ قال: أما إليك فلاء وأما إلى لله فبلى؛ فقال: فسله؛ فقال إبراههم
عليه السلام: حسبي من سؤالي علمه بحالي. وأن موسى عليه السلام قال: (إرتَانٍ
لِمَآَرَد )4 [القصص: 24]. قال علي رضي الله عنه: والله ما
طلب إلا خبرًا يأكله: ولككن المطلب وإن كان يسيرًا ليلا فقد صار لفتحه باب
المناجات جليلا؛ فموسى عليه السلام سأل من الله الشيء اليسير؛ وإبراهيم عليه
السلام قال في الأمر العظيم: حسبي من سؤالي علمه بحائي. قال في التتوير: اعلم
أن الأنياء عليهم السلام يعاملون كل موطن بما يفهمون عن اله أنه اللائق بهم: فهم
إبراهيم عليه السلام أن المراد به في ذلك الموطن عدم إظهار النشكي والطلب
والاكتفاء بالعلم أن يظهر منصب سره وعنايته به للملا الأعلى: وموسى عليه السلام

anchors:
- Root: د-ع-و (da-ʿa-wa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Calling, invoking, supplication; the act of summoning or requesting
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The servant's turning to Allah with humble request, acknowledging need (iftiqār)
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for verbal invocation; metaphorical (majāz) for the soul's innate disposition toward its Creator
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Response Construction (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb) — governing the relationship between the servant's state and the divine response
translation:
I say — and the Master Muḥyī al-Dīn al-Nawawī said: If this (supplication) occurs during prayer, it is excellent, sound, and commendable in every station. He said: And you should say it repeatedly and abundantly, to combine between the two transmitted narrations.

And among his supplications (upon him be peace): "O Allah, set right for me my religion, which is the safeguard of my affair; and set right for me my worldly life, wherein is my livelihood; and set right for me my Hereafter, wherein is my return; and make life an increase for me in every good, and make death a repose for me from every evil."

And among his supplications (upon him be peace): "O Allah, inspire me with my right guidance, and protect me from the evil of my own soul."

And a man said: "Woe to my sins!" — whereupon the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Say: 'Your forgiveness is vaster than my sins, and Your mercy is more hopeful to me than my deeds.'"

And the Master Muḥyī al-Dīn al-Nawawī transmitted that Allah Most High has an angel entrusted with the one who says: "O Most Merciful of the merciful." Whoever says it three times, the angel says to him: "Indeed, the Most Merciful of the merciful has turned toward you, so ask."

And it has preceded for us in the first litany (al-wird al-awwal) that when the time of His presence (ḥuḍūr) arrives, you should adopt for your turning (tawajjuh) that which is more tender to your heart, more fitting to your state, and more fluent upon your tongue.

Likewise, the Master Muḥyī al-Dīn transmitted in the chapter of supplication, narrated from al-Qushayrī: If you find in your heart an indication toward supplication, then supplication is more appropriate for you.

And consider that Gabriel (peace be upon him), when he said to Abraham — at the moment he was cast into the catapult, while suspended in the horizon of the air — "Do you have any need?" — he replied: "As for you, no; but as for Allah, yes." Gabriel said: "Then ask Him." Abraham (peace be upon him) said: "Sufficient for me, from my asking, is His knowledge of my state."

And Moses (peace be upon him) said: {«رَبِّ إِنِّي لِمَا أَنزَلْتَ إِلَيَّ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَقِيرٌ»} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 24] — "My Lord, indeed I am in need of whatever good You send down to me."

ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him) said: By Allah, he sought nothing but food to eat — yet the request, though it be small in itself, became, by opening the door of intimate communion (munājāt), great in dignity. For Moses (peace be upon him) asked Allah for a trifling thing; while Abraham (peace be upon him) said concerning a tremendous matter: "Sufficient for me, from my asking, is His knowledge of my state."

He said in al-Tanwīr: Know that the prophets (peace be upon them) deal with every station according to what they understand from Allah to be befitting them therein. # PageV1P242
anchors:
- Root: و-ر-د (w-r-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root denotes arriving at water, a place of watering, or a station of approach; hence a "portion" or "turn" of devotional practice.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the spiritual path, wird signifies a fixed liturgical portion assigned to a seeker, marking a station (maqām) of approach to the Divine.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: watering-place; metaphorical: the soul's appointed time of drawing near to God through prescribed worship.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The sequence of "wirds" is structured as coordinated appositives, each defining a temporal segment with its specific devotional content.
translation:
I say — and success is from God alone:

Know that the intent of the Real (al-Ḥaqq) from His servant in the varying of trials is the manifestation of the servant's neediness (ifḥār al-fāqah); so the servant undertakes what his moment requires. {«For each is a direction to which he turns»} [al-Baqarah: 148]. Thus everyone is upon clear proof, guidance, and divine care from God. End.

Consider also the affair of Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq (may God be pleased with him) at Badr: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was overcome by fear, and he did not cease supplicating and imploring until his cloak fell from his shoulders. And Abū Bakr (may God be pleased with him), due to the Prophet's extreme need, had the door of hope opened for him, and he said: "Enough, O Messenger of God, your pleading to your Lord; for God will surely fulfill for you what He has promised you."

This is the meaning of what Tāj al-Dīn said in his aphorisms (ḥikam): "The arrivals of spiritual states (wāridāt al-aḥwāl)."

---

**The Fifth Wird**: From the prayer of illumination (ṣalāt al-ishrāq) until mid-morning (ḍaḥwah); that is, the midpoint between sunrise and zenith (zawāl) — which is a quarter of the daytime. This is the time of the forenoon prayer (ṣalāt al-ḍuḥā). Abū Dāwūd narrated that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever leaves his house for an obligatory prayer, his reward is like the reward of a pilgrim (ḥājj); and whoever goes out for the glorification of the forenoon (tasbīḥ al-ḍuḥā), nothing impels him but it, his reward is like the reward of one performing ʿumrah."

The author of *al-Targhīb wa al-Tarhīb* said: His saying "nothing impels him" (lā yanṣibuhu) means: nothing follows him nor disturbs him except that [intention]. He said: Every supererogatory prayer is called a "glorification" (tasbīḥ) and a "supererogatory act" (sabḥah). In the Ṣaḥīḥ, on the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may God be pleased with him), he said: "My beloved (the Prophet) advised me to pray the forenoon prayer, and I shall not abandon it until I die." And the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) prayed the forenoon prayer on the day of the Conquest of Mecca eight rakʿahs. In al-Tirmidhī, the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever maintains the forenoon glorification (sabḥat al-ḍuḥā), his sins are forgiven even if they be like the foam of the sea." Ibn al-ʿArabī narrated: "Whoever prays the forenoon prayer twelve rakʿahs, God builds for him a palace in Paradise."

---

**The Sixth Wird**: From mid-morning (ḍuḥā) to zenith (zawāl). He said in *al-Iḥyāʾ*: In this wird, one should add engagement in earning a livelihood (al-kasb) and the midday nap (al-qaylūlah), which is a Sunnah. He said: If one occupies himself with worship and abandons sleep and earning, then it is fitting that God purify him and choose him for His nearness — because he has devoted himself to the service of his Lord during a time when people are heedless of God and occupied with worldly concerns. This is like the virtue of reviving the night, for it is a time of people's heedlessness in sleep. It has been said regarding His saying (Exalted is He): {«He it is Who made the night and the day in succession»} [al-Furqān: 62] — each one follows the other in virtue. End.

So reflect, O my brother in God, upon this entrance (madkhal). And know that if the motives and incentives are ever made available to you for it, then seize the opportunity.

---

**The Seventh Wird**: From zenith (zawāl) to the completion of the noon prayer (ẓuhr). He said in *al-Iḥyāʾ*: This is among the most virtuous of the daytime wirds, which the Exalted intended by His saying: {«And glorify Him in the evening and when you reach the noon»} [al-Rūm: 18]. And the report has come that the gates of heaven are opened at this time, and supplication is answered therein.

Consider, from the virtue of this time, the saying of ʿUmar: "Whoever misses his nightly portion (ḥizb) and prays it after the zenith, it is as if he had not missed it." And the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) used to pray four rakʿahs after the zenith, and he said: "This is an hour in which the gates of heaven are opened, and I love that a righteous deed of mine ascend therein." Sayyid Muḥyī al-Dīn said: It is recommended to increase in remembrances (adhkār) and other acts of worship immediately following the zenith. End, with his clarification.

---

**The Eighth Wird**: Between the two noons (i.e., between ẓuhr and ʿaṣr). He said in *al-Iḥyāʾ*: This is also a time of heedlessness; thus, devoting oneself to worship in it is like devoting oneself to worship in the night. It was from the practice of the Salaf to remain in seclusion (iʿtikāf) in the mosque during this time — unless being among people is safer for your religion and more concentrating for your concerns, for then it is superior. He said: This wird is one of the foundational pillars, for God (Exalted is He) says: {«And unto God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and their shadows, in the mornings and the evenings»} [al-Raʿd: 15]. So if inanimate objects prostrate, how can the intelligent one be heedless of the various types of worship?

Al-Ḥāfiẓ Abū ʿUmar narrated in his *Tamhīd* with his chain: That the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) supplicated on Monday and was not answered; he supplicated on Tuesday and Wednesday, and was answered on Wednesday between the two prayers. Jābir said: "Thereafter, no important matter befell me but that I sought out that hour and supplicated therein, and I recognized the answer."

---

**The Ninth Wird**: When the time of ʿaṣr enters until the yellowing of the sun. God (Exalted is He) swore by it, saying: {«By the afternoon (al-ʿaṣr), verily man is in loss»} [al-ʿAṣr: 1-2].

وخذ نصفه بين العشاءين خاليا وخذ نصفه الثاني على إثر الفجر

وقد تقدم أيضًا أن من قصد بالنوم تجميم نفسه ليقوم نشيطا لعبادة ريه أن نومه
محسوب في جملة الأوراد. قال السيد الساحلي: وليحافظ على وتره من أول الليلء
فذلك الحزم؛ ولا تمكر به النفس فتقول: آخر اليل أفضل؛ وليعمر آخر اليل كما
تقدم بأذكار الحضوره وكذا قال في الإحياء: إن تقديم الوتر أول الليل مع أن تأخيره
عند العلماء بأحكام الله أفضل؛ هل يكون هذا إمائة لحظ نفس؟ قال تاج الدين:
إحالتك الأعمال على وجود الفراغ من رعونات النفوس. قال شارحها: الرعونة:
ضرب من الحمق وحماقة من وجوه.

منها: ما في ذلك من رؤية التفس ودعو الحول.

وجه آخر: قد يتبدل عزمه أو يعرض له شغل.

وقد كان أبو بكر رضي الله عنه يقدم وتره؛ وفي صحيح البخاري ومسلم عن
أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه: أوصاني خليلي بثلاث لا أدعهن حتى أموت؛ صوم ثلاثة أيام
من كل شهر؛ وصلاة الضحى؛ ونوم على وتر. فقد تضمن مما قورته واخترته ولي فيه
أسوة لني فيه أقوى من ظني في غيره أن لكل وقت من هذه الأوقات الاثني عشر ورا
خاضًا به دون الهجير يكون ذلك في ذهنك كالوردء إن لم تفعل ذلك الورد الخاص
بادلك الوقت استخلفت ما فاتك في الوقت قبله؛ وإن لم يكن يفتح لك في ذلك
تتأسف على نفسك وتغيب بتقصيرها عن تفصير غيرك؛ وتنشدا""؛

العسرك إن في ذني لشفلا لنفسي عن ذنوب يني أميه

واسم أبي زياد مسلم وقد اختلف فيه على الأعمش ولابن مردويه من حدديث أنس "أنها
نزلت في الصلاة بين المغرب والعشاء" والحديث عند الترمذي وحسته بلفظ "نزلت في
انتظار الصلاة التي تدعى إل

اا انظر؛إعانة الطابين 284/4 والأذكار 336/1.

# PageV1P244
anchors:
- Root: ع-ص-ر (ʿ-ṣ-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The core meaning is "pressing, squeezing" (as of grapes or dates), and by extension "time" as that which presses upon and constrains human affairs; also "the afternoon" (al-ʿaṣr).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Quranic usage, al-ʿaṣr denotes the epoch or age in which humanity is at loss except those who believe and do righteous deeds; it carries a solemn oath-signifying the weight of time as a divine witness.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally "the pressing out" (ḥaqīqah); metaphorically (majāz), it is the "afternoon prayer" and "the passing time" — a metonymy for the fleeting nature of worldly life.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Taqdīm wa Taʾkhīr (Fronting and Delaying) — In the phrase "يستحب زيادة الاعتناء بالأذكار في الصبح والعصر" the prepositional phrase "في الصبح والعصر" is fronted for emphasis (ikhtiṣāṣ), restricting the recommendation to these two specific times.
translation:
I say — may Allah guide us and you: Know that the rightly guided conduct (sunan al-muhtadīn) in the stations of religion requires vigilance over the appointed times of remembrance (adhkār). The author of the Iḥyāʾ has said — and I transmit his words verbatim — that when the sun begins to yellow (i.e., near sunset), the state is like that from dawn until sunrise: this one is before the sun's rising, and that one is before its setting. Thus it is recommended (mustaḥabb) in this time to engage specifically in glorification (tasbīḥ) and seeking forgiveness (istighfār), due to His saying — exalted is He: {«فَسُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ حِينَ تُمْسُونَ وَحِينَ تُصْبِحُونَ»} [al-Rūm: 17] — "So glorify Allah when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning."

And let the servant call his own soul to account (yuḥāsib nafsahu), for it has come in the report: "There is no blessing in a day in which one does not increase in goodness." And let him repair in his night what he has neglected in his day. It was the practice of ʿUmar — may Allah be pleased with him — to strike his own feet with the whip (durrah) and say to his soul: "What have you done today?" And he also said — may Allah be pleased with him: "Call yourselves to account before you are called to account, and weigh your deeds before they are weighed against you."

The author of the Iḥyāʾ said: Know that just as the servant has a time at the beginning of the day in which he makes a covenant (mushāraṭah) with his soul, by way of enjoining the truth upon himself, likewise he should have at the end of the day an hour in which he calls his soul to task and accounts for all its movements and its silences. This is exactly what merchants do in this world with their partners at the end of every year, out of zeal for worldly gain — so how much more fitting is it for the seeker of the Hereafter to do so with his own soul that commands evil (al-nafs al-ammārah). And it is incumbent upon you, O my brother in Allah, to consult the Book of Self-Accounting (Kitāb al-Muḥāsabah) from the Iḥyāʾ.

As for the eleventh wird (oration) — between the two evening prayers (i.e., between Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ) — there is the report: "The prayer between the two evening prayers erases the frivolity of the day." It has already been mentioned that this time resembles the beginning of the day. And the master al-Sāḥilī said in his poem on the path (qaṣīdat al-sulūk) concerning the wirds:

"Keep to two times and be constant in them both..." — then he said:
"Take half of it between the two evening prayers, free from distractions, and take the other half immediately after dawn."

It has also been previously established that whoever intends by his sleep to strengthen his body so that he may rise energetically for the worship of his Lord — his sleep is counted among his wirds (i.e., as an act of devotion). The master al-Sāḥilī said: Let him be diligent in performing his witr (odd-numbered night prayer) at the beginning of the night, for that is prudence (ḥazm); and let not the soul deceive him by saying: "The end of the night is more virtuous." Rather, let him also enliven the end of the night with the remembrances of presence (adhkār al-ḥuḍūr), as has been previously mentioned. Likewise, the author of the Iḥyāʾ said: If one performs the witr at the beginning of the night, while the scholars of Allah's rulings hold that delaying it is more virtuous — is this not a concession to the soul's desire? Tāj al-Dīn said: "Your deferral of deeds upon the existence of leisure from the vanities of the souls." Its commentator said: "Al-raʿūnah (vanity) is a kind of foolishness and stupidity in certain respects."

Among these respects: what it entails of self-regard (ruʾyat al-nafs) and the claim of power (daʿwā al-ḥawl).

Another aspect: his resolve may change, or an occupation may present itself to him.

Abū Bakr — may Allah be pleased with him — used to perform his witr early. And in the Ṣaḥīḥ of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, on the authority of Abū Hurayrah — may Allah be pleased with him: "My intimate friend (khalīlī) — meaning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ — advised me with three things which I shall not abandon until I die: fasting three days of every month, the forenoon prayer (ḍuḥā), and sleeping after performing the witr."

Thus, from what I have gathered and chosen — and in it I have an exemplar (uswah) stronger than my opinion regarding others — it is established that for each of these twelve times there is a specific wird (wird khāṣṣ) particular to it, distinct from the midday heat (al-hajīr). Let this be in your mind like a fixed oration: if you do not perform that specific wird at its proper time, you make up what you missed in the time preceding it. And if no opening (fatḥ) is granted to you in that, then grieve over yourself and be saddened by your shortcoming compared to the shortcomings of others — and recite:

"Your hardship — indeed in my sin there is a distraction for my soul from the sins of my mother's sons."

And the name of Abū Ziyād is Muslim, and there is disagreement concerning him regarding al-Aʿmash. And Ibn Mardawayh has from the ḥadīth of Anas that "it was revealed concerning the prayer between Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ" — and the ḥadīth is found in al-Tirmidhī, who graded it ḥasan, with the wording: "It was revealed concerning the waiting for the prayer which is called..."

|فتكون نيتك أيها الأخ في لله أن أول ما تصرف فيه همتك إلى الله أول يقظة.
من الليل؛ وهذا هو الورد الأول. ثم تعود للنوم ليكون أسا لقيام السحرء وهذا هو
الورد الثاني. ثم تقوم سحرًا لتمام ما بقي من وردك أو لقراءة القرآن ريثما يطلع

الزوال؛ تنام فيه القيلولة. ثم الورد السابع إلى الفراغ من صلاة الظهر. ثم الورد
الثامن» وهو ما بين الظهرين. ثم الورد التاسع إلى اصفرار الشمس. ثم الورد العاشر
إذا اصفرت الشمس. ثم الورد الحادي عشر بين العشاءين.

ائم الورد الثاني عشر: بعد العثمة إلى أول يقظة. فينبغي إن لم تسرمد العيادة
وتعمر هذه الأوقات بالأوراد متى وجدت فراعًا في وقت منها أن تغتنمه؛ إما أن
تشتغل فيه بورده الخاص به أو بهجيرا يكون لك؛ أو تخلف فيه ما كان متأكدا عندك

ولتعين لكل وقت شغلاء فبذلك تظهر بركة الأوقات: فإن من ترك نقسه هملا
سدى إهمال البهائم لا يدري بماذا يشتغل في كل وقتء فتنقضي أكثر أوقاته
ضائعة. الى

وانظر في فرض الاعتكاف عمران الأوقات بالطاعات. فينبغي أن ينوي في
اتكانه هذه ان قال الحسن البصري رحمه اله قد قفتي كلمة سمعته من

هر ايكذ المرء في كل ون باهر ألى في الونتد وقد تقدم أذ هد مي

# PageV1P245

### | الصفحة 245

المقام التاسع
الأخن بالجد في الدين

.وهو المقام الذي كنت بدأت به وها أنا أختم به ختم الله لي به بمنه وقضلد
وهو أن يكون المرء كما حكاه في التنوير: لو قيل له: غدًا تموت لم يجد مستزافاء
وفي الرسالة: كان أبو علي التففي يتكلم يومًا قال له عبد الله بن منازل: يا أبا عليء
استعد للموت؛ فلا بد منه؛ فتوسد عبد الله ذراعه ووضع رأسه وقال: قد مث.
فانقطع أبو علي؛ لأنه لم يمكنه أن يقابل بما فعل؛ لأن أبا علي كانت له علاقات»
وكان عبد الله مجردًا لا شغل له؛ قال له سفيان الشوري رضي الله عنه: رأيت في
مسجد الكوفة شيِخًا يقول: أنا في هذا المسجد منذ ثلاثين سنة أننظر الموت أن
ينزل بي؛ لو أتاني ما أمرت بشيء ولا نهيت عن شيء ولا لي على أحد شيء ولا
الأحد عندي شي».

قال في الإحياء: كل نفس من أنفاسك خاتمة؛ إذ يمكن أن يكون الموت منصلا
به وهب أن الموت لم يكن متصلا به أليس يعرض عليك يوم القيامة؟. وقد قال رجل
الإبراهيم بن أدهم: كم من فرض علي في اليوم والليلة؟ فقال: ما لك والتعرض لما ل
تقوم به؟ عليك بما تعلمه؛ فألح الرجل عليه مرارا فقال له إبراهيم ابن أدهم: يجب
عليك في كل لحظة ثلاثة فروض لازمة تعصي الله إن تركت منها واحداء قال: وما هي؟
قال: ذكر الله والإخلاص له والرضا بكل ما يأتي من الله. له

ولاشك أن الحق هو هذا' إذ كل نفس يبدو من المرء فهو ظرف لقدر من
أقدار الله ونعمة من الله. وحقيقة الشكر تصريف النعمة في طاعة المنعم. قال في
الاحياء: في كل نفس تنقبض من الإنسان وتنبسط تعمتاذ؛ إذ باتبساطها يخرج
الدخان من القلب؛ ولو لم يخرج لهلك الإنسان» وباتقباض النفس ينجمع روح
الهواء إلى القلب» ولو سد منفذه لاحترق القلب؛ واليوم واللبلة أربع وعشرون
ساعة» في كل ساعة قريب من ألف نفس: وكل نفس قريب من عشر لحظات»

# PageV1P246
anchors:
- Root: ج-د-د (j-d-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Earnestness, exertion, and the cutting off of laxity; the opposite of jest (hazl).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The soul's striving in obedience with full resolve, untainted by worldly distraction.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: firmness in a matter; metaphorical: the heart's severance from negligence.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional apodosis with omitted protasis (Sharṭ muqaddar) — "If it were said to him: 'Tomorrow you die,' he would find no delay" implies an unspoken condition of total readiness.
translation:
I say — and with Allah is the success — this is the station with which I began this book, and with it I now conclude; may Allah seal it for me with His bounty and decree.

Know, O brother, that the reality of this station is that a person becomes as was related in *al-Tanwīr*: if it were said to him, "Tomorrow you will die," he would find no postponement (mustazāfah) in himself. And in *al-Risālah*: Abū ʿAlī al-Thaqafī was speaking one day when ʿAbd Allāh ibn Manāzil said to him: "O Abū ʿAlī, prepare for death, for it is inevitable." So ʿAbd Allāh pillowed his arm, laid his head down, and said: "It has come." Abū ʿAlī was then cut short, for he could not respond with what ʿAbd Allāh had done — because Abū ʿAlī had attachments, while ʿAbd Allāh was stripped bare, having no occupation. Sufyān al-Thawrī (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "I saw in the mosque of Kūfah an elder saying: 'I have been in this mosque for thirty years awaiting death to descend upon me; if it came to me, I would not have been commanded anything, nor forbidden anything, nor would anyone owe me anything, nor would I owe anyone anything.'"

He said in *al-Iḥyāʾ*: Every breath of yours is a final one (khātimah), for death could be attached to it. And even if death were not attached to it, would it not be presented to you on the Day of Resurrection? A man said to Ibrāhīm ibn Adham: "How many obligations (furūḍ) are upon me in the day and night?" He replied: "What is it to you to expose yourself to what you cannot fulfill? Upon you is what you know." The man pressed him repeatedly, so Ibrāhīm ibn Adham said: "Upon you, in every moment, are three binding obligations — you disobey Allah if you abandon any one of them." He asked: "What are they?" He said: "The remembrance of Allah (dhikr Allāh), sincerity to Him (ikhlāṣ lahu), and contentment with everything that comes from Allah (riḍā bi-mā yaʾtī min Allāh)."

There is no doubt that the truth is this — for every breath that issues from a person is a vessel for a decree of Allah's decrees and a blessing from Allah. The reality of gratitude (shukr) is the directing of the blessing toward obedience to the Benefactor. He said in *al-Iḥyāʾ*: In every breath that a person draws in and releases there is a benefit (niʿmah); for with its release, the smoke exits from the heart — and were it not to exit, the person would perish; and with its drawing in, the spirit of air gathers to the heart — and were its passage blocked, the heart would burn. The day and night are twenty-four hours; in each hour there are nearly a thousand breaths; and each breath is nearly ten moments (laḥaẓāt).

And know that the one who neglects these breaths, letting them pass in heedlessness, has squandered a capital that cannot be restored. The predecessors (salaf) used to say: "The breaths are counted, and each breath is a treasure — so guard it." Thus, the station of earnestness (jidd) is the summation of all the stations, for it is the soul's constant vigilance over its moments, not letting a single one slip without obedience — whether in remembrance, reflection, or action. This is the station of the sincerely truthful (ṣiddīqīn), and it is the seal of the conduct of the rightly guided.

arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 246

2-0 منهج الترقي) المقام التاسع: الأ بالجد في الدين
.وعليك في كل لحظة ألف ألف نعمة في كل جزء من أجزائك.

قال بعضهم: انظر انتصاب قامتك طالبة بنية العلوه وجعل ثقبي أذنيك متصلين
بالدماغ يؤديان ما أوصل إليهما إلى القلب؛ جعل سبحانه فيهما المرارة تمنع منهما
الهوام أن يصل إلبهماء كما جمل الملوحة في العينين تشدهما أن تذوباء وجعل
الحلاوة في اللسان يجد طعم الحلو من المر؛ وجعل الرطوبة في المنخرين لو كانا
يابسين لم تجد لرائحة شماء وجعل الحاجبين فوق العينين رقرفا واقيا ما ينزل من
الأعلى» فهذء كلها نعم لا تحصي شكرها عليك في كل جزئية منها بل في كل جزء
من أجزاء العالم أن تؤدي شكرهاء فإن صرفت جزئية من جزئياتك في غير رضاا
ريك فقد جنيت على جميع الملك والملكوت؛ فمن فتح جفنه وصرفه فيما لا يحل
فقد كفر كل نعمة عليه لله في السماوات والأرض وما بينهماء فإن لله في كل تطريفة
نعمتين في نفس الجفن؛ إذ خلق الله سبحانه تحت كل جفن عضلات ولها أوتار
وربطات متصلة بأعصاب الدماغ بها يتم انخفاض الجفن الأعلى وارتفاع الجفن
الأسفل وعلى كل جفن شعور؛ ونعمة الله في سوادها أنها تجمع ضوء العين؛ إذ
البياض يفرق الضوء والسواد يجمعه؛ ونعمة الله في ترتييها صمًا واحدًا أن يكون
مانا للهوام من الدبيب إلى باطن العينء ومحبسا للأقذاء التي تتناثر من الهواء؛ ولله
في كل شعرة منها نعمتان من حيث لين أصلها ومع اللين قوم نصبهاء وله في اشنتباك
الأهداب نعمة أعظم من الكل» وهو أن غبار الهواء قد يمنع من فتح العين ولو أطبق
الم بيصرء فجمع الأجفان مقدار ما تتشابك بالأهداب فينظر من وراء شياك الشعر
فيكون شباك الشعر مانغا من وصول القذا من خارج وغير مانع من امتداد البصر من
داخمل؛ وخلدق الله سبحائه وتعالى أطراف الأجفان حادة منطبقة على الحدقة
كالمصقلة: فإن أصاب الحدقة غبار فتتطبق الأجفان مرة أو مرتين فتنصقل الحدقة
عن الغبار وتخرج الأقذاء إلى زوايا العين؛ ولما لم يكن للذباب أجفان خلق الله له
يدين تراه على الدوام يمسح بهما جفنيه ليصقلهما من الغبارات؛ فمن فتح جفنه
حيث يجب غضه فقد كفر بفتح العين تعمة الله في الأجفانء ولا تقوم الأجفان إلا
بالعين؛ ولا العين إلا بالرأسء ولا الرأس إلا بجميع البدنء ولا اليدن إلا بالغذاء»
ولا الغذاء إلا بالماء والأرض والهواء والمطر والغيم والشمس والقمر والنجوم»
ولم يقم شيء من ذلك إلا بالسماوات؛ والسماوات بالملائكة: فإن الكل كالشيء

# PageV1P247
anchors:
- Root: ج-د (j-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Exertion, striving with full effort; the core sense of "earnestness" as opposed to laxity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the path of religion, it denotes the disciplined application of one's entire being toward divine obedience, not mere physical toil.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) here — the actual expenditure of effort in worship; metaphorical (majāz) if applied to God's attributes, which is not the case here.
- Root: ن-ع-م (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Grace, benefaction, ease; the root implies both the gift and the state of well-being it produces.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, niʿmah is every divine favor that leads to felicity, whether worldly or otherworldly; its opposite is naqmah (retribution).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for tangible gifts (eyes, ears); metaphorical when extended to the entire cosmos as a single integrated grace.
- Root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To cover, conceal; hence ingratitude that veils the recognition of a benefactor.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, kufr is the deliberate denial or misuse of divine favors, ranging from outright disbelief to the "lesser kufr" of ungratefulness in action.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for covering a seed in the ground; metaphorical for the heart that covers the truth of God's blessings.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Conditional Clause with In (إن) — The protasis (condition) and apodosis (result) are both in the past tense, indicating a general, timeless truth (e.g., "If one opens his eyelid... he has disbelieved"), with the apodosis carrying the force of a legal-moral verdict.
translation:
I say: And upon you, in every moment, are a thousand thousand graces — in every single part of your being.

One of the sages said: Consider the uprightness of your stature, seeking by its very constitution the intent of elevation; and how He made the two perforations of your ears connected to the brain, conveying to the heart whatever reaches them; He — glorified be He — placed in them a bitterness that prevents creeping creatures from reaching the brain, just as He placed a saltiness in the two eyes that keeps them from melting; and He placed a sweetness in the tongue, so that one may distinguish the taste of the sweet from the bitter; and He placed a moisture in the two nostrils — for were they dry, you would find no scent to smell; and He placed the two eyebrows above the eyes as a protective canopy against what descends from above. All these are graces whose gratitude you cannot enumerate — not in each particular of them, nor in every part of the world, could you render their due thanks. For if you turn a single particular of your particulars toward other than your Lord's good pleasure, you have indeed transgressed against the entire kingdom (mulk) and the dominion (malakūt). So whoever opens his eyelid and directs it toward what is not lawful has disbelieved in every grace of God upon him in the heavens and the earth and all that is between them. For in every single blink there are two graces in the eyelid itself: God — glorified be He — created beneath every eyelid muscles, with tendons and ligaments connected to the nerves of the brain, by which the lowering of the upper eyelid and the raising of the lower eyelid are accomplished; and upon each eyelid are lashes. And the grace of God in their blackness is that it gathers the light of the eye — for whiteness disperses light, while blackness collects it. And the grace of God in their arrangement as a single row is that it serves as a barrier against creeping creatures from crawling into the inner eye, and as a prison for the dust particles that scatter from the air. And for God, in every single lash of them, are two graces: from the aspect of the softness of its root, and — along with softness — the firmness of its uprightness. And in the interweaving of the lashes, He has a grace greater than all: namely, that the dust of the air may prevent the opening of the eye — and were it to close completely, one would see nothing. So He gathered the eyelids to the extent that they interlock with the lashes, and one looks through the lattice of the hair. Thus the lattice of the hair becomes a barrier against the entry of foreign particles from outside, yet not a barrier against the extension of vision from within. And God — glorified and exalted be He — created the edges of the eyelids sharp, closing over the pupil like a polisher: for if dust strikes the pupil, the eyelids close once or twice, and the pupil is polished clean of the dust, and the particles are expelled to the corners of the eye. And since the fly has no eyelids, God created for it two hands — you see it perpetually wiping its two eyes with them, to polish them of dust. So whoever opens his eyelid where lowering it is obligatory has disbelieved, by the opening of the eye, in the grace of God in the eyelids. And the eyelids stand not except by the eye; nor the eye except by the head; nor the head except by the entire body; nor the body except by nourishment; nor nourishment except by water, earth, air, rain, clouds, sun, moon, and stars; nor does any of that stand except by the heavens; and the heavens by the angels. For the whole is like a single thing.

الواحد يرتيط البعض منه بالبعض ارتباط أعضاء البدن بعضها ببعض: فإذا قد كفر

إلا ويلعنه وهكذا كل جارحة؛ جارحة منى صرفتها في غير ما يقربك إلى الله زلقى.
وهبك سلمت من المأثم فقد عرضت نفسك بالغفلة لغيينة وحسرة ما لهما متتهى»
«ردِد : »[مريم: 39]؛ ومن ذلك يدك أنعم اله بها
عليك باطشة تمتد إلى الأشياء مشتملة على مقاصل كثيرة لتتحرك في الجهات فتمتد
تنثني إليك فلا تكون كخشبة منصوبة؛ ثم جعل سبحانه رأس اليد فخلق الكفء
ثم قسم رأس الكف بخمسة أقسام؛ وهي: الأصابع وجعلها في صفين بحيث يكون
الإبهام في جانب ويدور على الأريعة الباقية

.ولو اجتمع الأولون والآخرون على أن يستنبطوا بدقيق الفكر وجها آخر في
وضع الأصابع سوى ما وضعت عليه من بعد الإبهام عن الأربعة وتفاوت الأربعة
في الطول وترتييها في صف واحد لم يقدروا عليه؛ إذ بها يصلح القبض والإعطاءء
فإن بسطها كانت طبنًا يضع عليها ما يريد وإن جمعها كانت آلة للضرب؛ وإن
اضمها ضمًا غير تام كانت مغرفة له وإن بسطها وضم أصابعها كانت مجرفة له ثم
خللن سبحاته الأظفار زبنة للأثامل أو ليلتقط بها الأشياء الدقيقة التي لا تتناولها
الأنامل؛ وليحك بها بدنه؛ فالظفر هو أخس الأعضاء ولو عدمه الإنسان وظهرت به
حكة لكان أعجز الخلق وأضعفهم ولم يقم أحد مقامه في حك بدنه: ثم هدى
اليدين إلى مواضع الحك حتى تمتد إليه ولو في النوم؛ ولو استعان بغيره لم يعثر
على موضع الحك إلا بعد تعب طويل: ثم هيأ له آلة يتناول بها الغذاء.

انم هب أنك أخذت الطعام ببدك؛ فمن أين يكفيك هذا ما لم يصل إلى
المعدة؟ فجعل سبحانه الفم منفذًا إلى المعدة ثم ما فيه من الحكم سوى كونه منفًا

وطبق الأضراس من العليا على السفلى ليطحن بها الطعام طحا

اثم الطعام تارة يحتاج إلى الكسر وتارة يحتاج إلى القطع ثم يحتاج إلى الطحن
بعد ذلكء فقسم الأسنان إلى طواحن وهي الأضراس: وإلى حادة قواطع

# PageV1P248
anchors:
- Root: ج-د-د (j-d-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Earnestness, exertion, newness; al-jadd = fortune/strength in striving
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Seriousness in religious affairs (jidd fī al-dīn) as opposed to laxity (tasāhul)
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: newness of garment; Metaphorical: renewal of resolve in worship
- Root: ن-ع-م (n-ʿ-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Softness, ease, abundance; niʿmah = benefaction, state of well-being
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine favor (niʿam Allāh) as comprehensive, encompassing all creation
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: pasture and softness; Metaphorical: all bounties from the Throne to the earth
- Root: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Measuring, shaping, creating; khilqah = innate constitution
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine creation (khalq) as purposeful origination (ījād ʿalā taqdīr)
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: smoothing/leveling; Metaphorical: fashioning with wisdom (ḥikmah)
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Repeated Protasis (al-sharṭ al-mukarrar) — The repeated "if" (fa-idhā) structures parallel conditions, each with its own apodosis, demonstrating cumulative argumentation.
translation:
I say: The stations of earnest striving in religion are interconnected, each part linked to the other like the limbs of the body are linked together. So when one has disbelieved in all the favors of God — from the farthest reaches of the Pleiades down to the very earth — then there remains no angel, no celestial sphere, no animal, no plant, except that it curses him. Likewise, every limb of yours — any limb you have diverted toward that which does not draw you nearer to God — is accursed. Even if you were spared from sin, you have exposed yourself through heedlessness to regret and remorse that have no end. God says: {«And warn them of the Day of Regret»} [Maryam: 39]. And from this [reflection] is your hand — a favor God bestowed upon you — an instrument that extends toward things, containing many joints so that it may move in various directions, extending and folding back toward you, not being like a fixed wooden post. Then He — glorified be He — made the head of the hand, creating the palm, then divided the head of the palm into five parts: the fingers, and He placed them in two rows such that the thumb stands on one side and rotates around the remaining four.

And if the first and the last [of mankind] were to gather together to devise, with the finest subtlety of thought, another arrangement for the fingers — other than that which they are placed upon, of the thumb's distance from the four, the four's variation in length, and their arrangement in a single row — they would not be able to do so. For by this [arrangement] grasping and giving are perfected. If one spreads them out, they become a flat surface upon which to place what one desires; if one closes them, they become an instrument for striking; if one closes them incompletely, they become a ladle; and if one spreads them and folds the fingers, they become a shovel. Then He — glorified be He — created the nails as an adornment for the fingertips, or so that one may pick up with them the delicate objects that the fingertips cannot grasp, and so that one may scratch the body with them. For the nail is the most insignificant of the limbs — yet if a person lacked it and an itch appeared on him, he would be the most incapable and weakest of creation, and no one could take its place in scratching his body. Then He guided the two hands to the places of itching, so that they extend to them even in sleep; and if one sought the help of another, he would not find the place of the itch except after great exertion. Then He prepared for him an instrument by which to take food.

Now consider: even if you took food with your hand, how would this suffice you unless it reached the stomach? So He — glorified be He — made the mouth a passage to the stomach, and within it are wisdoms beyond merely being a passage. Then when you place food in the mouth as a single piece, it is not easy to swallow; so one needs a mill to grind the food. Thus He — glorified be He — created two jaws from two bones, and set in them the teeth, and fitted the molars of the upper [jaw] upon the lower, to grind food with them thoroughly.

Then food sometimes needs to be broken, sometimes needs to be cut, and then needs to be ground after that. So He divided the teeth into grinders — which are the molars — and into sharp incisors.

### | الصفحة 249

بالأحجارء فجمسل يقول لهم: ارموني بهذه الأحجار الصفار لثلا أحتاج إلى
غسل الدمء فقيل له في ذلك فأنشد'”

السيس للهارب قي مهريه أبدا مين راحةإلا إل

رب رام لي بأحجار الأذى الم أجد بدا من العطف عليه

بلع الله عل اح القوم فيدنيني إل

ونحو هذا نل الطرطوشي عن أويسء ويقول: تشغلوني بغسل الدم عن

وقد تقدمت حكاية الذي سلب ثوبه فهتف بالسالب: جعلتك في حل. فقل:
قبلت؛ أن يلبس الثوب حلالا ولا يلبسه حرائ.

وعرف عياض بالبهلول بن راشد؛ وذكر من فضائله؛ أنه أخبر عن بعض
أصحابه أنه ضرب بمقرعة بالليل: فأتاه ابهلول يسأله أن يجعل الذي فعل ذلك في
حل؛ فقال الرجل: فعلوا بي؛ وفعلوا بي؛ وأجعلهم في حل؟ قال: أيسرك أن يحال
بين أخيك المسلم وبين الجنة بسبيك؟ فلم يزل بالرجل حتى جعل الجاني عليه في
حل.

وعرف أيضًا بعبد الجبار من الفقهاء المالكية ومن أكابر أصحاب سحنون»
قال: كان يغد إلى الجمعة إذا بشاب جميل حسن البزة يمشي في إثر صبية؛ فاتك
عبد الجبار على نعلهء فقطع شسعه؛ وناداء: يا شاب. فوقف يمشي إليه؛ وقال له: أنا
شيخ ضعيف بصري. وانقطع شسعي. فأصلحه لي؛ قتناوله الشاب؛ ورأى عبد
الجبار الصبية تتباطأ في مشيهاء فأصلحه؛ وأخحذ منه النعل» ومشى في إثر الصبية.
فقطعه ثاتئء وناداه ليصلحه» فعطف عليه. وقال: أنا قطعته يا شاب إشفاقًا على هذا
الشاب من لفح الشاره ويكى فيكى الفتى؛ وجزاه خيرًا؛ وصحبه إلى الجامع؛
وحسنت توبته. قال عياض: وكان يتكلم بالحكمة: ومن حكمه: فلو أهمك شأنك
الكل لسانك وتهيجت أحزاتك.

# PageV1P250
anchors:
- Root: ج-د-د (j-d-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of "newness" and "earnestness, seriousness, exertion" — the opposite of jest (hazl); also "freshness" and "vigor" in striving.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the theological context, jidd denotes the soul's sincere and unremitting application to the worship of God, free from negligence or frivolity — a station (maqām) of the rightly guided.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense is "cutting" or "renewing" (as in a new garment); metaphorically (majāz), it is the renewal of resolve in religious practice, as if one "cuts" through worldly distractions.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The phrase "المقام التاسع" is in apposition to the section heading, clarifying the specific station under discussion; the subsequent conditional clauses (law, idhā) follow the standard protasis-apodosis structure.
translation:
I say — and success is with God:

Know that the ninth station of the rightly guided in the stations of religion is earnestness in religion (al-jidd fī al-dīn). This is the station of those who have realized the truth of servitude, who have witnessed the overwhelming nature of the Divine blessings, and who have come to know that the tongue, even if it spent all its days in praise and thanksgiving, could never discharge the due of even one of God's favors.

Consider, O servant, the wisdom of your Lord in the creation of the jawbone. Had He not made the lower jaw movable with a circular motion, while the upper jaw remained fixed, the grinding of food would not be accomplished — for one jaw would merely strike against the other without any milling. But God, in His wisdom, made the lower jaw rotate upon the upper like the turning of a millstone. Then, when you place food in the cavity of the mouth, how does it move beneath the teeth? How do the teeth draw it to themselves? Or how could the hand manage it within the mouth? So God, in His mercy, created the tongue, which roams the sides of the mouth and returns the food from the center to the teeth according to need. This, along with the tongue's faculty of taste, and the fountain of saliva that God created within it, which flows forth in due measure to moisten the food — for a person cannot swallow unless the food is lubricated with saliva. And God subjugated this faculty such that the mouth waters at the mere sight of food from afar, the poor servant's saliva stirring before the food even reaches it.

Yet all these blessings of the tongue are but trifling beside its greatest benefit — the faculty of speech (quwwat al-manṭiq). For the tongue is among God's mighty blessings and wondrous works of His craftsmanship. Were it given no movement except to praise its Creator and to loose its utterance in thanksgiving, it could never, ever, discharge the due of God's glory. The master of the first and the last, upon him be peace, said: «لَا أُحْصِي ثَنَاءً عَلَيْكَ» — "I cannot enumerate the praises due to You" — so how could any tongue find room to slacken its rein?

If you say, "I have not sinned," I reply in verse:
*Your very existence is a sin that cannot be measured by any other.*

So whoever does not fear being called to account — yet if he is called to account, punishment will inevitably befall him — how could the Sufi's blood be considered shed in vain and his property lawful plunder?

It is related of Maʿrūf al-Karkhī that he passed by a man who was giving water in charity, saying, "May God have mercy on whoever drinks." Maʿrūf took that water and drank. It was said to him, "Were you not fasting?" He replied, "Yes, but it is the supplication of a Muslim — perhaps it will be answered."

And the boys used to harm Buhlūl, throwing stones at him. He would say to them, "Throw me with these small stones, so that I may not need to wash off blood." When questioned about this, he recited:

*The one fleeing from his pursuer never finds rest except in the refuge of God.*
*Many a thrower has thrown stones of harm at me, and I found no escape but in tenderness toward him.*
*May God bless the people who, by their harm, drew me nearer to Him.*

And similar is related of al-Ṭurṭūshī concerning Uways, who said, "You occupy me with washing off blood instead of prayer."

And there has already preceded the story of the man whose garment was snatched, and he called out to the thief, "I have made you lawful [in it]." The thief replied, "I accept — that the garment be worn lawfully, not unlawfully."

And ʿIyāḍ related of Buhlūl ibn Rāshid, mentioning among his virtues, that he was informed of one of his companions who had been struck with a whip at night. Buhlūl came to him asking that he forgive the one who had done it. The man said, "They did such-and-such to me, and such-and-such — and should I forgive them?" Buhlūl said, "Would it please you that a barrier be placed between your Muslim brother and Paradise because of you?" He kept at the man until he forgave the one who had wronged him.

And ʿIyāḍ also related of ʿAbd al-Jabbār, one of the Mālikī jurists and among the greatest companions of Saḥnūn, that he was going to the Friday prayer when he saw a handsome young man, well-dressed, walking behind a girl. ʿAbd al-Jabbār stepped on his own sandal and broke its strap, then called out, "O young man!" The youth stopped and came to him. He said, "I am an old, weak man with poor sight, and my sandal strap has broken — fix it for me." The young man took it, and ʿAbd al-Jabbār saw the girl slowing her pace. He fixed the sandal, took it back, and walked on behind the girl. Then he broke it a second time and called the youth to fix it again. The youth turned to him, and he said, "I broke it, O young man, out of compassion for this youth, fearing the scorching of the sun [upon him]." The young man wept, thanked him, accompanied him to the mosque, and his repentance became good. ʿIyāḍ said: "He used to speak with wisdom." Among his wise sayings: "If your own affair concerned you, your tongue would be restrained and your sorrows would be stirred."

title_en: Section 193 — The Ninth Station: Earnestness in Religion (al-Jidd fī al-Dīn)
arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 250

4 منهج الترقي) المقام التاسع: الأ بالجد في الدين

وعرف أيضًا بزيد بن بشيرء قال: كان فقيها ثقة» سمع من ابن القاسم وابن
وهب وأشهب. قال: من فضائله أن طريقه إلى الجامع كان على الخرازين؛ فأقبل
يوم مع الطلبة إذا بشاب من الخرازين قام على دكاته؛ وقال لجاره: قم الى التيسء
ما رأيت أوحش من هذا الشيخ؛ فتكس زيد رأسه» فلما انصرف من الجامع عاوده
الفتى بقبيح؛ فلم يلتفت إليه زيد؛ وهم طلبته بضرب الفتىء فبلغ ذلك زيّاء فسألهم
عنه» فقالوا: هو ما قيل أصلحك الله لاستخفافه بحقك: فقال لهم: أعطي الله عهدًا
تقدم إليه أحد لأقصيته ولا وطئن لي بساطاء أنا أصلح شأنه وصر في صرة
عشرة دراهم؛ وجعلها في جييه؛ واستعمل لفرد نعل قبالا واهئاء توجه إلى الجامع»
فلما مر بالشاب قام لعادته وتكلم بقبيح قوله: فلما حاذاه الشيخ انكأ على نعله فقطع
القبال: ثم مال إلى الشاب فسلم عليه وقال: أي بني. لعل عندك قبالا؟ فأدخل زيد
يده وأخرج الصرة من جيبه ودفعها له؛ فقال الشاب: ما هذا؟ فقال: صنعت لنا فالا
فكافآناك. فسار إلى الجامع: فلما كان انصرافه منهء ومر بالشاب قام على قدميه
وقال: الحمد لله الذي خص بلدنا بهذا الشيخ الفاضل؛ اللهم أبقه لناء واحرزه على
المسلمين.

.وقد تقدم قبل هذا بيسير مقام السبائي من العلماء المالكية ودينه وفضله؛ تقل
عنه عياض: أنه مر بموضع فإذا بشيخ لم ير أجمل منه لحية وهو يزمر بيوق» فقال
السبائي لبعض أصحابه: لعلك قالت لك نفسك: إنك خير منه إنه مسلم؛ ولله ما
أرى لي فضلًا على أهل الكبائر من المسلمين؛ فإذا رأيتم أهل البلاء فاحمدوا الله
على العافية. فذكر أن الرجل ريء بأثر ذلك وقد تاب وحمج وحسنت حاله. ولقي
سكران بشر الحافي وقال له: يا سيديء يا أبا نصرء فلم يدفعه بشر عن نفسه؛ فلما
آنولى تغرغرت عينا بشرء وقال: رجل أحب رجلا على خير توهمه؛ لعل المحب قد
نجا والمحبوب لا يدري ما حاله.

وعرف عياض أيضًا بأبي محرزء وذكر من دينه وفضله قال: أطلع الناس على
ماله يوم ولي القضاء؛ أشهدهم إن ظهرت زيادة على ما رأوا فهو خائن. قال: وقف
عليه رجل به نبيذ» فكثر من الكلام فأمر به أبو محرز إلى السجنء فقال الرجل: أيها
القاضي» إن زوجي مهرها ثلائمائة دينار وهي طالق إن لم تمن لي؛ فالتفت أبو
محرز إلى جلسائه وقال: أرأيتم ما حل بنا من هذا؟ ثم سكت ساعة وقال: "أتيناكم

# PageV1P251
anchors:
- Root: ج-د-د (j-d-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of "earnestness, seriousness, exertion" — the opposite of jest (hazl); also "newness" (jadīd) as renewal of effort.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the spiritual path, jidd denotes the soul's vigorous striving against base desires, a prerequisite for traversing the stations (maqāmāt).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "cutting" (qaṭʿ) — as one cuts through obstacles; metaphorically, the believer cuts through worldly distractions to reach the Divine.
- Root: و-ق-ر (w-q-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Heaviness, gravity, dignity (waqār) — the settled composure of a man of knowledge.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The outward calm that reflects inward God-consciousness (taqwā); a prophetic trait.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal "weight" (thiqal); metaphorically, the moral weight that silences frivolity.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Nasaq (Coordination) — The narrative uses wa (and) to sequence actions, each verb retaining its independent temporal frame, showing the saint's deliberate, unbroken response.
translation:
I say — may Allah grant us success — this is the ninth station: earnestness in religion.

It is also known regarding Zayd ibn Bashīr. He said: He was a jurist of reliability; he heard from Ibn al-Qāsim, Ibn Wahb, and Ashab. Among his virtues: his path to the mosque passed through the street of the shoemakers (al-kharrāzīn). One day he came with the students, when a young man from among the shoemakers stood upon his bench and said to his neighbor: "Get up to the billy-goat — I have never seen anyone more repulsive than this shaykh!" Zayd bowed his head. When he returned from the mosque, the youth accosted him again with foul speech, but Zayd paid him no heed. His students intended to strike the youth, and this reached Zayd, so he asked them about him. They said: "It is as was said — may Allah set you right — for his belittling of your due." He said to them: "I have made a covenant with Allah: if anyone approaches me, I will not banish him, nor will he tread my carpet [in vain]. I will mend his affair." He wrapped ten dirhams in a cloth and placed it in his pocket, and he used a sandal-strap (qibāl) that was worn out. When he set out for the mosque, as he passed the youth, the youth stood up as was his habit and spoke his foul words. When the shaykh drew alongside him, he leaned upon his sandal and broke the strap. Then he turned to the youth, greeted him, and said: "My son, perhaps you have a strap?" Zayd put his hand in, brought out the cloth from his pocket, and gave it to him. The youth said: "What is this?" He replied: "You made a strap for us, so we have rewarded you." Then he proceeded to the mosque. When he departed from it and passed the youth, the youth stood on his feet and said: "Praise be to Allah who has distinguished our town with this virtuous shaykh! O Allah, preserve him for us, and guard him for the Muslims."

And shortly before this, there has preceded the station of al-Sibāʿī among the Mālikī scholars, his religion and his virtue. ʿIyāḍ transmitted from him: that he passed by a place, and there was an old man — none more handsome in beard had he seen — who was playing a flute (bi-būq). Al-Sibāʿī said to one of his companions: "Perhaps your soul has said to you that you are better than him. He is a Muslim. By Allah, I do not see any merit for myself over the people of grave sins among the Muslims. When you see people of affliction, praise Allah for well-being." It was mentioned that the man was seen after that, having repented, grown earnest, and his state became good. And he met a drunkard — Bishr al-Ḥāfī — and said to him: "My master, O Abā Naṣr!" Bishr did not push him away. When he turned away, Bishr's eyes brimmed with tears, and he said: "A man loved a man for a good he imagined in him; perhaps the lover has been saved, while the beloved does not know his own state."

ʿIyāḍ also reported regarding Abū Muḥriz, and mentioned of his religion and virtue. He said: He showed the people his wealth on the day he assumed the judgeship, and made them witness: if any increase appeared beyond what they saw, he would be a traitor. He said: A man with wine (nabīdh) stood before him and spoke at length, so Abū Muḥriz ordered him to prison. The man said: "O judge! My wife's dowry is three hundred dīnārs, and she is divorced if you do not pardon me." Abū Muḥriz turned to his companions and said: "Do you see what has befallen us from this man?" Then he was silent for an hour and said: "We have come to you..."

وعرف عياض أيضًا بأبي العباس التميمي؛ قال: كان حافظا للمسائل من أهل

# PageV1P252
anchors:
- Root: س ت ر (s-t-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Covering, veiling, concealing; a screen or curtain that hides something from sight.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the divine context, 'satr' is Allah's attribute of veiling sins and faults of His servants in this world and the next; in human conduct, it is the praiseworthy act of not exposing another's transgression.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical covering; metaphorical (majāz) — concealing a moral blemish or legal offense, as in 'satara ʿalayhi' (he covered for him).
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of 'al-ʿaṭf ʿalā al-ḍamīr al-marfūʿ' (coordination on a nominative pronoun) — In the phrase "فدخلوا وأغلق الباب" (they entered and he closed the door), the verb 'aghlaqa' is coordinated on the understood pronoun of 'dakhalū', showing sequential actions with a single agent shift, permissible due to the explicit pronoun.
translation:
I say — and success is from Allah:

Know that the perfection of gentleness (al-rifq) in religion is that the one who administers the prescribed punishment (al-ḥadd) does so with complete justice, without exceeding the measure ordained by Allah, and without mixing personal rancor or tribal partisanship (ḥamiyyah) into the execution. For the punishment is a right of Allah, not a vent for human anger.

The Prophet ﷺ said to the one who had cursed the man upon whom he had carried out the prescribed punishment: "Do not be an aid to Satan against your brother. Verily, he loves Allah and His Messenger." {«لا تكونوا عونا للشيطان على أخيكم؛ إنه يحب الله ورسوله»} — meaning: the one punished had already been purified by the ḥadd; to revile him after that is to assist Satan in his enmity toward him.

Consider the case of ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) when he refrained from striking a drunkard, saying: "I do not love to strike a Muslim out of personal zeal (ḥamiyyah) for myself." And his case with those whom he observed drinking — he concealed them. And the case of ʿUthmān (may Allah be pleased with him) when he said: "Praise be to Allah who did not expose them at my hands," and he freed a slave in gratitude to Allah the Exalted that no disgrace of a Muslim man had occurred at his hands.

Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ also reported to us concerning Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Tamīmī, saying: He was a preserver of legal questions (masāʾil), one of the people of independent judgment (ijtihād) and scrupulous piety (waraʿ). It was read to him in Fayrawān, and he heard [hadith] from him. He said: The people agreed upon his excellence. They were sitting with him one day at the door of his house, when he suddenly rose and said to them: "Arise, enter!" So they entered, and he closed the door, and they did not know the reason. Then he began looking through the crack of the door, then opened it and said to them: "Go out." They asked him: "What is the reason?" He said: "I saw a drunkard, and I did not want you to see him." They said to him: "Who is he?" He said: "I concealed him from you; then shall I inform you of him?" — meaning: he refused to expose him even after the fact.

And he also reported to us concerning the Qāḍī Ibn al-Salīm, saying: He was a preserver of jurisprudence (fiqh), and despite his knowledge, he was one of the people of asceticism (zuhd) and piety (birr). His flight from the Sultan was prolonged until destiny (al-qadar) ensnared him, and he attained the leadership of this world and religion in al-Andalus. Yet he did not change from his guidance, nor did this world deceive him in any way. One day he attended a mosque on the outskirts of Cordoba to await a funeral procession. The time of prayer came, and no one gave the call to prayer (adhān) there. He said to a man from the common folk: "O you! Go out and give the call to prayer." And behold, the man was ignorant, and he was disturbed by his words and said to him: "Did you not see in the gathering anyone more ill-omened (anḥas) than me?" The Qāḍī smiled, sought forgiveness, and went out himself, gave the call to prayer, returned, and led the people in prayer. Then he said to the man: "I found someone more ill-omened than you — so do not repeat such a word, but [the matter is] upon us and upon you." The man said: "I do not do well; may Allah forgive [us]."

title_en: Section 195 — The Ninth Station: Earnestness (Jidd) in Religion

اللصوص الذين قالوا: لغير هذا جثناء جازوا للعصيان بقلوب قاسية؛ فنالوا بركة

والشيء بذكر بالشيء؛ من الرسالة عن الزجاجي قال: مانت أمي؛ فورثت دارا

# PageV1P253
anchors:
- Root: ج-د-د (j-d-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of "earnestness, exertion, seriousness" — the opposite of jest (hazl); also "newness" (jadīd), implying renewal of effort.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the spiritual path, jidd denotes the soul's vigorous striving against base desires, aligning with the Quranic command to "strive in God's cause with due striving" (jāhidū fī Allāhi ḥaqqa jihādihī).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "hardness of ground" (arḍ jaddāʾ); metaphorically, it is the firmness of resolve in religious practice — a ḥaqīqah in conduct, majāz in terrain.
- Root: و-ع-ظ (w-ʿ-ẓ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Admonition, exhortation — from waʿaẓa, "to remind of consequences"; implies both warning and counsel.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Waʿẓ is the reminder that softens the heart toward obedience and deters from transgression — a Quranic mode of guidance (faʿiẓah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal "piercing" (waʿẓ) of the ear; metaphorically, the piercing of the heart with truth.
- Root: ت-و-ب (t-w-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Return (tawbah) — the act of turning back from error to rectitude; root also yields tāba (to repent) and matāb (place of return).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, tawbah is the intellectual and moral reorientation of the soul from disobedience to obedience, contingent on sincere intention (niyyah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal "returning" to a place; metaphorically, the soul's return to God after straying — a majāz of spiritual geography.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — In "فقدمه صلى بالناس" (he put him forward, and he led the people in prayer), the verb sequence (fa-qaddamahu, ṣallā) shows consecutive actions without explicit conjunction, following the pattern of ḥāl (circumstantial clause) where the second verb explains the first's outcome.
translation:
I say — and God grants success:

Know that the ninth station of the path of ascent (manhaj al-taraqqī) is earnestness (jidd) in religion. Its reality is the soul's firm resolve in God's command, untainted by laxity or self-indulgence.

ʿIyāḍ related, on the authority of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mudārik, who said: He was a scholar of Mālik's school, a memorizer of ḥadīth, deeply rooted in his knowledge, devout, and given to much night prayer (tahajjud). Some of his companions died, leaving behind a young son. He inquired about him and was informed that his conduct was not upright. So he ordered that the boy be brought to him. The boy attended his gathering, and when the time of prayer came, he put him forward to lead the people in prayer. When they finished and he was alone with him, he admonished him (waʿaẓahu) and said: "Beware — do not let people say: 'Look at whom ʿAbd al-Raḥmān put forward to lead us in prayer!'"

And from the wondrous accounts: A certain shaykh had gathered wealth for the construction of some hospices (ribāṭāt). A group of thieves learned of this, disguised themselves in the garb of the righteous, concealed their weapons, and sought his hospitality. When food was set before them and they washed their hands, the shaykh had a chronically ill daughter (zamintah). She drank from that water and used it seeking blessing (tabarrukan) from the guests — and God healed her instantly. The shaykh came, treated them kindly, and said: "You are blessed!" — and recounted the story to them. Remorse fell upon them, and they said to him: "We did not come for this, but after God has bestowed this favor upon us and cast this veil of concealment over us, we have indeed repented (tubnā)."

And in the Risālah (of al-Qushayrī): "Chivalry (futūwah) is not that you do good to one who has done good to you — for that is recompense and requital. Rather, chivalry is that you do good to one who has wronged you." They said: "The Sufi is like the earth — every foul thing is cast upon it, yet nothing emerges from it but every beautiful thing." It is narrated that a certain Sufi was advancing in rank through the sincerity of his gratitude (ṣidq al-shukr). A man whose hand had been cut off by the sword visited him. He said: "A visit with a severed hand!" The man said: "O my master, I do not hold you to account for this — why did you not defend your companion and leave him to exact retribution from him?" End of quote.

The Sufis call this heart that seeks forgiveness for its oppressor until he is transformed — as mentioned previously in the story of the thieves who said, "We did not come for this," yet they passed from disobedience with hard hearts, and attained the blessing of repentance (tawbah) and the rectification of intention (iṣlāḥ al-niyyah).

And a thing is recalled by its like. From the Risālah, on the authority of al-Zajjājī, who said: "My mother died, and I inherited a house. I sold it for fifty dīnārs and set out for the Pilgrimage. When I reached Bābil, a man from the Qayāqinah met me and said: 'What do you have with you?' I said to myself: 'Truthfulness is best.' So I said: 'Fifty dīnārs.' He said: 'Hand it to me.' I handed him the purse. He counted it — and behold, it was fifty. He said to me: 'Take it — for your truthfulness has seized me.' Then he dismounted from his beast and said: 'Ride it.' I said: 'I do not wish to.' But he insisted, so I rode it. He said: 'And I am on your trail.' When the following year came, he caught up with me and stayed with me until he died."

And it has already preceded at the end of the Second Station the saying of Tāj al-Dīn: "The soul's share in disobedience is manifest."

title_en: On the Station of Earnestness in Religion and the Danger of Self-Amazement
arabic_text:
### | الصفحة 253

منيج الترفي/ المقاماتاسع: الأغط بالجد في الدين 7
جلي؛ وحظها في الطاعة باطن خفي؛ فراجعه. ومن نحو هذا قول السبائي: ما أرى
لي فضلًا على أهل الكبائر؛ حكاية حسان بن أبي سنان لقي رجلا به زهد وكان مع
حسان رجل؛ فسآله حسان مسألة لطيفة: فقال الرجل: تسائل هذا مثل هذه المساءلة».
حتى يظن في نفسه أنه شي؟ فقال له: وما يدريك لعله تكون فيه خصلة يحبها الله
وفيك خصلة يبغضها لله فقال له: يا عبد لله وما هذه الخصلة التي فيه يحبها الى
والخصلة التي فيه يبغضها له؟ قال له: لعله
ولعلك حين رأيته حدثتك نفسك أنك خير منه. وقد تقدم في آخر المقام الثاني في
محاجة معاوية للمسور إذ قال له: ألم يكن لك يا مسور ذنوب تخاف أن يؤاخذك
الله بها؟ فقال: بلى؛ فقال: وما جعلك أحق أن ترجو المغفرة مني وإني وإيلك على
دين يقبل الله فيه الحسنات؛ إلى آخر الحكاية حتى قال المسور: فعرفت أنه
خصمني: فكان بعد لا يذكره إلا بخير.

وفي الكتب المنزلة: حذر الصديقين أني إن وضعت عدلي عليهم عذبتهم.
وعن حفص بن حميد قال: قلت لابن المبارك: رأبت رجلا قدل رجلًاء فوقع في
نفسي إني أفضل منه؛ فقال لي ابن المبارك: أمنك على نفسك أشد من ذنيه. اه

.وانظر إذا كان متقي الشرك يوشك أن يغفر له فكيف لا يترك به من يوقن أنه
إن نوقش الحساب عذب؛ فقد صح: "من نوقش الحساب عذب”. وثبت القرآن:
[النساء: 48]. اه

عاد الكلام إلى سيد الأنام: "لا أحصي ثناء عليك؛ أنت كما أثنيت على
انفسك””» فكيف بمن دونه ي؟ فبالحري لمن رأى المنة وأيقن بالتقصير أن تصدر
منه الحالة التي هي ثمرتهاء وذلك الاستحياء حبق الحياء؛ وهذه حالة الرجل الذي
غبطه الحسن البصري رضي الله عنهء وذلك أنه قيل له: هاهنا رجل لم نره قط إلا
جالا وحده خلف سارية؛ فقال الحسن: إذا رأيتموه فأخبروني فنظروا إليه ذات
